Al-Sha'bi said: The ihsan of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she washes herself from impurity (janabah) and guards her private part.

Al-Hasan said: If a man sees immorality from his wife and is certain of it, he should not keep her.

Then they differed about whether the verse is general or specific. Some of them said: It is general, covering all women of the Book, whether they are at war or under protection (dhimmi). This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan.

Some of them said: It refers to the women under protection. As for the women at war, their women are forbidden to the Muslims. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

Al-Suddi narrated from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from him [Ibn Abbas], who said: Among the women of the People of the Book, some are lawful to us and some are not lawful to us. Then he recited: ﴿Fight those who do not believe...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿...while they are humbled.﴾ So whoever gives the jizyah (tax), his women are lawful to us; and whoever does not give the jizyah, his women are not lawful to us.

Al-Hakam said: I mentioned that to Ibrahim, and it pleased him. Ibn Umar did not consider marrying women of the Book permissible, and he interpreted this verse by His saying: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾, saying: I know of no polytheism greater than a woman saying that her lord is Jesus.

Al-Mubarak narrated from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, who said: A man asked al-Hasan: May a man marry a woman of the People of the Book? He said: What has he to do with the People of the Book, when Allah has made Muslim women abundant? If he must do it, then let him choose her as a chaste woman, not a fornicator. The man said: What is a fornicator? He said: She is the one who, when a man glances at her, she follows him. ﴿And whoever denies faith, his deeds are lost﴾.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that some men said, when the saying of Allah was revealed, ﴿And [lawful are] chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾: How can we marry women who are not on our religion? So Allah revealed this verse.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed concerning those of the women of the People of the Book whom Muslims had made chaste. He says: The Muslims' making them chaste does not bring them out of disbelief, meaning concerning them in their religion [...] [an unreadable word] and it made them among those who disbelieved in faith, so his deeds are lost. And this is general for people: ﴿And whoever denies faith, his deeds are lost, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾, meaning among the people of the Fire.

Ibn Abbas said concerning ﴿And whoever denies...﴾: "Whoever denies Allah." Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: If this narration is sound, its meaning is "with the Lord of faith," and it was said: "with those who believe in Him."

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿And whoever denies faith﴾, that is, what was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Tha'alibi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Juhani say: I heard Abu al-Haytham al-Sanjari say: The "ba'" (with) is a filler particle, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [76:6], and ﴿a tree that grows with oil﴾ [23:20]. The meaning is: ﴿And whoever denies faith﴾, that is, rejects it, ﴿his deeds are lost﴾.

Al-Hasan read it with a fatha on the "ba'." Ibn al-Sumay' read: "fa-qad habita amaluhu wa-huwa fi al-akhirati mina al-khasirin" (his deeds are lost, and he, in the Hereafter, is among the losers).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 1–5 (part 1 of 3):

Madaniyya, and among its abrogated (mansukh) verses are nine, including His saying:
﴿Do not violate the sacred rites of Allah﴾ – abrogated by the verse of the sword. [Marginal note in the manuscript: (﴿Some of them are closer to others in the Book of Allah﴾) (Surat al-Anfal: 75). What exceeds the bond of kinship in disobedience, a reward from Allah.]
The last complete surah revealed was "Bara'a" (al-Tawba), and the last verse revealed in Surat al-Nisa' was ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾.
Al-Suddi said: the last of the Qur'an to be revealed were these verses: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ (Surat al-Nisa': 176); ﴿But if they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾ (Surat al-Tawba: 129); ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ (Surat al-Baqara: 281).
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in his sermon on the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage: "O people, Surat al-Ma'ida is among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, so make lawful its lawful and make unlawful its unlawful." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/31.] [1] Its letters number eleven thousand, nine hundred and thirty-three; its words, two thousand, eight hundred and four; and its verses, one hundred and twenty.
From Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surat al-Ma'ida while on his mount, and it could not bear him until he dismounted.
Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Ma'ida will be given a reward equal to the number of every Jew and Christian who breathes in the world, ten good deeds, and ten of his sins will be erased." [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/257; in the source: "and ten degrees will be raised for him."] [2]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿O you who believe﴾: "Yā" is a call, meaning an indication; "hā" is an alert. ﴿Those who believe﴾ [Ibn al-Jawzi in Zad al-Masir: 2/230 said: it is disputed. It is said they are the believers of our community, and this is the view of the majority; and it is said they are the People of the Book, related by Ibn Jurayj.] [in apposition (badal) to "ayyuha" – as in the manuscript]. ﴿Fulfil the contracts﴾: meaning the covenants.

Al-Zajjaj said: "al-'uqud" means the contracts, or all covenants. It is said: "'aqadtu fulanan" and "'ahadtu fulanan," and from it comes "dhalika bi-stiwaq," and its root is tying a thing to another, as when a rope is tied to a rope when joined firmly. Al-Hutay'a said:
"A people who, when they make a contract with their neighbour, / they bind the 'anaj and bind the kurab upon it." [Al-Sihah: 1/331.]

They differed about what these contracts are. Ibn Juraij said: this address is specific to the People of the Book, who believed in the earlier scriptures and messengers: "Fulfil the covenants which were made among you concerning Muhammad," and His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: that which I have given you of Book and wisdom﴾ [Surat Al 'Imran: 81], and His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those given the Book: you shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it﴾ [Surat Al 'Imran: 187]. Others said: it is general.

Qatada said: it refers to what they contracted upon in the Jahiliyya; his evidence is His saying: ﴿And those whom your oaths have bound﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 33].

Ibn Abbas: they are the covenants of oaths and separation. Others: they are the contracts which people made among themselves.

﴿Lawful to you is the beast of cattle﴾: they differed about it. Al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Rabi', al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it is all livestock, and it is the name for cattle, sheep and camels; evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And of the cattle, some for burden and some for slaughter﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 142], then He explained what they are: ﴿eight pairs: of sheep two﴾. By it is meant what the people of the Jahiliyya had forbidden to themselves of livestock.

Al-Sha'bi said: "bahimat al-an'am" are the fetuses found dead in their mothers' wombs when they are slaughtered.

Atiyya al-Awfi related from Ibn Umar regarding His saying ﴿Lawful to you is the beast of cattle﴾, that he said: "It is what is in their bellies." I said: "If it comes out dead, may I eat it?" He said: "Yes, it is in the position of its lung and liver." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/68.] [3]

Qabus related from his father, from Ibn Abbas, that a cow was slaughtered and a fetus was found in its belly; Ibn Abbas took hold of the fetus's tail and said: "This is of the beast of cattle which is lawful to you." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/68.]

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the fetus, and he said: "Its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother." [Musnad Ahmad: 3/31.] [3]

Al-Kalbi said: "bahimat al-an'am" is its wild game, like gazelles and wild cattle, singly. It is called "bahima" only because every living creature that cannot discern is a "bahima"; it was so named because it is made obscure (ubhimat) from discernment.

﴿Except what is recited to you﴾: meaning, to you in the Qur'an, [because it is the judge], and it is His saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion and blood … and what is sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek decision by arrows; that is depravity﴾, and His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is depravity﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 121].

﴿Not lawful the game while you are in the state of ihram﴾: al-Akhfash said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning "Fulfil the contracts" while you are in pilgrim state, not making lawful the game; and in it is [the sense of prohibition] [an illegible word in the manuscript; what we have inserted appears to be correct].

Al-Kisa'i said: it is a circumstantial clause of His saying: ﴿Lawful to you is the beast of cattle﴾ … ﴿not making lawful the game﴾, as one says: "Lawful to you is food, without transgressing in it."

Its meaning: all cattle is made lawful to you except what of it is wild, for that is game, and it is not lawful to you when you are in the state of ihram. That is His saying: ﴿while you are in the state of ihram﴾. The majority read its first letter with a damma, from "harama, yahrumu, haraman" in the sense of movements; both are plurals of "haram." It is said: "rajul haram," "harm," and "muhrim," and "halal," "hall," and "muhall." ﴿Indeed Allah decrees what He wills﴾ [He forbids what He wills to whom He wills] [addition from Zad al-Masir: 2/231].

﴿O you who believe, do not violate the sacred rites of Allah﴾ – the verse.

It was revealed concerning al-Hutam, whose name was Shurayh ibn Dsubay'a ibn Hind ibn Shurahbil al-Bakri. It is said that when he came to Medina, he left his horses outside the city and entered alone upon the Prophet (ﷺ), who said to him: "To what do you invite the people?" He said: "To the testimony that there is no god but Allah, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakat." [Asbab al-Nuzul: 125; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/43.] [4] He said: "Good, except that I have people whom I do not decide any matter without; perhaps I will embrace Islam and bring them."

The Prophet (ﷺ) had said to his companions: "Some of Rabi'a will enter upon you, speaking with the tongue of Satan." Then Shurayh left his presence. When he had gone out, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He entered with the face of a disbeliever and left with the trace of a treacherous one." He passed by the herd of Medina, drove it off and departed with it, chanting:
"The night has wrapped it with a driver, fierce, / not a shepherd of camels nor of sheep,
nor a butcher upon the butchering-block; / they slept, and the son of Hind did not sleep.
He is accompanied by a youth like a mace, / bow-legged, with smooth-soled feet." [Jami' al-Bayan: 6/79.]

When the following year came, he set out as a pilgrim among the pilgrims of Bakr ibn Wa'il from al-Yamama, with great merchandise, and they had garlanded the offerings. Some of the companions said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "This is al-Hutam; he has set out as a pilgrim and has come between us and him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Enough, he has garlanded the offering." [5]

He said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "This is only something we used to do in the Jahiliyya." The Prophet (ﷺ) refused, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not violate the sacred rites of Allah﴾.

Ibn Abbas and Mujahid: they are the rites of the Hajj. The polytheists used to perform pilgrimage and offer sacrifices, and the Muslims wished to raid them, so Allah the Exalted forbade them from it. [Al-Hasan said: the whole religion of Allah.] Evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And whoever honours the sacred rites of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾ [Surat al-Hajj: 32].

Atiyya, from Ibn Abbas: it is that you hunt while in ihram; evidence for it is His saying: ﴿And when you come out of ihram, then hunt﴾.

Ata': the sacred rites are the sanctities of Allah: avoiding His displeasure and following His obedience in what Allah has forbidden.

Abu 'Ubayda: they are the marked offerings, which are those whose hump is pierced and which are garlanded, so it is known they are an offering; "al-ish'ar" is the mark, and from it [the hadith]: when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضي الله عنه) slaughtered, the Commander of the Faithful marked them, as if he informed with a sign. On this view it is of the pattern "fa'ila" in the sense of "mufa'ala."

Al-Kumayt said:
"We kill them generation after generation; you see them / as sacred offerings by which they draw near." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/60.]

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿And the camels We have made for you among the sacred rites of Allah; in them is good for you﴾ [Surat al-Hajj: 36]. It was also said: the sacred rites are the sacred places (mashaʿir).

Al-Qutayba said: "sha'a'ir Allah," its singular is "sha'ira," and it is everything made a sign of the signs of His obedience.

﴿Nor the sacred month﴾: by fighting in it, for it is forbidden, because of His saying: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it﴾ [Surat al-Baqara: 217].

He said: [it refers to] the postponement (nasi'), for they used to make it lawful one year and make it forbidden another year; evidence is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 37].

﴿Nor the offering﴾: which is everything offered to the House of Allah, whether a camel, a cow, or a sheep.

﴿Nor the garlands﴾: most of the exegetes said they are the offerings, and what is meant is [the garlanded animals]. In the Jahiliyya, when they went out toward the Sacred Precinct, they garlanded themselves with acacia, so no one would touch them; and when they returned, they garlanded themselves with a hair-garland, and no one would touch them. So it is a prohibition of making lawful what is obligatory from them.

Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir and Ata' said: they are the garlands themselves, because the polytheists used to take bark (liha') of the trees of Mecca and similar, and garland themselves with it, and be safe among the people by it. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade stripping its trees so that they would garland themselves with it as the people of the Jahiliyya did.

﴿Nor those coming to the Sacred House﴾, meaning intending the Ka'ba.

Al-A'mash read: "wa-la amm'i al-bayt al-haram" with an idafa, like His saying: ﴿not making lawful the game﴾.

﴿Seeking bounty from their Lord﴾: meaning provision through trade. ﴿And pleasure﴾: meaning according to their assumption and claim, for the disbeliever has no share in pleasure; this is like His saying: ﴿And look at your god﴾ [Surat Ta Ha: 97]. So Allah the Exalted is not pleased with them until they submit.

Qatada: it is that He would set right their livelihoods in this world and not hasten punishment upon them in it.

It was also said: seeking bounty is general for believers and polytheists, while seeking pleasure is specific to believers, because people used to perform pilgrimage, both Muslims and disbelievers. Evidence for this is the reading of Humayd ibn Qays: "tabtaghuna fadlan min rabbikum," addressed to the believers. This verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 5], and His saying: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs﴾.

So it is not permissible for a polytheist to perform the Hajj, nor for a disbeliever to be secure by means of the offering, the garlands, and the Hajj.

﴿And when you come out of ihram﴾ from your state of ihram, ﴿then hunt﴾: it is a command of permission and option, like His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty﴾ [Surat al-Jumu'a: 10]; and ﴿let not the enmity of a people provoke you﴾.

Rawh ibn 'Ubada related from Shabl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: A believing man who was an ally of Abu Sufyan ibn al-Hudhayl came on the day of the Conquest to 'Arafa, because he used to kill the allies of Muhammad (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"May Allah curse whoever entered upon the Jahiliyya [there is nothing of the Jahiliyya except that it is] under these two feet of mine, except the custody of the Ka'ba and the provision of the pilgrims, for these two are returned to their people." [Tarikh al-Ya'qubi: 2/60.] [6]

Others said: it was revealed concerning the pilgrims of the disbelieving Arabs. As for His saying: ﴿let not provoke you﴾ — Al-A'mash, 'Isa and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir read: "yujrimannakum" with a damma on the yā'; the rest read it with a fatḥa. Both are dialects, though the fatḥa is better and more widespread, and it is the choice of Abu Muhammad and Abu Hatim. Abu 'Ubayd said: because it is the prevalent dialect, though the other is acceptable.

They differed about its meaning. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: "la yahmilannakum" (let not carry you). Abu 'Ubayd said: one says "jaramani fulan 'ala an sana'tu kadhha," meaning it moved me to it.

The poet, who is Abu Asma' ibn al-Darriya, said:
"O Karz, you have indeed slain a horseman, / a champion, when the helmeted fear, a tested one.
And I struck Abu 'Uyayna a blow / which compelled Fazara after it not to be angry." [Lisan al-'Arab: 12/93–94.]

Al-Mu'arrij: "la yad'unannakum" (let not call you). Al-Farra': "la-ako'sibannakum" (I will earn you); it is said "fulan jarmahu ahluhu," meaning their sufficient one.

Al-Hudhali, describing an eagle, said:
"A jarma that rises on the top of a cliff; / you see for its bones, what it has gathered, no marrow." [Al-Sihah: 1/164.]

Some said, and it is al-Akhfash: His saying "la jarama anna lahumu al-nar" means: it is right for them to have the Fire.

﴿The hatred of a people﴾: meaning their enmity and hostility, and it is the verbal noun of "shani'tu."

The people of Medina and Syria, and 'Asim and al-A'mash, read with the first nun sukun; the others read with a fatḥa. Both are dialects, except that the fatḥa is better, as it is the more emphatic of the two dialects, and so it is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, because verbal nouns of this form are on "fa'lan" with a fatḥa on the 'ayn, like "al-darabān," "al-nazawān," "al-'asalān" and the like.

﴿That they barred you﴾: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu 'Amr read "in ṣaddūkum" with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption and conditional, and Abu 'Ubayd chose it, considering the reading of 'Abdullah: "an yasuddukum." The rest read with a fatḥa on the alif, meaning "because they barred you." The meaning of the verse: let not the hatred of a people move you to transgression, because they barred you. Abu Hatim and Muhammad ibn Jarir chose it. Ibn Jarir said: because no one among the people of knowledge disputes that this surah was revealed after the story of Hudaybiya, and if that is so, then the barring has precedence.

﴿To transgress﴾ against them, by killing them and taking their property.

﴿And cooperate﴾: meaning let some of you help others. It is said of a woman when her flesh and her limbs are fleshed out: "mut'awina." ﴿In righteousness﴾, which is following the command, ﴿and piety﴾, which is avoiding desire. ﴿And do not cooperate in sin and aggression﴾: meaning disobedience and wrongdoing.

From Wasib ibn Ma'bad, a companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking him about righteousness and sin. He said: "You have come to me asking about righteousness and sin?" I said: "By the One who sent you with truth, I did not come to ask you about anything else." He said: "Righteousness is what your breast is at ease with, and sin is what stirs in your breast, even if the people give you a fatwa about it." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/148.] [7]

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami said: my father related to me, saying: I heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Ansari say: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about righteousness and sin, and he said: "Righteousness is good character, and sin is what stirs in your self and you dislike that people should see it." [Musnad Ahmad: 4/182.] [8] ﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾, which is everything having a flowing soul, that Allah the Mighty and Majestic permitted to eat, whose soul departed from it without slaughter. We only said "having a flowing soul" because fish and locusts are two kinds of blood-less animals and they are lawful.

﴿And blood﴾: it is mentioned generally here and specified in another verse, where He, the Mighty, says: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 145]. So smeared blood is like flesh in eating; for the liver and spleen are two kinds of blood and they are lawful.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that Umar said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two carcasses and two bloods have been made lawful for us: the two carcasses are fish and locusts, and the two bloods are the spleen and the liver." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/277, no. 40972.] [9]

﴿And the flesh of swine﴾: all of it is forbidden, and only the flesh is singled out because flesh is among its greatest uses.

﴿And that over which other than Allah has been invoked﴾: that which was slaughtered for other than Allah, and over which a name other than Allah's was mentioned.

Abu Maysara said: in Surat al-Ma'ida there are eighteen obligations (fara'id) which are not in any other surah of the Qur'an, and it is the last surah revealed, in which there is nothing abrogated.

**Al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 5, verses 1–5 (part 2 of 3):**

Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, pork, what has been dedicated to other than Allah, the strangled animal (al-munkhaniqa), the animal beaten to death (al-mawqudha), the animal that falls to its death (al-mutaraddiyya), the animal gored to death (al-natiha), what a beast of prey has eaten, except what you have slaughtered properly (dhakkaytum), what is sacrificed on stone altars (al-nusub), and seeking decisions by divining arrows (al-azlam). And what trained hunting animals you have taught to hunt, [those that are] trained to pursue. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And [lawful for you are] the chaste women from among the believers and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you give them their bridal payments. And the thief, male and female.

"Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram," up to His saying, "Mighty in retribution." [Surah al-Ma'ida: 95.] Allah did not decree any bahira, sa'iba, wasila or ham [pre-Islamic practices]. [Surah al-Ma'ida: 103–104.] "Testimony between you when death approaches one of you."

As for al-munkhaniqa, it is the animal that is strangled and dies. Ibn 'Abbas said: The people of the Jahiliyya used to strangle the sheep until it died, and then they would eat it. Al-mawqudha is the animal beaten with wood until it dies.

Qatada said: The people of the Jahiliyya used to beat it with a stick until it died, and then they would eat it. He said about it: qadhdhahu yaqudhdhuhu qadhdhan, meaning he beat it until it was near death.

Al-Farazdaq said:

A she-camel that raises her legs to kick, striking the young camel with her hind leg, [she is] a flier to the forelocks of the virgin [camels]. [Kitab al-'Ayn: 7/417; Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/92; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/48.]

Al-mutaraddiyya is the animal that falls from a high place or into a well and dies.

Al-natiha is the animal gored by its companion and dies. The feminine marker "ha'" enters the form fa'il when it means fa'il (active). When it means maf'ul (passive), the masculine and feminine are the same, as in *lihya dahin* (a greased beard), *'ayn kahil* (a kohled eye), and *kaff khadib* (a dyed hand). The ha' is added here because the noun is not dropped; if the ha' were dropped, one would not know whether the adjective describes a feminine or masculine noun. The Arabs say *lihya dahin*, *'ayn kahil*, *kaff khadib*, but when they omit the noun and use the adjective alone, they add the ha': they say *ra'ayna kahila wa khadiba wa dahina*, and *akilat al-sab'* (what the beast of prey has eaten), so they add the ha' just as in *al-dhabiha* and *al-sakina*.

Wa ma akala al-sab'u (what a beast of prey has eaten) — *ghayr* [al-mu'allam] (apart from what has been trained).

Ibn 'Abbas read: *wa akil al-sab'* (masculine). Ibn Abi Za'ida read: *wa akilat al-sab'* (feminine). Al-Hasan and Talha ibn Sulayman read: *wa ma akala al-sab'u* with the ba' vowelled with sukun, and this is a dialect of the people of Najd. [Addition from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/50.]

Hassan ibn Thabit said about 'Utba ibn Abi Lahab:

"Whoever returns to his family in this year, / then the one eaten by the beast will not be among those who return."

Qatada said: When the beast of prey had eaten much of the animal, or had eaten part of it, the people of the Jahiliyya would eat what remained. *Illa ma dhakkaytum* means: except what you have reached while it still had its slaughter (dhakat) among these things. Dhakat is the completion of cutting the jugular veins and the flow of blood. From the same root comes *dhakat* in the sense of a tooth's maturity, which is when it has been present for a full year, and this is the completion of full strength. Similarly the common proverb: *jarri al-muzakkiyat ghallab* (the race of the mature ones is one of contest), where *al-ghab* means contest: the mature one contests its runners and overcomes them through its strength.

The poet [who is Zuhayr] said:

"He surpasses them when they strive against him, / through the maturity of his teeth and his strength."

From the same root comes *dhaka'* (intelligence) in understanding, when a person has complete reason and quick acceptance.

It is said *dhakat al-nar* when you have completed its kindling. So the meaning of *dhakaytum* is that you reached its slaughter in completion.

Ibn 'Abbas and 'Utba ibn 'Umayr said: If it blinks its eye, or flicks its tail, or kicks with its leg, or moves, then it is lawful for you.

On the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit: A wolf attacked a sheep, and they slaughtered it with a sharp stone (*marwa*), and the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted its eating. [Musnad Ahmad: 5/184.]

Abu Qilaba, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has prescribed excellence (ihsan) in everything. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well, and let each of you sharpen his blade and ease the suffering of his slaughtered animal." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1058.] [10]

'Asim, from 'Ikrima, said: A man laid his sheep down and began to sharpen his knife to slaughter it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Do you want to make it die many deaths before you slaughter it?" [al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim: 4/231.] [11]

*Wa ma dhubiha 'ala al-nusub* (what is sacrificed on stone altars): Some said: *nusub* is the plural of *nisab*. It was also said: it is a singular whose plural is *ansab*, like *'unuq* and *a'naq*.

Al-Hasan ibn Salih and Talha ibn Musarrif read: *al-nasbi* with the sad vowelled with a jazm (sukun).

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi related from Abu 'Amr: *al-nasbi* with a fatha on the nun and sukun on the sad.

Al-Jahdari read: with a fatha on the nun and on the sad, taking it as a singular noun, like *al-jabal* and *al-jamal*, while the plural is *ansab*, like *al-ajmal* and *al-ajbal*. All of these are dialects. It means "that which is set up," and from it is the saying of Allah: "as though they were rushing toward a *nusub*." [Surah al-Ma'arij: 43.] They differed about the meaning of *nusub* here.

Mujahid, Qatada and Ibn Jurayj said: Around the House there were three hundred and sixty stones, and the people of the Jahiliyya would slaughter upon them, cutting the meat over them. They would venerate these stones, worship them and sacrifice to them. Along with this, they would exchange them for other stones whenever they wished. They said: "These are not idols; an idol is only that which is shaped and carved."

Others said: They are the idols that are erected.

Al-A'sha said:

"And the set-up stone (*nusub*), do not hide it / from the consequence, and your Lord is Allah, so worship." [Al-Sihah: 1/225; Taj al-'Arus: 1/486.]

Then they differed about its meaning. Some said: its implied sense is "upon the name of the nusub." Ibn Zayd said: *wa ma dhubiha 'ala al-nusub* and *wa ma uhilla li-ghayr Allah bihi* are one and the same.

Qutrub said: the meaning is "what is slaughtered *for* the nusub," meaning "for their sake," the preposition *li* and *'ala* alternating in speech. Allah said: "Then peace be upon you" (*fa-salamun laka*), meaning "upon you" [Surah al-Waqi'a: 91]; and He said: "And if you do evil, it is against yourselves" (*fa-laha*), meaning "against it" [Surah al-Isra': 7].

*Wa an tastaqsimu* is coordinated with what came before: the *an* is in the nominative position, meaning: "and it is forbidden for you to seek decisions through the azlam." *Al-istiqsam* is seeking a portion and a judgment from the azlam, which are arrows with no feathers and no head. Their singular is *zalam*, like *'umar*; and *zalam* also means the arrows themselves.

The poet said:

"If Jadhima has killed its chieftains, / then its women strike with the azlam." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/58.]

Their practice of *istiqsam* with the azlam, as the commentators mentioned, was this: when the people of the Jahiliyya were about to travel, or go to war, or trade, or marry, or do something else, they would cast the arrows. Some arrows had written on them: "My Lord has forbidden me," and others: "My Lord has commanded me." If the one for "command" came out, they would proceed with their matter; if the one for "prohibition" came out, they would refrain.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The azlam are white pebbles that they used to cast.

Abu Hisham, from Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, said: Hubal was the greatest idol of the Quraysh in Mecca. It stood over a well inside the Ka'ba, and that well was where what was offered to the Ka'ba was gathered. Beside Hubal were seven arrows, each arrow with a written phrase. One arrow read "the blood-money" (*al-'aql*): when they disputed about who should bear the blood-money among them, they cast the seven arrows, and whichever came out on the "blood-money" arrow, that person bore it. Another arrow read "yes" (*na'am*), for a matter: when they wanted to do something, they cast the arrows, and if that arrow came out, they did the thing. Another read "no" (*la*): when they wanted to do something, they cast, and if the "no" arrow came out, they did not do it. Another read "from among you" (*minkum*); another read "attached" (*mulsaq*); another read "from other than you" (*min ghayrikum*); and another arrow was for water: when they wanted to dig for water, they cast the arrows, and wherever the arrow came out, they acted upon it.

When they wanted to circumcise a boy, marry a woman, bury a dead person, or doubted the lineage of a rival, they would take the person to Hubal with a hundred dirhams and a camel, give them to the keeper of the arrows who cast them, then bring forward the person they intended to deal with, and say: "O our god, this is so-and-so the son of so-and-so; we intend with him such-and-such, so bring forth the truth." Then they would say to the keeper of the arrows: "Cast!" He would cast. If it came out "from among you," he was a kinsman among them; if it came out "from other than you," he was an ally; if it came out "attached," he remained in his position among them, without lineage and without alliance. If the matter was something other than these, such as a journey, they acted upon what came out; but if it came out "no," they postponed the matter that year until they came back to it again, and they ended their affairs according to what the arrows showed.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "That is transgression (*fisq*)." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/104; the wording is corrected from his text.]

Mujahid said: They are the dice of the Persians and the Romans with which they gamble. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/102.]

Sufyan ibn Wakf said: they are chess.

Raja' ibn Haywa, from Abu al-Darda', said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever foretells the future, or seeks decisions by arrows, or takes omens (*tiyara*) that turn him back from his journey, will not look upon the high ranks of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection." [Tarikh Dimashq: 18/98, Dar al-Fikr ed.] [12]

*Al-yawma ya'isa alladhina kafaru min dinikum* (Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion): meaning, of their returning to their religion as disbelievers. It has two forms. Al-Sha'bi said: *wa'is* and *ya'is*, *ya'isa* *iyasan* and *iyasatan*.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: *fa-la takhshawhum wa-khshawni. Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum* (So do not fear them, but fear Me. Today I have perfected your religion for you).

The verse was revealed on Friday, which was the Day of 'Arafa, after the afternoon prayer, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, in the tenth year of the Hijra. The Prophet (ﷺ) was standing at 'Arafat on his she-camel al-'Adba', and her shoulder was nearly broken from its weight, so she knelt down. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/61.]

Tariq ibn Shihab said: A Jewish man came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "A verse which we read: if it had been revealed to us, we would have taken that day as a festival." He said: "Which verse?" He said: "*Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favour upon you*." 'Umar said: "I know on which day it was revealed and in which place: it was revealed on the Day of 'Arafa, on a Friday, while we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing at 'Arafat. Both of them, praise be to Allah, are a festival for us, and that day will remain a festival for the Muslims as long as any of them remains." From that day there are five festivals: Friday, 'Arafa, and the festivals of the Jews, the Christians and the Magians. The festivals of the people of the religions were never combined on one day before it or after it.

Harun ibn 'Antara related from his father, who said: When this verse was revealed, 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What makes you weep, O 'Umar?" He said: "It made me weep: we were in an increase of our religion, but now that it is complete, nothing completes except that it diminishes." He said: "You are right." [13] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/107, 106.]

This verse was the announcement of the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he lived after it eighty-one days or thereabouts.

The commentators differed about the meaning of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: *al-yawma*, which is the day this verse was revealed, *akmaltu lakum dinakum*: meaning the obligations, the sunnas, the limits, the rulings, the lawful and the unlawful. No lawful or unlawful matter, nor any obligation, was revealed after this verse. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatada said: *al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum* means: no polytheist performed the pilgrimage with you. It was also said: Allah gave this community of every kind of knowledge and wisdom that He had given to all the messengers and nations, and added to them.

It was also said: the laws of the prophets were abrogated and annulled, and the law of this community remains, not erased and not changed until the Day of Resurrection [...] [An unreadable passage.] "He has given you allegiance; then they separated it; this will be for others." It was also said: there was none except this community. It was also said: Allah, by this verse, gathered all [...] [The text breaks off here.] the wilaya (guardianship) and its causes.

Al-Tha'alabi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Hasib say: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Razi say: I heard al-'Abbas ibn Hamza say: I heard Dhu al-Nun say, teaching us from the governance (*siyasa*): it is four things: the Book, the Messenger, the robe of honour (*khil'a*), and the guardianship (*wilaya*).

He said: The Book, which He made the noblest of books, the most abundant in ease, the lightest in command, the richest in knowledge and the most complete in judgment. The Messenger of Allah, He made the greatest and most excellent of the messengers. The robe of honour He made a gift and did not make it a loan. And the guardianship He made lasting until the blowing of the Trumpet.

*Wa atmamtu 'alaykum ni'mati* (And I have completed My favour upon you): meaning, He fulfilled His promise in His saying: "And that I may complete My favour upon you" (*wa li-utimma ni'mati 'alaykum*). Among the completion of His favour was that they entered Mecca in security, prevailed over it, and performed the pilgrimage in tranquillity, with no polytheist mixing among them.

Al-Sha'bi said: This verse was revealed at 'Arafat, when the landmarks and rites of the Jahiliyya were demolished, shirk was extinguished, no polytheist performed the pilgrimage with them that year, and no one circumambulated the House other than them.

Al-Suddi said: [It means] I made you victorious over the Arabs.

*Wa radītu lakumu al-Islama dinan* (And I have approved Islam as your religion). *Fa-man idturra* (whoever is compelled): one who exerts himself in *makhmasa*, which means famine. It is said: he is *khamis al-batn* (hollow-bellied) when he is empty and hungry; a man is *khamsan* and a woman *khamsana* when they are lean and emaciated. *Al-khamas* and *al-khimas* mean hunger.

The poet said:

"He considers hunger a torment, and if he meets satiety, / his heart spends the night bewildered from the lack of worry." [Zad al-Masir: 2/240.]

*Ghayra mutajanifin li-ithm* (without inclining toward sin).

Abu 'Ubayda said: *ghayra mutaharrifin* (not deviating), meaning inclining. Qutrub said: inclining. Al-Mubarrad said: [turning aside]. Al-Nakha'i read *mutajannifin*, and both have the same meaning; it is said *tajannafa* and *tajanafa*, like *ta'ahhada* and *ta'ahada*.

Qatada: not transgressing into sin in one's intention. This is the view of al-Shafi'i.

Abu Hanifa said: [it means] whoever eats beyond satiety.

*Fa-inna Allaha Ghafurun Rahim* (then Allah is Forgiving, Merciful): there is an implied element in it. Its implied meaning is "then he eats it," and the sense of the speech points to it. *Fa-inna Allaha Ghafurun Rahim*: meaning, Forgiving to him, Forgiving, as when one says "'Abd Allah struck," meaning "I struck him."

The poet said:

"Three, all of them, you killed deliberately, / so may Allah bring back a fourth to be counted." [Sharh al-Radi 'ala al-Kafiya: 1/239.]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained the *makhmasa* [by what] al-Awza'i related from Hassan ibn 'Atiyya from Abu Waqid, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We are in a land where we suffer hunger; when is carrion lawful for us?"

He (ﷺ) said: "When you have not gone to bed with morning drink (*tasbahu*), nor evening drink (*taghtabiqu*), and have not gathered green herbs (*tahtafi*), then you may do as you wish with it." [Musnad Ahmad: 5/218.] [14]

*Yas'alunaka madha uhilla lahum* (They ask you what has been made lawful for them): the verse.

Abu Rafi' said: Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked permission to enter. He was given permission, but he delayed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took his cloak and went out, and said: "We have given you permission, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, but we do not enter a house in which there is an image or a dog." They looked, and in some of their houses there was a puppy.

On the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The angels do not enter a house in which there is an image, a dog, or a person in ritual impurity (*junub*)." [al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/148.] [15]

Returning to the hadith of Abu Rafi': He said: So he (the Prophet) commanded me not to leave any dog in Medina without killing it, and I said... until I feared the high places [...]. Then I came to a woman on the outskirts of Medina who had a dog guarding her, and I took pity on it and left it. I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of my action, and he commanded me to kill it, so I returned to the dog and killed it.

Ibn 'Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, raising his voice: "Kill the dogs." [16] [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 6/252.]

He said: We used to meet a woman coming from Medina with her dog, and we would kill it. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that she be killed and prohibited its price.

'Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi related from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The price of dogs is not lawful, nor the earnings of the soothsayer, nor the wages of a prostitute." [Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/141, no. 3448; Sunan al-Nasa'i: 1/177.] [17]

He prohibited keeping and holding them, and commanded that a vessel licked by one be washed seven times, the first time with dust.

We return to the first hadith.

He said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the killing of dogs, some people came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is lawful for us from this community that we kill?" The Messenger of Allah was silent, and then Allah revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah permitted keeping those dogs from which benefit is gained, and prohibited keeping those of no benefit. He commanded the killing of the savage dog and any that harms or injures, and lifted the killing from all others that do no harm.

Al-Hasan related from 'Abd Allah ibn Mu'aqqal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Were it not that dogs are a nation among the nations, I would have commanded their killing. So kill the solid black ones. And whatever people keep a dog other than a dog for the field, for hunting, or for livestock, will lose a qirat of their reward every day." [Musnad Ahmad: 4/85.] [18]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verses 1–5 (part 3 of 3):

It was narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever keeps a dog that is neither a hunting dog, nor a herding dog, nor a guard for a field, will have two qirats (a unit of reward) deducted from his reward every day." [Sahih Muslim: 5/38.] [19]

As for the wisdom behind this, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Abd al-Razzaq al-Sari'i, who said: It was said to Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak: What do you say about the saying of the Chosen One (ﷺ): "Whoever keeps a dog that is not a hunting dog or a herding dog, his deeds are diminished by such-and-such an amount of reward every day"? [Musnad Ahmad: 2/60.] [20]

He said: Al-Asma'i told me, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Mansur said to Amr ibn Ubayd: What has reached you concerning the dog? He said: It has reached me that whoever takes a dog, other than for crops or guarding, has one qirat deducted from his reward every day. He said to him: And why is that? He said: That is what the hadith says. He said: Take it in its proper sense; that is only because it barks at the guest and frightens the one who asks. [Tanwir al-Hawalik: 697, no. 1742.]

The generous among the Arabs used to dislike dogs for this reason, and they blamed whoever tied one up and intended to kill it.

Al-Tha'alibi said: Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi recited to me, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Harrani al-Basri recited to me that one of the poets of Basra had alighted at the house of Ammar, and he heard the barking of his dogs, so he composed:

"We alighted at Ammar, and he set his dogs upon us,
and we nearly became food between his tents."

I said to my companions, secretly:
"Is today longer, or the Day of Resurrection?"

[Ammar: the name of a person; the verse is in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/74.]

Ata' ibn Dinar narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning this verse, who said: It was revealed concerning Adi ibn Hatim and Zayd ibn al-Muhalhil al-Ta'iyyayn, and he is Zayd al-Khayl, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named Zayd al-Khayr (Zayd of Goodness). They both came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, we are a people who hunt with dogs and hawks. The dogs of Al Dir' and Al Hawriyyah catch cattle, donkeys, gazelles and lizards. Some of what they catch we can slaughter, and some they kill without our being able to slaughter it. Allah has forbidden carrion, so what is lawful for us of it? Then it was revealed: ﴿They ask you, [O Muhammad], what has been made lawful for them. Say: "Lawful for you are the good things"﴾, meaning the slaughtered animals that Allah has made lawful, ﴿and [those hunted by] what you have taught of the trained hunting animals﴾, meaning and the game caught by what you have trained of the hunting beasts ﴿among the hunting animals﴾.

They differed concerning these hunting animals whose game is lawful through training, when the trainer did not slaughter it: if they caught it, is its slaughter yours? Otherwise it is not to be eaten. This view is not acted upon.

The rest of the scholars said: They are the predatory animals among beasts, birds and wild creatures, such as the leopard, the panther, the dog, the eagle, the falcon, the hawk, the buzzard, the shaheen and the like, which accept training. They were named "jawarih" (hunting animals) because they "wound" (jaraha) their owners' food from the game, that is, they earn it. It is said: "So-and-so is the jarihah of his household," meaning their earner. And "for so-and-so there is no jarihah," meaning he has no earnings.

"Mukallibin" (﻿مُكَلِّبِينَ) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) in meaning, and the sense is: ﴿and the game caught by what you have trained of the hunting animals, [being] mukallibin﴾, i.e., in the state of your hunting, [with] dogs. Al-Taklib is inciting the game and setting it on the prey. [Ashlaytu al-kalb ala al-sayd: I called the dog to the game and released it; it is also said: I incited it.]

The poet said:
"At dawn, a trainer set his dog on it,
swift as a wolf of al-Qusaymah, dust-coloured."
[Lisan al-Arab: 12/486.]

Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Zarin and al-Hasan read ﴿mukliബin﴾ with the lam lightened, in this sense. It is also the reading of al-Hasan and al-Qutaybi. It may also derive from their saying "akleba al-rajul" when his dogs became many, like "amsha" when his livestock became many. The mention of dogs is because they are the most numerous and most general, and the intended meaning is all hunting animals.

﴿You teach them [some] of what Allah has taught you﴾: that is, of the knowledge Allah has taught you. Al-Suddi said: "min" here means "ka" (like), i.e., as Allah has taught you, which is that they should not ﴿yajthumna﴾ [crouch over the prey and eat of it, as in the original text], nor bite, nor kill, nor eat. ﴿So eat of what they hold for you, and mention the name of Allah over it﴾, at the time of releasing the beasts and the hunting animals.

The ruling of the verse:
The trained hunting animal whose game is lawful is one which, when its owner releases it and incites it, goes forward; when it seizes game, holds it and does not eat it; when it is called, it answers; and when it is sought, it does not flee from it. If it does this several times, then it is trained. Whenever it has this description and hunts, its game is lawful to eat. If it holds the game and does not eat from it, its game is lawful to eat and is permissible. If it eats from it, then al-Shafi'i has two opinions. The first: it is not permissible and not to be eaten; this is the more well-known and apparent position of his school, because Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿So eat of what they hold for you﴾, and it did not hold it for us; it held it for itself. This is the view of al-Hasan, Tawus, al-Sha'bi, Ata' and al-Suddi.

Ibn Abbas said: If you release the dog and it eats from the game, it is carrion, not lawful to eat, because it is a beast which held it for itself, not for you, and it did not learn what you taught it. So beat it and do not eat from its game.

What supports this is what al-Sha'bi narrated from Adi ibn Hatim, that he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about game, and he said: "When you release your dog, mention the name of Allah over it. If you find it has not killed, then slaughter it and mention Allah's name over it. If you find it has killed and not eaten, then eat, for it has held it for you. But if you find it has eaten from it, then do not eat any of it, for it held it for itself. If your dog mixes with other dogs and they kill and do not eat, then do not eat it, for you do not know which of them killed it." [Sunan al-Nasa'i: 7/179.] (And when you shoot your arrow, mention the name of Allah; if you find it, eat, unless you find it has fallen into water and died, for you do not know whether the water killed it or your arrow.) If you find it after a night or two nights and you do not see your arrow in it, then if you wish to eat from it, eat. [al-Sunan al-Kubra: 9/242 and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 17/74, with slight variation.] [21]

The second opinion: it is lawful even if it has eaten. This is the view of Salman al-Farisi, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah.

Humayd ibn Abd Allah and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: We have dogs that are trained, which eat and yet remain. He said: Eat, even if only half or two-thirds of it remains, eat it; it is not carrion.

This was narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ).

There is no difference in applying it to the birds and the trained beasts that we have mentioned.

Abu Qilabah narrated from Tha'labah [in the source: from Abu Tha'labah] al-Khushani that he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, our land is a land of game. I release my arrow and mention the name of Allah, and I release my trained dog and mention the name of Allah, and I release my dog which is not trained. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "What your arrow holds for you, and you mention Allah's name, eat. What your trained dog holds for you, and you mention Allah's name, eat. What your dog which is not trained holds for you, and you find its slaughter [before it dies], eat; but if you do not find its slaughter, do not eat." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/231.] [22]

﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning. Today, the good things have been made lawful for you﴾, meaning the slaughtered animals; ﴿and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾, meaning the slaughtered animals of the Jews and Christians, and whoever entered their religion among the other nations before Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent is lawful for you. As for whoever entered their religion after the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, his slaughter is not lawful. As for when one of them mentions other than Allah at the time of slaughter, such as the saying of the Christians "in the name of the Messiah," they differed concerning it.

Rabi'ah said: I heard Ibn Umar say: Do not eat the slaughtered animals of the Christians, for they say "in the name of the Messiah." They are not able to be guided, and they have wronged themselves. Its proof is His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiance.﴾

The second opinion: their slaughter is permitted, the People of the Book, even if they mention other than Allah, because this is an exception from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.﴾ That verse was revealed concerning the slaughtered animals of the polytheists, which they used to slaughter for their idols. Most scholars hold this view.

Al-Sha'bi and Ata' said: Concerning a Christian who slaughters and says "in the name of the Messiah," both said: it is lawful. For Allah, mighty and majestic, has made their slaughter lawful, and He knows best what they say.

Al-Zuhri and Makhul were asked about the slaughter of the worshippers of the People of the Book, and what is slaughtered for their churches, and both said: It is lawful, and both recited this verse.

Al-Hasan and al-Harith al-Ukli said: I would not ask about his slaughter, for Allah has made his food lawful for us. If a Jew or a Christian slaughters and mentions other than the name of Allah while you are listening, do not eat it; but if he is out of your sight, then eat, for Allah has made lawful for you [what is in] the Qur'an. The slaughter and sacrifice of Jews and Christians is disliked.

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Your sacrifices should not be slaughtered by Jews or Christians, and your rites should not be performed except by a Muslim." [al-Sunan al-Kubra: 5/239, similar.] [23]

His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And [lawful are] chaste women from among the believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾. The scholars differed concerning the meaning and ruling of the verse. Some people said: By "ihsan" (chastity) in this verse is meant freedom, and they permitted marriage to every free woman, whether believing or People of the Book, whether immoral or chaste, and they forbade the female slaves of the People of the Book to be married by a Muslim in any case. This is the view of Mujahid and most jurists. The proof for it is His saying: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women...﴾ (the verse), for it made faith a condition in marrying slave women.

Others said: Allah, exalted is He, meant by "chaste women" in this verse the chaste women of both groups, whether their slave women or free women. They permitted marrying the slave women of the People of the Book by this verse, and forbade adulterous women among the believing women and the women of the Book. This is the view of Abu Maysarah and al-Suddi.

Al-Sha'bi said: The ihsan of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she washes herself from impurity (janabah) and guards her private part.

Al-Hasan said: If a man sees immorality from his wife and is certain of it, he should not keep her.

Then they differed about whether the verse is general or specific. Some of them said: It is general, covering all women of the Book, whether they are at war or under protection (dhimmi). This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan.

Some of them said: It refers to the women under protection. As for the women at war, their women are forbidden to the Muslims. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

Al-Suddi narrated from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from him [Ibn Abbas], who said: Among the women of the People of the Book, some are lawful to us and some are not lawful to us. Then he recited: ﴿Fight those who do not believe...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿...while they are humbled.﴾ So whoever gives the jizyah (tax), his women are lawful to us; and whoever does not give the jizyah, his women are not lawful to us.

Al-Hakam said: I mentioned that to Ibrahim, and it pleased him. Ibn Umar did not consider marrying women of the Book permissible, and he interpreted this verse by His saying: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾, saying: I know of no polytheism greater than a woman saying that her lord is Jesus.

Al-Mubarak narrated from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, who said: A man asked al-Hasan: May a man marry a woman of the People of the Book? He said: What has he to do with the People of the Book, when Allah has made Muslim women abundant? If he must do it, then let him choose her as a chaste woman, not a fornicator. The man said: What is a fornicator? He said: She is the one who, when a man glances at her, she follows him. ﴿And whoever denies faith, his deeds are lost﴾.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that some men said, when the saying of Allah was revealed, ﴿And [lawful are] chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾: How can we marry women who are not on our religion? So Allah revealed this verse.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed concerning those of the women of the People of the Book whom Muslims had made chaste. He says: The Muslims' making them chaste does not bring them out of disbelief, meaning concerning them in their religion [...] [an unreadable word] and it made them among those who disbelieved in faith, so his deeds are lost. And this is general for people: ﴿And whoever denies faith, his deeds are lost, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾, meaning among the people of the Fire.

Ibn Abbas said concerning ﴿And whoever denies...﴾: "Whoever denies Allah." Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: If this narration is sound, its meaning is "with the Lord of faith," and it was said: "with those who believe in Him."

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿And whoever denies faith﴾, that is, what was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Tha'alibi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Juhani say: I heard Abu al-Haytham al-Sanjari say: The "ba'" (with) is a filler particle, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [76:6], and ﴿a tree that grows with oil﴾ [23:20]. The meaning is: ﴿And whoever denies faith﴾, that is, rejects it, ﴿his deeds are lost﴾.

Al-Hasan read it with a fatha on the "ba'." Ibn al-Sumay' read: "fa-qad habita amaluhu wa-huwa fi al-akhirati mina al-khasirin" (his deeds are lost, and he, in the Hereafter, is among the losers).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 1–5 (part 1 of 3):

Madaniyya, and among its abrogated (mansukh) verses are nine, including His saying:
﴿Do not violate the sacred rites of Allah﴾ – abrogated by the verse of the sword. [Marginal note in the manuscript: (﴿Some of them are closer to others in the Book of Allah﴾) (Surat al-Anfal: 75). What exceeds the bond of kinship in disobedience, a reward from Allah.]
The last complete surah revealed was "Bara'a" (al-Tawba), and the last verse revealed in Surat al-Nisa' was ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾.
Al-Suddi said: the last of the Qur'an to be revealed were these verses: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ (Surat al-Nisa': 176); ﴿But if they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾ (Surat al-Tawba: 129); ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ (Surat al-Baqara: 281).
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in his sermon on the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage: "O people, Surat al-Ma'ida is among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, so make lawful its lawful and make unlawful its unlawful." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/31.] [1] Its letters number eleven thousand, nine hundred and thirty-three; its words, two thousand, eight hundred and four; and its verses, one hundred and twenty.
From Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surat al-Ma'ida while on his mount, and it could not bear him until he dismounted.
Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Ma'ida will be given a reward equal to the number of every Jew and Christian who breathes in the world, ten good deeds, and ten of his sins will be erased." [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/257; in the source: "and ten degrees will be raised for him."] [2]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿O you who believe﴾: "Yā" is a call, meaning an indication; "hā" is an alert. ﴿Those who believe﴾ [Ibn al-Jawzi in Zad al-Masir: 2/230 said: it is disputed. It is said they are the believers of our community, and this is the view of the majority; and it is said they are the People of the Book, related by Ibn Jurayj.] [in apposition (badal) to "ayyuha" – as in the manuscript]. ﴿Fulfil the contracts﴾: meaning the covenants.

Al-Zajjaj said: "al-'uqud" means the contracts, or all covenants. It is said: "'aqadtu fulanan" and "'ahadtu fulanan," and from it comes "dhalika bi-stiwaq," and its root is tying a thing to another, as when a rope is tied to a rope when joined firmly. Al-Hutay'a said:
"A people who, when they make a contract with their neighbour, / they bind the 'anaj and bind the kurab upon it." [Al-Sihah: 1/331.]

They differed about what these contracts are. Ibn Juraij said: this address is specific to the People of the Book, who believed in the earlier scriptures and messengers: "Fulfil the covenants which were made among you concerning Muhammad," and His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: that which I have given you of Book and wisdom﴾ [Surat Al 'Imran: 81], and His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those given the Book: you shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it﴾ [Surat Al 'Imran: 187]. Others said: it is general.

Qatada said: it refers to what they contracted upon in the Jahiliyya; his evidence is His saying: ﴿And those whom your oaths have bound﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 33].

Ibn Abbas: they are the covenants of oaths and separation. Others: they are the contracts which people made among themselves.

﴿Lawful to you is the beast of cattle﴾: they differed about it. Al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Rabi', al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it is all livestock, and it is the name for cattle, sheep and camels; evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And of the cattle, some for burden and some for slaughter﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 142], then He explained what they are: ﴿eight pairs: of sheep two﴾. By it is meant what the people of the Jahiliyya had forbidden to themselves of livestock.

Al-Sha'bi said: "bahimat al-an'am" are the fetuses found dead in their mothers' wombs when they are slaughtered.

Atiyya al-Awfi related from Ibn Umar regarding His saying ﴿Lawful to you is the beast of cattle﴾, that he said: "It is what is in their bellies." I said: "If it comes out dead, may I eat it?" He said: "Yes, it is in the position of its lung and liver." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/68.] [3]

Qabus related from his father, from Ibn Abbas, that a cow was slaughtered and a fetus was found in its belly; Ibn Abbas took hold of the fetus's tail and said: "This is of the beast of cattle which is lawful to you." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/68.]

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the fetus, and he said: "Its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother." [Musnad Ahmad: 3/31.] [3]

Al-Kalbi said: "bahimat al-an'am" is its wild game, like gazelles and wild cattle, singly. It is called "bahima" only because every living creature that cannot discern is a "bahima"; it was so named because it is made obscure (ubhimat) from discernment.

﴿Except what is recited to you﴾: meaning, to you in the Qur'an, [because it is the judge], and it is His saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion and blood … and what is sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek decision by arrows; that is depravity﴾, and His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is depravity﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 121].

﴿Not lawful the game while you are in the state of ihram﴾: al-Akhfash said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning "Fulfil the contracts" while you are in pilgrim state, not making lawful the game; and in it is [the sense of prohibition] [an illegible word in the manuscript; what we have inserted appears to be correct].

Al-Kisa'i said: it is a circumstantial clause of His saying: ﴿Lawful to you is the beast of cattle﴾ … ﴿not making lawful the game﴾, as one says: "Lawful to you is food, without transgressing in it."

Its meaning: all cattle is made lawful to you except what of it is wild, for that is game, and it is not lawful to you when you are in the state of ihram. That is His saying: ﴿while you are in the state of ihram﴾. The majority read its first letter with a damma, from "harama, yahrumu, haraman" in the sense of movements; both are plurals of "haram." It is said: "rajul haram," "harm," and "muhrim," and "halal," "hall," and "muhall." ﴿Indeed Allah decrees what He wills﴾ [He forbids what He wills to whom He wills] [addition from Zad al-Masir: 2/231].

﴿O you who believe, do not violate the sacred rites of Allah﴾ – the verse.

It was revealed concerning al-Hutam, whose name was Shurayh ibn Dsubay'a ibn Hind ibn Shurahbil al-Bakri. It is said that when he came to Medina, he left his horses outside the city and entered alone upon the Prophet (ﷺ), who said to him: "To what do you invite the people?" He said: "To the testimony that there is no god but Allah, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakat." [Asbab al-Nuzul: 125; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/43.] [4] He said: "Good, except that I have people whom I do not decide any matter without; perhaps I will embrace Islam and bring them."

The Prophet (ﷺ) had said to his companions: "Some of Rabi'a will enter upon you, speaking with the tongue of Satan." Then Shurayh left his presence. When he had gone out, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He entered with the face of a disbeliever and left with the trace of a treacherous one." He passed by the herd of Medina, drove it off and departed with it, chanting:
"The night has wrapped it with a driver, fierce, / not a shepherd of camels nor of sheep,
nor a butcher upon the butchering-block; / they slept, and the son of Hind did not sleep.
He is accompanied by a youth like a mace, / bow-legged, with smooth-soled feet." [Jami' al-Bayan: 6/79.]

When the following year came, he set out as a pilgrim among the pilgrims of Bakr ibn Wa'il from al-Yamama, with great merchandise, and they had garlanded the offerings. Some of the companions said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "This is al-Hutam; he has set out as a pilgrim and has come between us and him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Enough, he has garlanded the offering." [5]

He said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "This is only something we used to do in the Jahiliyya." The Prophet (ﷺ) refused, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not violate the sacred rites of Allah﴾.

Ibn Abbas and Mujahid: they are the rites of the Hajj. The polytheists used to perform pilgrimage and offer sacrifices, and the Muslims wished to raid them, so Allah the Exalted forbade them from it. [Al-Hasan said: the whole religion of Allah.] Evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And whoever honours the sacred rites of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾ [Surat al-Hajj: 32].

Atiyya, from Ibn Abbas: it is that you hunt while in ihram; evidence for it is His saying: ﴿And when you come out of ihram, then hunt﴾.

Ata': the sacred rites are the sanctities of Allah: avoiding His displeasure and following His obedience in what Allah has forbidden.

Abu 'Ubayda: they are the marked offerings, which are those whose hump is pierced and which are garlanded, so it is known they are an offering; "al-ish'ar" is the mark, and from it [the hadith]: when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضي الله عنه) slaughtered, the Commander of the Faithful marked them, as if he informed with a sign. On this view it is of the pattern "fa'ila" in the sense of "mufa'ala."

Al-Kumayt said:
"We kill them generation after generation; you see them / as sacred offerings by which they draw near." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/60.]

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿And the camels We have made for you among the sacred rites of Allah; in them is good for you﴾ [Surat al-Hajj: 36]. It was also said: the sacred rites are the sacred places (mashaʿir).

Al-Qutayba said: "sha'a'ir Allah," its singular is "sha'ira," and it is everything made a sign of the signs of His obedience.

﴿Nor the sacred month﴾: by fighting in it, for it is forbidden, because of His saying: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it﴾ [Surat al-Baqara: 217].

He said: [it refers to] the postponement (nasi'), for they used to make it lawful one year and make it forbidden another year; evidence is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 37].

﴿Nor the offering﴾: which is everything offered to the House of Allah, whether a camel, a cow, or a sheep.

﴿Nor the garlands﴾: most of the exegetes said they are the offerings, and what is meant is [the garlanded animals]. In the Jahiliyya, when they went out toward the Sacred Precinct, they garlanded themselves with acacia, so no one would touch them; and when they returned, they garlanded themselves with a hair-garland, and no one would touch them. So it is a prohibition of making lawful what is obligatory from them.

Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir and Ata' said: they are the garlands themselves, because the polytheists used to take bark (liha') of the trees of Mecca and similar, and garland themselves with it, and be safe among the people by it. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade stripping its trees so that they would garland themselves with it as the people of the Jahiliyya did.

﴿Nor those coming to the Sacred House﴾, meaning intending the Ka'ba.

Al-A'mash read: "wa-la amm'i al-bayt al-haram" with an idafa, like His saying: ﴿not making lawful the game﴾.

﴿Seeking bounty from their Lord﴾: meaning provision through trade. ﴿And pleasure﴾: meaning according to their assumption and claim, for the disbeliever has no share in pleasure; this is like His saying: ﴿And look at your god﴾ [Surat Ta Ha: 97]. So Allah the Exalted is not pleased with them until they submit.

Qatada: it is that He would set right their livelihoods in this world and not hasten punishment upon them in it.

It was also said: seeking bounty is general for believers and polytheists, while seeking pleasure is specific to believers, because people used to perform pilgrimage, both Muslims and disbelievers. Evidence for this is the reading of Humayd ibn Qays: "tabtaghuna fadlan min rabbikum," addressed to the believers. This verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 5], and His saying: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs﴾.

So it is not permissible for a polytheist to perform the Hajj, nor for a disbeliever to be secure by means of the offering, the garlands, and the Hajj.

﴿And when you come out of ihram﴾ from your state of ihram, ﴿then hunt﴾: it is a command of permission and option, like His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty﴾ [Surat al-Jumu'a: 10]; and ﴿let not the enmity of a people provoke you﴾.

Rawh ibn 'Ubada related from Shabl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: A believing man who was an ally of Abu Sufyan ibn al-Hudhayl came on the day of the Conquest to 'Arafa, because he used to kill the allies of Muhammad (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"May Allah curse whoever entered upon the Jahiliyya [there is nothing of the Jahiliyya except that it is] under these two feet of mine, except the custody of the Ka'ba and the provision of the pilgrims, for these two are returned to their people." [Tarikh al-Ya'qubi: 2/60.] [6]

Others said: it was revealed concerning the pilgrims of the disbelieving Arabs. As for His saying: ﴿let not provoke you﴾ — Al-A'mash, 'Isa and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir read: "yujrimannakum" with a damma on the yā'; the rest read it with a fatḥa. Both are dialects, though the fatḥa is better and more widespread, and it is the choice of Abu Muhammad and Abu Hatim. Abu 'Ubayd said: because it is the prevalent dialect, though the other is acceptable.

They differed about its meaning. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: "la yahmilannakum" (let not carry you). Abu 'Ubayd said: one says "jaramani fulan 'ala an sana'tu kadhha," meaning it moved me to it.

The poet, who is Abu Asma' ibn al-Darriya, said:
"O Karz, you have indeed slain a horseman, / a champion, when the helmeted fear, a tested one.
And I struck Abu 'Uyayna a blow / which compelled Fazara after it not to be angry." [Lisan al-'Arab: 12/93–94.]

Al-Mu'arrij: "la yad'unannakum" (let not call you). Al-Farra': "la-ako'sibannakum" (I will earn you); it is said "fulan jarmahu ahluhu," meaning their sufficient one.

Al-Hudhali, describing an eagle, said:
"A jarma that rises on the top of a cliff; / you see for its bones, what it has gathered, no marrow." [Al-Sihah: 1/164.]

Some said, and it is al-Akhfash: His saying "la jarama anna lahumu al-nar" means: it is right for them to have the Fire.

﴿The hatred of a people﴾: meaning their enmity and hostility, and it is the verbal noun of "shani'tu."

The people of Medina and Syria, and 'Asim and al-A'mash, read with the first nun sukun; the others read with a fatḥa. Both are dialects, except that the fatḥa is better, as it is the more emphatic of the two dialects, and so it is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, because verbal nouns of this form are on "fa'lan" with a fatḥa on the 'ayn, like "al-darabān," "al-nazawān," "al-'asalān" and the like.

﴿That they barred you﴾: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu 'Amr read "in ṣaddūkum" with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption and conditional, and Abu 'Ubayd chose it, considering the reading of 'Abdullah: "an yasuddukum." The rest read with a fatḥa on the alif, meaning "because they barred you." The meaning of the verse: let not the hatred of a people move you to transgression, because they barred you. Abu Hatim and Muhammad ibn Jarir chose it. Ibn Jarir said: because no one among the people of knowledge disputes that this surah was revealed after the story of Hudaybiya, and if that is so, then the barring has precedence.

﴿To transgress﴾ against them, by killing them and taking their property.

﴿And cooperate﴾: meaning let some of you help others. It is said of a woman when her flesh and her limbs are fleshed out: "mut'awina." ﴿In righteousness﴾, which is following the command, ﴿and piety﴾, which is avoiding desire. ﴿And do not cooperate in sin and aggression﴾: meaning disobedience and wrongdoing.

From Wasib ibn Ma'bad, a companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking him about righteousness and sin. He said: "You have come to me asking about righteousness and sin?" I said: "By the One who sent you with truth, I did not come to ask you about anything else." He said: "Righteousness is what your breast is at ease with, and sin is what stirs in your breast, even if the people give you a fatwa about it." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/148.] [7]

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami said: my father related to me, saying: I heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Ansari say: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about righteousness and sin, and he said: "Righteousness is good character, and sin is what stirs in your self and you dislike that people should see it." [Musnad Ahmad: 4/182.] [8] ﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾, which is everything having a flowing soul, that Allah the Mighty and Majestic permitted to eat, whose soul departed from it without slaughter. We only said "having a flowing soul" because fish and locusts are two kinds of blood-less animals and they are lawful.

﴿And blood﴾: it is mentioned generally here and specified in another verse, where He, the Mighty, says: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 145]. So smeared blood is like flesh in eating; for the liver and spleen are two kinds of blood and they are lawful.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that Umar said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two carcasses and two bloods have been made lawful for us: the two carcasses are fish and locusts, and the two bloods are the spleen and the liver." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/277, no. 40972.] [9]

﴿And the flesh of swine﴾: all of it is forbidden, and only the flesh is singled out because flesh is among its greatest uses.

﴿And that over which other than Allah has been invoked﴾: that which was slaughtered for other than Allah, and over which a name other than Allah's was mentioned.

Abu Maysara said: in Surat al-Ma'ida there are eighteen obligations (fara'id) which are not in any other surah of the Qur'an, and it is the last surah revealed, in which there is nothing abrogated.

**Al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 5, verses 1–5 (part 2 of 3):**

Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, pork, what has been dedicated to other than Allah, the strangled animal (al-munkhaniqa), the animal beaten to death (al-mawqudha), the animal that falls to its death (al-mutaraddiyya), the animal gored to death (al-natiha), what a beast of prey has eaten, except what you have slaughtered properly (dhakkaytum), what is sacrificed on stone altars (al-nusub), and seeking decisions by divining arrows (al-azlam). And what trained hunting animals you have taught to hunt, [those that are] trained to pursue. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And [lawful for you are] the chaste women from among the believers and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you give them their bridal payments. And the thief, male and female.

"Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram," up to His saying, "Mighty in retribution." [Surah al-Ma'ida: 95.] Allah did not decree any bahira, sa'iba, wasila or ham [pre-Islamic practices]. [Surah al-Ma'ida: 103–104.] "Testimony between you when death approaches one of you."

As for al-munkhaniqa, it is the animal that is strangled and dies. Ibn 'Abbas said: The people of the Jahiliyya used to strangle the sheep until it died, and then they would eat it. Al-mawqudha is the animal beaten with wood until it dies.

Qatada said: The people of the Jahiliyya used to beat it with a stick until it died, and then they would eat it. He said about it: qadhdhahu yaqudhdhuhu qadhdhan, meaning he beat it until it was near death.

Al-Farazdaq said:

A she-camel that raises her legs to kick, striking the young camel with her hind leg, [she is] a flier to the forelocks of the virgin [camels]. [Kitab al-'Ayn: 7/417; Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/92; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/48.]

Al-mutaraddiyya is the animal that falls from a high place or into a well and dies.

Al-natiha is the animal gored by its companion and dies. The feminine marker "ha'" enters the form fa'il when it means fa'il (active). When it means maf'ul (passive), the masculine and feminine are the same, as in *lihya dahin* (a greased beard), *'ayn kahil* (a kohled eye), and *kaff khadib* (a dyed hand). The ha' is added here because the noun is not dropped; if the ha' were dropped, one would not know whether the adjective describes a feminine or masculine noun. The Arabs say *lihya dahin*, *'ayn kahil*, *kaff khadib*, but when they omit the noun and use the adjective alone, they add the ha': they say *ra'ayna kahila wa khadiba wa dahina*, and *akilat al-sab'* (what the beast of prey has eaten), so they add the ha' just as in *al-dhabiha* and *al-sakina*.

Wa ma akala al-sab'u (what a beast of prey has eaten) — *ghayr* [al-mu'allam] (apart from what has been trained).

Ibn 'Abbas read: *wa akil al-sab'* (masculine). Ibn Abi Za'ida read: *wa akilat al-sab'* (feminine). Al-Hasan and Talha ibn Sulayman read: *wa ma akala al-sab'u* with the ba' vowelled with sukun, and this is a dialect of the people of Najd. [Addition from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/50.]

Hassan ibn Thabit said about 'Utba ibn Abi Lahab:

"Whoever returns to his family in this year, / then the one eaten by the beast will not be among those who return."
