Abu Idris narrated from Abu Dharr from ʿAli, may God honour his face, who said: While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was among a gathering of the Muhajirun, ten rabbis of the Jews approached him and said: "O Muhammad, we came to ask you about things that none knows except a prophet sent or an angel brought near." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ask me to gain understanding, and do not ask me to trouble me." They said: "O Muhammad, inform us why God commanded the washing of these four places, which are the cleanest parts?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Adam looked at the tree, he directed his face toward it, then walked toward it — and it was the first foot that walked to disobedience — then he reached out with his hand and smelled it and ate from it; so the ornaments and garments fell from him, and he placed his sinful hand upon his head. God the Mighty and Majestic commanded the washing of the face because he looked at the tree and directed himself to it, and commanded the washing of the two forearms and the washing of the hand, and commanded the wiping of his head, which the tree had wetted, and his placing his hand upon his head; and commanded the washing of the two feet because he walked to the sin. When Adam did that, God expiated the sin for him; so God made these obligatory upon my community, that they might expiate their sins from one ablution to the next." [31]

They said: "You have spoken truly," and they embraced Islam.

The jurists differed concerning the ruling of the sequences mentioned in the verse. They took them to mean sequence and succession (tartib and ta'qib), and made the order obligatory in ablution, namely that one performs the acts of ablution consecutively, one after another: he washes his face, then his hands, then wipes his head, then washes his feet. This is the choice of al-Shafiʿi, who cited the verse ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 158].

Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah said: We went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the Hajj — and he mentioned the hadith until he said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out to al-Safa and said: 'Begin with what God began with.'"

This indicates two things, the first of which is:

that the particle *wa* (and) requires sequence, and the second is that beginning with the wording requires beginning with the action, unless there is evidence to the contrary [Musnad Ahmad: 3/394].

He also argued with His saying ﴿Bow down and prostrate yourselves﴾ [22:77], so bowing (rukuʿ) comes before prostration (sujud). He also argued with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ):
"Allah will not accept the prayer of a person until he performs the wudu' (ablution) in its proper places: he washes his face, then washes his hands, then wipes his head, then washes his feet" [Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/423] [32]. And *thumma* (then) in the speech of the Arabs denotes sequence.

From Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, that he said to Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari: "Can you show us how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed wudu'?" Abdullah said: "Yes." He asked for water, poured it over his hands, washed his face three times, washed his hands three times, and wiped his head with his hands, moving them forward and backward: he began with the front of his head, then took his hands to the back of his neck, then brought them back to the place where he had begun. Then he washed his feet.

Malik said: if one deliberately omits the order in wudu', he must repeat his wudu'; if he omits it forgetfully, he does not need to repeat it. This is also the view chosen by al-Muzani.

Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa and his two companions said: the order in wudu' is a sunnah (recommended practice). If one omits it, whether forgetfully or deliberately, there is no need to repeat it. They understood *wa* to mean joining together, and they argued with the saying of Allah, ﴿The alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾ [9:60]. There is no disagreement that giving the shares to some of the categories before others is a matter of distinction (in the order of giving).
They also argued with the saying ﴿O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾ [33:56], and it is prohibited to put one of them before the other.

As for the virtue of wudu':
Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related from Zayd, from Ibn Sallam, from Abu Malik, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Purity is half of faith" [Musnad Ahmad: 5/344] [33].

Hammad ibn Salama related from Ali ibn Zayd, from Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I was with Salman, and he took a branch from a dry tree and shook it, then said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever performs wudu' well [then prays the five prayers], his sins fall away from him as these leaves fall" [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/297] [34].

Zirr ibn Hubaysh related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those of your community whom you have not seen on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "They will be radiant with white marks from the traces of wudu'" [Musnad Ahmad: 5/199] [35].

Abu Umama related from Amr ibn Abasa, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is wudu'? Tell me about it." He said:
"None of you draws near to his wudu' and rinses his mouth, draws water into his nose and blows it out, except that his sins come out from his mouth and nostrils with the water. Then, when he washes his face as Allah has commanded, the sins of his face come out from the edges of his beard with the water. Then, when he washes his hands up to the elbows, the sins of his hands come out from his fingertips with the water. Then he wipes his head, and the sins of his head come out from the ends of his hair with the water. Then he washes his feet up to the ankles, and the sins of his feet come out from beneath his toenails with the water. Then, when he stands and prays, praises Allah, extols Him and glorifies Him, and empties his heart for Allah, he departs from his sin like the day his mother bore him" [Sahih Muslim: 2/210] [36].

From Anas ibn Malik, who said: I served the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when I was eight years old. The first thing he taught me was to say: "O Anas, O my son, perform your wudu' well for your prayer; Allah will love you and your life will be lengthened" [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/271; and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/307, with variation] [37].

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab related from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamza al-Ansari, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us while we were in the mosque of Madina and said: "Last night I saw a marvel: I saw a man of my community upon whom the punishment of the grave was spread, but his wudu' came and rescued him from it" [38].

﴿And if you are in a state of janabah (major impurity), then purify yourselves [by bathing]﴾ [5:6].
Abu Dhar related from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: Ten rabbis of the Jews came and said: "O Muhammad, why did Allah command bathing from janabah but not from urine and excrement, which are filthier than semen?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Adam ate from the tree, it moved into his veins and hair, and when a person has intercourse, it descends from the root of every hair. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it obligatory upon me and my community as expiation, purification, and thanks for the pleasure He has granted them through it."
They said: "You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad. Then tell us the reward for one who bathes in a lawful state." He (ﷺ) said: "When a believer wishes to bathe in a lawful state, Allah builds for him a palace in Paradise, and it is a secret between the believer and his Lord. The hypocrite does not bathe from janabah. There is no servant or female servant of my community who stands to bathe from janabah, certain that I am their Lord, [and I say:] I bear witness that I have forgiven them; for every hair on his head and body I write a thousand [years] for him, and a similar amount is erased from him, and a similar amount is raised for him." They said: "You have spoken the truth. We bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah."

From Abu Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "O my son, the bath from janabah: perform it thoroughly, for under every hair there is janabah." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should I be thorough?" He said:
"Cleanse the roots of the hair, and make your skin clean; you will emerge from your bath with every sin forgiven" [Kanz al-Ummal: 9/549, no. 27361] [39].

Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamza said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us one day while we were in the mosque of Madina and said: "I saw last night a marvel: I saw a man of my community while the prophets were sitting in circles, circle after circle; whenever he approached a circle, they drove him away. Then his bath from janabah came and took him by the hand and seated him beside me" [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/555] [40].

﴿And if you are sick or on a journey…﴾ up to His saying ﴿and your hands from it﴾, meaning from the clean earth (sa'id). ﴿Allah does not desire to place upon you any hardship﴾, meaning by what He has prescribed for you of wudu', ghusl and tayammum (dry ablution), ﴿from hardship﴾, meaning from constraint. ﴿But He desires to purify you﴾, meaning from minor and major impurities, sins and wrongdoings, ﴿and to complete His favor upon you﴾, in what He has permitted you of tayammum when water is absent, and all His other countless favors, ﴿that you may be grateful﴾, to Allah for them.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi related from Abdullah ibn Dara, the freedman of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), from Imran, the freedman of Uthman, who said: Uthman was brought a jug of water. He asked for it and performed wudu' thoroughly, then said: "Had I not heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once, twice, or three times, I would not have related it to you" [Musnad Ibn al-Mubarak: 21].

I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No servant performs wudu' and perfects it, then stands to pray, except that Allah forgives what lies between it and the next prayer" [Musnad Ibn al-Mubarak: 21] [41].

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Whenever I heard a hadith from a man among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would seek it in the Qur'an. I sought this in the Qur'an and found ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins and complete His favor upon you﴾ [48:1–2]. So I knew that Allah had not completed His favor upon him until He forgave his sins.
Then I recited the verse in al-Ma'ida, ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…﴾ until His saying ﴿He desires to purify you and to complete His favor upon you﴾, and I understood that Allah had not completed His favor upon them until He had forgiven them.

Qatada, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from al-Sudayy ibn Ajlan, who is Abu Umama, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said:
"Purification (wudu') expiates what came before it, and then the prayer becomes a supererogatory act" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 8/125, where it reads "wudu'" instead of "purification"] [42].

﴿And remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾, meaning all favors, ﴿and His covenant with which He bound you﴾, His pact, ﴿which you made when you said: "We hear and we obey"﴾. This was when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey in what they liked and disliked. This is the view of most exegetes.
Mujahid said: [the covenant is] the covenant which Allah took from His servants when He brought them out of the loins of Adam (peace be upon him).
﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, knowing what is in hearts of good and evil.
﴿O you who believe, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice﴾: He commanded them to be truthful and just in their words and deeds. ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾, meaning do not let their enmity lead you to abandon justice toward them. Then He said: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾, meaning nearer to piety. ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, who will reward you for it.
﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾. Its implied sense is: "He said to them, 'forgiveness'," because a promise is a statement, and therefore the speech is phrased this way. ﴿But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs are the companions of Hellfire﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 6–10 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer﴾, God the Exalted commanded ablution upon rising to prayer. The scholars differed concerning the ruling of the verse. A group said: this is from the general (ʿam) which is intended to be particular (khass),

and the mujmal (the general or ambiguous statement) whose clarification was entrusted to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The meaning of the verse: ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾ while you are not in a state of purity. This is indicated by what is narrated from ʿIkrimah: he was asked about this verse and said: "Must I perform ablution every hour?" And he said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "There is no ablution except from a breach (ḥadath)."

Al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashshir said: I saw Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah pray the five prayers with one ablution.

If he urinated or breached his purity, he performed ablution and wiped over his socks with the remainder of his water. It was said to him: "What do you do by your own opinion?" He said: "Rather, I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do it, and I do as I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do."

Muharib ibn Dithar narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed the Dhuhr, ʿAsr, Maghrib and ʿIsha with one ablution.

Al-Musawwar ibn Makhramah said to Ibn ʿAbbas: "Would you like to see ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr? When he hears the call, he leaves the mosque." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "This is how Satan does." He called him and said: "What prompts you to do what you do: when you hear the call, you leave and perform ablution?" He said: "God the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿When you rise to prayer, wash your faces…﴾ the verse." He said: "This is not so; when you have performed ablution you are in a state of purity until you breach it." Then he said: "This is how Satan does: when he hears the call, he turns away and has wind (dirat)."

Al-Aʿmash narrated from ʿUmarah, who said: al-Aswad had a cup (qaʿb) which had been used by a man, and he would perform ablution with it and then pray all the prayers with that ablution.

Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Suddi said: the meaning of the verse, ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾, is from sleep. Others said: it means every rising of the servant to his prayer, that he renew purity for it as a recommended and desirable practice. ʿIkrimah said: ʿAli used to perform ablution at every prayer and recite this verse: "O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…"

From Abu ʿAfif (in the source: Ghutayf) al-Hudhali: he saw Ibn ʿUmar perform ablution for the Dhuhr, then the ʿAsr, then the Maghrib. I said: "O Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, is this ablution a sunnah?" He said: "My ablution was sufficient for all the prayers as long as I did not breach it, but I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity, God records for him ten good deeds.' [Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/23.] So I was eager for this, O nephew."

Others said: rather, this was a command from God the Exalted to His Prophet and to the believers, obligatory and as a trial, that they perform ablution for every prayer; then it was abrogated (naskh) for lightening.

Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Jabal al-Ansari said: I said to ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar: "Inform me about ʿAbd Allah's performing ablution for every prayer, whether he was in a state of purity or not — from whom is this?" He said: "Asma' bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab told me that ʿAbd Allah ibn Handhalah ibn Abi ʿAmir al-Ghasil told her that the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded ablution at every prayer; this was difficult for him, so he commanded the siwak and lifted the ablution from him except from a breach. ʿAbd Allah saw that he had strength for it, so he would perform ablution."

Sulayman ibn Buraydah narrated from his father that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to perform ablution for every prayer, but when the day of the Conquest of Makkah came, he prayed all five prayers with one ablution. ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said: "You are doing something you did not used to do!" He said: "Deliberately I did it, O ʿUmar." [al-Sunan al-Kubra: 1/118; Sunan al-Nasa'i: 1/85.] [24]

Others said: this is an announcement from God the Exalted to His Messenger (ﷺ) that there is no ablution obligatory upon him except when he rises to his prayer, not for other actions.

That is because, when he was in a state of breach, he would refrain from all actions until he performed ablution; so God the Mighty and Majestic permitted by this verse that he do whatever actions occurred to him after the breach, other than prayer.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqas from his father, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) relieved himself, we would speak to him and he would not answer us, and we would greet him and he would not return the greeting, until he came to his dwelling and performed ablution for prayer, until the verse of dispensation was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces…﴾

The limit of the face is from the roots of the hair of the head to the tip of the chin in length, and what is between the two ears in breadth. As for what hangs down from the beard below the chin, al-Shafiʿi has two opinions here:

The first: it is not obligatory for the one performing ablution to wash it. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and the choice of al-Muzani, and they argued that hair hanging from the head is not given the ruling of the head; likewise from the face.

The second: it is obligatory to wash it, and the evidence for this view is the apparent meaning of this verse, because the face is that which is faced with; so everything that is faced with from this organ is obligatory to wash by the apparent ruling.

From the hadith is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) when he forbade covering the beard in prayer: "It is from the face." And from the language is the Arabic saying "badal wajh fulan" and "kharaja wajhuhu" when his beard grew.

﴿and your hands up to the elbows﴾. Washing the hands from the elbows is obligatory by consensus; they differed concerning the elbows.

Al-Shaʿbi, Malik, al-Farra', Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Jarir said: washing the elbows is not obligatory in ablution; ilaa here means limit and end. They then cited the verse ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187], and the night is not included in the fast. The rest of the jurists said: it is obligatory to wash them, and ilaa means "with"; they argued with the verse ﴿and do not consume their wealth along with your wealth﴾ [al-Nisa': 2], and the verse ﴿so it added to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾ [al-Tawbah: 125], and the verse ﴿who are my helpers toward God?﴾ [Al ʿImran: 52].

﴿and wipe your heads﴾. The jurists differed concerning the required amount of wiping the head.

Malik and al-Muzani said: wiping the whole head in ablution is obligatory. They took the bi' to mean generalization, as in the verse ﴿so wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6] and the verse ﴿and let them circle the ancient House﴾.

Abu Hanifah said: wiping a quarter of the head is obligatory. Abu Yusuf: half the head. Al-Shafiʿi: it is permissible to limit oneself to less than a quarter of the head; so if one wipes the amount that is called wiping, it suffices. He cited the verse ﴿and wipe your heads﴾, and he has two proofs in this verse. The first: wiping part of his head, however little, has been achieved by the two ends of the [tongue] of one wiping his head; he thus fulfils the obligation of the command.

The second: in the two limbs for which God commanded purification with washing, He said ﴿wash your faces and your hands﴾, and He gave an unrestricted command for washing them; but concerning the head He said ﴿and wipe your heads﴾, and introduced the bi' for partiality, because when the verb transitively reaches its object without the particle bi', the introduction of bi' is for partiality, as in the saying of one who says: "I wiped my hand with the handkerchief," even though he wiped only part of it.

ʿAntarah said:
"I drank with the water of al-Dahrdayn, so she became
turned away, avoiding the basins of the Daylam." [Lisan al-ʿArab: 2/95.]

From the Sunnah that supports this is what was narrated: ʿAmr ibn Wahb al-Naqli narrated from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah that the Prophet (ﷺ) performed ablution and wiped over his forelock, his turban and his two socks, thereby limiting the wiping to the forelock rather than the rest of the head.

﴿and your feet﴾. The reciters differed concerning it.

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and his son Hisham, Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Taymi, Abu Wa'il, al-A'mash, al-Dahhak, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmir, ʿAmir, Nafi', al-Kisa'i, Hafs, Salam and Ya'qub read (wa-arjulakum) in the accusative (naṣb), and this is the reading of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him).

ʿAsim ibn Kulayb narrated from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: ʿAli heard al-Hasan and al-Husayn reading, and they read ﴿wa-arjulikum﴾ in the genitive; ʿAli heard that, and he was judging between people, and said: "﴿wa-arjulakum﴾ in the accusative," and said: "This is from the advancing and postponing (taqdim and ta'khir) of speech."

The reading of ʿAbd Allah and his companions: al-A'mash said: the companions of ʿAbd Allah read ﴿wa-arjulakum﴾ in the accusative, and so they washed.

The reading of Ibn ʿAbbas: ʿIkrimah narrated from him that he read it in the accusative and said: "The matter returned to washing," and this is the choice of Abu ʿUbayd. The rest read it in the genitive (kasr), and this is the reading of Anas, al-Hasan, ʿAlqamah and al-Sha'bi, and the choice of Abu Hatim. Whoever reads it in the accusative, its meaning is "and wash your feet." Whoever reads it in the genitive has three possibilities: the first, that "masḥ" means washing, and the bi' means generalization; one says "tamassahtu lil-salah," meaning "I performed ablution," because the one performing ablution is not content for his face, forearms and feet to be touched until he wipes them and thereby washes them; so washing is called by it. This is the view of Abu Zayd al-Ansari and Abu Hatim al-Sijistani.

Abu ʿUbaydah, al-Akhfash and others said: the feet are conjoined to the heads by way of following (ittiba') in pronunciation, not meaning, as in the Arab saying "juhr ḍabb kharib" (the hole of a lizard, ruined). God the Exalted said: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers﴾ [al-Nisa': 75].

The poet said:
"And I saw your spouse in battle, girded with a sword and a spear."
And the spear is not girded; it is carried.

Labid said:
"And her gazelles and ostriches gave birth between the two lava-fields (al-Jalhatayn)."
And the ostrich does not give birth (ṭafl); rather it lays eggs (tufriKh).

Others said: it means wiping the feet, because of the nearness of their neighbourhood, like the saying: "ghamar al-ridaʾ" (the mantle covered), meaning broad of breast. And it is said: "He kissed the head, hand and foot of the amir," even though the head is in the turban, the hand in the sleeve, and the foot in the boot.

In a hadith it is that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he bowed, placed his hands upon his knees; the meaning is not that there was no barrier between them. God the Exalted said: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 4]; many exegetes said: it means your heart, purify it.

Hammam ibn al-Harith said: Jarir ibn ʿAbd Allah urinated, then performed ablution and wiped over his socks; he was asked about that, and he said: "I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do it."

Al-A'mash said: Ibrahim liked this hadith, namely that Jarir's acceptance of Islam came after the revelation of al-Ma'idah.

Some scholars took the verse according to its apparent meaning and permitted wiping over the feet. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Ablution is two wipings and two washings."

And the saying of Anas: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated from Humayd from Musa ibn Anas that he said to Anas while we were with him: "al-Hajjaj addressed us in al-Ahwaz and mentioned purification, and said: 'Wash your faces and your hands, and wipe your heads,' for there is no part of the son of Adam closer to his filth than his feet; so wash their bellies, their backs, their ankles and their heels." He said: "God spoke truly and al-Hajjaj lied; God the Exalted said: ﴿and wipe your heads and your feet﴾." And Anas, when he wiped his feet, would wet them.

Hammad narrated from ʿAsim al-Ahwal from Anas who said: "The Qur'an was revealed with wiping, and the Sunnah with washing."

And the saying of al-Hasan and al-Sha'bi; al-Sha'bi said: "Jibril brought down the wiping; do you not see that the one performing tayammum wipes what was washing and cancels what was wiping?"

And the saying of ʿIkrimah: Yunus said: "Someone who accompanied ʿIkrimah to Wasit told me: I never saw him wash his feet; rather he wiped over them until he left it."

And the saying of Qatadah: he said: "God imposed two washings and two wipings." The view of Dawud ibn ʿAli al-Isfahani, Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari and Abu Ya'la; and some went to the view that the one performing ablution may choose between washing them and wiping them. The evidence for the obligation of washing the two feet in ablution is the saying of God the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿up to the two ankles﴾; its limit by the two ankles is evidence for washing, like the hands: since its limit for them was up to the elbows, their obligation is washing, not wiping.

The evidence from the Sunnah for this is what was narrated from ʿUthman, ʿAli, Abu Hurayrah and ʿAbd Allah ibn Zayd: they related the ablution of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and washed their feet.

Khallad ibn al-Sa'ib narrated from his father from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "God does not accept the prayer of a man until he places ablution in its places: he washes his face and his hands, wipes his head, and washes his feet." [Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/423.] [25]

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated from ʿAta' from Jabir that he said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded us to wash our feet when we perform ablution."

Ibn Abi Layla said: "The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) agreed upon the obligation of washing the two feet."

Abu Yahya narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by people whose heels were gleaming, and he said: "Complete the ablution; woe to the heels from the Fire." [Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi: 302 and Jami' al-Bayan: 6/182.] [26]

Humayd al-Tawil said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw a blind man performing ablution and said: "Wash the inside of your feet." So he kept washing until he was named "Abu Ghasil." [al-Musannaf: 1/32.] [27]

Abu Qilabah narrated that ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) saw a man performing ablution who left the inside of his feet; he ordered him to repeat the ablution and the prayer.

ʿAisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "If you were both cut off would be dearer to me than that I wipe over the two feet without two socks, up to the ankles."

These are the two protrusions on either side of the foot, at the junction of the joint of the shin and the foot; the Arabs named them al-manjamayn (the two ankle-bones), and washing them is obligatory, like the elbows. This is the view of the jurists, but Muhammad ibn al-Hasan differed from them concerning the ankle (kaʿb), saying: it is the protrusion on the upper part of the foot over which the strap (shirak) runs. He said: it was named so for its elevation, and from it comes "al-Kaʿbah".

Our evidence is His saying: ﴿and your feet up to the two ankles﴾; He put the feet in the plural and the ankles in the dual. If each foot had one ankle, He would have put them together in the mention, as with the elbows: for each hand there is one elbow, so the elbows are plural. Since He put the feet in the plural and the ankles in the dual, it is established that each foot has two ankles. This is also evidenced by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to one in ihram: "Let him wear sandals; and if he does not find sandals, let him wear [two socks] and cut them below the ankles." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/3.] [28]

This shows that the ankles are what we have said; for if the ankle were the protrusion on the top of the foot, then cutting the sock from its bottom would have made its use and walking in it impossible, and the Prophet (ﷺ) would not command the squandering and destruction of wealth.

And what is also narrated from him (ﷺ): he passed through the market of Makkah saying: "Say: there is no god but God, and you will prosper," while Abu Lahab was pelting him from behind with stones until his ankles bled. [Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 8/442, with variation.]

If what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan held were correct, it would not be said "until they bled," since he was pelted from behind.

And what is narrated: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Straighten your rows, or God will surely cause discord between your hearts," [Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 7/630; in it: "your faces on the Day of Resurrection" instead of "your hearts"] so that each of us would press his ankle against his companion's ankle and his shoulder against his shoulder. This is evidenced by his saying (ﷺ): "Woe to the heels and the heel-tendons from the Fire." [Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi: 302, with variation.] [30] The root of the heels and heel-tendons is only attained by one who washes the ankles.

Abu Idris narrated from Abu Dharr from ʿAli, may God honour his face, who said: While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was among a gathering of the Muhajirun, ten rabbis of the Jews approached him and said: "O Muhammad, we came to ask you about things that none knows except a prophet sent or an angel brought near." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ask me to gain understanding, and do not ask me to trouble me." They said: "O Muhammad, inform us why God commanded the washing of these four places, which are the cleanest parts?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Adam looked at the tree, he directed his face toward it, then walked toward it — and it was the first foot that walked to disobedience — then he reached out with his hand and smelled it and ate from it; so the ornaments and garments fell from him, and he placed his sinful hand upon his head. God the Mighty and Majestic commanded the washing of the face because he looked at the tree and directed himself to it, and commanded the washing of the two forearms and the washing of the hand, and commanded the wiping of his head, which the tree had wetted, and his placing his hand upon his head; and commanded the washing of the two feet because he walked to the sin. When Adam did that, God expiated the sin for him; so God made these obligatory upon my community, that they might expiate their sins from one ablution to the next." [31]

They said: "You have spoken truly," and they embraced Islam.

The jurists differed concerning the ruling of the sequences mentioned in the verse. They took them to mean sequence and succession (tartib and ta'qib), and made the order obligatory in ablution, namely that one performs the acts of ablution consecutively, one after another: he washes his face, then his hands, then wipes his head, then washes his feet. This is the choice of al-Shafiʿi, who cited the verse ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 158].

Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah said: We went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the Hajj — and he mentioned the hadith until he said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out to al-Safa and said: 'Begin with what God began with.'"

This indicates two things, the first of which is:

that the particle *wa* (and) requires sequence, and the second is that beginning with the wording requires beginning with the action, unless there is evidence to the contrary [Musnad Ahmad: 3/394].

He also argued with His saying ﴿Bow down and prostrate yourselves﴾ [22:77], so bowing (rukuʿ) comes before prostration (sujud). He also argued with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ):
"Allah will not accept the prayer of a person until he performs the wudu' (ablution) in its proper places: he washes his face, then washes his hands, then wipes his head, then washes his feet" [Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/423] [32]. And *thumma* (then) in the speech of the Arabs denotes sequence.

From Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, that he said to Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari: "Can you show us how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed wudu'?" Abdullah said: "Yes." He asked for water, poured it over his hands, washed his face three times, washed his hands three times, and wiped his head with his hands, moving them forward and backward: he began with the front of his head, then took his hands to the back of his neck, then brought them back to the place where he had begun. Then he washed his feet.

Malik said: if one deliberately omits the order in wudu', he must repeat his wudu'; if he omits it forgetfully, he does not need to repeat it. This is also the view chosen by al-Muzani.

Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa and his two companions said: the order in wudu' is a sunnah (recommended practice). If one omits it, whether forgetfully or deliberately, there is no need to repeat it. They understood *wa* to mean joining together, and they argued with the saying of Allah, ﴿The alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾ [9:60]. There is no disagreement that giving the shares to some of the categories before others is a matter of distinction (in the order of giving).
They also argued with the saying ﴿O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾ [33:56], and it is prohibited to put one of them before the other.

As for the virtue of wudu':
Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related from Zayd, from Ibn Sallam, from Abu Malik, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Purity is half of faith" [Musnad Ahmad: 5/344] [33].

Hammad ibn Salama related from Ali ibn Zayd, from Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I was with Salman, and he took a branch from a dry tree and shook it, then said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever performs wudu' well [then prays the five prayers], his sins fall away from him as these leaves fall" [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/297] [34].

Zirr ibn Hubaysh related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those of your community whom you have not seen on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "They will be radiant with white marks from the traces of wudu'" [Musnad Ahmad: 5/199] [35].

Abu Umama related from Amr ibn Abasa, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is wudu'? Tell me about it." He said:
"None of you draws near to his wudu' and rinses his mouth, draws water into his nose and blows it out, except that his sins come out from his mouth and nostrils with the water. Then, when he washes his face as Allah has commanded, the sins of his face come out from the edges of his beard with the water. Then, when he washes his hands up to the elbows, the sins of his hands come out from his fingertips with the water. Then he wipes his head, and the sins of his head come out from the ends of his hair with the water. Then he washes his feet up to the ankles, and the sins of his feet come out from beneath his toenails with the water. Then, when he stands and prays, praises Allah, extols Him and glorifies Him, and empties his heart for Allah, he departs from his sin like the day his mother bore him" [Sahih Muslim: 2/210] [36].

From Anas ibn Malik, who said: I served the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when I was eight years old. The first thing he taught me was to say: "O Anas, O my son, perform your wudu' well for your prayer; Allah will love you and your life will be lengthened" [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/271; and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/307, with variation] [37].

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab related from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamza al-Ansari, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us while we were in the mosque of Madina and said: "Last night I saw a marvel: I saw a man of my community upon whom the punishment of the grave was spread, but his wudu' came and rescued him from it" [38].

﴿And if you are in a state of janabah (major impurity), then purify yourselves [by bathing]﴾ [5:6].
Abu Dhar related from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: Ten rabbis of the Jews came and said: "O Muhammad, why did Allah command bathing from janabah but not from urine and excrement, which are filthier than semen?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Adam ate from the tree, it moved into his veins and hair, and when a person has intercourse, it descends from the root of every hair. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it obligatory upon me and my community as expiation, purification, and thanks for the pleasure He has granted them through it."
They said: "You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad. Then tell us the reward for one who bathes in a lawful state." He (ﷺ) said: "When a believer wishes to bathe in a lawful state, Allah builds for him a palace in Paradise, and it is a secret between the believer and his Lord. The hypocrite does not bathe from janabah. There is no servant or female servant of my community who stands to bathe from janabah, certain that I am their Lord, [and I say:] I bear witness that I have forgiven them; for every hair on his head and body I write a thousand [years] for him, and a similar amount is erased from him, and a similar amount is raised for him." They said: "You have spoken the truth. We bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah."

From Abu Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "O my son, the bath from janabah: perform it thoroughly, for under every hair there is janabah." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should I be thorough?" He said:
"Cleanse the roots of the hair, and make your skin clean; you will emerge from your bath with every sin forgiven" [Kanz al-Ummal: 9/549, no. 27361] [39].

Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamza said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us one day while we were in the mosque of Madina and said: "I saw last night a marvel: I saw a man of my community while the prophets were sitting in circles, circle after circle; whenever he approached a circle, they drove him away. Then his bath from janabah came and took him by the hand and seated him beside me" [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/555] [40].

﴿And if you are sick or on a journey…﴾ up to His saying ﴿and your hands from it﴾, meaning from the clean earth (sa'id). ﴿Allah does not desire to place upon you any hardship﴾, meaning by what He has prescribed for you of wudu', ghusl and tayammum (dry ablution), ﴿from hardship﴾, meaning from constraint. ﴿But He desires to purify you﴾, meaning from minor and major impurities, sins and wrongdoings, ﴿and to complete His favor upon you﴾, in what He has permitted you of tayammum when water is absent, and all His other countless favors, ﴿that you may be grateful﴾, to Allah for them.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi related from Abdullah ibn Dara, the freedman of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), from Imran, the freedman of Uthman, who said: Uthman was brought a jug of water. He asked for it and performed wudu' thoroughly, then said: "Had I not heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once, twice, or three times, I would not have related it to you" [Musnad Ibn al-Mubarak: 21].

I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No servant performs wudu' and perfects it, then stands to pray, except that Allah forgives what lies between it and the next prayer" [Musnad Ibn al-Mubarak: 21] [41].

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Whenever I heard a hadith from a man among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would seek it in the Qur'an. I sought this in the Qur'an and found ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins and complete His favor upon you﴾ [48:1–2]. So I knew that Allah had not completed His favor upon him until He forgave his sins.
Then I recited the verse in al-Ma'ida, ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…﴾ until His saying ﴿He desires to purify you and to complete His favor upon you﴾, and I understood that Allah had not completed His favor upon them until He had forgiven them.

Qatada, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from al-Sudayy ibn Ajlan, who is Abu Umama, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said:
"Purification (wudu') expiates what came before it, and then the prayer becomes a supererogatory act" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 8/125, where it reads "wudu'" instead of "purification"] [42].

﴿And remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾, meaning all favors, ﴿and His covenant with which He bound you﴾, His pact, ﴿which you made when you said: "We hear and we obey"﴾. This was when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey in what they liked and disliked. This is the view of most exegetes.
Mujahid said: [the covenant is] the covenant which Allah took from His servants when He brought them out of the loins of Adam (peace be upon him).
﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, knowing what is in hearts of good and evil.
﴿O you who believe, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice﴾: He commanded them to be truthful and just in their words and deeds. ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾, meaning do not let their enmity lead you to abandon justice toward them. Then He said: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾, meaning nearer to piety. ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, who will reward you for it.
﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾. Its implied sense is: "He said to them, 'forgiveness'," because a promise is a statement, and therefore the speech is phrased this way. ﴿But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs are the companions of Hellfire﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 6–10 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer﴾, God the Exalted commanded ablution upon rising to prayer. The scholars differed concerning the ruling of the verse. A group said: this is from the general (ʿam) which is intended to be particular (khass),

and the mujmal (the general or ambiguous statement) whose clarification was entrusted to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The meaning of the verse: ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾ while you are not in a state of purity. This is indicated by what is narrated from ʿIkrimah: he was asked about this verse and said: "Must I perform ablution every hour?" And he said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "There is no ablution except from a breach (ḥadath)."

Al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashshir said: I saw Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah pray the five prayers with one ablution.

If he urinated or breached his purity, he performed ablution and wiped over his socks with the remainder of his water. It was said to him: "What do you do by your own opinion?" He said: "Rather, I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do it, and I do as I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do."

Muharib ibn Dithar narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed the Dhuhr, ʿAsr, Maghrib and ʿIsha with one ablution.

Al-Musawwar ibn Makhramah said to Ibn ʿAbbas: "Would you like to see ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr? When he hears the call, he leaves the mosque." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "This is how Satan does." He called him and said: "What prompts you to do what you do: when you hear the call, you leave and perform ablution?" He said: "God the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿When you rise to prayer, wash your faces…﴾ the verse." He said: "This is not so; when you have performed ablution you are in a state of purity until you breach it." Then he said: "This is how Satan does: when he hears the call, he turns away and has wind (dirat)."

Al-Aʿmash narrated from ʿUmarah, who said: al-Aswad had a cup (qaʿb) which had been used by a man, and he would perform ablution with it and then pray all the prayers with that ablution.

Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Suddi said: the meaning of the verse, ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾, is from sleep. Others said: it means every rising of the servant to his prayer, that he renew purity for it as a recommended and desirable practice. ʿIkrimah said: ʿAli used to perform ablution at every prayer and recite this verse: "O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…"

From Abu ʿAfif (in the source: Ghutayf) al-Hudhali: he saw Ibn ʿUmar perform ablution for the Dhuhr, then the ʿAsr, then the Maghrib. I said: "O Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, is this ablution a sunnah?" He said: "My ablution was sufficient for all the prayers as long as I did not breach it, but I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity, God records for him ten good deeds.' [Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/23.] So I was eager for this, O nephew."

Others said: rather, this was a command from God the Exalted to His Prophet and to the believers, obligatory and as a trial, that they perform ablution for every prayer; then it was abrogated (naskh) for lightening.

Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Jabal al-Ansari said: I said to ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar: "Inform me about ʿAbd Allah's performing ablution for every prayer, whether he was in a state of purity or not — from whom is this?" He said: "Asma' bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab told me that ʿAbd Allah ibn Handhalah ibn Abi ʿAmir al-Ghasil told her that the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded ablution at every prayer; this was difficult for him, so he commanded the siwak and lifted the ablution from him except from a breach. ʿAbd Allah saw that he had strength for it, so he would perform ablution."

Sulayman ibn Buraydah narrated from his father that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to perform ablution for every prayer, but when the day of the Conquest of Makkah came, he prayed all five prayers with one ablution. ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said: "You are doing something you did not used to do!" He said: "Deliberately I did it, O ʿUmar." [al-Sunan al-Kubra: 1/118; Sunan al-Nasa'i: 1/85.] [24]

Others said: this is an announcement from God the Exalted to His Messenger (ﷺ) that there is no ablution obligatory upon him except when he rises to his prayer, not for other actions.

That is because, when he was in a state of breach, he would refrain from all actions until he performed ablution; so God the Mighty and Majestic permitted by this verse that he do whatever actions occurred to him after the breach, other than prayer.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqas from his father, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) relieved himself, we would speak to him and he would not answer us, and we would greet him and he would not return the greeting, until he came to his dwelling and performed ablution for prayer, until the verse of dispensation was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces…﴾

The limit of the face is from the roots of the hair of the head to the tip of the chin in length, and what is between the two ears in breadth. As for what hangs down from the beard below the chin, al-Shafiʿi has two opinions here:

The first: it is not obligatory for the one performing ablution to wash it. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and the choice of al-Muzani, and they argued that hair hanging from the head is not given the ruling of the head; likewise from the face.

The second: it is obligatory to wash it, and the evidence for this view is the apparent meaning of this verse, because the face is that which is faced with; so everything that is faced with from this organ is obligatory to wash by the apparent ruling.

From the hadith is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) when he forbade covering the beard in prayer: "It is from the face." And from the language is the Arabic saying "badal wajh fulan" and "kharaja wajhuhu" when his beard grew.

﴿and your hands up to the elbows﴾. Washing the hands from the elbows is obligatory by consensus; they differed concerning the elbows.

Al-Shaʿbi, Malik, al-Farra', Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Jarir said: washing the elbows is not obligatory in ablution; ilaa here means limit and end. They then cited the verse ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187], and the night is not included in the fast. The rest of the jurists said: it is obligatory to wash them, and ilaa means "with"; they argued with the verse ﴿and do not consume their wealth along with your wealth﴾ [al-Nisa': 2], and the verse ﴿so it added to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾ [al-Tawbah: 125], and the verse ﴿who are my helpers toward God?﴾ [Al ʿImran: 52].

﴿and wipe your heads﴾. The jurists differed concerning the required amount of wiping the head.

Malik and al-Muzani said: wiping the whole head in ablution is obligatory. They took the bi' to mean generalization, as in the verse ﴿so wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6] and the verse ﴿and let them circle the ancient House﴾.

Abu Hanifah said: wiping a quarter of the head is obligatory. Abu Yusuf: half the head. Al-Shafiʿi: it is permissible to limit oneself to less than a quarter of the head; so if one wipes the amount that is called wiping, it suffices. He cited the verse ﴿and wipe your heads﴾, and he has two proofs in this verse. The first: wiping part of his head, however little, has been achieved by the two ends of the [tongue] of one wiping his head; he thus fulfils the obligation of the command.

The second: in the two limbs for which God commanded purification with washing, He said ﴿wash your faces and your hands﴾, and He gave an unrestricted command for washing them; but concerning the head He said ﴿and wipe your heads﴾, and introduced the bi' for partiality, because when the verb transitively reaches its object without the particle bi', the introduction of bi' is for partiality, as in the saying of one who says: "I wiped my hand with the handkerchief," even though he wiped only part of it.

ʿAntarah said:
"I drank with the water of al-Dahrdayn, so she became
turned away, avoiding the basins of the Daylam." [Lisan al-ʿArab: 2/95.]

From the Sunnah that supports this is what was narrated: ʿAmr ibn Wahb al-Naqli narrated from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah that the Prophet (ﷺ) performed ablution and wiped over his forelock, his turban and his two socks, thereby limiting the wiping to the forelock rather than the rest of the head.

﴿and your feet﴾. The reciters differed concerning it.

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and his son Hisham, Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Taymi, Abu Wa'il, al-A'mash, al-Dahhak, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmir, ʿAmir, Nafi', al-Kisa'i, Hafs, Salam and Ya'qub read (wa-arjulakum) in the accusative (naṣb), and this is the reading of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him).

ʿAsim ibn Kulayb narrated from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: ʿAli heard al-Hasan and al-Husayn reading, and they read ﴿wa-arjulikum﴾ in the genitive; ʿAli heard that, and he was judging between people, and said: "﴿wa-arjulakum﴾ in the accusative," and said: "This is from the advancing and postponing (taqdim and ta'khir) of speech."

The reading of ʿAbd Allah and his companions: al-A'mash said: the companions of ʿAbd Allah read ﴿wa-arjulakum﴾ in the accusative, and so they washed.

The reading of Ibn ʿAbbas: ʿIkrimah narrated from him that he read it in the accusative and said: "The matter returned to washing," and this is the choice of Abu ʿUbayd. The rest read it in the genitive (kasr), and this is the reading of Anas, al-Hasan, ʿAlqamah and al-Sha'bi, and the choice of Abu Hatim. Whoever reads it in the accusative, its meaning is "and wash your feet." Whoever reads it in the genitive has three possibilities: the first, that "masḥ" means washing, and the bi' means generalization; one says "tamassahtu lil-salah," meaning "I performed ablution," because the one performing ablution is not content for his face, forearms and feet to be touched until he wipes them and thereby washes them; so washing is called by it. This is the view of Abu Zayd al-Ansari and Abu Hatim al-Sijistani.

Abu ʿUbaydah, al-Akhfash and others said: the feet are conjoined to the heads by way of following (ittiba') in pronunciation, not meaning, as in the Arab saying "juhr ḍabb kharib" (the hole of a lizard, ruined). God the Exalted said: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers﴾ [al-Nisa': 75].

The poet said:
"And I saw your spouse in battle, girded with a sword and a spear."
And the spear is not girded; it is carried.

Labid said:
"And her gazelles and ostriches gave birth between the two lava-fields (al-Jalhatayn)."
And the ostrich does not give birth (ṭafl); rather it lays eggs (tufriKh).

Others said: it means wiping the feet, because of the nearness of their neighbourhood, like the saying: "ghamar al-ridaʾ" (the mantle covered), meaning broad of breast. And it is said: "He kissed the head, hand and foot of the amir," even though the head is in the turban, the hand in the sleeve, and the foot in the boot.

In a hadith it is that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he bowed, placed his hands upon his knees; the meaning is not that there was no barrier between them. God the Exalted said: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 4]; many exegetes said: it means your heart, purify it.

Hammam ibn al-Harith said: Jarir ibn ʿAbd Allah urinated, then performed ablution and wiped over his socks; he was asked about that, and he said: "I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do it."

Al-A'mash said: Ibrahim liked this hadith, namely that Jarir's acceptance of Islam came after the revelation of al-Ma'idah.

Some scholars took the verse according to its apparent meaning and permitted wiping over the feet. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Ablution is two wipings and two washings."

And the saying of Anas: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated from Humayd from Musa ibn Anas that he said to Anas while we were with him: "al-Hajjaj addressed us in al-Ahwaz and mentioned purification, and said: 'Wash your faces and your hands, and wipe your heads,' for there is no part of the son of Adam closer to his filth than his feet; so wash their bellies, their backs, their ankles and their heels." He said: "God spoke truly and al-Hajjaj lied; God the Exalted said: ﴿and wipe your heads and your feet﴾." And Anas, when he wiped his feet, would wet them.

Hammad narrated from ʿAsim al-Ahwal from Anas who said: "The Qur'an was revealed with wiping, and the Sunnah with washing."

And the saying of al-Hasan and al-Sha'bi; al-Sha'bi said: "Jibril brought down the wiping; do you not see that the one performing tayammum wipes what was washing and cancels what was wiping?"

And the saying of ʿIkrimah: Yunus said: "Someone who accompanied ʿIkrimah to Wasit told me: I never saw him wash his feet; rather he wiped over them until he left it."

And the saying of Qatadah: he said: "God imposed two washings and two wipings." The view of Dawud ibn ʿAli al-Isfahani, Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari and Abu Ya'la; and some went to the view that the one performing ablution may choose between washing them and wiping them. The evidence for the obligation of washing the two feet in ablution is the saying of God the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿up to the two ankles﴾; its limit by the two ankles is evidence for washing, like the hands: since its limit for them was up to the elbows, their obligation is washing, not wiping.

The evidence from the Sunnah for this is what was narrated from ʿUthman, ʿAli, Abu Hurayrah and ʿAbd Allah ibn Zayd: they related the ablution of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and washed their feet.

Khallad ibn al-Sa'ib narrated from his father from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "God does not accept the prayer of a man until he places ablution in its places: he washes his face and his hands, wipes his head, and washes his feet." [Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/423.] [25]

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated from ʿAta' from Jabir that he said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded us to wash our feet when we perform ablution."

Ibn Abi Layla said: "The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) agreed upon the obligation of washing the two feet."

Abu Yahya narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by people whose heels were gleaming, and he said: "Complete the ablution; woe to the heels from the Fire." [Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi: 302 and Jami' al-Bayan: 6/182.] [26]

Humayd al-Tawil said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw a blind man performing ablution and said: "Wash the inside of your feet." So he kept washing until he was named "Abu Ghasil." [al-Musannaf: 1/32.] [27]

Abu Qilabah narrated that ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) saw a man performing ablution who left the inside of his feet; he ordered him to repeat the ablution and the prayer.

ʿAisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "If you were both cut off would be dearer to me than that I wipe over the two feet without two socks, up to the ankles."

These are the two protrusions on either side of the foot, at the junction of the joint of the shin and the foot; the Arabs named them al-manjamayn (the two ankle-bones), and washing them is obligatory, like the elbows. This is the view of the jurists, but Muhammad ibn al-Hasan differed from them concerning the ankle (kaʿb), saying: it is the protrusion on the upper part of the foot over which the strap (shirak) runs. He said: it was named so for its elevation, and from it comes "al-Kaʿbah".

Our evidence is His saying: ﴿and your feet up to the two ankles﴾; He put the feet in the plural and the ankles in the dual. If each foot had one ankle, He would have put them together in the mention, as with the elbows: for each hand there is one elbow, so the elbows are plural. Since He put the feet in the plural and the ankles in the dual, it is established that each foot has two ankles. This is also evidenced by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to one in ihram: "Let him wear sandals; and if he does not find sandals, let him wear [two socks] and cut them below the ankles." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/3.] [28]

This shows that the ankles are what we have said; for if the ankle were the protrusion on the top of the foot, then cutting the sock from its bottom would have made its use and walking in it impossible, and the Prophet (ﷺ) would not command the squandering and destruction of wealth.

And what is also narrated from him (ﷺ): he passed through the market of Makkah saying: "Say: there is no god but God, and you will prosper," while Abu Lahab was pelting him from behind with stones until his ankles bled. [Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 8/442, with variation.]

If what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan held were correct, it would not be said "until they bled," since he was pelted from behind.

And what is narrated: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Straighten your rows, or God will surely cause discord between your hearts," [Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 7/630; in it: "your faces on the Day of Resurrection" instead of "your hearts"] so that each of us would press his ankle against his companion's ankle and his shoulder against his shoulder. This is evidenced by his saying (ﷺ): "Woe to the heels and the heel-tendons from the Fire." [Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi: 302, with variation.] [30] The root of the heels and heel-tendons is only attained by one who washes the ankles.

Abu Idris narrated from Abu Dharr from ʿAli, may God honour his face, who said: While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was among a gathering of the Muhajirun, ten rabbis of the Jews approached him and said: "O Muhammad, we came to ask you about things that none knows except a prophet sent or an angel brought near." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ask me to gain understanding, and do not ask me to trouble me." They said: "O Muhammad, inform us why God commanded the washing of these four places, which are the cleanest parts?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Adam looked at the tree, he directed his face toward it, then walked toward it — and it was the first foot that walked to disobedience — then he reached out with his hand and smelled it and ate from it; so the ornaments and garments fell from him, and he placed his sinful hand upon his head. God the Mighty and Majestic commanded the washing of the face because he looked at the tree and directed himself to it, and commanded the washing of the two forearms and the washing of the hand, and commanded the wiping of his head, which the tree had wetted, and his placing his hand upon his head; and commanded the washing of the two feet because he walked to the sin. When Adam did that, God expiated the sin for him; so God made these obligatory upon my community, that they might expiate their sins from one ablution to the next." [31]

They said: "You have spoken truly," and they embraced Islam.

The jurists differed concerning the ruling of the sequences mentioned in the verse. They took them to mean sequence and succession (tartib and ta'qib), and made the order obligatory in ablution, namely that one performs the acts of ablution consecutively, one after another: he washes his face, then his hands, then wipes his head, then washes his feet. This is the choice of al-Shafiʿi, who cited the verse ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 158].

Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah said: We went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the Hajj — and he mentioned the hadith until he said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out to al-Safa and said: 'Begin with what God began with.'"

This indicates two things, the first of which is:

that the particle *wa* (and) requires sequence, and the second is that beginning with the wording requires beginning with the action, unless there is evidence to the contrary [Musnad Ahmad: 3/394].

He also argued with His saying ﴿Bow down and prostrate yourselves﴾ [22:77], so bowing (rukuʿ) comes before prostration (sujud). He also argued with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ):
"Allah will not accept the prayer of a person until he performs the wudu' (ablution) in its proper places: he washes his face, then washes his hands, then wipes his head, then washes his feet" [Ahkam al-Qur'an: 2/423] [32]. And *thumma* (then) in the speech of the Arabs denotes sequence.

From Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, that he said to Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari: "Can you show us how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed wudu'?" Abdullah said: "Yes." He asked for water, poured it over his hands, washed his face three times, washed his hands three times, and wiped his head with his hands, moving them forward and backward: he began with the front of his head, then took his hands to the back of his neck, then brought them back to the place where he had begun. Then he washed his feet.

Malik said: if one deliberately omits the order in wudu', he must repeat his wudu'; if he omits it forgetfully, he does not need to repeat it. This is also the view chosen by al-Muzani.

Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa and his two companions said: the order in wudu' is a sunnah (recommended practice). If one omits it, whether forgetfully or deliberately, there is no need to repeat it. They understood *wa* to mean joining together, and they argued with the saying of Allah, ﴿The alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾ [9:60]. There is no disagreement that giving the shares to some of the categories before others is a matter of distinction (in the order of giving).
They also argued with the saying ﴿O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾ [33:56], and it is prohibited to put one of them before the other.

As for the virtue of wudu':
Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related from Zayd, from Ibn Sallam, from Abu Malik, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Purity is half of faith" [Musnad Ahmad: 5/344] [33].

Hammad ibn Salama related from Ali ibn Zayd, from Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I was with Salman, and he took a branch from a dry tree and shook it, then said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever performs wudu' well [then prays the five prayers], his sins fall away from him as these leaves fall" [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/297] [34].

Zirr ibn Hubaysh related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those of your community whom you have not seen on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "They will be radiant with white marks from the traces of wudu'" [Musnad Ahmad: 5/199] [35].

Abu Umama related from Amr ibn Abasa, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is wudu'? Tell me about it." He said:
"None of you draws near to his wudu' and rinses his mouth, draws water into his nose and blows it out, except that his sins come out from his mouth and nostrils with the water. Then, when he washes his face as Allah has commanded, the sins of his face come out from the edges of his beard with the water. Then, when he washes his hands up to the elbows, the sins of his hands come out from his fingertips with the water. Then he wipes his head, and the sins of his head come out from the ends of his hair with the water. Then he washes his feet up to the ankles, and the sins of his feet come out from beneath his toenails with the water. Then, when he stands and prays, praises Allah, extols Him and glorifies Him, and empties his heart for Allah, he departs from his sin like the day his mother bore him" [Sahih Muslim: 2/210] [36].

From Anas ibn Malik, who said: I served the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when I was eight years old. The first thing he taught me was to say: "O Anas, O my son, perform your wudu' well for your prayer; Allah will love you and your life will be lengthened" [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/271; and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/307, with variation] [37].

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab related from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamza al-Ansari, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us while we were in the mosque of Madina and said: "Last night I saw a marvel: I saw a man of my community upon whom the punishment of the grave was spread, but his wudu' came and rescued him from it" [38].

﴿And if you are in a state of janabah (major impurity), then purify yourselves [by bathing]﴾ [5:6].
Abu Dhar related from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: Ten rabbis of the Jews came and said: "O Muhammad, why did Allah command bathing from janabah but not from urine and excrement, which are filthier than semen?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Adam ate from the tree, it moved into his veins and hair, and when a person has intercourse, it descends from the root of every hair. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it obligatory upon me and my community as expiation, purification, and thanks for the pleasure He has granted them through it."
They said: "You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad. Then tell us the reward for one who bathes in a lawful state." He (ﷺ) said: "When a believer wishes to bathe in a lawful state, Allah builds for him a palace in Paradise, and it is a secret between the believer and his Lord. The hypocrite does not bathe from janabah. There is no servant or female servant of my community who stands to bathe from janabah, certain that I am their Lord, [and I say:] I bear witness that I have forgiven them; for every hair on his head and body I write a thousand [years] for him, and a similar amount is erased from him, and a similar amount is raised for him." They said: "You have spoken the truth. We bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah."

From Abu Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "O my son, the bath from janabah: perform it thoroughly, for under every hair there is janabah." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should I be thorough?" He said:
"Cleanse the roots of the hair, and make your skin clean; you will emerge from your bath with every sin forgiven" [Kanz al-Ummal: 9/549, no. 27361] [39].

Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamza said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us one day while we were in the mosque of Madina and said: "I saw last night a marvel: I saw a man of my community while the prophets were sitting in circles, circle after circle; whenever he approached a circle, they drove him away. Then his bath from janabah came and took him by the hand and seated him beside me" [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/555] [40].

﴿And if you are sick or on a journey…﴾ up to His saying ﴿and your hands from it﴾, meaning from the clean earth (sa'id). ﴿Allah does not desire to place upon you any hardship﴾, meaning by what He has prescribed for you of wudu', ghusl and tayammum (dry ablution), ﴿from hardship﴾, meaning from constraint. ﴿But He desires to purify you﴾, meaning from minor and major impurities, sins and wrongdoings, ﴿and to complete His favor upon you﴾, in what He has permitted you of tayammum when water is absent, and all His other countless favors, ﴿that you may be grateful﴾, to Allah for them.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi related from Abdullah ibn Dara, the freedman of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), from Imran, the freedman of Uthman, who said: Uthman was brought a jug of water. He asked for it and performed wudu' thoroughly, then said: "Had I not heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once, twice, or three times, I would not have related it to you" [Musnad Ibn al-Mubarak: 21].

I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No servant performs wudu' and perfects it, then stands to pray, except that Allah forgives what lies between it and the next prayer" [Musnad Ibn al-Mubarak: 21] [41].

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Whenever I heard a hadith from a man among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would seek it in the Qur'an. I sought this in the Qur'an and found ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins and complete His favor upon you﴾ [48:1–2]. So I knew that Allah had not completed His favor upon him until He forgave his sins.
Then I recited the verse in al-Ma'ida, ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…﴾ until His saying ﴿He desires to purify you and to complete His favor upon you﴾, and I understood that Allah had not completed His favor upon them until He had forgiven them.

Qatada, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from al-Sudayy ibn Ajlan, who is Abu Umama, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said:
"Purification (wudu') expiates what came before it, and then the prayer becomes a supererogatory act" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 8/125, where it reads "wudu'" instead of "purification"] [42].

﴿And remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾, meaning all favors, ﴿and His covenant with which He bound you﴾, His pact, ﴿which you made when you said: "We hear and we obey"﴾. This was when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey in what they liked and disliked. This is the view of most exegetes.
Mujahid said: [the covenant is] the covenant which Allah took from His servants when He brought them out of the loins of Adam (peace be upon him).
﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, knowing what is in hearts of good and evil.
﴿O you who believe, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice﴾: He commanded them to be truthful and just in their words and deeds. ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾, meaning do not let their enmity lead you to abandon justice toward them. Then He said: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾, meaning nearer to piety. ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, who will reward you for it.
﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾. Its implied sense is: "He said to them, 'forgiveness'," because a promise is a statement, and therefore the speech is phrased this way. ﴿But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs are the companions of Hellfire﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 6–10 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer﴾, God the Exalted commanded ablution upon rising to prayer. The scholars differed concerning the ruling of the verse. A group said: this is from the general (ʿam) which is intended to be particular (khass),

and the mujmal (the general or ambiguous statement) whose clarification was entrusted to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The meaning of the verse: ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾ while you are not in a state of purity. This is indicated by what is narrated from ʿIkrimah: he was asked about this verse and said: "Must I perform ablution every hour?" And he said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "There is no ablution except from a breach (ḥadath)."

Al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashshir said: I saw Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah pray the five prayers with one ablution.

If he urinated or breached his purity, he performed ablution and wiped over his socks with the remainder of his water. It was said to him: "What do you do by your own opinion?" He said: "Rather, I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do it, and I do as I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do."

Muharib ibn Dithar narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed the Dhuhr, ʿAsr, Maghrib and ʿIsha with one ablution.

Al-Musawwar ibn Makhramah said to Ibn ʿAbbas: "Would you like to see ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr? When he hears the call, he leaves the mosque." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "This is how Satan does." He called him and said: "What prompts you to do what you do: when you hear the call, you leave and perform ablution?" He said: "God the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿When you rise to prayer, wash your faces…﴾ the verse." He said: "This is not so; when you have performed ablution you are in a state of purity until you breach it." Then he said: "This is how Satan does: when he hears the call, he turns away and has wind (dirat)."

Al-Aʿmash narrated from ʿUmarah, who said: al-Aswad had a cup (qaʿb) which had been used by a man, and he would perform ablution with it and then pray all the prayers with that ablution.

Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Suddi said: the meaning of the verse, ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾, is from sleep. Others said: it means every rising of the servant to his prayer, that he renew purity for it as a recommended and desirable practice. ʿIkrimah said: ʿAli used to perform ablution at every prayer and recite this verse: "O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…"

From Abu ʿAfif (in the source: Ghutayf) al-Hudhali: he saw Ibn ʿUmar perform ablution for the Dhuhr, then the ʿAsr, then the Maghrib. I said: "O Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, is this ablution a sunnah?" He said: "My ablution was sufficient for all the prayers as long as I did not breach it, but I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity, God records for him ten good deeds.' [Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/23.] So I was eager for this, O nephew."

Others said: rather, this was a command from God the Exalted to His Prophet and to the believers, obligatory and as a trial, that they perform ablution for every prayer; then it was abrogated (naskh) for lightening.

Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Jabal al-Ansari said: I said to ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar: "Inform me about ʿAbd Allah's performing ablution for every prayer, whether he was in a state of purity or not — from whom is this?" He said: "Asma' bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab told me that ʿAbd Allah ibn Handhalah ibn Abi ʿAmir al-Ghasil told her that the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded ablution at every prayer; this was difficult for him, so he commanded the siwak and lifted the ablution from him except from a breach. ʿAbd Allah saw that he had strength for it, so he would perform ablution."

Sulayman ibn Buraydah narrated from his father that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to perform ablution for every prayer, but when the day of the Conquest of Makkah came, he prayed all five prayers with one ablution. ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said: "You are doing something you did not used to do!" He said: "Deliberately I did it, O ʿUmar." [al-Sunan al-Kubra: 1/118; Sunan al-Nasa'i: 1/85.] [24]

Others said: this is an announcement from God the Exalted to His Messenger (ﷺ) that there is no ablution obligatory upon him except when he rises to his prayer, not for other actions.

That is because, when he was in a state of breach, he would refrain from all actions until he performed ablution; so God the Mighty and Majestic permitted by this verse that he do whatever actions occurred to him after the breach, other than prayer.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqas from his father, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) relieved himself, we would speak to him and he would not answer us, and we would greet him and he would not return the greeting, until he came to his dwelling and performed ablution for prayer, until the verse of dispensation was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces…﴾

The limit of the face is from the roots of the hair of the head to the tip of the chin in length, and what is between the two ears in breadth. As for what hangs down from the beard below the chin, al-Shafiʿi has two opinions here:

The first: it is not obligatory for the one performing ablution to wash it. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and the choice of al-Muzani, and they argued that hair hanging from the head is not given the ruling of the head; likewise from the face.

The second: it is obligatory to wash it, and the evidence for this view is the apparent meaning of this verse, because the face is that which is faced with; so everything that is faced with from this organ is obligatory to wash by the apparent ruling.

From the hadith is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) when he forbade covering the beard in prayer: "It is from the face." And from the language is the Arabic saying "badal wajh fulan" and "kharaja wajhuhu" when his beard grew.

﴿and your hands up to the elbows﴾. Washing the hands from the elbows is obligatory by consensus; they differed concerning the elbows.

Al-Shaʿbi, Malik, al-Farra', Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Jarir said: washing the elbows is not obligatory in ablution; ilaa here means limit and end. They then cited the verse ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187], and the night is not included in the fast. The rest of the jurists said: it is obligatory to wash them, and ilaa means "with"; they argued with the verse ﴿and do not consume their wealth along with your wealth﴾ [al-Nisa': 2], and the verse ﴿so it added to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾ [al-Tawbah: 125], and the verse ﴿who are my helpers toward God?﴾ [Al ʿImran: 52].

﴿and wipe your heads﴾. The jurists differed concerning the required amount of wiping the head.

Malik and al-Muzani said: wiping the whole head in ablution is obligatory. They took the bi' to mean generalization, as in the verse ﴿so wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6] and the verse ﴿and let them circle the ancient House﴾.

Abu Hanifah said: wiping a quarter of the head is obligatory. Abu Yusuf: half the head. Al-Shafiʿi: it is permissible to limit oneself to less than a quarter of the head; so if one wipes the amount that is called wiping, it suffices. He cited the verse ﴿and wipe your heads﴾, and he has two proofs in this verse. The first: wiping part of his head, however little, has been achieved by the two ends of the [tongue] of one wiping his head; he thus fulfils the obligation of the command.
