Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 1 of 2):

And when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you, when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings," (5:20). Scholars differ regarding the meaning of "kings."

Abu al-Haytham narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a wife and a mount, he was recorded as a king." [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/29.]] [44]

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and al-Hakam said: "Whoever has a house, a servant and a wife is a king."

Abu Abd al-Rahman said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As being asked by a man: "Are we not among the poor emigrants?" Abdullah said to him: "Do you have a wife to whom you retreat?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the wealthy." He said: "I have a servant and wealth." He said: "Then you are among the kings."

Abu Ubaylah narrated from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, and has his food for the day, it is as if the world has been gathered for him in its entirety. O son of Ju'sham, what suffices you of it is what satisfies your hunger and covers your nakedness. If there is a house that shelters you, that is well; if there is a mount you ride, that is excellent. But a morsel of bread and water, and whatever is beyond that, will be a reckoning for you." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 70/147.]] [45]

Al-Dahhak said: Their dwellings were spacious, with flowing waters. Whoever has a spacious dwelling with flowing water is a king.

Qatadah said: They were the first to own servants, and the first to have servants from among the children of Adam subjected to them.

Al-Suddi said: The meaning is that He made you free, owning yourselves, after you had been under the hands of the Copts, in the position of the people of the jizya (the poll tax paid by non-Muslim subjects) among us. Allah thus delivered you from humiliation. "And He gave you what He had not given anyone else in the worlds," meaning, the worlds other than yourselves.

Mujahid said: The meaning is the manna and the quails, the stone and the clouds.

"O my people, enter the Holy Land," (5:21). Scholars differ regarding what the Holy Land is.

Mujahid said: It is Mount Sinai (al-Tur) and what surrounds it. Al-Dahhak said: It is Iliya and Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). The Sacred House is sacred in its measure, and the heavens and the earth: Bayt al-Maqdis is sanctified in its measure out of the heavens and the earth.

Ikrimah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: It is Jericho (Ariha).

Al-Kalbi said: Damascus, Palestine and part of Jordan.

Qatadah said: It is all of Syria (al-Sham).

Zayd ibn Thabit said: While we were around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was compiling the Qur'an from the scraps, he said: "Blessed is Syria!" It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, why is that?" He said: "Because the angels of the Most Merciful spread their wings over it."[46] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 5/158.]]

Nusayr ibn Alqama al-Himsi narrated from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abdullah ibn Hawalah, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he said: "By Allah, this affair will continue among you until Allah opens the lands of Persia and Rome and the land of Himyar, and until you become three armies: one army in Syria, one army in Iraq, and one army in Yemen."

Ibn Hawalah said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I should live to see that?" He said: "Choose Syria for yourself, for it is the chosen land of Allah among your lands, and to it Allah gathers His chosen ones from among His servants. O people of Islam, hold fast to Syria, for the chosen land of Allah on earth is Syria. Whoever refuses, let him attach himself to his right hand and drink from his pool. Indeed Allah has guaranteed for me Syria and its people." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 1/74; Mu'jam al-Buldan: 3/314.]] [47]

Al-A'mash narrated from Abdullah ibn Sabbar, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: Good was divided into ten parts: nine of it was placed in Syria and one in Iraq. Evil was divided into ten parts: nine of it was placed in Iraq and one in Syria. Ten thousand eyes that saw the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Syria, and five hundred and seventy of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) settled there, among them seventy companions. [[Up to here in Tarikh Dimashq: 1/327.]]

"Which Allah has prescribed for you," (5:21), meaning: He wrote it in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) that it would be your dwellings.

Ibn Ishaq said: "Allah has decreed it for you." Al-Suddi said: "He commanded you to it, calling you to it." Qatadah said: "They were ordered to it as they were ordered to prayer."

"And do not turn back on your heels," meaning, do not turn back on your heels in opposition to Allah, "and so you will turn about as losers," (5:21).

Al-Kalbi said: Ibrahim, upon whom be peace, ascended Mount Lebanon, and it was said to him: "Look. Whatever your sight reaches is sacred, and it is an inheritance for your descendants after you." They said: meaning the Children of Israel. Musa said: "O Musa, keep their affair secret. Do not tell anyone from the camp, lest they spread it." Each man went and told his relative and cousin, except two men who were faithful. Musa said to them... and they were Yushi' ibn Nun ibn Afraithim ibn Yusuf, Musa's attendant, and Caleb ibn Yufunna, Musa's brother-in-law through his sister Miriam, daughter of Imran, and both were from Iliya. The community of the Children of Israel came to know of this, raised their voices in weeping, and said: "Woe to us! Would that we had died in the land of Egypt! Would that we might die in this wilderness, and that Allah would not bring us to these people, so that our women, children and goods become spoils for them." A man would say to his companions: "Come, let us appoint a leader over us and return to Egypt." This is the statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reporting about them: "They said: 'O Musa, there are a people of tyrants in it, and we will never enter it'" (5:22).

Qatadah said: They had bodies and a strange creation that no others had. "And we will never enter it until they leave it. If they leave it, then we will enter" (5:22). When they said that and intended to return to Egypt, Musa and Harun, upon them be peace, fell down prostrating, and Yushi' and Caleb tore their garments. They are the two whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His statement: "Two men from among those who feared spoke, on whom Allah had bestowed favour" (5:23), meaning those who feared Allah.

Said ibn Jubayr read "yukhafun" (with the yā' vowelled with a ḍammah) and said: They were of the tyrants, then they embraced Islam and followed Musa. "On whom Allah had bestowed favour," with success and protection. "Enter upon them through the gate," meaning the town of the tyrants. "When you enter it, you will surely be victorious," because Allah fulfils His promise and does not forget them. Their bodies were great and strong, but their hearts were weak, so they did not fear them. "And upon Allah rely, if you are believers" (5:23). But the Children of Israel wanted to stone them to death and disobeyed them. They said: "O Musa, we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here" (5:24).

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions on the day of Hudaybiyah, when he was prevented from the House: "I am going with the offering, so I will slaughter it at the House." Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said: "By Allah, we will not say to you what the people of Musa said: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed we are sitting right here.' Rather, we will fight on your right and your left, before you and behind you. If you were to plunge into the sea, we would plunge in with you, and if you were to climb a mountain, we would climb it with you. So proceed with us in the blessing of Allah." When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard this, they pledged allegiance to him upon it, and the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brightened and he was pleased by it.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "For me to be the companion of this mosque is dearer to me than what has been given to me."

When the Children of Israel did what they did of disobedience among themselves, and opposed the command of their Lord, and intended to harm Yushi' and Caleb, Musa became angry and invoked a curse upon them. He said: "My Lord, I have no control except over myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiant people" (5:25), meaning: decide and judge between us.

Ubayd ibn Umayr read "fa-friq" with a kasrah on the rā'. "Between us and the defiant people," meaning the disobedient. There was a calf that Musa had made, and the cloud appeared over the entrance of the tent of meeting, the place of his private conversation. Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Musa: "How long will this people disobey Me? How long will they not believe in the signs? I would destroy them all, and make a people for you that is mightier and more numerous than them." Musa, upon him be peace, said: "My God, if You were to kill this people all at once, like one man, the nations who heard would say: 'This people was only killed because it could not bring them into the holy land, so He killed them in the wilderness.' You are patient, abundant in favours, and You forgive sins and preserve the fathers for the sons and the sons' sons. So forgive them their repentance." Allah said to Musa: "I have forgiven them at your word, but after you named them defiant and invoked a curse upon them, I will surely forbid them to enter the holy land, except for My two servants Yushi' and Caleb. And I will make them wander in this wilderness forty years, each day of which they count as a year. They will die in these deserts, but their sons, who do not know good from evil, will enter the holy land." This is His statement, the Exalted: "He said: 'It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land'" (5:26), meaning they will be bewildered in the land.

They remained forty years in six farsakhs (a farsakh being a distance of about three miles). They would travel each day in a straight line, but when they reached evening and camped, they found themselves at the very place they had set out from. They numbered six hundred thousand fighting men, and hundreds of the ten chiefs who had spread the news suddenly. Everyone who entered the wandering and was over twenty years old died in the wandering, except Yushi' and Caleb. None of those who had said "we will never enter it" entered Jericho. When they had perished and the forty years had passed, and the young men among their descendants had grown up, they set out to fight the tyrants. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/249.]]

The scholars differ over who undertook that battle and at whose hand the conquest occurred. Some said: Musa, upon him be peace, himself conquered Jericho, with Yushi' in the vanguard. Musa set out toward them with those of the Children of Israel who remained, and Yushi' entered with them and fought the tyrants who were there. Then Musa, upon him be peace, entered it with the Children of Israel, remained there as long as Allah willed, and then Allah took him to Himself, and no one among the creatures knows his grave. This is the most correct of the opinions, due to the scholarly consensus that Musa killed Uj ibn Anaq. And Allah knows best.

Others said: It was Yushi' who fought the tyrants, and he did not march against them until after the death of Musa and the destruction of all who had refused to march against them. They said: Musa and Harun died in the wilderness.

The Story of the Death of Harun (peace be upon him)

Al-Suddi said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa: "I am causing Harun to die. Bring him to such-and-such a mountain." Musa and Harun set out toward the mountain, and suddenly they saw trees the like of which had never been seen, and a house built in which there was a couch with bedding on it, and in it a pleasant fragrance. When Harun saw that and sat beside it, he liked it and said: "O Musa, I would love to sleep on this couch." He said: "Sleep on it." He said: "I fear that the owner of this house will come and become angry with me." Musa said to him: "No, I will take care of the owner of this house for you, so sleep." He said: "O Musa, rather sleep with me, for if the owner of the house comes, he will be angry with both of us." When they both slept, Harun was seized by death. When he felt his end coming, he said: "O Musa, take my eye." When he died, that house was lifted up, the tree disappeared, and the couch was raised to the sky. When Musa returned to the Children of Israel without Harun, they said: "Musa has killed Harun, and envy of the love the Children of Israel had for him drove him to it." Musa said: "Woe to you! My brother died and I did not kill him." When they pressed him, he stood and prayed two rak'ahs, then called upon Allah, and the couch descended until they saw it between the heaven and the earth, and so they believed him.

Amr ibn Maymun said: The death of Musa and Harun was in the wilderness, and Harun died before Musa. They had gone out into the wilderness toward some caves. Harun died, and Musa buried him, and returned to the Children of Israel. They said: "What has become of Harun?" He said: "He died." They said: "You are lying, but you killed him because of our love for him," for he was beloved among the Children of Israel.

Musa then complained to his Lord and told Him what he had suffered from the Children of Israel. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "Take them to the grave of Harun until you inform them that he died a natural death and that you did not kill him." So he took them to the grave of Harun, and called out: "O Harun!" He came out of his grave shaking the dust from his head and said: "Did I kill you?" He said: "No, by Allah, but I died." He said: "Return to your resting place," and they dispersed.

As for the death of Musa, upon him be peace:

Ibn Ishaq said: The chosen one of Allah, Musa, had disliked death and considered it great. When he disliked it, Allah wished to make death beloved to him and life hateful to him. Yushi' ibn Nun, who used to visit him morning and evening, met him, and Musa said: "O Prophet of Allah, what has Allah revealed?" Yushi' said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, did I not accompany you for so many years, and did I ever ask you about anything Allah had revealed to you, so that you would be the one guided by it and recounting it, yet not mention anything to me?" When Musa saw that, he disliked life and loved death. Then they differed about the manner of his death.

Hammam ibn Munabbih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The Angel of Death came to Musa, upon him be peace, and said to him: 'Answer your Lord.' Musa struck the eye of the Angel of Death and gouged it out. The Angel of Death returned to Allah, the Exalted, and said: 'You sent me to a servant of Yours who does not want death, and he has gouged out my eye.' Allah restored his eye and said: 'Return to My servant and say to him: Do you want life? If you want life, place your hand on the back of an ox; for every hair your hand covers, you will live a year for each hair.' He said: 'And then what?' He said: 'Then you will die.' He said: 'Then let it be now.' He said: 'My Lord, bring me near to the holy land, the distance of a stone's throw.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, if I were with him, I would show you his grave beside the road at the foot of Mount Sinai, by the red sand dune." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 61/178.]] [48]

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu Sa'id ibn Hamdun say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Maqri say: I heard Muhammad ibn Yahya say: "This story of the Angel of Death and Musa has been authenticated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in meaning, and none rejects it except one who is astray."

In another report, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Angel of Death used to come to people openly, until he came to Musa to seize him. Musa struck him and gouged out his eye, so the Angel of Death returned. Afterward he came secretly." [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/533; Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/305.]] [49]

Al-Suddi said, in a report he mentioned from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Musa, upon him be peace, was walking with his young attendant Yushi', when a black wind came. When Yushi' saw it, he thought it was the Hour, and he clung to Musa. He said: 'The Hour is coming, and I am clinging to Musa, the Prophet of Allah.' Musa slipped out from under his shirt and left the shirt in Yushi's hand. When Yushi' brought the shirt, the Children of Israel seized him and said: 'Did you kill the Prophet of Allah?' He said: 'No, by Allah, I did not kill him, but he slipped away from me.' They did not believe him and wanted to kill him. He said: 'If you do not believe me, then give me three days.' He called upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and each man who had been guarding him came to him in a dream and was informed that Yushi' had not killed him, and that We had raised him to Ourselves. So they left him." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/304.]] [50]

Wahb said: Musa, upon him be peace, went out on some errand, and passed by a group of angels digging a grave. He recognised them and came to them, and stood over them. They were digging a grave the like of which he had never seen, more beautiful than it, and he had never seen such greenery, radiance and delight as was in it. He said to them: "O angels of Allah, for whom are you digging this grave?" They said: "We are digging it, by Allah, for a servant noble before his Lord." He said: "This servant has a station with Allah, for I have never seen a resting place like this today." The angels said: "O chosen one of Allah, would you like it to be yours?" He said: "I would love it." They said: "Then descend, lie down in it, turn to your Lord, and then breathe the gentlest breath you have ever breathed." He descended, lay down in it, turned to his Lord, then breathed, and Allah took his soul. Then the angels smoothed the earth over him. [[The previous source: 305.]]

It was also said: The Angel of Death came to him and said: "O Musa, have you drunk wine?" He said: "No." So he (the Angel of Death) forced him and took his soul. It was also said: Rather, he brought him an apple from Paradise, and he smelled it, and his soul was taken.

It is reported that Yushi' ibn Nun saw him in a dream after his death and said: "How did you find death?" He said: "Like a sheep being skinned while still alive." The age of Musa, upon him be peace, was one hundred and twenty years: twenty of them in the reign of Afridun and a hundred in the reign of Manuchihr. [[In Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/306, "Afridhun" and "Manushihr."]] When the forty years were completed, he died.

When Moses died, God sent Joshua (Yusha') to them as a prophet. He informed them that he was a prophet of God and that God had commanded them to fight the tyrants (al-Jabbarin). They believed him and pledged allegiance to him. He set out with the Children of Israel toward Jericho (Ariha), carrying the Ark of the Covenant (tabut al-mithaq). He besieged the city of Jericho for six months. When it was the seventh, he blew the horns (al-qurun), and the people raised a single great cry, and the wall of the city collapsed. They entered, fought the tyrants, defeated them, and fell upon them, killing them. The victory belonged to the Children of Israel, who would gather around a man's neck and strike it until they severed it. The fighting took place on Friday, and a remnant of them remained. The sun was nearly setting, and the night of Saturday came in. He feared that they would be unable (to finish), so he said: "O God, return the sun to me." He said to the sun: "You are under God's command," and he asked the sun to stand still and the moon to stand still, until he might take vengeance on his enemies before the Sabbath began. The sun was returned to him, and an extra hour of daylight was granted to him, until he had destroyed them all.

Then the kings of the Armanites (al-Armaniyyin) sent to one another, and they were five. They united their word upon Joshua and his people. The Children of Israel defeated the kings, until they drove them down to the valley of Khawran. God pelted them with stones of hail (ahjar mubarrad), and the hail that fell upon them was more numerous than those whom the Children of Israel had slain by the sword. The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave. Joshua commanded them, and they were brought out, and he killed them and crucified them. Then he took them down and threw them into that cave. He pursued the remaining kings of Syria (al-Sham) and seized from them thirty-one kings, until he prevailed over all the land of Syria, and all of Syria became the possession of the Children of Israel. He dispersed his agents throughout its regions. Then he gathered the spoils, but the fire did not descend (upon them).

God revealed to Joshua that there was embezzlement (ghulul) among them. He said: "Command them that they pledge allegiance to you." They pledged allegiance to him, and a man's hand clung to his. He said to them: "Among you is the embezzlement." He (the Prophet ﷺ) said: "Bring what you have." So they brought him the head of an ox adorned with rubies and jewels, which he had embezzled. He placed it with the offering, and the man was with it. Then the fire came and consumed the man and the offering. [With variation in the history of al-Tabari: 1/311 and the history of Ibn Khaldun: 2/87.]

Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A prophet among the prophets went out to fight, and he said to his people: 'Let no man follow me who has married a woman and wishes to consummate the marriage with her and has not yet done so; nor any man who has built a house and has not yet raised its roof; nor any man who has bought sheep or pregnant camels and is awaiting their young.'" He said: So he went out to fight, and he drew near to the town (al-Dayr) at the time of the afternoon prayer (al-'asr) or close to it. He said to the sun: "You are commanded and I am commanded. O God, hold it back for me for an hour." So it was held back for him for an hour, until God granted him victory. He (the narrator) said: "From what I know, it was not held back for anyone before him or after him."

Then the spoils were gathered, and the fire came but did not consume them. He said: "There is embezzlement among you. Let one man from each of your tribes pledge allegiance to me." They pledged allegiance to him, and a man's hand clung to his. He said: "The embezzlement is among you; you have embezzled." They brought out something like the head of a cow made of gold and placed it among the spoils, in the open ground, and the fire came and consumed them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The spoils were not lawful for anyone before us, and that is because God saw our weakness and our incapacity, so He made them lawful for us." [Sahih Ibn Hibban: 11/138, and Sharh Sahih Muslim by al-Nawawi: 12/51.] [51]

They said: Then Joshua (peace be upon him) died and was buried in the mountain of Ephraim (Afraim). His age was one hundred and twenty-six years. And the affairs of the Children of Israel were governed after the death of Moses for twenty-seven years.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 1 of 2):

And when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you, when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings," (5:20). Scholars differ regarding the meaning of "kings."

Abu al-Haytham narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a wife and a mount, he was recorded as a king." [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/29.]] [44]

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and al-Hakam said: "Whoever has a house, a servant and a wife is a king."

Abu Abd al-Rahman said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As being asked by a man: "Are we not among the poor emigrants?" Abdullah said to him: "Do you have a wife to whom you retreat?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the wealthy." He said: "I have a servant and wealth." He said: "Then you are among the kings."

Abu Ubaylah narrated from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, and has his food for the day, it is as if the world has been gathered for him in its entirety. O son of Ju'sham, what suffices you of it is what satisfies your hunger and covers your nakedness. If there is a house that shelters you, that is well; if there is a mount you ride, that is excellent. But a morsel of bread and water, and whatever is beyond that, will be a reckoning for you." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 70/147.]] [45]

Al-Dahhak said: Their dwellings were spacious, with flowing waters. Whoever has a spacious dwelling with flowing water is a king.

Qatadah said: They were the first to own servants, and the first to have servants from among the children of Adam subjected to them.

Al-Suddi said: The meaning is that He made you free, owning yourselves, after you had been under the hands of the Copts, in the position of the people of the jizya (the poll tax paid by non-Muslim subjects) among us. Allah thus delivered you from humiliation. "And He gave you what He had not given anyone else in the worlds," meaning, the worlds other than yourselves.

Mujahid said: The meaning is the manna and the quails, the stone and the clouds.

"O my people, enter the Holy Land," (5:21). Scholars differ regarding what the Holy Land is.

Mujahid said: It is Mount Sinai (al-Tur) and what surrounds it. Al-Dahhak said: It is Iliya and Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). The Sacred House is sacred in its measure, and the heavens and the earth: Bayt al-Maqdis is sanctified in its measure out of the heavens and the earth.

Ikrimah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: It is Jericho (Ariha).

Al-Kalbi said: Damascus, Palestine and part of Jordan.

Qatadah said: It is all of Syria (al-Sham).

Zayd ibn Thabit said: While we were around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was compiling the Qur'an from the scraps, he said: "Blessed is Syria!" It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, why is that?" He said: "Because the angels of the Most Merciful spread their wings over it."[46] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 5/158.]]

Nusayr ibn Alqama al-Himsi narrated from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abdullah ibn Hawalah, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he said: "By Allah, this affair will continue among you until Allah opens the lands of Persia and Rome and the land of Himyar, and until you become three armies: one army in Syria, one army in Iraq, and one army in Yemen."

Ibn Hawalah said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I should live to see that?" He said: "Choose Syria for yourself, for it is the chosen land of Allah among your lands, and to it Allah gathers His chosen ones from among His servants. O people of Islam, hold fast to Syria, for the chosen land of Allah on earth is Syria. Whoever refuses, let him attach himself to his right hand and drink from his pool. Indeed Allah has guaranteed for me Syria and its people." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 1/74; Mu'jam al-Buldan: 3/314.]] [47]

Al-A'mash narrated from Abdullah ibn Sabbar, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: Good was divided into ten parts: nine of it was placed in Syria and one in Iraq. Evil was divided into ten parts: nine of it was placed in Iraq and one in Syria. Ten thousand eyes that saw the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Syria, and five hundred and seventy of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) settled there, among them seventy companions. [[Up to here in Tarikh Dimashq: 1/327.]]

"Which Allah has prescribed for you," (5:21), meaning: He wrote it in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) that it would be your dwellings.

Ibn Ishaq said: "Allah has decreed it for you." Al-Suddi said: "He commanded you to it, calling you to it." Qatadah said: "They were ordered to it as they were ordered to prayer."

"And do not turn back on your heels," meaning, do not turn back on your heels in opposition to Allah, "and so you will turn about as losers," (5:21).

Al-Kalbi said: Ibrahim, upon whom be peace, ascended Mount Lebanon, and it was said to him: "Look. Whatever your sight reaches is sacred, and it is an inheritance for your descendants after you." They said: meaning the Children of Israel. Musa said: "O Musa, keep their affair secret. Do not tell anyone from the camp, lest they spread it." Each man went and told his relative and cousin, except two men who were faithful. Musa said to them... and they were Yushi' ibn Nun ibn Afraithim ibn Yusuf, Musa's attendant, and Caleb ibn Yufunna, Musa's brother-in-law through his sister Miriam, daughter of Imran, and both were from Iliya. The community of the Children of Israel came to know of this, raised their voices in weeping, and said: "Woe to us! Would that we had died in the land of Egypt! Would that we might die in this wilderness, and that Allah would not bring us to these people, so that our women, children and goods become spoils for them." A man would say to his companions: "Come, let us appoint a leader over us and return to Egypt." This is the statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reporting about them: "They said: 'O Musa, there are a people of tyrants in it, and we will never enter it'" (5:22).

Qatadah said: They had bodies and a strange creation that no others had. "And we will never enter it until they leave it. If they leave it, then we will enter" (5:22). When they said that and intended to return to Egypt, Musa and Harun, upon them be peace, fell down prostrating, and Yushi' and Caleb tore their garments. They are the two whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His statement: "Two men from among those who feared spoke, on whom Allah had bestowed favour" (5:23), meaning those who feared Allah.

Said ibn Jubayr read "yukhafun" (with the yā' vowelled with a ḍammah) and said: They were of the tyrants, then they embraced Islam and followed Musa. "On whom Allah had bestowed favour," with success and protection. "Enter upon them through the gate," meaning the town of the tyrants. "When you enter it, you will surely be victorious," because Allah fulfils His promise and does not forget them. Their bodies were great and strong, but their hearts were weak, so they did not fear them. "And upon Allah rely, if you are believers" (5:23). But the Children of Israel wanted to stone them to death and disobeyed them. They said: "O Musa, we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here" (5:24).

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions on the day of Hudaybiyah, when he was prevented from the House: "I am going with the offering, so I will slaughter it at the House." Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said: "By Allah, we will not say to you what the people of Musa said: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed we are sitting right here.' Rather, we will fight on your right and your left, before you and behind you. If you were to plunge into the sea, we would plunge in with you, and if you were to climb a mountain, we would climb it with you. So proceed with us in the blessing of Allah." When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard this, they pledged allegiance to him upon it, and the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brightened and he was pleased by it.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "For me to be the companion of this mosque is dearer to me than what has been given to me."

When the Children of Israel did what they did of disobedience among themselves, and opposed the command of their Lord, and intended to harm Yushi' and Caleb, Musa became angry and invoked a curse upon them. He said: "My Lord, I have no control except over myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiant people" (5:25), meaning: decide and judge between us.

Ubayd ibn Umayr read "fa-friq" with a kasrah on the rā'. "Between us and the defiant people," meaning the disobedient. There was a calf that Musa had made, and the cloud appeared over the entrance of the tent of meeting, the place of his private conversation. Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Musa: "How long will this people disobey Me? How long will they not believe in the signs? I would destroy them all, and make a people for you that is mightier and more numerous than them." Musa, upon him be peace, said: "My God, if You were to kill this people all at once, like one man, the nations who heard would say: 'This people was only killed because it could not bring them into the holy land, so He killed them in the wilderness.' You are patient, abundant in favours, and You forgive sins and preserve the fathers for the sons and the sons' sons. So forgive them their repentance." Allah said to Musa: "I have forgiven them at your word, but after you named them defiant and invoked a curse upon them, I will surely forbid them to enter the holy land, except for My two servants Yushi' and Caleb. And I will make them wander in this wilderness forty years, each day of which they count as a year. They will die in these deserts, but their sons, who do not know good from evil, will enter the holy land." This is His statement, the Exalted: "He said: 'It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land'" (5:26), meaning they will be bewildered in the land.

They remained forty years in six farsakhs (a farsakh being a distance of about three miles). They would travel each day in a straight line, but when they reached evening and camped, they found themselves at the very place they had set out from. They numbered six hundred thousand fighting men, and hundreds of the ten chiefs who had spread the news suddenly. Everyone who entered the wandering and was over twenty years old died in the wandering, except Yushi' and Caleb. None of those who had said "we will never enter it" entered Jericho. When they had perished and the forty years had passed, and the young men among their descendants had grown up, they set out to fight the tyrants. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/249.]]

The scholars differ over who undertook that battle and at whose hand the conquest occurred. Some said: Musa, upon him be peace, himself conquered Jericho, with Yushi' in the vanguard. Musa set out toward them with those of the Children of Israel who remained, and Yushi' entered with them and fought the tyrants who were there. Then Musa, upon him be peace, entered it with the Children of Israel, remained there as long as Allah willed, and then Allah took him to Himself, and no one among the creatures knows his grave. This is the most correct of the opinions, due to the scholarly consensus that Musa killed Uj ibn Anaq. And Allah knows best.

Others said: It was Yushi' who fought the tyrants, and he did not march against them until after the death of Musa and the destruction of all who had refused to march against them. They said: Musa and Harun died in the wilderness.

The Story of the Death of Harun (peace be upon him)

Al-Suddi said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa: "I am causing Harun to die. Bring him to such-and-such a mountain." Musa and Harun set out toward the mountain, and suddenly they saw trees the like of which had never been seen, and a house built in which there was a couch with bedding on it, and in it a pleasant fragrance. When Harun saw that and sat beside it, he liked it and said: "O Musa, I would love to sleep on this couch." He said: "Sleep on it." He said: "I fear that the owner of this house will come and become angry with me." Musa said to him: "No, I will take care of the owner of this house for you, so sleep." He said: "O Musa, rather sleep with me, for if the owner of the house comes, he will be angry with both of us." When they both slept, Harun was seized by death. When he felt his end coming, he said: "O Musa, take my eye." When he died, that house was lifted up, the tree disappeared, and the couch was raised to the sky. When Musa returned to the Children of Israel without Harun, they said: "Musa has killed Harun, and envy of the love the Children of Israel had for him drove him to it." Musa said: "Woe to you! My brother died and I did not kill him." When they pressed him, he stood and prayed two rak'ahs, then called upon Allah, and the couch descended until they saw it between the heaven and the earth, and so they believed him.

Amr ibn Maymun said: The death of Musa and Harun was in the wilderness, and Harun died before Musa. They had gone out into the wilderness toward some caves. Harun died, and Musa buried him, and returned to the Children of Israel. They said: "What has become of Harun?" He said: "He died." They said: "You are lying, but you killed him because of our love for him," for he was beloved among the Children of Israel.

Musa then complained to his Lord and told Him what he had suffered from the Children of Israel. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "Take them to the grave of Harun until you inform them that he died a natural death and that you did not kill him." So he took them to the grave of Harun, and called out: "O Harun!" He came out of his grave shaking the dust from his head and said: "Did I kill you?" He said: "No, by Allah, but I died." He said: "Return to your resting place," and they dispersed.

As for the death of Musa, upon him be peace:

Ibn Ishaq said: The chosen one of Allah, Musa, had disliked death and considered it great. When he disliked it, Allah wished to make death beloved to him and life hateful to him. Yushi' ibn Nun, who used to visit him morning and evening, met him, and Musa said: "O Prophet of Allah, what has Allah revealed?" Yushi' said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, did I not accompany you for so many years, and did I ever ask you about anything Allah had revealed to you, so that you would be the one guided by it and recounting it, yet not mention anything to me?" When Musa saw that, he disliked life and loved death. Then they differed about the manner of his death.

Hammam ibn Munabbih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The Angel of Death came to Musa, upon him be peace, and said to him: 'Answer your Lord.' Musa struck the eye of the Angel of Death and gouged it out. The Angel of Death returned to Allah, the Exalted, and said: 'You sent me to a servant of Yours who does not want death, and he has gouged out my eye.' Allah restored his eye and said: 'Return to My servant and say to him: Do you want life? If you want life, place your hand on the back of an ox; for every hair your hand covers, you will live a year for each hair.' He said: 'And then what?' He said: 'Then you will die.' He said: 'Then let it be now.' He said: 'My Lord, bring me near to the holy land, the distance of a stone's throw.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, if I were with him, I would show you his grave beside the road at the foot of Mount Sinai, by the red sand dune." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 61/178.]] [48]

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu Sa'id ibn Hamdun say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Maqri say: I heard Muhammad ibn Yahya say: "This story of the Angel of Death and Musa has been authenticated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in meaning, and none rejects it except one who is astray."

In another report, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Angel of Death used to come to people openly, until he came to Musa to seize him. Musa struck him and gouged out his eye, so the Angel of Death returned. Afterward he came secretly." [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/533; Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/305.]] [49]

Al-Suddi said, in a report he mentioned from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Musa, upon him be peace, was walking with his young attendant Yushi', when a black wind came. When Yushi' saw it, he thought it was the Hour, and he clung to Musa. He said: 'The Hour is coming, and I am clinging to Musa, the Prophet of Allah.' Musa slipped out from under his shirt and left the shirt in Yushi's hand. When Yushi' brought the shirt, the Children of Israel seized him and said: 'Did you kill the Prophet of Allah?' He said: 'No, by Allah, I did not kill him, but he slipped away from me.' They did not believe him and wanted to kill him. He said: 'If you do not believe me, then give me three days.' He called upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and each man who had been guarding him came to him in a dream and was informed that Yushi' had not killed him, and that We had raised him to Ourselves. So they left him." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/304.]] [50]

Wahb said: Musa, upon him be peace, went out on some errand, and passed by a group of angels digging a grave. He recognised them and came to them, and stood over them. They were digging a grave the like of which he had never seen, more beautiful than it, and he had never seen such greenery, radiance and delight as was in it. He said to them: "O angels of Allah, for whom are you digging this grave?" They said: "We are digging it, by Allah, for a servant noble before his Lord." He said: "This servant has a station with Allah, for I have never seen a resting place like this today." The angels said: "O chosen one of Allah, would you like it to be yours?" He said: "I would love it." They said: "Then descend, lie down in it, turn to your Lord, and then breathe the gentlest breath you have ever breathed." He descended, lay down in it, turned to his Lord, then breathed, and Allah took his soul. Then the angels smoothed the earth over him. [[The previous source: 305.]]

It was also said: The Angel of Death came to him and said: "O Musa, have you drunk wine?" He said: "No." So he (the Angel of Death) forced him and took his soul. It was also said: Rather, he brought him an apple from Paradise, and he smelled it, and his soul was taken.

It is reported that Yushi' ibn Nun saw him in a dream after his death and said: "How did you find death?" He said: "Like a sheep being skinned while still alive." The age of Musa, upon him be peace, was one hundred and twenty years: twenty of them in the reign of Afridun and a hundred in the reign of Manuchihr. [[In Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/306, "Afridhun" and "Manushihr."]] When the forty years were completed, he died.

When Moses died, God sent Joshua (Yusha') to them as a prophet. He informed them that he was a prophet of God and that God had commanded them to fight the tyrants (al-Jabbarin). They believed him and pledged allegiance to him. He set out with the Children of Israel toward Jericho (Ariha), carrying the Ark of the Covenant (tabut al-mithaq). He besieged the city of Jericho for six months. When it was the seventh, he blew the horns (al-qurun), and the people raised a single great cry, and the wall of the city collapsed. They entered, fought the tyrants, defeated them, and fell upon them, killing them. The victory belonged to the Children of Israel, who would gather around a man's neck and strike it until they severed it. The fighting took place on Friday, and a remnant of them remained. The sun was nearly setting, and the night of Saturday came in. He feared that they would be unable (to finish), so he said: "O God, return the sun to me." He said to the sun: "You are under God's command," and he asked the sun to stand still and the moon to stand still, until he might take vengeance on his enemies before the Sabbath began. The sun was returned to him, and an extra hour of daylight was granted to him, until he had destroyed them all.

Then the kings of the Armanites (al-Armaniyyin) sent to one another, and they were five. They united their word upon Joshua and his people. The Children of Israel defeated the kings, until they drove them down to the valley of Khawran. God pelted them with stones of hail (ahjar mubarrad), and the hail that fell upon them was more numerous than those whom the Children of Israel had slain by the sword. The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave. Joshua commanded them, and they were brought out, and he killed them and crucified them. Then he took them down and threw them into that cave. He pursued the remaining kings of Syria (al-Sham) and seized from them thirty-one kings, until he prevailed over all the land of Syria, and all of Syria became the possession of the Children of Israel. He dispersed his agents throughout its regions. Then he gathered the spoils, but the fire did not descend (upon them).

God revealed to Joshua that there was embezzlement (ghulul) among them. He said: "Command them that they pledge allegiance to you." They pledged allegiance to him, and a man's hand clung to his. He said to them: "Among you is the embezzlement." He (the Prophet ﷺ) said: "Bring what you have." So they brought him the head of an ox adorned with rubies and jewels, which he had embezzled. He placed it with the offering, and the man was with it. Then the fire came and consumed the man and the offering. [With variation in the history of al-Tabari: 1/311 and the history of Ibn Khaldun: 2/87.]

Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A prophet among the prophets went out to fight, and he said to his people: 'Let no man follow me who has married a woman and wishes to consummate the marriage with her and has not yet done so; nor any man who has built a house and has not yet raised its roof; nor any man who has bought sheep or pregnant camels and is awaiting their young.'" He said: So he went out to fight, and he drew near to the town (al-Dayr) at the time of the afternoon prayer (al-'asr) or close to it. He said to the sun: "You are commanded and I am commanded. O God, hold it back for me for an hour." So it was held back for him for an hour, until God granted him victory. He (the narrator) said: "From what I know, it was not held back for anyone before him or after him."

Then the spoils were gathered, and the fire came but did not consume them. He said: "There is embezzlement among you. Let one man from each of your tribes pledge allegiance to me." They pledged allegiance to him, and a man's hand clung to his. He said: "The embezzlement is among you; you have embezzled." They brought out something like the head of a cow made of gold and placed it among the spoils, in the open ground, and the fire came and consumed them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The spoils were not lawful for anyone before us, and that is because God saw our weakness and our incapacity, so He made them lawful for us." [Sahih Ibn Hibban: 11/138, and Sharh Sahih Muslim by al-Nawawi: 12/51.] [51]

They said: Then Joshua (peace be upon him) died and was buried in the mountain of Ephraim (Afraim). His age was one hundred and twenty-six years. And the affairs of the Children of Israel were governed after the death of Moses for twenty-seven years.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verses 20–26 (part 1 of 2):

And when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you, when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings," (5:20). Scholars differ regarding the meaning of "kings."

Abu al-Haytham narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a wife and a mount, he was recorded as a king." [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/29.]] [44]

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and al-Hakam said: "Whoever has a house, a servant and a wife is a king."

Abu Abd al-Rahman said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As being asked by a man: "Are we not among the poor emigrants?" Abdullah said to him: "Do you have a wife to whom you retreat?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you have a dwelling in which you live?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are among the wealthy." He said: "I have a servant and wealth." He said: "Then you are among the kings."

Abu Ubaylah narrated from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, and has his food for the day, it is as if the world has been gathered for him in its entirety. O son of Ju'sham, what suffices you of it is what satisfies your hunger and covers your nakedness. If there is a house that shelters you, that is well; if there is a mount you ride, that is excellent. But a morsel of bread and water, and whatever is beyond that, will be a reckoning for you." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 70/147.]] [45]

Al-Dahhak said: Their dwellings were spacious, with flowing waters. Whoever has a spacious dwelling with flowing water is a king.

Qatadah said: They were the first to own servants, and the first to have servants from among the children of Adam subjected to them.

Al-Suddi said: The meaning is that He made you free, owning yourselves, after you had been under the hands of the Copts, in the position of the people of the jizya (the poll tax paid by non-Muslim subjects) among us. Allah thus delivered you from humiliation. "And He gave you what He had not given anyone else in the worlds," meaning, the worlds other than yourselves.

Mujahid said: The meaning is the manna and the quails, the stone and the clouds.

"O my people, enter the Holy Land," (5:21). Scholars differ regarding what the Holy Land is.

Mujahid said: It is Mount Sinai (al-Tur) and what surrounds it. Al-Dahhak said: It is Iliya and Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). The Sacred House is sacred in its measure, and the heavens and the earth: Bayt al-Maqdis is sanctified in its measure out of the heavens and the earth.

Ikrimah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: It is Jericho (Ariha).

Al-Kalbi said: Damascus, Palestine and part of Jordan.

Qatadah said: It is all of Syria (al-Sham).

Zayd ibn Thabit said: While we were around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was compiling the Qur'an from the scraps, he said: "Blessed is Syria!" It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, why is that?" He said: "Because the angels of the Most Merciful spread their wings over it."[46] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 5/158.]]

Nusayr ibn Alqama al-Himsi narrated from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abdullah ibn Hawalah, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he said: "By Allah, this affair will continue among you until Allah opens the lands of Persia and Rome and the land of Himyar, and until you become three armies: one army in Syria, one army in Iraq, and one army in Yemen."

Ibn Hawalah said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I should live to see that?" He said: "Choose Syria for yourself, for it is the chosen land of Allah among your lands, and to it Allah gathers His chosen ones from among His servants. O people of Islam, hold fast to Syria, for the chosen land of Allah on earth is Syria. Whoever refuses, let him attach himself to his right hand and drink from his pool. Indeed Allah has guaranteed for me Syria and its people." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 1/74; Mu'jam al-Buldan: 3/314.]] [47]

Al-A'mash narrated from Abdullah ibn Sabbar, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: Good was divided into ten parts: nine of it was placed in Syria and one in Iraq. Evil was divided into ten parts: nine of it was placed in Iraq and one in Syria. Ten thousand eyes that saw the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Syria, and five hundred and seventy of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) settled there, among them seventy companions. [[Up to here in Tarikh Dimashq: 1/327.]]

"Which Allah has prescribed for you," (5:21), meaning: He wrote it in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) that it would be your dwellings.

Ibn Ishaq said: "Allah has decreed it for you." Al-Suddi said: "He commanded you to it, calling you to it." Qatadah said: "They were ordered to it as they were ordered to prayer."

"And do not turn back on your heels," meaning, do not turn back on your heels in opposition to Allah, "and so you will turn about as losers," (5:21).

Al-Kalbi said: Ibrahim, upon whom be peace, ascended Mount Lebanon, and it was said to him: "Look. Whatever your sight reaches is sacred, and it is an inheritance for your descendants after you." They said: meaning the Children of Israel. Musa said: "O Musa, keep their affair secret. Do not tell anyone from the camp, lest they spread it." Each man went and told his relative and cousin, except two men who were faithful. Musa said to them... and they were Yushi' ibn Nun ibn Afraithim ibn Yusuf, Musa's attendant, and Caleb ibn Yufunna, Musa's brother-in-law through his sister Miriam, daughter of Imran, and both were from Iliya. The community of the Children of Israel came to know of this, raised their voices in weeping, and said: "Woe to us! Would that we had died in the land of Egypt! Would that we might die in this wilderness, and that Allah would not bring us to these people, so that our women, children and goods become spoils for them." A man would say to his companions: "Come, let us appoint a leader over us and return to Egypt." This is the statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reporting about them: "They said: 'O Musa, there are a people of tyrants in it, and we will never enter it'" (5:22).

Qatadah said: They had bodies and a strange creation that no others had. "And we will never enter it until they leave it. If they leave it, then we will enter" (5:22). When they said that and intended to return to Egypt, Musa and Harun, upon them be peace, fell down prostrating, and Yushi' and Caleb tore their garments. They are the two whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His statement: "Two men from among those who feared spoke, on whom Allah had bestowed favour" (5:23), meaning those who feared Allah.

Said ibn Jubayr read "yukhafun" (with the yā' vowelled with a ḍammah) and said: They were of the tyrants, then they embraced Islam and followed Musa. "On whom Allah had bestowed favour," with success and protection. "Enter upon them through the gate," meaning the town of the tyrants. "When you enter it, you will surely be victorious," because Allah fulfils His promise and does not forget them. Their bodies were great and strong, but their hearts were weak, so they did not fear them. "And upon Allah rely, if you are believers" (5:23). But the Children of Israel wanted to stone them to death and disobeyed them. They said: "O Musa, we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here" (5:24).

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions on the day of Hudaybiyah, when he was prevented from the House: "I am going with the offering, so I will slaughter it at the House." Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said: "By Allah, we will not say to you what the people of Musa said: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed we are sitting right here.' Rather, we will fight on your right and your left, before you and behind you. If you were to plunge into the sea, we would plunge in with you, and if you were to climb a mountain, we would climb it with you. So proceed with us in the blessing of Allah." When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard this, they pledged allegiance to him upon it, and the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brightened and he was pleased by it.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "For me to be the companion of this mosque is dearer to me than what has been given to me."

When the Children of Israel did what they did of disobedience among themselves, and opposed the command of their Lord, and intended to harm Yushi' and Caleb, Musa became angry and invoked a curse upon them. He said: "My Lord, I have no control except over myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiant people" (5:25), meaning: decide and judge between us.

Ubayd ibn Umayr read "fa-friq" with a kasrah on the rā'. "Between us and the defiant people," meaning the disobedient. There was a calf that Musa had made, and the cloud appeared over the entrance of the tent of meeting, the place of his private conversation. Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Musa: "How long will this people disobey Me? How long will they not believe in the signs? I would destroy them all, and make a people for you that is mightier and more numerous than them." Musa, upon him be peace, said: "My God, if You were to kill this people all at once, like one man, the nations who heard would say: 'This people was only killed because it could not bring them into the holy land, so He killed them in the wilderness.' You are patient, abundant in favours, and You forgive sins and preserve the fathers for the sons and the sons' sons. So forgive them their repentance." Allah said to Musa: "I have forgiven them at your word, but after you named them defiant and invoked a curse upon them, I will surely forbid them to enter the holy land, except for My two servants Yushi' and Caleb. And I will make them wander in this wilderness forty years, each day of which they count as a year. They will die in these deserts, but their sons, who do not know good from evil, will enter the holy land." This is His statement, the Exalted: "He said: 'It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land'" (5:26), meaning they will be bewildered in the land.

They remained forty years in six farsakhs (a farsakh being a distance of about three miles). They would travel each day in a straight line, but when they reached evening and camped, they found themselves at the very place they had set out from. They numbered six hundred thousand fighting men, and hundreds of the ten chiefs who had spread the news suddenly. Everyone who entered the wandering and was over twenty years old died in the wandering, except Yushi' and Caleb. None of those who had said "we will never enter it" entered Jericho. When they had perished and the forty years had passed, and the young men among their descendants had grown up, they set out to fight the tyrants. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/249.]]

The scholars differ over who undertook that battle and at whose hand the conquest occurred. Some said: Musa, upon him be peace, himself conquered Jericho, with Yushi' in the vanguard. Musa set out toward them with those of the Children of Israel who remained, and Yushi' entered with them and fought the tyrants who were there. Then Musa, upon him be peace, entered it with the Children of Israel, remained there as long as Allah willed, and then Allah took him to Himself, and no one among the creatures knows his grave. This is the most correct of the opinions, due to the scholarly consensus that Musa killed Uj ibn Anaq. And Allah knows best.

Others said: It was Yushi' who fought the tyrants, and he did not march against them until after the death of Musa and the destruction of all who had refused to march against them. They said: Musa and Harun died in the wilderness.

The Story of the Death of Harun (peace be upon him)

Al-Suddi said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa: "I am causing Harun to die. Bring him to such-and-such a mountain." Musa and Harun set out toward the mountain, and suddenly they saw trees the like of which had never been seen, and a house built in which there was a couch with bedding on it, and in it a pleasant fragrance. When Harun saw that and sat beside it, he liked it and said: "O Musa, I would love to sleep on this couch." He said: "Sleep on it." He said: "I fear that the owner of this house will come and become angry with me." Musa said to him: "No, I will take care of the owner of this house for you, so sleep." He said: "O Musa, rather sleep with me, for if the owner of the house comes, he will be angry with both of us." When they both slept, Harun was seized by death. When he felt his end coming, he said: "O Musa, take my eye." When he died, that house was lifted up, the tree disappeared, and the couch was raised to the sky. When Musa returned to the Children of Israel without Harun, they said: "Musa has killed Harun, and envy of the love the Children of Israel had for him drove him to it." Musa said: "Woe to you! My brother died and I did not kill him." When they pressed him, he stood and prayed two rak'ahs, then called upon Allah, and the couch descended until they saw it between the heaven and the earth, and so they believed him.

Amr ibn Maymun said: The death of Musa and Harun was in the wilderness, and Harun died before Musa. They had gone out into the wilderness toward some caves. Harun died, and Musa buried him, and returned to the Children of Israel. They said: "What has become of Harun?" He said: "He died." They said: "You are lying, but you killed him because of our love for him," for he was beloved among the Children of Israel.

Musa then complained to his Lord and told Him what he had suffered from the Children of Israel. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "Take them to the grave of Harun until you inform them that he died a natural death and that you did not kill him." So he took them to the grave of Harun, and called out: "O Harun!" He came out of his grave shaking the dust from his head and said: "Did I kill you?" He said: "No, by Allah, but I died." He said: "Return to your resting place," and they dispersed.

As for the death of Musa, upon him be peace:

Ibn Ishaq said: The chosen one of Allah, Musa, had disliked death and considered it great. When he disliked it, Allah wished to make death beloved to him and life hateful to him. Yushi' ibn Nun, who used to visit him morning and evening, met him, and Musa said: "O Prophet of Allah, what has Allah revealed?" Yushi' said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, did I not accompany you for so many years, and did I ever ask you about anything Allah had revealed to you, so that you would be the one guided by it and recounting it, yet not mention anything to me?" When Musa saw that, he disliked life and loved death. Then they differed about the manner of his death.

Hammam ibn Munabbih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The Angel of Death came to Musa, upon him be peace, and said to him: 'Answer your Lord.' Musa struck the eye of the Angel of Death and gouged it out. The Angel of Death returned to Allah, the Exalted, and said: 'You sent me to a servant of Yours who does not want death, and he has gouged out my eye.' Allah restored his eye and said: 'Return to My servant and say to him: Do you want life? If you want life, place your hand on the back of an ox; for every hair your hand covers, you will live a year for each hair.' He said: 'And then what?' He said: 'Then you will die.' He said: 'Then let it be now.' He said: 'My Lord, bring me near to the holy land, the distance of a stone's throw.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, if I were with him, I would show you his grave beside the road at the foot of Mount Sinai, by the red sand dune." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 61/178.]] [48]

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu Sa'id ibn Hamdun say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Maqri say: I heard Muhammad ibn Yahya say: "This story of the Angel of Death and Musa has been authenticated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in meaning, and none rejects it except one who is astray."

In another report, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Angel of Death used to come to people openly, until he came to Musa to seize him. Musa struck him and gouged out his eye, so the Angel of Death returned. Afterward he came secretly." [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/533; Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/305.]] [49]

Al-Suddi said, in a report he mentioned from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Musa, upon him be peace, was walking with his young attendant Yushi', when a black wind came. When Yushi' saw it, he thought it was the Hour, and he clung to Musa. He said: 'The Hour is coming, and I am clinging to Musa, the Prophet of Allah.' Musa slipped out from under his shirt and left the shirt in Yushi's hand. When Yushi' brought the shirt, the Children of Israel seized him and said: 'Did you kill the Prophet of Allah?' He said: 'No, by Allah, I did not kill him, but he slipped away from me.' They did not believe him and wanted to kill him. He said: 'If you do not believe me, then give me three days.' He called upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and each man who had been guarding him came to him in a dream and was informed that Yushi' had not killed him, and that We had raised him to Ourselves. So they left him." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/304.]] [50]

Wahb said: Musa, upon him be peace, went out on some errand, and passed by a group of angels digging a grave. He recognised them and came to them, and stood over them. They were digging a grave the like of which he had never seen, more beautiful than it, and he had never seen such greenery, radiance and delight as was in it. He said to them: "O angels of Allah, for whom are you digging this grave?" They said: "We are digging it, by Allah, for a servant noble before his Lord." He said: "This servant has a station with Allah, for I have never seen a resting place like this today." The angels said: "O chosen one of Allah, would you like it to be yours?" He said: "I would love it." They said: "Then descend, lie down in it, turn to your Lord, and then breathe the gentlest breath you have ever breathed." He descended, lay down in it, turned to his Lord, then breathed, and Allah took his soul. Then the angels smoothed the earth over him. [[The previous source: 305.]]

It was also said: The Angel of Death came to him and said: "O Musa, have you drunk wine?" He said: "No." So he (the Angel of Death) forced him and took his soul. It was also said: Rather, he brought him an apple from Paradise, and he smelled it, and his soul was taken.

It is reported that Yushi' ibn Nun saw him in a dream after his death and said: "How did you find death?" He said: "Like a sheep being skinned while still alive." The age of Musa, upon him be peace, was one hundred and twenty years: twenty of them in the reign of Afridun and a hundred in the reign of Manuchihr. [[In Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/306, "Afridhun" and "Manushihr."]] When the forty years were completed, he died.

When Moses died, God sent Joshua (Yusha') to them as a prophet. He informed them that he was a prophet of God and that God had commanded them to fight the tyrants (al-Jabbarin). They believed him and pledged allegiance to him. He set out with the Children of Israel toward Jericho (Ariha), carrying the Ark of the Covenant (tabut al-mithaq). He besieged the city of Jericho for six months. When it was the seventh, he blew the horns (al-qurun), and the people raised a single great cry, and the wall of the city collapsed. They entered, fought the tyrants, defeated them, and fell upon them, killing them. The victory belonged to the Children of Israel, who would gather around a man's neck and strike it until they severed it. The fighting took place on Friday, and a remnant of them remained. The sun was nearly setting, and the night of Saturday came in. He feared that they would be unable (to finish), so he said: "O God, return the sun to me." He said to the sun: "You are under God's command," and he asked the sun to stand still and the moon to stand still, until he might take vengeance on his enemies before the Sabbath began. The sun was returned to him, and an extra hour of daylight was granted to him, until he had destroyed them all.

Then the kings of the Armanites (al-Armaniyyin) sent to one another, and they were five. They united their word upon Joshua and his people. The Children of Israel defeated the kings, until they drove them down to the valley of Khawran. God pelted them with stones of hail (ahjar mubarrad), and the hail that fell upon them was more numerous than those whom the Children of Israel had slain by the sword. The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave. Joshua commanded them, and they were brought out, and he killed them and crucified them. Then he took them down and threw them into that cave. He pursued the remaining kings of Syria (al-Sham) and seized from them thirty-one kings, until he prevailed over all the land of Syria, and all of Syria became the possession of the Children of Israel. He dispersed his agents throughout its regions. Then he gathered the spoils, but the fire did not descend (upon them).

God revealed to Joshua that there was embezzlement (ghulul) among them. He said: "Command them that they pledge allegiance to you." They pledged allegiance to him, and a man's hand clung to his. He said to them: "Among you is the embezzlement." He (the Prophet ﷺ) said: "Bring what you have." So they brought him the head of an ox adorned with rubies and jewels, which he had embezzled. He placed it with the offering, and the man was with it. Then the fire came and consumed the man and the offering. [With variation in the history of al-Tabari: 1/311 and the history of Ibn Khaldun: 2/87.]

Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A prophet among the prophets went out to fight, and he said to his people: 'Let no man follow me who has married a woman and wishes to consummate the marriage with her and has not yet done so; nor any man who has built a house and has not yet raised its roof; nor any man who has bought sheep or pregnant camels and is awaiting their young.'" He said: So he went out to fight, and he drew near to the town (al-Dayr) at the time of the afternoon prayer (al-'asr) or close to it. He said to the sun: "You are commanded and I am commanded. O God, hold it back for me for an hour." So it was held back for him for an hour, until God granted him victory. He (the narrator) said: "From what I know, it was not held back for anyone before him or after him."

Then the spoils were gathered, and the fire came but did not consume them. He said: "There is embezzlement among you. Let one man from each of your tribes pledge allegiance to me." They pledged allegiance to him, and a man's hand clung to his. He said: "The embezzlement is among you; you have embezzled." They brought out something like the head of a cow made of gold and placed it among the spoils, in the open ground, and the fire came and consumed them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The spoils were not lawful for anyone before us, and that is because God saw our weakness and our incapacity, so He made them lawful for us." [Sahih Ibn Hibban: 11/138, and Sharh Sahih Muslim by al-Nawawi: 12/51.] [51]

They said: Then Joshua (peace be upon him) died and was buried in the mountain of Ephraim (Afraim). His age was one hundred and twenty-six years. And the affairs of the Children of Israel were governed after the death of Moses for twenty-seven years.

Said ibn Jubayr read "yukhafun" (with the yā' vowelled with a ḍammah) and said: They were of the tyrants, then they embraced Islam and followed Musa. "On whom Allah had bestowed favour," with success and protection. "Enter upon them through the gate," meaning the town of the tyrants. "When you enter it, you will surely be victorious," because Allah fulfils His promise and does not forget them. Their bodies were great and strong, but their hearts were weak, so they did not fear them. "And upon Allah rely, if you are believers" (5:23). But the Children of Israel wanted to stone them to death and disobeyed them. They said: "O Musa, we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here" (5:24).

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions on the day of Hudaybiyah, when he was prevented from the House: "I am going with the offering, so I will slaughter it at the House." Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said: "By Allah, we will not say to you what the people of Musa said: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed we are sitting right here.' Rather, we will fight on your right and your left, before you and behind you. If you were to plunge into the sea, we would plunge in with you, and if you were to climb a mountain, we would climb it with you. So proceed with us in the blessing of Allah." When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard this, they pledged allegiance to him upon it, and the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brightened and he was pleased by it.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "For me to be the companion of this mosque is dearer to me than what has been given to me."

When the Children of Israel did what they did of disobedience among themselves, and opposed the command of their Lord, and intended to harm Yushi' and Caleb, Musa became angry and invoked a curse upon them. He said: "My Lord, I have no control except over myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiant people" (5:25), meaning: decide and judge between us.

Ubayd ibn Umayr read "fa-friq" with a kasrah on the rā'. "Between us and the defiant people," meaning the disobedient. There was a calf that Musa had made, and the cloud appeared over the entrance of the tent of meeting, the place of his private conversation. Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Musa: "How long will this people disobey Me? How long will they not believe in the signs? I would destroy them all, and make a people for you that is mightier and more numerous than them." Musa, upon him be peace, said: "My God, if You were to kill this people all at once, like one man, the nations who heard would say: 'This people was only killed because it could not bring them into the holy land, so He killed them in the wilderness.' You are patient, abundant in favours, and You forgive sins and preserve the fathers for the sons and the sons' sons. So forgive them their repentance." Allah said to Musa: "I have forgiven them at your word, but after you named them defiant and invoked a curse upon them, I will surely forbid them to enter the holy land, except for My two servants Yushi' and Caleb. And I will make them wander in this wilderness forty years, each day of which they count as a year. They will die in these deserts, but their sons, who do not know good from evil, will enter the holy land." This is His statement, the Exalted: "He said: 'It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land'" (5:26), meaning they will be bewildered in the land.

They remained forty years in six farsakhs (a farsakh being a distance of about three miles). They would travel each day in a straight line, but when they reached evening and camped, they found themselves at the very place they had set out from. They numbered six hundred thousand fighting men, and hundreds of the ten chiefs who had spread the news suddenly. Everyone who entered the wandering and was over twenty years old died in the wandering, except Yushi' and Caleb. None of those who had said "we will never enter it" entered Jericho. When they had perished and the forty years had passed, and the young men among their descendants had grown up, they set out to fight the tyrants. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/249.]]

The scholars differ over who undertook that battle and at whose hand the conquest occurred. Some said: Musa, upon him be peace, himself conquered Jericho, with Yushi' in the vanguard. Musa set out toward them with those of the Children of Israel who remained, and Yushi' entered with them and fought the tyrants who were there. Then Musa, upon him be peace, entered it with the Children of Israel, remained there as long as Allah willed, and then Allah took him to Himself, and no one among the creatures knows his grave. This is the most correct of the opinions, due to the scholarly consensus that Musa killed Uj ibn Anaq. And Allah knows best.

Others said: It was Yushi' who fought the tyrants, and he did not march against them until after the death of Musa and the destruction of all who had refused to march against them. They said: Musa and Harun died in the wilderness.

The Story of the Death of Harun (peace be upon him)

Al-Suddi said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa: "I am causing Harun to die. Bring him to such-and-such a mountain." Musa and Harun set out toward the mountain, and suddenly they saw trees the like of which had never been seen, and a house built in which there was a couch with bedding on it, and in it a pleasant fragrance. When Harun saw that and sat beside it, he liked it and said: "O Musa, I would love to sleep on this couch." He said: "Sleep on it." He said: "I fear that the owner of this house will come and become angry with me." Musa said to him: "No, I will take care of the owner of this house for you, so sleep." He said: "O Musa, rather sleep with me, for if the owner of the house comes, he will be angry with both of us." When they both slept, Harun was seized by death. When he felt his end coming, he said: "O Musa, take my eye." When he died, that house was lifted up, the tree disappeared, and the couch was raised to the sky. When Musa returned to the Children of Israel without Harun, they said: "Musa has killed Harun, and envy of the love the Children of Israel had for him drove him to it." Musa said: "Woe to you! My brother died and I did not kill him." When they pressed him, he stood and prayed two rak'ahs, then called upon Allah, and the couch descended until they saw it between the heaven and the earth, and so they believed him.

Amr ibn Maymun said: The death of Musa and Harun was in the wilderness, and Harun died before Musa. They had gone out into the wilderness toward some caves. Harun died, and Musa buried him, and returned to the Children of Israel. They said: "What has become of Harun?" He said: "He died." They said: "You are lying, but you killed him because of our love for him," for he was beloved among the Children of Israel.

Musa then complained to his Lord and told Him what he had suffered from the Children of Israel. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "Take them to the grave of Harun until you inform them that he died a natural death and that you did not kill him." So he took them to the grave of Harun, and called out: "O Harun!" He came out of his grave shaking the dust from his head and said: "Did I kill you?" He said: "No, by Allah, but I died." He said: "Return to your resting place," and they dispersed.

As for the death of Musa, upon him be peace:

Ibn Ishaq said: The chosen one of Allah, Musa, had disliked death and considered it great. When he disliked it, Allah wished to make death beloved to him and life hateful to him. Yushi' ibn Nun, who used to visit him morning and evening, met him, and Musa said: "O Prophet of Allah, what has Allah revealed?" Yushi' said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, did I not accompany you for so many years, and did I ever ask you about anything Allah had revealed to you, so that you would be the one guided by it and recounting it, yet not mention anything to me?" When Musa saw that, he disliked life and loved death. Then they differed about the manner of his death.

Hammam ibn Munabbih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The Angel of Death came to Musa, upon him be peace, and said to him: 'Answer your Lord.' Musa struck the eye of the Angel of Death and gouged it out. The Angel of Death returned to Allah, the Exalted, and said: 'You sent me to a servant of Yours who does not want death, and he has gouged out my eye.' Allah restored his eye and said: 'Return to My servant and say to him: Do you want life? If you want life, place your hand on the back of an ox; for every hair your hand covers, you will live a year for each hair.' He said: 'And then what?' He said: 'Then you will die.' He said: 'Then let it be now.' He said: 'My Lord, bring me near to the holy land, the distance of a stone's throw.'"
