The reason for their offering the sacrifice, as mentioned by the scholars of the Qur'an, is that Hawwa' used to give birth to twins for Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) in every pregnancy, a boy and a girl, except Shith, whom she bore alone. The total number of children Hawwa' bore was forty, male and female, across twenty pregnancies. The first of them was Qabil with his twin Aqlima, and the last was ʿAbd al-Mughith with his twin Amat al-Mughith. Then God blessed the offspring of Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam). [[There is a discrepancy here with what al-Mas'udi reports in Akhbar al-Zaman: 74.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) did not die until his children and grandchildren reached forty thousand, a number of descendants (banun). [[So also in Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/114 and al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: 1/39.]]

Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) saw among them fornication, drinking of wine, and corruption.

The scholars differed about the time of the births of Qabil and Habil, and the point of their disagreement. Some of them said: Adam approached Hawwa' sexually after they had descended to earth, a hundred years later, and she bore him Qabil with his twin Aqlima in one pregnancy, and then Habil with his twin in another.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of some of the People of the Book: The first knowledge is that Adam used to approach Hawwa' in Paradise before he committed the sin. She conceived by him there Qabil and his twin. He experienced no nausea (wahm), no fatigue (wasab), and no labour pains (talq) when she gave birth to them, and she saw no blood with them, because of the purity of Paradise. But when he descended to earth and they settled there, he approached her again, and she conceived Habil and his twin. She then experienced fatigue, nausea, labour pains and bleeding.

When their children grew up, Adam would marry the boy of one pregnancy to the girl of another, and the girl of one pregnancy to the boy of another. A man among them could marry whichever of his sisters he wished, except his twin who was born with him, for she was not lawful to him. That was because at that time there were no women except their sisters and their mother Hawwa'. When Qabil and Aqlima were born, then Habil and his twin Layuda in one pregnancy, with two years between them, according to al-Kalbi's account, they reached the command of God, the Mighty and Majestic, to Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam): that Qabil should marry Layuda, Habil's sister, and Habil should marry Aqlima, Qabil's sister. Aqlima was among the most beautiful of people. Adam mentioned this to his children. Habil was pleased, but Qabil was displeased and said: She is my sister, born with me in one pregnancy. She is more beautiful than Habil's sister, and I have more right to her than he does, because she is from the birth of Paradise and they are from the birth of the earth. I have more right to my sister. His father told him: She is not lawful to you. But he refused to accept this from him, and said: God has not commanded this; it is only his own opinion. Then Adam said to them both: Offer a sacrifice, and whichever of you is accepted, he has more right to her.

Muʿawiya ibn ʿAmmar said: I asked al-Sadiq (peace of God be upon him) whether Adam had married his daughter to his son. He said: God forbid! By God, if Adam had done that, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would not have turned away from it. The religion of Adam was none other than the religion of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When God, blessed and exalted, sent Adam and Hawwa' down to earth and brought them together, Hawwa' gave birth to a daughter whom she named Layuda, and she committed fornication, and she was the first to commit fornication on the face of the earth. So God sent upon her someone who killed her. Then she bore Qabil to Adam in her stead, and then Habil was born to him. When Qabil reached maturity, God caused to appear a jinn-female from the offspring of the jinn, called Jihana, in human form, and God revealed to Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) that he should marry her to Qabil, and he did. When Habil reached maturity, God sent down a houri (hawraʾ) to Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) in human form, and created for her a womb, and her name was Nuzla. When Qabil saw her, he desired her, and God revealed to Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) that he should marry Nuzla to Habil, and he did. Qabil said to him: Am I not older than my brother, and more deserving of what you have done for him? Adam said to him: My son, "Grace is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills." Qabil said: No, but you preferred him over me out of your own desire. Adam said to him: If you wish to know that, then offer a sacrifice, and whichever of you is accepted, he is more worthy of grace than his companion. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/134.]]

They said: When sacrifices were accepted, fire would descend from heaven and consume them. When they were not accepted, the fire would not descend, and the birds and beasts would eat them. So they went out to offer their sacrifices. Qabil was a farmer, and he offered a portion of food from the worst of his crops, and he privately resolved: I do not care whether it is accepted from me or not, I will never marry my sister. Habil was a shepherd with livestock, and he offered a fat ram from among his flock, along with milk and butter, and in his heart he intended to be pleased with God, the Mighty and Majestic.

Isma'il ibn Rafi' said: I have been told that Habil had a ewe that he milked, and among her offspring was a lamb. He loved it so much that he had no property more precious to him than it, and he used to carry it on his back. When he was commanded to offer a sacrifice, he offered it. He said: They placed their sacrifices upon the mountain, and then Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) called them, and fire descended from heaven and consumed the lamb, the butter and the milk, and it did not consume any grain from Qabil's offering, because he was not pure of heart. Habil's offering was accepted because he was pure of heart. The lamb continued to graze in Paradise until it was ransomed for the son of Ibrahim. That is the meaning of His words, ﴿and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other﴾. They came down from the mountain, and they knew. Qabil became angry when God rejected his offering, and envy and insolence appeared in him, and he used to conceal this within himself. Until Adam came to Mecca to visit the House. When he wanted to go to Mecca, he said to the heavens: Guard my son with trust. They refused. He said the same to the earth, and it refused; to the mountains, and they refused. Then he said it to Qabil, and he accepted it, and said: Yes, go and see your son as will please you. Adam returned, and Qabil had killed his brother. Concerning this is His word: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it﴾ [[Surah al-Ahzab: 72.]], meaning Qabil, ﴿indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, when he bore his father's trust and then betrayed it.

They said: When Adam was absent, Qabil came to Habil while he was at Ghazza and said: I will kill you. He said: Why? He said: Because God accepted your sacrifice and rejected mine, and you will marry my beautiful sister, and I will marry your ugly sister, and people will say that you are better and more excellent than I am, and your offspring will boast over my offspring. Habil said to him: And what is my fault? ﴿God accepts only from the God-fearing. If you stretch out your hand to me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand to you to kill you. Indeed I fear God, the Lord of the worlds﴾.

ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: By God, the one who was killed was truly the stronger of the two men, but his scruple prevented him from stretching his hand out against his brother.

Mujahid said: At that time it was prescribed that if a man wanted to kill another man, the latter should let him do so and not resist him. ﴿Indeed I want you to bear my sin and your sin﴾, meaning the sin of killing me in addition to your sin that you committed before killing me. This is the view of the majority of the commentators.

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid, who said: The meaning is: I want my sin that I committed, if you kill me, to be upon you, and your sin, so that you bear my sin and my blood together. ﴿So you will be among the companions of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾. In this is evidence that they were then accountable, and that they were subject to promise and threat. ﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother seem good to him﴾, meaning it obeyed him and agreed with him in the killing of his brother.

Mujahid said: It encouraged him. Qatada said: It adorned it for him. ﴿So he killed him﴾.

Al-Suddi said: When he wanted to kill Habil, the youth (Qabil) hid in the mountain tops. Then one day he came to him while he was tending his sheep and sleeping, and lifted a rock and crushed his head with it, and he died.

Ibn Jurayj said: Qabil did not know how to kill Habil, so Iblis appeared to him and took a bird, placed its head on a stone, and crushed its head with another stone while Qabil watched. So he taught him killing, and Qabil placed his brother's head between two stones. Habil was twenty years old when he was killed. They differed about the place of his fall and the location of his killing.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: On the mountain of Nawd. Others said: At the pass of Hira. Muhammad ibn Jarir related it.

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: In Basra, at the site of the Great Mosque.

When he killed him in the open, he did not know what to do with him, because he was the first dead person on the face of the earth from the children of Adam. Beasts approached him, so he carried him on his back in a bag for a year, until he decayed, and birds and beasts clung to him, watching when he would drop him so they could eat him. ﴿God sent two ravens, which fought, and one killed the other. Then it dug for it with its beak and its feet until it had made room for it, and then it put it into the pit and covered it﴾. Qabil was watching it. When he saw that, he said: ﴿Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this raven, and conceal my brother's corpse?﴾, that is, his carcass. In this is evidence that the whole of a dead body is a private part (ʿawra) to be covered. ﴿So he became one of the remorseful﴾ for carrying him, not for killing him. It was also said: for his brother's death, not for committing the sin.

This is supported by what al-Awzaʿi reported from al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Makhzumi, who said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, the earth shook with what was on it for seven days. Then the earth drank his blood as water is drunk. God called out: Where is your brother Habil? He said: I do not know; I was not his keeper. God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Indeed the voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the earth. Why did you kill your brother? Where is his blood, if you killed him? God, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade the earth from ever drinking blood again after that.

Muqatil ibn al-Dahhak related from Ibn ʿAbbas: When Qabil killed Habil while Adam was in Mecca, the trees became shrivelled, the foods changed, the fruits became sour, the water became bitter, and the earth became dusty.

Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) said: Something has happened on the earth. He went to India, and there he found Qabil had killed Habil. He composed verse, and he was the first to compose poetry:

The lands have changed, and whoever is upon them,
and the face of the earth is dusty and ugly.
Every thing with colour and taste has changed,
and the radiance of the beautiful face has diminished.

[[In Tabari: "fulun" (a colour) instead of "wajh".]] [[Jami' al-Bayan: 6/258; and in Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/98 "al-Malih" instead of "al-Sabih".]]

Maymun ibn Mihran related from Ibn ʿAbbas: Whoever says that Adam composed poetry has lied against God and His Messenger, and has accused Adam of sins. Indeed Muhammad (ﷺ) and all the prophets, may the blessings of God be upon them, are equal in prohibiting poetry. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him﴾. But when Qabil killed Habil, Adam lamented him, and he was Syriac-speaking. Only one who speaks Arabic composes poetry. When Adam uttered a dirge for his son Habil, who was the first martyr on the face of the earth, Adam said to his son Shith, who was his eldest child and his successor: O my son, you are my successor. Keep this speech so that it may be inherited. It continued to be passed down until it reached Yaʿrub ibn Qahtan, who spoke Arabic and Syriac, and was the first to write in Arabic, and used to compose poetry. He examined the lament and found that it was rhymed prose (saj'), and said: This indeed can be made into verse. He moved the front to the back and the back to the front, and it became verse, without adding or omitting a single letter. He said:

The lands have changed, and whoever is upon them,
and the face of the earth is dusty and ugly.
Every thing with taste and colour has changed,
and the radiance of the beautiful face has diminished.
Qabil made Habil taste death, so alas for my grief! The fair one has perished.
Why should I not pour out tears, while Habil is contained in the grave?
Killing the son of the prophet without any crime,
my heart is wounded beside his heart.
I see the length of life as a sorrow to me,
and am I at rest from my life?
We have neighbours, an enemy that does not perish,
so that we would rest if he died.
Leave off complaining, for both have perished,
by one who perished, not for a worthy price.
What use is weeping to those who weep,
when a man has been buried in the grave?
So weep for yourself, and leave its desires,
for you will not be immortal after the sacrificed one.

Then Iblis answered him in the middle of the night, gloating:

Withdraw from the lands and their inhabitants,
O youth, for the wide Paradise has grown narrow for you.
You were in it with your wife in ease,
and your heart was at rest from the harms of the world.
My plots and my deceit did not cease
until the goodly Paradise escaped you.
Had it not been for the mercy of the Almighty, there would have arisen
from your palm a wind from the gardens of Paradise. [[Tarikh Baghdad, with variations: 5/336, biography no. 2868.]]

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd said: When Habil was killed, Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) remained for only one hundred years. Then he came, and it was said to him: May God welcome you and make you laugh (bayyaka), that is, make you laugh. When Adam's age had reached one hundred and thirty years, which was five years after the killing of Habil, Hawwa' bore him Shith. His name means "gift of God", meaning that he was a replacement for Habil. God taught him the hours of the night and the day, and informed him of the worship of creation in each hour. He sent down to him the Gift of God (Hibat Allah), and he became Adam's successor (wasi) and heir to his covenant (waliy ʿahdih), peace be upon them both. As for Qabil, it was said to him: Go, a fugitive and vagrant, terrified and feared, and no one who sees you will feel safe. He took his sister Hibat Allah by the hand and went with her to Aden in the land of Yemen. Iblis came to him and said: The fire consumed Habil's offering only because he used to worship fire and serve it. So you set up a fire that will belong to you and your descendants. He set up a fire, and he was the first to set up a fire and worship it.

They said: Whenever any of his offspring passed by him, he would shoot at them. Then a blind descendant of Qabil approached, with a son of his. The blind man said: This is your father, Qabil. Then Qabil's son shot the blind man and killed him. The blind man's son said: You have killed your father! He raised his hand and struck his son, and he died. The blind man said: Woe to me! I killed my father with my shot, and I killed my son with my slap.

Mujahid said: One of Qabil's legs was tied to his thigh and calf, and he remains tied so until the Day of Resurrection. His face was turned toward the sun, which revolved around him, and in summer it was surrounded by a fence of fire, and in winter by a fence of ice.

They said: The offspring of Qabil made musical instruments of reed pipes, lutes, flutes, lutes ('idan) and drums (tanabir). They became immersed in amusement, drinking wine, worshipping fire, fornication and abominations, until God, the Mighty and Majestic, sent the Flood upon them in the days of Nuh (ʿalayhi al-salam), and the line of Shith survived.

ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: We find that the murderous son of Adam shares the punishment of the people of the Fire in a correct division: the punishment upon him is half of their punishment.

Al-Aʿmash related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murra, from Masruq ibn ʿAbd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No soul is killed unjustly except that a portion of its blood falls upon the first son of Adam, because he was the first to establish killing." [52]

Muslim ibn ʿAbd Allah related from Saʿid ibn Sur, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about Tuesday, and he said: "It is a day of blood." They said: How is that, O Messenger of God? He said: "On it Hawwa' menstruated, and the son of Adam was killed by his brother." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/140.]] [53]

And on the authority of Yahya ibn Zuhdam, who said: My father related to me from his father, from Anas, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, bestowed three favours upon the son of Adam, one after another: the wind after the spirit, for if the wind did not come after the spirit, no beloved would be buried by a beloved. And the worm in the grain, for if the worm did not come into the grain, kings would hoard it, and it would be more valuable to them than gold and silver. And death after old age, for a man grows old until he wearies of himself, and his family, children and relatives weary of him, and so death is easier for him." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/142.]] [54]

﴿Because of that﴾, that is, because of that killer and his savagery. It is said: "ajala fulan ya'jalu ajalan", like "akhadha yakhudhu akhdhan" (he committed an offence).

The poet said:
"And the people of a tent that is righteous among themselves,
they have fought over a matter I am postponing."
[[Al-Sihah: 4/1621.]]

﴿We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, not in retaliation for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾. Its meaning is His word: ﴿The recompense of those who wage war against God and His Messenger is only...﴾ [the verse], ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾.

Mujahid: People differed about it. Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of ʿIkrima and ʿAtiyya, said: Whoever kills a prophet or a just imam, ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾, and whoever assists a prophet or a just imam, ﴿it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾.

Mujahid: Whoever kills a soul that is sacred, he will burn in the Fire for killing it, just as he would burn if he had killed all people. And whoever preserves it, by refraining from killing it, has preserved all people. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/273.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 27–32 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Suddi: "Whoever kills..." — ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾ — in the sense of the sin borne by the one who is killed. ﴿And whoever gives it life﴾ — that is, rescues it from destruction, such as drowning, burning, collapse, or other such things — ﴿it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾ in the sense of the one who is rescued.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾ means that he is liable to retaliation (qisas) for killing it, equal to what he intended in his heart, had he killed all mankind. ﴿And whoever gives it life﴾ means one who pardons the person against whom retaliation was due to him, and does not kill him. ﴿It is as if he had given life to all mankind.﴾

Qatadah and al-Dahhak: The meaning, whether the Almighty's killing of it is great or its burden is great, is that whoever deems it lawful to kill a Muslim without right ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾, because they are not safe from him. ﴿And whoever gives it life﴾ — who holds it sacred and refrains from killing it — ﴿it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾, because they are safe from him.

Sulayman ibn Ali al-Rab'i said: I said to al-Hasan, "O Abu Sa'id, it applies to us as it applied to the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes, by the One besides whom there is no god, the blood of the Children of Israel is more honoured before God than our blood."

﴿And certainly Our messengers came to them with clear proofs; then, after that, many of them were indeed transgressors in the land.﴾

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated from al-Zayyat ibn Amr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives water to a believer who is thirsty [[In the source: a believer a sip of water while water is available.]] it is as if he freed seventy slaves, and whoever gives water in a place where it is not available, it is as if he gave life to a soul. ﴿And whoever gives it life, it is as if he had given life to all mankind.﴾"

[[Dhikr akhbar Isfahan: 1/197.]] [55]

And recite to them the account (nabaʾ) of the two sons of Adam, that is, Habil and Qabil. Habil's name has three dialectal forms: Habil, Habl and Habin. Qabil's name has five: Qabil, Qabin, Qabl, Qabn and Qabn. ﴿When the two of them offered a sacrifice﴾. The reason for their offering the sacrifice, as mentioned by the scholars of the Qur'an, is that Hawwa' used to give birth to twins for Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) in every pregnancy, a boy and a girl, except Shith, whom she bore alone. Aqlima was among the most beautiful of people. Adam mentioned this to his children. Habil was pleased, but Qabil was displeased and said: She is my sister, born with me in one pregnancy. She is more beautiful than Habil's sister, and I have more right to her than he does, because she is from the birth of Paradise and they are from the birth of the earth. I have more right to my sister. His father told him: She is not lawful to you. But he refused to accept this from him, and said: God has not commanded this; it is only his own opinion. By God, if Adam had done that, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would not have turned away from it. The religion of Adam was none other than the religion of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When God, blessed and exalted, sent Adam and Hawwa' down to earth and brought them together, Hawwa' gave birth to a daughter whom she named Layuda, and she committed fornication, and she was the first to commit fornication on the face of the earth. He said: Because God accepted your sacrifice and rejected mine, and you will marry my beautiful sister, and I will marry your ugly sister, and people will say that you are better and more excellent than I am, and your offspring will boast over my offspring. Habil said to him: And what is my fault? ﴿God accepts only from the God-fearing. If you stretch out your hand to me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand to you to kill you. Indeed I fear God, the Lord of the worlds﴾.

ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: By God, the one who was killed was truly the stronger of the two men, but his scruple prevented him from stretching his hand out against his brother.

Mujahid said: At that time it was prescribed that if a man wanted to kill another man, the latter should let him do so and not resist him. ﴿Indeed I want you to bear my sin and your sin﴾, meaning the sin of killing me in addition to your sin that you committed before killing me. This is the view of the majority of the commentators.

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid, who said: The meaning is: I want my sin that I committed, if you kill me, to be upon you, and your sin, so that you bear my sin and my blood together. ﴿So you will be among the companions of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾. In this is evidence that they were then accountable, and that they were subject to promise and threat. ﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother seem good to him﴾, meaning it obeyed him and agreed with him in the killing of his brother.

Mujahid said: It encouraged him. Qatada said: It adorned it for him. ﴿So he killed him﴾.

Al-Suddi said: When he wanted to kill Habil, the youth (Qabil) hid in the mountain tops. Then one day he came to him while he was tending his sheep and sleeping, and lifted a rock and crushed his head with it, and he died.

Ibn Jurayj said: Qabil did not know how to kill Habil, so Iblis appeared to him and took a bird, placed its head on a stone, and crushed its head with another stone while Qabil watched. So he taught him killing, and Qabil placed his brother's head between two stones. Habil was twenty years old when he was killed. They differed about the place of his fall and the location of his killing.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: On the mountain of Nawd. Others said: At the pass of Hira. Muhammad ibn Jarir related it.

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: In Basra, at the site of the Great Mosque.

When he killed him in the open, he did not know what to do with him, because he was the first dead person on the face of the earth from the children of Adam. Beasts approached him, so he carried him on his back in a bag for a year, until he decayed, and birds and beasts clung to him, watching when he would drop him so they could eat him. ﴿God sent two ravens, which fought, and one killed the other. Then it dug for it with its beak and its feet until it had made room for it, and then it put it into the pit and covered it﴾. Qabil was watching it. When he saw that, he said: ﴿Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this raven, and conceal my brother's corpse?﴾, that is, his carcass. In this is evidence that the whole of a dead body is a private part (ʿawra) to be covered. ﴿So he became one of the remorseful﴾ for carrying him, not for killing him. It was also said: for his brother's death, not for committing the sin.

This is supported by what al-Awzaʿi reported from al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Makhzumi, who said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, the earth shook with what was on it for seven days. Then the earth drank his blood as water is drunk. God called out: Where is your brother Habil? He said: I do not know; I was not his keeper. God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Indeed the voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the earth. Why did you kill your brother? Where is his blood, if you killed him? God, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade the earth from ever drinking blood again after that.

Muqatil ibn al-Dahhak related from Ibn ʿAbbas: When Qabil killed Habil while Adam was in Mecca, the trees became shrivelled, the foods changed, the fruits became sour, the water became bitter, and the earth became dusty.

Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) said: Something has happened on the earth. He went to India, and there he found Qabil had killed Habil. He composed verse, and he was the first to compose poetry:

The lands have changed, and whoever is upon them,
and the face of the earth is dusty and ugly.
Every thing with colour and taste has changed,
and the radiance of the beautiful face has diminished.

[[In Tabari: "fulun" (a colour) instead of "wajh".]] [[Jami' al-Bayan: 6/258; and in Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/98 "al-Malih" instead of "al-Sabih".]]

Maymun ibn Mihran related from Ibn ʿAbbas: Whoever says that Adam composed poetry has lied against God and His Messenger, and has accused Adam of sins. Indeed Muhammad (ﷺ) and all the prophets, may the blessings of God be upon them, are equal in prohibiting poetry. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him﴾. But when Qabil killed Habil, Adam lamented him, and he was Syriac-speaking. Only one who speaks Arabic composes poetry. When Adam uttered a dirge for his son Habil, who was the first martyr on the face of the earth, Adam said to his son Shith, who was his eldest child and his successor: O my son, you are my successor. Keep this speech so that it may be inherited. It continued to be passed down until it reached Yaʿrub ibn Qahtan, who spoke Arabic and Syriac, and was the first to write in Arabic, and used to compose poetry. He examined the lament and found that it was rhymed prose (saj'), and said: This indeed can be made into verse. He moved the front to the back and the back to the front, and it became verse, without adding or omitting a single letter. He said:

The lands have changed, and whoever is upon them,
and the face of the earth is dusty and ugly.
Every thing with taste and colour has changed,
and the radiance of the beautiful face has diminished.
Qabil made Habil taste death, so alas for my grief! The fair one has perished.
Why should I not pour out tears, while Habil is contained in the grave?
Killing the son of the prophet without any crime,
my heart is wounded beside his heart.
I see the length of life as a sorrow to me,
and am I at rest from my life?
We have neighbours, an enemy that does not perish,
so that we would rest if he died.
Leave off complaining, for both have perished,
by one who perished, not for a worthy price.
What use is weeping to those who weep,
when a man has been buried in the grave?
So weep for yourself, and leave its desires,
for you will not be immortal after the sacrificed one.

Then Iblis answered him in the middle of the night, gloating:

Withdraw from the lands and their inhabitants,
O youth, for the wide Paradise has grown narrow for you.
You were in it with your wife in ease,
and your heart was at rest from the harms of the world.
My plots and my deceit did not cease
until the goodly Paradise escaped you.
Had it not been for the mercy of the Almighty, there would have arisen
from your palm a wind from the gardens of Paradise. [[Tarikh Baghdad, with variations: 5/336, biography no. 2868.]]

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd said: When Habil was killed, Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) remained for only one hundred years. Then he came, and it was said to him: May God welcome you and make you laugh (bayyaka), that is, make you laugh. When Adam's age had reached one hundred and thirty years, which was five years after the killing of Habil, Hawwa' bore him Shith. His name means "gift of God", meaning that he was a replacement for Habil. God taught him the hours of the night and the day, and informed him of the worship of creation in each hour. He sent down to him the Gift of God (Hibat Allah), and he became Adam's successor (wasi) and heir to his covenant (waliy ʿahdih), peace be upon them both. As for Qabil, it was said to him: Go, a fugitive and vagrant, terrified and feared, and no one who sees you will feel safe. He took his sister Hibat Allah by the hand and went with her to Aden in the land of Yemen. Iblis came to him and said: The fire consumed Habil's offering only because he used to worship fire and serve it. So you set up a fire that will belong to you and your descendants. He set up a fire, and he was the first to set up a fire and worship it.

They said: Whenever any of his offspring passed by him, he would shoot at them. Then a blind descendant of Qabil approached, with a son of his. The blind man said: This is your father, Qabil. Then Qabil's son shot the blind man and killed him. The blind man's son said: You have killed your father! He raised his hand and struck his son, and he died. The blind man said: Woe to me! I killed my father with my shot, and I killed my son with my slap.

Mujahid said: One of Qabil's legs was tied to his thigh and calf, and he remains tied so until the Day of Resurrection. His face was turned toward the sun, which revolved around him, and in summer it was surrounded by a fence of fire, and in winter by a fence of ice.

They said: The offspring of Qabil made musical instruments of reed pipes, lutes, flutes, lutes ('idan) and drums (tanabir). They became immersed in amusement, drinking wine, worshipping fire, fornication and abominations, until God, the Mighty and Majestic, sent the Flood upon them in the days of Nuh (ʿalayhi al-salam), and the line of Shith survived.

ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: We find that the murderous son of Adam shares the punishment of the people of the Fire in a correct division: the punishment upon him is half of their punishment.

Al-Aʿmash related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murra, from Masruq ibn ʿAbd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No soul is killed unjustly except that a portion of its blood falls upon the first son of Adam, because he was the first to establish killing." [52]

Muslim ibn ʿAbd Allah related from Saʿid ibn Sur, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about Tuesday, and he said: "It is a day of blood." They said: How is that, O Messenger of God? He said: "On it Hawwa' menstruated, and the son of Adam was killed by his brother." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/140.]] [53]

And on the authority of Yahya ibn Zuhdam, who said: My father related to me from his father, from Anas, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, bestowed three favours upon the son of Adam, one after another: the wind after the spirit, for if the wind did not come after the spirit, no beloved would be buried by a beloved. And the worm in the grain, for if the worm did not come into the grain, kings would hoard it, and it would be more valuable to them than gold and silver. And death after old age, for a man grows old until he wearies of himself, and his family, children and relatives weary of him, and so death is easier for him." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/142.]] [54]

﴿Because of that﴾, that is, because of that killer and his savagery. It is said: "ajala fulan ya'jalu ajalan", like "akhadha yakhudhu akhdhan" (he committed an offence).

The poet said:
"And the people of a tent that is righteous among themselves,
they have fought over a matter I am postponing."
[[Al-Sihah: 4/1621.]]

﴿We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, not in retaliation for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾. Its meaning is His word: ﴿The recompense of those who wage war against God and His Messenger is only...﴾ [the verse], ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾.

Mujahid: People differed about it. Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of ʿIkrima and ʿAtiyya, said: Whoever kills a prophet or a just imam, ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾, and whoever assists a prophet or a just imam, ﴿it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾.

Mujahid: Whoever kills a soul that is sacred, he will burn in the Fire for killing it, just as he would burn if he had killed all people. And whoever preserves it, by refraining from killing it, has preserved all people. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/273.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 27–32 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Suddi: "Whoever kills..." — ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾ — in the sense of the sin borne by the one who is killed. ﴿And whoever gives it life﴾ — that is, rescues it from destruction, such as drowning, burning, collapse, or other such things — ﴿it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾ in the sense of the one who is rescued.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾ means that he is liable to retaliation (qisas) for killing it, equal to what he intended in his heart, had he killed all mankind. ﴿And whoever gives it life﴾ means one who pardons the person against whom retaliation was due to him, and does not kill him. ﴿It is as if he had given life to all mankind.﴾

Qatadah and al-Dahhak: The meaning, whether the Almighty's killing of it is great or its burden is great, is that whoever deems it lawful to kill a Muslim without right ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾, because they are not safe from him. ﴿And whoever gives it life﴾ — who holds it sacred and refrains from killing it — ﴿it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾, because they are safe from him.

Sulayman ibn Ali al-Rab'i said: I said to al-Hasan, "O Abu Sa'id, it applies to us as it applied to the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes, by the One besides whom there is no god, the blood of the Children of Israel is more honoured before God than our blood."

﴿And certainly Our messengers came to them with clear proofs; then, after that, many of them were indeed transgressors in the land.﴾

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated from al-Zayyat ibn Amr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives water to a believer who is thirsty [[In the source: a believer a sip of water while water is available.]] it is as if he freed seventy slaves, and whoever gives water in a place where it is not available, it is as if he gave life to a soul. ﴿And whoever gives it life, it is as if he had given life to all mankind.﴾"

[[Dhikr akhbar Isfahan: 1/197.]] [55]

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verses 33–40 (part 1 of 2):

[Verse 33] "The only recompense for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger..." etc.

Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning a group of the People of the Book who had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They broke the covenant, cut off the road, and spread corruption on earth.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning the people of Hilal ibn Uwaymir. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a truce with Hilal ibn Uwaymir, who was Abu Burda al-Aslami, on the condition that he would not aid against him, nor aid anyone against him, and that whoever among the Muslims came to him would not be harmed.

He said: A group from Banu Kinanah, wishing to embrace Islam, passed by some people of Hilal's tribe, and Hilal was not present at that time. They attacked them, killed them, and seized their property. When this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with the ruling concerning them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It was revealed concerning some people of 'Uraynah and Ghatafan who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and pledged allegiance to him for Islam, while they were liars and did not truly desire Islam. Then they said: "We find Madinah unhealthy, for our bellies have swelled and our complexions have turned yellow." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Go out to our milch camels and drink their urine and milk." [[See al-Musannaf: 5/456, and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/225. And Jami' al-Bayan: 6/281, 283.]] [56] So they went, killed the herdsmen, and drove off the camels. They apostatized from Islam. Then it was proclaimed among the people: "O cavalry of Allah, mount up!" So they mounted, without a rider waiting for another, and set out in pursuit of them. They were brought back, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that their hands and feet be cut off, their eyes be branded with hot iron, and they were left in the heat until they died.

Then they differed regarding the ruling of the two verses. Some of them said: It has been abrogated, because mutilation is not permitted, and drinking camel urine is not permitted.

Others said: The ruling stands, except for the branding of the eyes and mutilation. Al-Layth ibn Sa'd said: This verse was revealed as a rebuke to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and as his instruction regarding their punishment, so He said: "Their recompense is only this," meaning the mutilation. [57]

For this reason, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood to deliver a sermon, he forbade mutilation.

They differed regarding who is the muharib (one who wages war) who deserves this punishment.

Some said: He is the highwayman who cuts off the road, and the one who openly commits robbery in the cities, and who bears arms against the Muslims and targets them in any place, including by ghilah (treacherous ambush), which is when a man deceives a man, a woman, or a child, takes him into a house, and betrays him, then kills him and takes his property. This is the view of al-Awza'i, Malik, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah, and al-Shafi'i.

Others said: He is only the highway robber (qati' al-tariq); as for the one who openly commits robbery, he is not a muharib. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions.

"And they strive in the land to cause corruption": by corruption, meaning by fornication and murder, destruction of crops and offspring.

"That they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be banished." They differed regarding the ruling of this verse.

A group said: The Imam has the choice regarding them; whichever of these he wills, he may carry out. This is the view of al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Nakha'i, Mujahid, and a narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas.

They argued with His saying, "then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice" [[Surah al-Baqarah: 196.]] and with His saying concerning the expiation for oaths, "then its expiation is feeding ten needy persons with the average of what you feed your families" [[Surah al-Ma'idah: 89.]], and so on.

Others said: This is a ruling that varies according to the crime. If he killed, he is killed; if he killed and took property, he is killed and crucified; if he took property without killing, his hand and foot are cut off on opposite sides; if he terrorized the road without killing and took property, he is banished.

This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Nakha'i, and al-Rabi'. And it is a narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of banishment (nafy). Ibn 'Abbas said: It is the ruling for one who escapes you; if he has eluded you so that you cannot reach him, and he leaves whoever encounters him, he is to be killed.

Others said: [the banishment applies to] the one who is seized. Then they differed about its meaning. A group said: It is that he be expelled from his town to another town other than it. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i.

Others said, and al-Hasan (said), and this is the view of Abu Hanifah. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: It is that he be expelled from his land to another, and imprisoned in the prison of the town to which he was exiled until his repentance becomes evident. This is the preferred view, and it is supported by what Ibn Wahb narrated from Abu Sayfah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that Habban ibn Shurayh wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: "Some people from the Copts had evidence established against them that they waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the land with corruption, and that Allah says: 'The only recompense for those who wage war against Allah...' up to His saying 'on opposite sides.' He was silent about the banishment. So if the Commander of the Faithful sees fit to carry out the decree of Allah concerning them, let him write accordingly." When Umar read his letter, he said: "Habban has become bold." Then he wrote: "Your letter reached me and I understood it. You have become bold when you wrote about the beginning of the verse and remained silent about its end, wishing to embolden yourself to killing and crucifixion. You are a servant of the Banu 'Aqil," meaning al-Hajjaj, "for Allah says 'or be banished' at the end of the verse. If evidence was established against them, then put iron around their necks and banish them to a mountain pass or a dwelling." The root of nafy is expulsion.

Aws ibn Hajar said:
"They are banished from the paths of the noble, as the wild rice (?) is expelled ..." 
meaning what is adjacent to it is the qurd, which is inferior wool. From this comes the saying that inferior dirhams are nafayah (dross), and what is spattered of water from a bucket is nafy.

The rajaz poet said:
"As if his two flanks, from the nafy, were the places where birds alight upon a rock."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 8/404, and Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/59.]]

"That is for them a disgrace" — that is, the punishment and humiliation — "in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment." Then He said: "Except those who repent before you have power over them."

Most scholars said: Except those who repent from their shirk, their waging of war, and their corruption, and believe and do righteous deeds, before you have power over them. Then there is no way against them with any of the penalties mentioned by Allah in this verse, for anything they did in the state of their disbelief, whether concerning property, blood, or sanctity. This is the ruling for polytheists and combatants.

As for Muslims who wage war, they differed concerning them.

Some said: By their repentance before they are captured, the divine penalty (hadd) falls from them, but the rights of the children of Adam are not dropped by it. This is the view of al-Shafi'i.

Some said: All of that falls from them, and nothing is taken from their property, except that if a particular property is found in their possession, it is returned to its owner. And if a victim's guardian (wali al-dam) seeks retaliation for a killing, and evidence is established regarding it, he is subjected to qisas. As for the blood and property they took which the victims' heirs did not pursue, the Imam does not pursue it. This is the view of Malik, al-Awza'i, and al-Layth ibn Sa'd.

Some said: If he seeks safe conduct from our authorities before he is taken, Allah accepts his repentance, and he is not held to account for any of the crimes that preceded it, so no one has any claim against him regarding blood or property. This is the view of al-Suddi, which supports it.

Al-Sha'bi narrated that Harithah ibn Yazid went out waging war in the time of Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), terrorizing the roads, shedding blood, and taking property. Then he came repentant before he was captured, and went to al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and asked him to intercede for him with safe conduct. He went to Ibn Ja'far, and he went to Sa'id ibn Qays al-Hamdani, who kissed him and embraced him. When Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) had prayed the morning prayer, Sa'id ibn Qays came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger?" He said: "That they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be banished from the land." He said: "What do you say about one who repents before you have power over him?" He said: "I say as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Except those who repent before you have power over them,' the verse."

Sa'id said: "Even if it is Harithah ibn Badr?" He said: "Yes." So he came to him, pledged allegiance to him, granted him safe conduct, and wrote for him a public letter of amnesty.

Then Harithah said:
"Ah, convey to Hamdan, if you meet them, at a distance, that no enemy who finds fault with them is safe.
By the life of their father, indeed Hamdan fears God, and their orator judges by the Book."
[[Jami' al-Bayan: 6/302.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa, who was governor of Kufa in the days of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), after he had prayed the obligatory prayer, and said: "O Abu Musa, this is the station of one who seeks refuge in you. I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so, the Mahdi. I waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the land, and I have repented before he has power over me." Abu Musa stood and said: "This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, who waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the land with corruption, but he has repented before he was captured. Whoever meets him should not approach him except with good; if he is truthful, his path is the path of one who is truthful, and if he is lying, his sins will overtake him." The man stayed, then asked permission and went out, and Allah overtook him with his sins and he was killed.

Al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq that Ali al-Asadi waged war, terrorized the road, and caused bloodshed and the taking of property. The rulers and the common people sought him, but he eluded them and they could not capture him until he came repentant. That was because he heard a man reciting this verse: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves..." [[Surah al-Zumar: 53.]] He stopped beside him and said: "O servant of Allah, repeat it." He repeated it to him, so he sheathed his sword and came repentant, arriving at Madinah at dawn. Then he bathed, went to the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and prayed the dawn prayer. Then he went to Abu Hurayrah, who was among his companions. When he asked forgiveness, people recognized him and stood up to him. He said: "You have no way against me; I came repentant before you could overpower me."

Abu Hurayrah said: "He is right," and took him by the hand until they came to Marwan ibn al-Hakam during his governorship of Madinah in the time of Mu'awiyah. He said: "This is Ali; he came repentant, and you have no way against him," and he was left alone. Ali went out repentant, striving in the way of Allah at sea. They encountered the Romans, and he brought a ship close to their ship. He stormed onto the Romans' ship; they fled to its other side, so it tilted, and he overturned it upon them, and they all drowned. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/304.]]

[Verse 35] "O you who believe, fear Allah and seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him..." — that is, seek nearness to Him. Al-wasilah, in its original sense, is that by which one reaches a thing and draws near to it; one says "wasala ilayhi wasilah" and "tawassala." Its plural is wasa'il.

The poet said:
"When the slanderers are heedless, we return to our union, and the purity between us and the means of approach return."
[[Jami' al-Bayan: 6/308.]]

'Ata' said: Al-wasilah is the highest rank of Paradise.

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-wasilah is the highest rank of Paradise."
[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/327.]] [58]

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah for al-wasilah for me, for it is the highest rank in Paradise, which none attains except one servant, and I hope that I am he."
[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/162, with variation; and Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/327.]] [59]

Sa'id ibn Tarif narrated from al-Asma'i, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: "In Paradise there are two pearls at the bottom of the Throne. One is white and the other yellow; each contains seventy thousand chambers whose doors and cups are of one vein. The white one, called al-Wasilah, belongs to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his household, and the yellow one belongs to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his household." [60] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/56.]]

[Verse 36] "Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is on earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves with it from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment."

It is narrated from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It will be said to the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection: 'Would you, if you had the earth full of gold, ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' It will be said: 'You were asked for something easier than that.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/291.]] "They wish to come out of the Fire" — the general readers recite it with a fatha on the ya', as in His saying, "and they will not come out of it, and for them is a lasting punishment."

Abu Waqidah and al-Jarrah recited yukhrajuna with a damma on the ya', as in His saying, "Our Lord, bring us out of it," "and they will not be brought out of it."

[Verse 38] "As for the thief, male and female, cut off their hands..." The verse was revealed concerning Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, the thief of the coat of mail, and his story has passed in Surah al-Nisa'.

As for the reason for their being in the nominative: some said it is nominative as the subject of an inceptive (mubtada'), with its predicate following. Others said it is in the sense of a conditional (jaza'), its meaning being: whoever steals, cut off their hands... and the adulterer, flog each one of them a hundred lashes. If he had intended a specific thief and a specific adulterer, the construction would be in the accusative.

Al-Akhfash said: It is nominative as a predicate of an omitted inceptive, as if he said: "Of what is related to you and revealed to you: 'And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands.'"

Abu 'Ubaydah said: It is nominative according to the dialect of those who say... [text unreadable]... as in "the game is at its hunter's disposal," and "the crescent has risen, so look at it," meaning: the game is available to you, and the crescent has risen, so look at it.

'Isa ibn 'Amr recited "wa-l-sariqa wa-l-sariqata" in the accusative, on the supposition of an implied "iqta'u" (cut off) the thief and the thief-woman.

The evidence for the nominative is the reading of Abdullah: "And the thieves, male and female, cut off their right hands."

There is disagreement concerning the thief whom Allah means by cutting off his hand, and concerning the amount for which a thief's hand is cut.

Some said: He is cut if he steals ten dirhams or more, and is not cut for less than that. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions. They argued with what Ata' and Mujahid narrated from Ayman ibn Umm Ayman: "The thief's hand is cut for the value of a shield, and the value of a shield in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a dinar or ten dirhams."

Ayyub ibn Musa narrated from Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas: "The value of a shield in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was ten dirhams."

'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman narrated from Ata': "The lowest value of a shield is ten dirhams."

Sulayman ibn Yasar said: "The hand is not cut for less than five."

And he cited what Sufyan narrated from Abdullah: that the Prophet (ﷺ) cut off a hand for the value of five dirhams. [62]

Sufyan narrated from 'Isa from al-Sha'bi from Abdullah that the Prophet (ﷺ) cut off a hand for five dirhams.

Shu'bah narrated from Dawud ibn [Farahij], who said: "I heard Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: 'The hand is cut for four dirhams or more, and is not cut for three dirhams or less.'"

And he argued with what was narrated from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut off a thief's hand for a shield worth three dirhams.

Others said: The hand is cut for a quarter dinar or more. This is the view of al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, Ishaq al-Handhali, and Abu Thawr. They argued with what Sufyan narrated from al-Zuhri, from Hamzah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It is cut for a quarter dinar or more." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/335.]] [63]

And Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad narrated from Umar, from Aisha, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The thief's hand is not cut except for a quarter dinar or more.'" [[Sahih Muslim: 5/112.]] [64]

Others said: The hand of a thief is cut for little or much, even if he steals a dang (a sixth of a dirham). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Because the verse is general, not specific." And the saying of al-Zubayr: it is narrated that he is cut for a dirham. The evidence for this position is what al-A'mash narrated from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah curses the thief who steals an egg and has his hand cut off, and steals a rope and has his hand cut off." [[Sahih Muslim: 5/113; Musnad Ahmad: 2/253.]] [65]

And Thawban narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a thief who had stolen a cloak. He said: "Did you steal? I do not think you stole." He said: "Yes." He said: "Take him and cut him off, then bring him back to me." He did so, and he said: "Woe to you, repent to Allah." [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/248.]] [66]

He said: "O Allah, accept his repentance."

Then they differed concerning the manner of the cutting. 'Amr ibn Dinar said: The Prophet (ﷺ) would cut the hand from the wrist; and it was cut from the joint; and Ali would cut the palm from the fingers and the foot from the middle of the sole.

If he is cut and then returns to theft, is he cut again or not? The people of Kufa said: He is not cut. They argued with the hadith of 'Abd Khayr, who said: Ali was brought a thief, so he cut off his hand; then he was brought back, and he cut off his foot; then he was brought back, and he beat him and imprisoned him, and said: "I am ashamed to leave him no hand with which to cleanse himself, nor a foot with which to walk."

The people of the Hijaz said: He is cut. They argued for this with His saying, "then cut off their hands," as an agreed consensus.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 33–40 (part 2 of 2):

Ḥammād ibn Salama narrates from Yūsuf ibn Saʿd, from al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥāṭib, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought a thief, and he said: "Kill him." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, he only stole." He said: "Kill him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he only stole." He said: "Cut off his hand." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 8/89.]] [67]

He said: Then he stole again, and his foot was cut off. Then he stole during the time of Abū Bakr, until all of his limbs were cut off. Then he stole a fifth time, and Abū Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knew better about this when he said, 'Kill him.'" Then they handed him over to a clan of Quraysh to kill him, during the time of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, and he loved leadership. He said: "Appoint me as your leader," so they appointed him over them. Whenever he was struck, they struck him until they killed him.

Then, if the thief's hand is cut off, is he also required to pay back the stolen goods or not? Sufyān and the people of Kufa said: If the thief's hand is cut off, he is not required to pay for it, unless he returns the stolen item to its owner.

Al-Muswir ibn Ibrāhīm narrates from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The owner of stolen goods shall not be made to pay when the prescribed punishment is carried out." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 8/93.]] [68] It was said: This is a mursal ḥadīth. Anas ibn Mālik and al-Zuhrī and Mālik said: If the thief is wealthy, he must pay.

Al-Shāfiʿī said: Then he must pay the value of the stolen goods, whether he is poor or wealthy.

﴿As a recompense for what they earned﴾. The word jazāʾan is in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), and the verb "cut off" (al-qaṭʿ) — this is what al-Kisāʾī said. Qaṭrub said: it is in the accusative as an infinitive of cause (maṣdar), and similarly nakālan, meaning a punishment from Allah. ﴿And Allah is Mighty, Wise﴾.

From Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, who said: I heard my father say: "No thief steals a theft except that it diminishes from his provision that was decreed for him."

﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing﴾, meaning his theft. Its parallel in Surah Yūsuf is ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ [[Surah Yusuf: 75.]], meaning the thieves. ﴿And makes amends, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness﴾. This is what is between him and Allah the Exalted. As for the amputation, it is obligatory. This is shown by what

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrates from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥanbalī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: A woman stole during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and those whom she had stolen from brought her. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, this woman stole from us." Her people said: "We will ransom her for five hundred dinars." The Messenger of Allah said: "Cut off her hand." Her right hand was cut off. The woman said: "Is there repentance for me?" He said: "Yes, today you are as free of your sin as the day your mother bore you." [[Musnad Aḥmad: 2/177.]] [69] So Allah revealed in Surah al-Mā'ida: ﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and makes amends﴾, the verse.

Maʿmar narrates from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: A woman of the Makhzūm clan used to borrow goods and deny them, so the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered her hand to be cut off. Her family came to Usāma and spoke to him, and Usāma spoke to the Prophet (ﷺ) about her. The Prophet said to him: "O Usāma, do you intercede concerning one of the prescribed punishments of Allah?" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) stood to deliver a sermon and said: "Those before you were destroyed because when a noble person among them stole, they let him go, and when a weak person among them stole, they cut off his hand. By Him in whose hand is my soul, even if Fāṭima bint Muḥammad had stolen, I would cut off her hand." [[Sunan al-Dārimī: 2/173.]] [70]

He said: So he cut off the hand of the Makhzūmī woman.

Al-Shaʿbī and ʿAṭāʾ used to say: If he returns the stolen goods before he is caught, the hand is not cut off, based on His saying: ﴿Except those who repent before you have power over them﴾, the verse. ﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills.﴾

Al-Suddī and al-Kalbī said: ﴿He punishes whom He wills﴾ refers to those among them who died in their disbelief, and ﴿forgives whom He wills﴾ refers to those who repented from their disbelief.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿He punishes whom He wills﴾ refers to the minor offense when it is established against him, and ﴿forgives whom He wills﴾ refers to the major offense when he desists from it. ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verses 33–40 (part 1 of 2):

[Verse 33] "The only recompense for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger..." etc.

Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning a group of the People of the Book who had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They broke the covenant, cut off the road, and spread corruption on earth.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning the people of Hilal ibn Uwaymir. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a truce with Hilal ibn Uwaymir, who was Abu Burda al-Aslami, on the condition that he would not aid against him, nor aid anyone against him, and that whoever among the Muslims came to him would not be harmed.

He said: A group from Banu Kinanah, wishing to embrace Islam, passed by some people of Hilal's tribe, and Hilal was not present at that time. They attacked them, killed them, and seized their property. When this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with the ruling concerning them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It was revealed concerning some people of 'Uraynah and Ghatafan who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and pledged allegiance to him for Islam, while they were liars and did not truly desire Islam. Then they said: "We find Madinah unhealthy, for our bellies have swelled and our complexions have turned yellow." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Go out to our milch camels and drink their urine and milk." [[See al-Musannaf: 5/456, and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/225. And Jami' al-Bayan: 6/281, 283.]] [56] So they went, killed the herdsmen, and drove off the camels. They apostatized from Islam. Then it was proclaimed among the people: "O cavalry of Allah, mount up!" So they mounted, without a rider waiting for another, and set out in pursuit of them. They were brought back, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that their hands and feet be cut off, their eyes be branded with hot iron, and they were left in the heat until they died.

Then they differed regarding the ruling of the two verses. Some of them said: It has been abrogated, because mutilation is not permitted, and drinking camel urine is not permitted.

Others said: The ruling stands, except for the branding of the eyes and mutilation. Al-Layth ibn Sa'd said: This verse was revealed as a rebuke to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and as his instruction regarding their punishment, so He said: "Their recompense is only this," meaning the mutilation. [57]

For this reason, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood to deliver a sermon, he forbade mutilation.

They differed regarding who is the muharib (one who wages war) who deserves this punishment.

Some said: He is the highwayman who cuts off the road, and the one who openly commits robbery in the cities, and who bears arms against the Muslims and targets them in any place, including by ghilah (treacherous ambush), which is when a man deceives a man, a woman, or a child, takes him into a house, and betrays him, then kills him and takes his property. This is the view of al-Awza'i, Malik, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah, and al-Shafi'i.

Others said: He is only the highway robber (qati' al-tariq); as for the one who openly commits robbery, he is not a muharib. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions.

"And they strive in the land to cause corruption": by corruption, meaning by fornication and murder, destruction of crops and offspring.

"That they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be banished." They differed regarding the ruling of this verse.

A group said: The Imam has the choice regarding them; whichever of these he wills, he may carry out. This is the view of al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Nakha'i, Mujahid, and a narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas.

They argued with His saying, "then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice" [[Surah al-Baqarah: 196.]] and with His saying concerning the expiation for oaths, "then its expiation is feeding ten needy persons with the average of what you feed your families" [[Surah al-Ma'idah: 89.]], and so on.

Others said: This is a ruling that varies according to the crime. If he killed, he is killed; if he killed and took property, he is killed and crucified; if he took property without killing, his hand and foot are cut off on opposite sides; if he terrorized the road without killing and took property, he is banished.

This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Nakha'i, and al-Rabi'. And it is a narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of banishment (nafy). Ibn 'Abbas said: It is the ruling for one who escapes you; if he has eluded you so that you cannot reach him, and he leaves whoever encounters him, he is to be killed.

Others said: [the banishment applies to] the one who is seized. Then they differed about its meaning. A group said: It is that he be expelled from his town to another town other than it. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i.

Others said, and al-Hasan (said), and this is the view of Abu Hanifah. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: It is that he be expelled from his land to another, and imprisoned in the prison of the town to which he was exiled until his repentance becomes evident. This is the preferred view, and it is supported by what Ibn Wahb narrated from Abu Sayfah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that Habban ibn Shurayh wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: "Some people from the Copts had evidence established against them that they waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the land with corruption, and that Allah says: 'The only recompense for those who wage war against Allah...' up to His saying 'on opposite sides.' He was silent about the banishment. So if the Commander of the Faithful sees fit to carry out the decree of Allah concerning them, let him write accordingly." When Umar read his letter, he said: "Habban has become bold." Then he wrote: "Your letter reached me and I understood it. You have become bold when you wrote about the beginning of the verse and remained silent about its end, wishing to embolden yourself to killing and crucifixion. You are a servant of the Banu 'Aqil," meaning al-Hajjaj, "for Allah says 'or be banished' at the end of the verse. If evidence was established against them, then put iron around their necks and banish them to a mountain pass or a dwelling." The root of nafy is expulsion.

Aws ibn Hajar said:
"They are banished from the paths of the noble, as the wild rice (?) is expelled ..." 
meaning what is adjacent to it is the qurd, which is inferior wool. From this comes the saying that inferior dirhams are nafayah (dross), and what is spattered of water from a bucket is nafy.

The rajaz poet said:
"As if his two flanks, from the nafy, were the places where birds alight upon a rock."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 8/404, and Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/59.]]

"That is for them a disgrace" — that is, the punishment and humiliation — "in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment." Then He said: "Except those who repent before you have power over them."

Most scholars said: Except those who repent from their shirk, their waging of war, and their corruption, and believe and do righteous deeds, before you have power over them. Then there is no way against them with any of the penalties mentioned by Allah in this verse, for anything they did in the state of their disbelief, whether concerning property, blood, or sanctity. This is the ruling for polytheists and combatants.

As for Muslims who wage war, they differed concerning them.

Some said: By their repentance before they are captured, the divine penalty (hadd) falls from them, but the rights of the children of Adam are not dropped by it. This is the view of al-Shafi'i.

Some said: All of that falls from them, and nothing is taken from their property, except that if a particular property is found in their possession, it is returned to its owner. And if a victim's guardian (wali al-dam) seeks retaliation for a killing, and evidence is established regarding it, he is subjected to qisas. As for the blood and property they took which the victims' heirs did not pursue, the Imam does not pursue it. This is the view of Malik, al-Awza'i, and al-Layth ibn Sa'd.

Some said: If he seeks safe conduct from our authorities before he is taken, Allah accepts his repentance, and he is not held to account for any of the crimes that preceded it, so no one has any claim against him regarding blood or property. This is the view of al-Suddi, which supports it.

Al-Sha'bi narrated that Harithah ibn Yazid went out waging war in the time of Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), terrorizing the roads, shedding blood, and taking property. Then he came repentant before he was captured, and went to al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and asked him to intercede for him with safe conduct. He went to Ibn Ja'far, and he went to Sa'id ibn Qays al-Hamdani, who kissed him and embraced him. When Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) had prayed the morning prayer, Sa'id ibn Qays came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger?" He said: "That they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be banished from the land." He said: "What do you say about one who repents before you have power over him?" He said: "I say as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Except those who repent before you have power over them,' the verse."

Sa'id said: "Even if it is Harithah ibn Badr?" He said: "Yes." So he came to him, pledged allegiance to him, granted him safe conduct, and wrote for him a public letter of amnesty.

Then Harithah said:
"Ah, convey to Hamdan, if you meet them, at a distance, that no enemy who finds fault with them is safe.
By the life of their father, indeed Hamdan fears God, and their orator judges by the Book."
[[Jami' al-Bayan: 6/302.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa, who was governor of Kufa in the days of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), after he had prayed the obligatory prayer, and said: "O Abu Musa, this is the station of one who seeks refuge in you. I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so, the Mahdi. I waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the land, and I have repented before he has power over me." Abu Musa stood and said: "This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, who waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the land with corruption, but he has repented before he was captured. Whoever meets him should not approach him except with good; if he is truthful, his path is the path of one who is truthful, and if he is lying, his sins will overtake him." The man stayed, then asked permission and went out, and Allah overtook him with his sins and he was killed.

Al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq that Ali al-Asadi waged war, terrorized the road, and caused bloodshed and the taking of property. The rulers and the common people sought him, but he eluded them and they could not capture him until he came repentant. That was because he heard a man reciting this verse: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves..." [[Surah al-Zumar: 53.]] He stopped beside him and said: "O servant of Allah, repeat it." He repeated it to him, so he sheathed his sword and came repentant, arriving at Madinah at dawn. Then he bathed, went to the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and prayed the dawn prayer. Then he went to Abu Hurayrah, who was among his companions. When he asked forgiveness, people recognized him and stood up to him. He said: "You have no way against me; I came repentant before you could overpower me."

Abu Hurayrah said: "He is right," and took him by the hand until they came to Marwan ibn al-Hakam during his governorship of Madinah in the time of Mu'awiyah. He said: "This is Ali; he came repentant, and you have no way against him," and he was left alone. Ali went out repentant, striving in the way of Allah at sea. They encountered the Romans, and he brought a ship close to their ship. He stormed onto the Romans' ship; they fled to its other side, so it tilted, and he overturned it upon them, and they all drowned. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/304.]]

[Verse 35] "O you who believe, fear Allah and seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him..." — that is, seek nearness to Him. Al-wasilah, in its original sense, is that by which one reaches a thing and draws near to it; one says "wasala ilayhi wasilah" and "tawassala." Its plural is wasa'il.

The poet said:
"When the slanderers are heedless, we return to our union, and the purity between us and the means of approach return."
[[Jami' al-Bayan: 6/308.]]

'Ata' said: Al-wasilah is the highest rank of Paradise.

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-wasilah is the highest rank of Paradise."
[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/327.]] [58]

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah for al-wasilah for me, for it is the highest rank in Paradise, which none attains except one servant, and I hope that I am he."
[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/162, with variation; and Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/327.]] [59]

Sa'id ibn Tarif narrated from al-Asma'i, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: "In Paradise there are two pearls at the bottom of the Throne. One is white and the other yellow; each contains seventy thousand chambers whose doors and cups are of one vein. The white one, called al-Wasilah, belongs to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his household, and the yellow one belongs to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his household." [60] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/56.]]

[Verse 36] "Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is on earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves with it from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment."

It is narrated from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It will be said to the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection: 'Would you, if you had the earth full of gold, ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' It will be said: 'You were asked for something easier than that.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/291.]] "They wish to come out of the Fire" — the general readers recite it with a fatha on the ya', as in His saying, "and they will not come out of it, and for them is a lasting punishment."

Abu Waqidah and al-Jarrah recited yukhrajuna with a damma on the ya', as in His saying, "Our Lord, bring us out of it," "and they will not be brought out of it."

[Verse 38] "As for the thief, male and female, cut off their hands..." The verse was revealed concerning Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, the thief of the coat of mail, and his story has passed in Surah al-Nisa'.

As for the reason for their being in the nominative: some said it is nominative as the subject of an inceptive (mubtada'), with its predicate following. Others said it is in the sense of a conditional (jaza'), its meaning being: whoever steals, cut off their hands... and the adulterer, flog each one of them a hundred lashes. If he had intended a specific thief and a specific adulterer, the construction would be in the accusative.

Al-Akhfash said: It is nominative as a predicate of an omitted inceptive, as if he said: "Of what is related to you and revealed to you: 'And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands.'"

Abu 'Ubaydah said: It is nominative according to the dialect of those who say... [text unreadable]... as in "the game is at its hunter's disposal," and "the crescent has risen, so look at it," meaning: the game is available to you, and the crescent has risen, so look at it.

'Isa ibn 'Amr recited "wa-l-sariqa wa-l-sariqata" in the accusative, on the supposition of an implied "iqta'u" (cut off) the thief and the thief-woman.

The evidence for the nominative is the reading of Abdullah: "And the thieves, male and female, cut off their right hands."

There is disagreement concerning the thief whom Allah means by cutting off his hand, and concerning the amount for which a thief's hand is cut.

Some said: He is cut if he steals ten dirhams or more, and is not cut for less than that. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions. They argued with what Ata' and Mujahid narrated from Ayman ibn Umm Ayman: "The thief's hand is cut for the value of a shield, and the value of a shield in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a dinar or ten dirhams."

Ayyub ibn Musa narrated from Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas: "The value of a shield in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was ten dirhams."

'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman narrated from Ata': "The lowest value of a shield is ten dirhams."

Sulayman ibn Yasar said: "The hand is not cut for less than five."

And he cited what Sufyan narrated from Abdullah: that the Prophet (ﷺ) cut off a hand for the value of five dirhams. [62]

Sufyan narrated from 'Isa from al-Sha'bi from Abdullah that the Prophet (ﷺ) cut off a hand for five dirhams.

Shu'bah narrated from Dawud ibn [Farahij], who said: "I heard Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: 'The hand is cut for four dirhams or more, and is not cut for three dirhams or less.'"

And he argued with what was narrated from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut off a thief's hand for a shield worth three dirhams.

Others said: The hand is cut for a quarter dinar or more. This is the view of al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, Ishaq al-Handhali, and Abu Thawr. They argued with what Sufyan narrated from al-Zuhri, from Hamzah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It is cut for a quarter dinar or more." [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/335.]] [63]

And Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad narrated from Umar, from Aisha, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The thief's hand is not cut except for a quarter dinar or more.'" [[Sahih Muslim: 5/112.]] [64]

Others said: The hand of a thief is cut for little or much, even if he steals a dang (a sixth of a dirham). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Because the verse is general, not specific." And the saying of al-Zubayr: it is narrated that he is cut for a dirham. The evidence for this position is what al-A'mash narrated from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah curses the thief who steals an egg and has his hand cut off, and steals a rope and has his hand cut off."
