He said to him: "You have spoken truly. Your affair is the affair of a prophet." Ibn Suriya then embraced Islam and said: "O Muhammad, which of the angels comes to you?" He said: "Jibril."

He said: "Describe him to me." The Prophet (ﷺ) described him to him, and he said: "I testify that he is in the Torah as you have said, and that you are truly the Messenger of Allah." When Ibn Suriya embraced Islam, the Jews attacked him and reviled him. When they wanted to rise, the Banu Qurayzah clung to the Banu Nadir, and said: "O Muhammad, our brothers the Banu Nadir: our father is one, our religion is one, our prophet is one. If they kill one of us, they do not pay us blood-money but give us its diya of seventy wasq of dates; and if we kill one of them, they kill the killer and take from us double: one hundred and forty wasq of dates. If the victim is a woman, they pay for her with a man; and for a man of theirs, two men of ours; and for a slave of theirs, a free man of ours; and our wounds are half of their wounds." Judge between us and them. Allah the Exalted then revealed concerning the stoning and retaliation: "O Messenger, let not those grieve you who race to disbelief, of those who say with their mouths 'We believe' but whose hearts have not believed, and of those who are Jews, listeners for falsehood" (Qur'an 5:41).

The predicate is governed by the particle of relation: "and of those who are Jews" (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا), so they are "listeners for falsehood." If you wish, you may take it as the predicate of an implied subject, meaning they are "listeners for falsehood." It was also said that the lam means "to" (إلى).

Abu Hatim used to say: the lam in "lil-kadhib" (للكذب) is the lam of purpose: "they listen in order to lie about you." The lam in His saying "li-qawmin akharin" is the lam of cause: "for the sake of other people, who did not come to you," namely the people of Khaybar. "They distort the words (al-kalim), the plural of kalimah, from their places (min ba'di mawadi'ihi)," that is, after their placement in their proper positions, like His saying: "But righteousness is in one who fears Allah" (Qur'an 2:177). He mentioned writing only as a return to the wording, which is al-kalim.

Ali read: "yuharrifuna al-kalama min ba'di mawadi'ihi."

"They say: If you are given this, then take it" (Qur'an 5:41), meaning: if Muhammad gives you a ruling of flogging and stoning, accept it; "and if you are not given it, then beware." "Whoever Allah desires to test (fitnatahu)," meaning his disbelief and misguidance.

Mujahid said: its evidence is His saying: "And fight them until there is no more fitnah" (Qur'an 8:39).

Al-Dahhak said: his destruction. Qatadah said: his punishment, with the parallel: "and He did not command them concerning whom they should believe." "For you cannot avail him anything against Allah. Those are the ones whom Allah did not intend to purify their hearts" (Qur'an 5:41), that is, by guidance, by His power. "For them in this world is disgrace" (Qur'an 5:41): for the hypocrites, exposure, tearing of the veil, and fear of being killed; and for the Jews, the jizyah, killing and captivity, [...] [unreadable text] from Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companions, and among them is what they dislike. "And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment" (Qur'an 5:41): abiding forever in the Fire.

"Listeners for falsehood, devourers of what is forbidden (lil-suht)" (Qur'an 5:42). In it there are four readings: al-suht with a damma on the sin and the ha', which is the reading of the people of the Hijaz and Basra; al-Kisa'i preferred "suht" with a light pronunciation, which is the reading of the people of Syria, 'Asim, Hamzah and Khalaf. "Al-saht" with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the ha' is the transmission of al-'Abbas from Nafi'. "Al-suht" with a damma on the sin and a sukun on the ha' is the reading of 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, and it means what is unlawful.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every flesh that grew from what is forbidden, the Fire is more deserving of it."

Its root is "ma ashudda ashuddahu" (what most intensifies it). Allah the Exalted said: "lest He destroy you with a punishment" (fa-yusbitakum bi-'adhab, Qur'an 20:61).

Al-Farazdaq said:

"Time has bitten, O son of Marwan, leaving of wealth only the stripped or the stripped-bare."

He said: "Whoever remains behind when the tree is uprooted is suht."

Al-Farra' said: its origin is the hunger-sickness: a man is said to be "suht al-ma'idah" (stomach-stricken) when he is a glutton who is never found except hungry. So it is as if the one who takes bribes and eats the unlawful is, out of greed, like one whose stomach is stricken with insatiable appetite. This verse was revealed about the Jewish judges, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and their like, who used to take bribes and give preference to whoever bribed them.

Abu 'Aqil narrated from al-Hasan concerning His saying "listeners for falsehood, devourers of what is forbidden": he said: those judges hear his lie and eat the bribe.

And from him in another narration: he said: the judge among them, when someone brought him a bribe, placed it [before him, looking at its giver and speaking with him], and listened to him without looking at his opponent; so he eats the bribe and hears the lie. And from him also: he said: that applies only to judgement, when one bribes someone to make a falsehood right for you or to nullify a right of yours; but if a man gives a ruler whose injustice he fears something to ward off harm from himself, there is no harm.

According to al-Hasan, al-suht is the bribe in judgement. Likewise Muqatil, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.

Ibn Mas'ud said: it is a bribe in everything.

Muslim ibn Subayh said: Masruq did a favour for a man in a matter, and the man gave him a slave-girl as a gift, and he became very angry and said: "Had I known you would do this, I would not have spoken on your behalf in your affair, nor will I speak for what remains of your affair." He had heard Ibn Mas'ud say: "Whoever intercedes to restore a right or to repel an injustice and is given a gift for it, that is suht." It was said to him: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, we did not think that this applied except to taking payment for judgement." He said: "Taking payment for judgement is kufr. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers'" (Qur'an 5:44).

Abu Hanifah said: if the judge takes a bribe, he is dismissed at that moment, even if he is not formally dismissed.

'Umar, 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) said: suht is fifteen things: the bribe in judgement, the mahr of a prostitute, the earnings of a soothsayer, the price of a dog, a monkey, wine, a pig, carrion, blood, the stallion's fee, the wage of a wailing woman and a singer, the procuress, the sorcerer, the payment for making images, and the gift for intercession.

From Ja'far ibn Kaysan, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: if you have a debt owed to you by a man, then whatever you eat in his house is suht.

Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The curse of Allah be upon the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it."

Al-Akhfash said: suht is every earning that is not lawful.

Then He said: "If they come to you, O Muhammad, then judge between them or turn away from them" (Qur'an 5:42). Allah gave him the choice regarding their suht by His saying: in judging between them, if he wishes he judges, and if he wishes he leaves them.

They differed over whether the ruling of this verse is firm, and whether the rulers today have the choice in judging the dhimmis when they bring their disputes to them, as Allah granted His Prophet (ﷺ), or whether it is abrogated. Most scholars said: it is a firm ruling that nothing has abrogated, and the rulers of Islam have the choice: if they wish, they may decide between the People of the Book and all the dhimmis, and if they wish they may turn away and not judge between them; and if they judge, they judge by the ruling of the people of Islam. This is His saying: "that He may make it prevail over all religion" (Qur'an 9:33), namely the application of our rule over them. This is the view of al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, 'Ata' and Qatadah. Others said it is abrogated, abrogated by His saying: "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed" (Qur'an 5:49). This was the view of al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and al-Suddi. Ibn 'Abbas narrated it, saying: only these two verses were abrogated in al-Ma'idah, and His saying "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah" (Qur'an 5:2) was abrogated by "then kill the polytheists wherever you find them" (Qur'an 9:5); and His saying "If they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them" was abrogated by "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed."

As for enforcing the hudud upon them: the people of Iraq hold that the hudud are enforced upon them, except that they do not hold stoning, and they said: because they are not muhsan. They interpreted the Prophet's (ﷺ) stoning of the two Jews as his stoning them according to their own Torah, since they had agreed to accept the judgement of the Torah, and then denied stoning, although it was in the Torah; so they concealed it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) revealed what they had hidden. The people of the Hijaz do not hold that the hudud are enforced upon them, and they show that they were reconciled upon their polytheism, which is greater than the hudud they commit. They interpreted the Prophet's (ﷺ) stoning of the two Jews as having occurred before the jizyah was taken from them. However, the imam must prevent them from injustice and corruption. As for when one of the two parties is a Muslim, such as a dhimmi committing adultery with a Muslim woman, or stealing from a Muslim, the hadd is enforced upon him and he is judged by the ruling of Islam. "And if you judge, then judge between them with justice" (Qur'an 5:42), that is, with fairness, "Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly" (Qur'an 5:42), the doers of justice.

O Messenger, let not those grieve you who race to disbelief among those who say with their mouths, "We believe," but their hearts have not believed. (Qur'an 5:41)

Al-Salami read "yusari'una fi al-kufr" (يسارعون في الكفر). That means: among these disbelievers and their supporting one another. "So they will not harm Allah" (فلم يعجزوا الله). "Among those who say, 'We believe,' with their mouths, but their hearts have not believed" refers to the hypocrites. A parallel to this is His saying: "Faith has not yet entered your hearts" (Qur'an 49:14).

"And among those who are Jews are listeners for falsehood" (Qur'an 5:41), meaning those who relay it, i.e., the Banu Qurayzah. "Listeners for another people" (Qur'an 5:41), meaning the Jews of Khaybar. This is exactly what the people of tafsir have said, and the reason was:

A man and a woman of the nobles of Khaybar committed adultery. The woman's name was Basrah. Khaybar had been at war with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Both adulterers were married (muhsanun), and their punishment in the Torah was stoning. The Jews disliked stoning them because of their high status, so they said: "This prophet in Yathrib does not have stoning in his book, but only flogging. Send to your brothers, the Banu Qurayzah, for they are allies and neighbours of his; let them ask him." So they sent a group of them secretly. They told them: "Ask Muhammad about the two adulterers. If one of them is married, and he orders you to flog, then accept it from him; but if he orders you to stone, beware of him and do not accept it from him." And they sent the adulterers with them. The delegation arrived and stayed with Qurayzah and Nadir. He (the Qurayzi) said to them: "You are neighbours of this man and are with him in his city. An incident has occurred among us: two people committed adultery, and both are married. It is necessary that you ask Muhammad for us about his judgement." The Banu Qurayzah and Nadir said: "By Allah, he will order you to do what you dislike." Then a group of them set out: Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Ka'b ibn Asad, Sa'd ibn 'Amr, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Kinanah ibn Abi al-Huqayq, 'Abbas ibn Qays, Abu Nafi', Abu Yusuf, 'Azar and Salul, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said: "O Muhammad, tell us about the man and woman who are married (idha ahsana) if they commit adultery: what is their punishment, and how do you find it in your book?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Are you content with my judgement concerning that?"

They said: "Yes." Then Jibril descended with the ruling of stoning, and informed them of that, but they refused to adopt it. Jibril said to him: "Make between you and them Ibn Suriya," and described him to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you know a young, beardless, white, one-eyed man who lives in Fadak, called Ibn Suriya?" He said: "What kind of man is he among you?"

They said: "He is the most knowledgeable Jew remaining on the face of the earth about what Allah the Exalted revealed to Musa in the Torah." He said: "Send for him." They did, and 'Abd Allah ibn Suriya came to them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Are you Ibn Suriya?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Are you the most knowledgeable of the Jews?" He said: "So they claim." He said: "Will you make him (the judge) between me and you?" They said: "Yes, we are content with him, since you are content with him." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "I adjure you by Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Mighty, the God of the Children of Israel, who revealed the Torah to Musa, who brought you out of Egypt, split the sea for you, saved you, drowned the family of Pharaoh, who shaded you with clouds, who sent down upon you the manna and the quails, and who revealed to you His Book in which is its lawful and unlawful: do you find in your book the stoning of the married?"

Ibn Suriya said: "Yes, by the One who revealed this to me. Were I not afraid that the Torah would burn me if I lied or changed it, I would not have acknowledged it to you. But how is it in your book, O Muhammad?" He said: "When four upright witnesses testify that he has entered her as the kohl-stick enters the kohl-pot, stoning becomes obligatory." Ibn Suriya said: "By the One who revealed the Torah to Musa, this is how Allah revealed it in the Torah to Musa." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Then what was the first thing with which you permitted yourselves to disregard the command of Allah?"

He said: "When we took a nobleman, we left him; and when we took a weak man, we enforced the legal punishment on him. Adultery spread among our nobles until the son of a king of ours committed adultery, and we did not stone him. Then another man committed adultery among ordinary people, and the king wanted to stone him, but his people stood between him and the punishment. He said: 'By Allah, you will not stone him until you stone so-and-so, the king's cousin.'"

Then he said: "Come, let us gather and devise something other than stoning that will be applied to both the noble and the lowly." So we devised flogging and tahmim, which is: to flog forty lashes with a rope coated in pitch, then blacken their faces, then have them mounted on two donkeys, their faces turned toward the donkeys' rears, and be paraded around. This they made in place of stoning. The Jews said to Ibn Suriya: "How quickly you told him! You did not accuse us of this with anything, but you were absent, and we disliked to backbite you." He said to them: "I adjure in the Torah; had the Torah not feared to destroy me, I would not have told him." The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them, and they were stoned near the door of his mosque, and he said: "I am the first to revive his command when they had caused it to die."

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: "I witnessed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he ordered the stoning of the two Jews; I saw him bending over them to shield them with the stones." Then the verse was revealed: "O People of the Book, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you concealed of the Book and pardoning much" (Qur'an 5:15). So he did not inform them of it. Ibn Suriya placed his hand on the knee of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I adjure you by Allah and ask Allah's protection for you, that you tell us of the much that you were ordered to pardon." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from him. Ibn Suriya said to him: "Tell me about three qualities I will ask you about." He said: "What are they?" He said:

"Tell me about your sleep." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "My eyes sleep while my heart is awake." He said: "You have spoken truly. Tell me about a child's resemblance to its father: does it have none of its mother's resemblance, or does it have none of its father's resemblance?" He said: "Whichever of the two rises and its water precedes the other's water, the resemblance is his." He said: "You have spoken truly. Tell me: what does a man contribute to the child, and what does a woman contribute to it?" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fainted for a long time, then recovered, his face flushed and sweating, and said: "Flesh, blood, nails and hair are from the woman; bone, sinew and veins are from the man." He said to him: "You have spoken truly. Your affair is the affair of a prophet." Ibn Suriya then embraced Islam and said: "O Muhammad, which of the angels comes to you?" He said: "Jibril."

He said: "Describe him to me." The Prophet (ﷺ) described him to him, and he said: "I testify that he is in the Torah as you have said, and that you are truly the Messenger of Allah." When Ibn Suriya embraced Islam, the Jews attacked him and reviled him. When they wanted to rise, the Banu Qurayzah clung to the Banu Nadir, and said: "O Muhammad, our brothers the Banu Nadir: our father is one, our religion is one, our prophet is one. If they kill one of us, they do not pay us blood-money but give us its diya of seventy wasq of dates; and if we kill one of them, they kill the killer and take from us double: one hundred and forty wasq of dates. If the victim is a woman, they pay for her with a man; and for a man of theirs, two men of ours; and for a slave of theirs, a free man of ours; and our wounds are half of their wounds." Judge between us and them. Allah the Exalted then revealed concerning the stoning and retaliation: "O Messenger, let not those grieve you who race to disbelief, of those who say with their mouths 'We believe' but whose hearts have not believed, and of those who are Jews, listeners for falsehood" (Qur'an 5:41).

The predicate is governed by the particle of relation: "and of those who are Jews" (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا), so they are "listeners for falsehood." If you wish, you may take it as the predicate of an implied subject, meaning they are "listeners for falsehood." It was also said that the lam means "to" (إلى).

Abu Hatim used to say: the lam in "lil-kadhib" (للكذب) is the lam of purpose: "they listen in order to lie about you." The lam in His saying "li-qawmin akharin" is the lam of cause: "for the sake of other people, who did not come to you," namely the people of Khaybar. "They distort the words (al-kalim), the plural of kalimah, from their places (min ba'di mawadi'ihi)," that is, after their placement in their proper positions, like His saying: "But righteousness is in one who fears Allah" (Qur'an 2:177). He mentioned writing only as a return to the wording, which is al-kalim.

Ali read: "yuharrifuna al-kalama min ba'di mawadi'ihi."

"They say: If you are given this, then take it" (Qur'an 5:41), meaning: if Muhammad gives you a ruling of flogging and stoning, accept it; "and if you are not given it, then beware." "Whoever Allah desires to test (fitnatahu)," meaning his disbelief and misguidance.

Mujahid said: its evidence is His saying: "And fight them until there is no more fitnah" (Qur'an 8:39).

Al-Dahhak said: his destruction. Qatadah said: his punishment, with the parallel: "and He did not command them concerning whom they should believe." "For you cannot avail him anything against Allah. Those are the ones whom Allah did not intend to purify their hearts" (Qur'an 5:41), that is, by guidance, by His power. "For them in this world is disgrace" (Qur'an 5:41): for the hypocrites, exposure, tearing of the veil, and fear of being killed; and for the Jews, the jizyah, killing and captivity, [...] [unreadable text] from Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companions, and among them is what they dislike. "And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment" (Qur'an 5:41): abiding forever in the Fire.

"Listeners for falsehood, devourers of what is forbidden (lil-suht)" (Qur'an 5:42). In it there are four readings: al-suht with a damma on the sin and the ha', which is the reading of the people of the Hijaz and Basra; al-Kisa'i preferred "suht" with a light pronunciation, which is the reading of the people of Syria, 'Asim, Hamzah and Khalaf. "Al-saht" with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the ha' is the transmission of al-'Abbas from Nafi'. "Al-suht" with a damma on the sin and a sukun on the ha' is the reading of 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, and it means what is unlawful.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every flesh that grew from what is forbidden, the Fire is more deserving of it."

Its root is "ma ashudda ashuddahu" (what most intensifies it). Allah the Exalted said: "lest He destroy you with a punishment" (fa-yusbitakum bi-'adhab, Qur'an 20:61).

Al-Farazdaq said:

"Time has bitten, O son of Marwan, leaving of wealth only the stripped or the stripped-bare."

He said: "Whoever remains behind when the tree is uprooted is suht."

Al-Farra' said: its origin is the hunger-sickness: a man is said to be "suht al-ma'idah" (stomach-stricken) when he is a glutton who is never found except hungry. So it is as if the one who takes bribes and eats the unlawful is, out of greed, like one whose stomach is stricken with insatiable appetite. This verse was revealed about the Jewish judges, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and their like, who used to take bribes and give preference to whoever bribed them.

Abu 'Aqil narrated from al-Hasan concerning His saying "listeners for falsehood, devourers of what is forbidden": he said: those judges hear his lie and eat the bribe.

And from him in another narration: he said: the judge among them, when someone brought him a bribe, placed it [before him, looking at its giver and speaking with him], and listened to him without looking at his opponent; so he eats the bribe and hears the lie. And from him also: he said: that applies only to judgement, when one bribes someone to make a falsehood right for you or to nullify a right of yours; but if a man gives a ruler whose injustice he fears something to ward off harm from himself, there is no harm.

According to al-Hasan, al-suht is the bribe in judgement. Likewise Muqatil, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.

Ibn Mas'ud said: it is a bribe in everything.

Muslim ibn Subayh said: Masruq did a favour for a man in a matter, and the man gave him a slave-girl as a gift, and he became very angry and said: "Had I known you would do this, I would not have spoken on your behalf in your affair, nor will I speak for what remains of your affair." He had heard Ibn Mas'ud say: "Whoever intercedes to restore a right or to repel an injustice and is given a gift for it, that is suht." It was said to him: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, we did not think that this applied except to taking payment for judgement." He said: "Taking payment for judgement is kufr. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers'" (Qur'an 5:44).

Abu Hanifah said: if the judge takes a bribe, he is dismissed at that moment, even if he is not formally dismissed.

'Umar, 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) said: suht is fifteen things: the bribe in judgement, the mahr of a prostitute, the earnings of a soothsayer, the price of a dog, a monkey, wine, a pig, carrion, blood, the stallion's fee, the wage of a wailing woman and a singer, the procuress, the sorcerer, the payment for making images, and the gift for intercession.

From Ja'far ibn Kaysan, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: if you have a debt owed to you by a man, then whatever you eat in his house is suht.

Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The curse of Allah be upon the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it."

Al-Akhfash said: suht is every earning that is not lawful.

Then He said: "If they come to you, O Muhammad, then judge between them or turn away from them" (Qur'an 5:42). Allah gave him the choice regarding their suht by His saying: in judging between them, if he wishes he judges, and if he wishes he leaves them.

They differed over whether the ruling of this verse is firm, and whether the rulers today have the choice in judging the dhimmis when they bring their disputes to them, as Allah granted His Prophet (ﷺ), or whether it is abrogated. Most scholars said: it is a firm ruling that nothing has abrogated, and the rulers of Islam have the choice: if they wish, they may decide between the People of the Book and all the dhimmis, and if they wish they may turn away and not judge between them; and if they judge, they judge by the ruling of the people of Islam. This is His saying: "that He may make it prevail over all religion" (Qur'an 9:33), namely the application of our rule over them. This is the view of al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, 'Ata' and Qatadah. Others said it is abrogated, abrogated by His saying: "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed" (Qur'an 5:49). This was the view of al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and al-Suddi. Ibn 'Abbas narrated it, saying: only these two verses were abrogated in al-Ma'idah, and His saying "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah" (Qur'an 5:2) was abrogated by "then kill the polytheists wherever you find them" (Qur'an 9:5); and His saying "If they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them" was abrogated by "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed."

As for enforcing the hudud upon them: the people of Iraq hold that the hudud are enforced upon them, except that they do not hold stoning, and they said: because they are not muhsan. They interpreted the Prophet's (ﷺ) stoning of the two Jews as his stoning them according to their own Torah, since they had agreed to accept the judgement of the Torah, and then denied stoning, although it was in the Torah; so they concealed it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) revealed what they had hidden. The people of the Hijaz do not hold that the hudud are enforced upon them, and they show that they were reconciled upon their polytheism, which is greater than the hudud they commit. They interpreted the Prophet's (ﷺ) stoning of the two Jews as having occurred before the jizyah was taken from them. However, the imam must prevent them from injustice and corruption. As for when one of the two parties is a Muslim, such as a dhimmi committing adultery with a Muslim woman, or stealing from a Muslim, the hadd is enforced upon him and he is judged by the ruling of Islam. "And if you judge, then judge between them with justice" (Qur'an 5:42), that is, with fairness, "Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly" (Qur'an 5:42), the doers of justice.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 5, verses 43–46:**

﴿And how do they make you judge?﴾ This is an expression of wonder, and it is abbreviated. The full sense is: "How do they make you a judge and accept Muhammad (ﷺ), when they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of God, which is stoning, and yet they do not accept that?"

﴿Then they turn away after that﴾ up to His words ﴿for those who are Jews.﴾ If it is said: "Is there among us anyone other than Muslims?"

The answer: These are the prophets of Islam. This does not mean that the other prophets did not submit to Muslims. This is like His words ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾ [Surah al-Fath 48:29], and ﴿So believe in God and His Messenger, the Unlettered Prophet, who believes in God and His words﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:158]. It does not mean that the other prophets did not believe in God and His words. It was also said that the word does not refer to Islam, which is the opposite of disbelief (kufr).

Rather, what is meant are those who submitted to the judgment of God and did not conceal it, as these (Jews) concealed it. This is an allusion to the People of the Book.

This is like His words ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran 3:83].

Yazid ibn 'Amr ibn Fuqayl said: "I have submitted my face to Him to whom the earth submits, bearing heavy rocks; and I have submitted my face to Him to whom the springs submit, bearing sweet, pure water." It was also said that the meaning is: "those who submitted themselves to God." This is as it was narrated: the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say when he went to his bed: "I have submitted my soul to You."

It was also said that the meaning is: "By it the prophets who submitted judge, by what is in the Torah of the laws, and it was not acted upon, like 'Isa (peace be upon him)." This is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:48]. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Hayyan: "He judges by what is in the Torah from (the time of) Musa to 'Isa, peace be upon them both."

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: he meant Muhammad (ﷺ), who ruled over the Jews with stoning, and He mentioned him in the plural form, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a nation﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:120]. He also said: ﴿Or do you envy the people for what God has given them?﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 4:54]. And ﴿the rabbis and the rabbis (al-Rabbaniyyun wa al-Ahbar)﴾ means the scholars, and they are the descendants of Harun (peace be upon him). One of them is called *mihbar* and *hibr*, and the *hibr* is the scholar who firmly establishes a matter. From this comes Ka'b ibn Qani', Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Ka'b al-Hibr.

Al-Farra' said: The most common I have heard the Arabs say for the singular of *al-ahbar* is with a kasra on the *ha'*. They differed about the derivation of this name.

Al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is from *al-hibr*, the ink with which one writes. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: I asked al-Khalil about it, and he said: it is from *al-hibar*, which is a good trace. He recited:

"Do not fill the bucket while its rope is in it; do you not see the trace of the one who waters it?"

Qutrub said: it is from *al-hibr*, which is beauty and appearance, and it points to them. This is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man will come out of the Fire whose *hibr* and *sibr* have gone," [meaning his beauty and splendor].

Al-'Abbas said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "O son of my brother, what is beauty?" He said: "In the tongue."

Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr said to his son: "O my son, learn knowledge; for if you have wealth, it is beauty, and if you do not have knowledge, it is wealth."

﴿Because they were entrusted with the Book of God, and they were witnesses to it﴾, indeed it is so. ﴿So do not fear the people, but fear Me﴾ up to His words ﴿the disbelievers﴾. The scholars differed about the meaning of the verse and its ruling.

Al-Dahhak, Abu Ishaq, Abu Salih, and Qatadah said: these three verses were revealed concerning the Jews, and there is nothing of them in the people of Islam. As for this community, whoever among them does wrong while knowing he has done wrong, that is not (true) religion.

He said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari relate from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani that he was asked about these verses, and he said: they apply to all that God has revealed, not to some of it. So whoever does not judge by all that God has revealed is a disbeliever, a wrongdoer, and defiant.

As for one who judges by some of what God has revealed, of monotheism [and abandoning] polytheism, [then did not judge by these two (Hadha al-zahir min al-asl)], of the laws, he does not incur the ruling of these verses.

The jurists said: this applies when one rejects the clear text of God's ruling deliberately and openly. As for one who is ignorant of it, or it is hidden from him, or he errs in an interpretation he invented, or in an inference he reached, then it does not apply. Some of them applied it to its apparent meaning.

Ibn Mas'ud and al-Suddi said: whoever takes a bribe in judgment and judges in it by other than God's judgment is a disbeliever.

﴿And We prescribed for them therein﴾, that is, We revealed to the Children of Israel in the Torah, ﴿that the life is for the life﴾, meaning the killer is to be killed for the one he killed unjustly [zulman]; ﴿and the eye for the eye﴾, by gouging it out; ﴿and the nose for the nose﴾, by slitting it; ﴿and the ear for the ear﴾, by cutting off its ear; ﴿and the tooth for the tooth﴾, by pulling it out; and the rest of the limbs are analogous to the eye, the nose, and the ear; ﴿and wounds for retaliation﴾. This is restricted to what retaliation is possible for. As for what is a fracture of flesh or a fracture of bone, and it is not possible to know it with certainty, then it is by analogy or by judgment (hukumah).

The jurists differed about this verse. Al-Kisa'i read ﴿and the eye﴾ in the nominative case (raf'), to the end. Abu 'Ubayd preferred what Ibn Shihab narrated from Anas: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that the life is for the life﴾ in the accusative (nasb), and ﴿the eye for the eye, the nose for the nose, the ear for the ear, the tooth for the tooth, and wounds for retaliation,﴾ all in the nominative.

As for Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir, and Abu 'Amr, they used the nominative for ﴿wounds﴾ and the accusative for the rest. Qatadah and Abu Hatim said: because they have parallels in the Qur'an, such as His words: ﴿that God is free of the polytheists and His Messenger﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah 9:3], ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to God; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:128], and ﴿And when it is said, "Indeed the promise of God is true, and the Hour..."﴾ [Surah al-Jathiyah 45:32].

Nafi', 'Asim, al-A'mash, Hamzah, and Ya'qub read all of them in the accusative by coordination, and their evidence is His words: ﴿that the life is for the life, and that the eye is for the eye, and that the nose is for the nose, and that the ear is for the ear, and that the wounds are for retaliation.﴾

﴿Whoever forgoes it as charity﴾: They differed about the pronoun in His words "bihi" ("it"). Some said it refers to the one wounded and the guardian of the slain. The meaning is: whoever forgoes it as charity, then it is an expiation (kaffarah) for him, for the one who gives charity; his sins are removed to the extent of what he gave in charity.

This is the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, and Jabir ibn Zayd. The evidence for this view is what al-Sha'bi narrated from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives charity from his body with something, God will expiate for him to the extent of that from his sins."

Waki' narrated from Yusuf ibn Abi Ishaq, from Abu al-Shahr, who said: A man from Quraysh broke the tooth of a man from the Ansar, so the Ansari sought redress against him from Mu'awiyah. The Qurashi said: "Indeed, this one has bitten my tooth."

Mu'awiyah said: "Never! Will you not seek his pardon?" When the Ansari persisted against him, Mu'awiyah said: "It is up to you and your companion." Abu al-Darda' was sitting there.

Abu al-Darda' said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "No Muslim is afflicted with something in his body and then forgoes it as charity, except that God raises him by it one degree and removes from him a sin."

The Ansari said: "Did you hear this from the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, my ears heard it and my heart retained it." So he pardoned him.

'Awf narrated from 'Alqamah ibn Wa'il al-Hadrami, from his father, who said: The killer who had killed was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by the guardian of the slain. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Will you pardon?" He said: "No." He said: "Will you take the blood-money?" He said: "No." He said: "Then execution?" He said: "Yes." [He said: "Go," and he went.] Then he called him and said: "Will you pardon?" He said: "No." He said: "Will you take the blood-money?" He said: "No." He said: "Then execution?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Go." When he had gone, he said: "As for you, if you pardon, then he will bear your sin and the sin of your companion." He said: So he pardoned him, and he let him go, and I saw him dragging his sandal-thongs.

'Imran narrated from 'Adi ibn Thabit al-Ansari, who said: a man stabbed another man in the time of Mu'awiyah, so they gave him two blood-payments on condition that he be satisfied. He was not satisfied, so they gave him three blood-payments, and he was not satisfied.

A man narrated from the Muslims, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever gives charity with blood or less than it, it will be an expiation for him from the day he was born until the day he gave charity."

From 'Umar ibn Nabhan, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever comes with three things along with faith, will enter Paradise by whichever gate of Paradise he wishes, and will marry from the Houris whichever he wishes: whoever pays a debt [secretly] and pardons a killer, and recites after each obligatory prayer ten times: 'Say: He is God, the One' [Surah al-Ikhlas]."

Abu Bakr said: "And one of them, O Messenger of God?" He said: "And one of them."

Others said: what is meant is the one who wounds and the one who kills; meaning, if the injured person pardons the offender, then his pardon of the offender is an expiation for the offender's sin, and he will not be held accountable for it in the Hereafter, just as retaliation is an expiation for him. And as for the one who pardons and gives charity, his reward is with God, Exalted is He, who said: ﴿But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with God﴾ [Surah al-Shura 42:40]. This is the view of Ibrahim, Mujahid, and Zayd ibn Aslam, and it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

The first view is better, because the one who gave charity may not have repented, and the one who committed the act may not turn back from it, and it is an expiation for him. The evidence for this is the reading of Ubayy: "Whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him."

﴿And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, those are the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿And We sent, following in their footsteps﴾, that is, following in the footsteps of the prophets who submitted, who confirmed the Torah and acted upon it, ﴿'Isa son of Maryam, confirming what was before him of the Torah. And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light, and confirming what was before it of the Torah, and as guidance and instruction for the righteous.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 5, verses 43–46:**

﴿And how do they make you judge?﴾ This is an expression of wonder, and it is abbreviated. The full sense is: "How do they make you a judge and accept Muhammad (ﷺ), when they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of God, which is stoning, and yet they do not accept that?"

﴿Then they turn away after that﴾ up to His words ﴿for those who are Jews.﴾ If it is said: "Is there among us anyone other than Muslims?"

The answer: These are the prophets of Islam. This does not mean that the other prophets did not submit to Muslims. This is like His words ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾ [Surah al-Fath 48:29], and ﴿So believe in God and His Messenger, the Unlettered Prophet, who believes in God and His words﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:158]. It does not mean that the other prophets did not believe in God and His words. It was also said that the word does not refer to Islam, which is the opposite of disbelief (kufr).

Rather, what is meant are those who submitted to the judgment of God and did not conceal it, as these (Jews) concealed it. This is an allusion to the People of the Book.

This is like His words ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran 3:83].

Yazid ibn 'Amr ibn Fuqayl said: "I have submitted my face to Him to whom the earth submits, bearing heavy rocks; and I have submitted my face to Him to whom the springs submit, bearing sweet, pure water." It was also said that the meaning is: "those who submitted themselves to God." This is as it was narrated: the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say when he went to his bed: "I have submitted my soul to You."

It was also said that the meaning is: "By it the prophets who submitted judge, by what is in the Torah of the laws, and it was not acted upon, like 'Isa (peace be upon him)." This is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:48]. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Hayyan: "He judges by what is in the Torah from (the time of) Musa to 'Isa, peace be upon them both."

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: he meant Muhammad (ﷺ), who ruled over the Jews with stoning, and He mentioned him in the plural form, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a nation﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:120]. He also said: ﴿Or do you envy the people for what God has given them?﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 4:54]. And ﴿the rabbis and the rabbis (al-Rabbaniyyun wa al-Ahbar)﴾ means the scholars, and they are the descendants of Harun (peace be upon him). One of them is called *mihbar* and *hibr*, and the *hibr* is the scholar who firmly establishes a matter. From this comes Ka'b ibn Qani', Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Ka'b al-Hibr.

Al-Farra' said: The most common I have heard the Arabs say for the singular of *al-ahbar* is with a kasra on the *ha'*. They differed about the derivation of this name.

Al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is from *al-hibr*, the ink with which one writes. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: I asked al-Khalil about it, and he said: it is from *al-hibar*, which is a good trace. He recited:

"Do not fill the bucket while its rope is in it; do you not see the trace of the one who waters it?"

Qutrub said: it is from *al-hibr*, which is beauty and appearance, and it points to them. This is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man will come out of the Fire whose *hibr* and *sibr* have gone," [meaning his beauty and splendor].

Al-'Abbas said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "O son of my brother, what is beauty?" He said: "In the tongue."

Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr said to his son: "O my son, learn knowledge; for if you have wealth, it is beauty, and if you do not have knowledge, it is wealth."

﴿Because they were entrusted with the Book of God, and they were witnesses to it﴾, indeed it is so. ﴿So do not fear the people, but fear Me﴾ up to His words ﴿the disbelievers﴾. The scholars differed about the meaning of the verse and its ruling.

He said: "All of them are about the disbelievers."

'Ata' said: it is a disbelief lesser than disbelief, a wrongdoing lesser than wrongdoing, and a defiance lesser than defiance.

وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْإِنْجِيلِ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ ﴿Let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein﴾. The majority of reciters (al-'amma) read the *lam* and the *mim* with a *jazm* (the sukun ending), as an imperative. Hamza read the *lam* with a kasra and the *mim* with a fatha, meaning "so that the People of the Gospel may judge" (wa-li-kay yahkuma ahl al-Injil).

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Allah the Exalted commanded the rabbis (al-ahbar, Jewish scholars) and the rabbanis (al-rabbaniyyun, Jewish religious authorities) to judge by what is in the Torah, and He commanded the qissisin (Christian priests) and the ruhban (monks) to judge by what is in the Gospel. But they disbelieved and denied Muhammad (ﷺ), and they said: "Uzayr is the son of Allah," and "the Messiah is the son of Allah."

﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾. Muqatil said: they are those who leave the command of Allah. Ibn Zayd said: they are the liars.

A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿If a defiant one (fasiq) brings you news...﴾ and ﴿And We have revealed to you the Book with truth, confirming what is before it of the Book﴾, meaning the books (al-kutub), ﴿and as a guardian over it﴾, meaning a witness (shahidan). This was said by al-Suddi and al-Kisa'i, and it is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas. Hassan said:

*"Indeed the Book is a guardian (muhaymin) over our Prophet,*
*And the truth is known to those of understanding."*

Here muhaymin means confirming (musaddiq).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu 'Ubayda said: it means trustworthy (mu'minan). This is the narration of Abu Ishaq from al-Tamimi from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan said: it means trustworthy (amina). This is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. The sense of the Qur'an's trustworthiness (amanat al-Qur'an) is what Ibn Jurayj said: the Qur'an is a trustworthy witness over the books that came before it. Whatever the People of the Book report in their books of a matter, if it is in the Qur'an they are to confirm it, and otherwise they are to deny it.

Al-Mubarrad said: its origin is *mu'ayman*, and the hamza was changed into *ha'*, as it is said: *araqtu al-ma'* and *harraqtu* (I poured out water). Similarly: the water that is shaken off the head when rubbed (*ablayah* and *habriyah*), *nahat* and *hayhat*. And: *atak* and *hayyak*. So it is a form like *amin* and *mu'amin*, as *bayṭar* and *mubayṭir* derive from *bayṭar* (farrier).

Al-Nabigha said:

*"Like the farrier's stitching when he healed the arm wound."*

Al-Dahhak said: it means dominant (mahdi'an)... [as recorded: "ma diyan," i.e., one who prevails over]. 'Ikrima said: it means one who points to it (dall 'alayhi). Ibn Zayd said: confirming (musaddiqan). Al-Khalil said: watchful and guarding (raqiban wa-hafizan). It is said: *haymana fulan 'ala kadha* when he witnessed it and guarded it.

I say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard al-Mansur ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Bustī say: I heard Abu 'Umar Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Lughawi say: The Arabs say: when a bird begins to fly around its nest and fears for its chick, guarding it, it is said: *haymana al-ta'ir* (the bird has hovered protectively), and it is *muhaymin*. Likewise, when a bird spreads its wings and covers its eggs and its young with them, it is called *muhaymin*. Thus its concealment (ikhtiba'uhu) is also its sense, and from this it is said that Allah the Exalted is *al-Muhaymin*, meaning the Watchful, the Merciful. He said: I saw in some books that it is in the Ajami language and was Arabized. 'Ikrima recited *hayman* and *muhayman*, in the manner of the kings' speech (bi-qawlihim al-muluk).

﴿So judge between them, O Muhammad,﴾ between the People of the Book, when they come to you for judgment, ﴿by what Allah has revealed﴾ in the Qur'an, ﴿and do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you. For each of you We have appointed a law (shir'a) and a path (minhaj)﴾. That is, a way (sabilan) and a custom (sunnah). The plural of *shir'a* is *shar'*, and everything He has legislated (sharra'a) is a *shir'a* and a *shari'a*. From this comes *shari'at al-ma'* (the watering place of water) and *mash'aratuhu*. From it also come the *shara'i'* (laws) of Islam, the entry of its people into them. It is said: "Someone began (shara'a) a matter" when they entered upon a matter and proceeded in it. The *minhaj*, *manhaj*, and *nahj* are the clear, evident road.

The reciter (al-rajiz) said:

*"Whoever is in doubt, why does he not enter*
*the clear road?"*

The exegetes (al-mufassirun) said: this refers to all the different religious communities. Allah made for each community a law and a path. For the People of the Torah there is a law, for the People of the Gospel a law, and for the People of the Qur'an a law, in which He makes lawful what He wills and forbids what He wills. The religion is one, but the laws differ.

﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community﴾, all of you one religion, ﴿but He wills to test you (li-yabluwakum)﴾, meaning to inform you, and He knows best; the meaning of testing has already passed, ﴿in what He has given you﴾ of the books, ﴿and what He has made clear to you﴾ of the [sunan, i.e., the prophetic traditions]. Thus He distinguishes the obedient from the disobedient, and the steadfast from the opposer. ﴿So race to the good deeds (fastabiqu al-khayrat)﴾, that is, hasten to the good things and righteous deeds. ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you about what you used to dispute.﴾

﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: Ka'b ibn Asad, 'Abd Allah ibn Suriya, and Shas ibn Qays said to one another: "Go with us to Muhammad; perhaps we can tempt him away from his religion." Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verses 51–56 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾. Scholars differed about the occasion of the revelation of this verse, and whether its ruling is general for all believers.

Al-'Awfi and al-Zuhri said: When the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish allies, "Flee before Allah afflicts you with a day like the day of Badr." Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Has it deceived you that you struck a group of Quraysh who had no knowledge of fighting? If we had resolved to gather against you, you would have had no power to kill us."

'Ubadah ibn al-Samit al-Khazraji came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have many allies among the Jews, numerous in their number, strong in their spirit, mighty in their power, abundant in their weapons. I disavow before Allah and His Messenger their allegiance and the allegiance of the Jews. I have no ally except Allah and His Messenger." 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: "But I do not disavow the allegiance of the Jews, for I fear the reversals of fortune and I cannot do without them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu al-Hubab, what you have withheld from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit regarding the allegiance of the Jews, it is yours instead of him." He said: "I have accepted." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: When the battle of Uhud took place, it weighed heavily on a group of people, and they feared that the disbelievers would gain the upper hand over them.

A man among the Muslims said: "As for me, I will go to Dhimmi (a Jew) and take safe-conduct from him, for I fear the Jews will inform on us." Another man said: "As for me, I will go to so-and-so, a Christian from some of the people of Syria, and take safe-conduct from him." Allah revealed this verse forbidding both of them.

'Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir when he said to the Prophet (ﷺ), when they (the Banu Qurayzah) accepted the judgment of Sa'd: "It is the slaughter." ﴿Some of them are allies of others﴾ in support and aid, their hand is one against the Muslims. ﴿And whoever among you allies with them﴾, agreeing with them in their religion and aiding them, ﴿then he is indeed one of them﴾.

Ibn Sirin said, concerning a man who sold his house to Christians, who made it a church (bai'ah), that he recited this verse. ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions among the hypocrites, who used to be allied with the Jews, flatter them and advise them. ﴿They hasten toward them﴾, that is, toward their alliance, ﴿saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us"﴾, meaning a turn of fortune (dawlah), that is, that the times may turn and we will need their help, so we ally with them for that reason.

The rajiz (rajaz poet) said:
"It turns away from you the decreed fate, / and the reversals of time, that they may turn."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/217.]]

﴿Perhaps Allah will bring a victory﴾, that is, a decision (qada'), and it was said: victory. Al-Suddi said: the conquest of Makkah. ﴿Or a command from Him﴾, ﴿so they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful﴾, meaning these hypocrites.

﴿And those who believe will say﴾, at that time. The readers (qurra') differed concerning it. The people of Kufa read (wa-yaqulu) with the waw and the raf' (nominative), as a new sentence. The people of Basra read (wa-yaqula) in the accusative, the waw being a conjunction with (an ya'tiya). The rest read with raf' of the lam and without the waw, and it is so in the codices of the people of Syria.
[[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/218.]]
﴿Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that they were with you?﴾ the verse.

﴿O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion﴾, and the people of Madinah and Syria read (yartadda) with two dals, to show the lightening of the form, ﴿then (he will turn back to) disbelief﴾.

This is a sign (majaz) of the Qur'an and of the Chosen One (ﷺ), since he informed of their apostasy, and it did not occur in his lifetime. It happened as he had informed, after a period. The people of apostasy (ahl al-ridda) were eleven groups: three in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the end of his life, seven in the time of Abu Bakr, and one in the time of 'Umar.

As for the three who were in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):
Among them were the Banu Madhhij and their chief Dhu al-Khimar 'Ayhalah ibn Ka'b al-Qays, who was given the epithet al-Aswad (the Black). He was a soothsayer and a trickster, and he claimed prophethood in Yemen. The Messenger (ﷺ) had appointed him over the call to prayer (adhan) in all its regions, and he was the first of the non-Arab kings to embrace Islam and the first governor of the lands of Yemen in Islam. Then he died, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (a month later) ... Then al-Aswad the liar killed Shahr ibn Badhan and married his wife Lubad, took control of the lands of Yemen, and expelled the agents of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from them. He wrote to Mu'adh ibn Jabal and those Muslims with him, instructing them to urge the people to hold to their religion and to rise up to fight al-Aswad, either by stealth or by open confrontation. The Messenger (ﷺ) wrote similarly to the Himyar, to the chiefs of Yemen: 'Amir ibn Sahw, Dhu Ru'ud, Dhu Mirān, Dhu al-Kala' and Dhu Zulm.
[[See al-Isabah: 2/158.]]
They did what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded them, and they fought al-Aswad until Allah destroyed al-Aswad at the hands of Fayruz al-Daylami, who struck him and killed him by hitting his head.

Ibn 'Umar said: News came to the Prophet (ﷺ) from heaven on the night in which al-Ansi was killed.
He (ﷺ) said: "al-Aswad was killed last night; he was killed by a blessed man." It was asked: "And who is he?" He said: "Fayruz."
Fayruz triumphed. So he gave glad tidings to his companions of the destruction of al-Aswad today. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, and news of the killing of al-Ansi reached Madinah at the end of Rabi' al-Awwal, after the departure of Usamah. That was the first conquest that came to Abu Bakr.
[[See Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/473.]]

The second group: the Banu Hanifah and al-Yamamah, and their prophet Musaylimah the liar. He had claimed prophethood in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the end of the tenth year, and he asserted that he was made a partner with Muhammad in prophethood.
He wrote to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "From Musaylimah, the Messenger of Allah, to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. As to what follows, the earth is half mine and half yours." He sent this with two of his men, al-Rajjal ibn Shahb and al-Hakam ibn al-Tufayl, who was one of the chiefs of the people of al-Yamamah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Do you two testify that Musaylimah is the Messenger of Allah?"
They said: "Yes." He said: "Were it not that messengers are not killed, I would have struck your necks." Then he replied: "From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Musaylimah the liar. As to what follows: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous﴾."
[[Surah al-A'raf: 128.]] [82] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/315.]]

The Messenger (ﷺ) fell ill and died, and Musaylimah's affair kept rising in al-Yamamah day after day. Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to him with a large army, until Allah destroyed him at the hands of Wahshi, the slave of Mut'im ibn 'Adi, who had killed Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, after a fierce and hard battle. Wahshi used to say: "I killed the best of people in the Jahiliyyah and I killed the worst of people in Islam."

The third group: the Banu Asad and their chief Tulayhah ibn Khuwaylid. Tulayhah was the last to apostatize; he claimed prophethood in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and was the first of the people of apostasy to be killed after his death (ﷺ). He mustered his forces and tested his position. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid against him, and they defeated them with Khalid after a fierce battle. Tulayhah escaped and passed by his wife fleeing toward Syria, and took refuge with the Banu Jafnah, who gave him protection. Then he embraced Islam afterward and his Islam was good.

These are the three who apostatized in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

As for the seven who apostatized after the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the caliphate of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) died, the Jews and the Christians rejoiced, those who had concealed hypocrisy displayed it, the people were in turmoil, and rumor and gossip increased. The Arabs turned back on their heels. Banu Fazarah apostatized and appointed as their leader 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Badr. Ghatafan apostatized and appointed over them Qurrah ibn Salamah al-Qushayri. Banu Sulaym apostatized and appointed as their leader al-Najjah ibn 'Abd Yalil. Banu Yarbu' apostatized and appointed as their leader Malik ibn Nuwayrah. Another group of Banu Tamim apostatized, and they appointed as their leader a woman of theirs called Sajah bint al-Mundhir, who claimed prophethood; then she married herself to Musaylimah the liar.
Kindah apostatized and made al-Ash'ath ibn Qays their leader. Banu Bakr ibn Wa'il apostatized in the land of Bahrain and appointed over them al-Hutam ibn Zayd. Allah then dealt with the affair of these apostates and gave victory to His religion at the hands of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him).
As for those in the time of 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), their leader was al-Ghani and his companions.
The accounts of the people of apostasy are well known in the histories and written down, and mentioning them would lengthen the book.
[[See Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/482, 489.]]

﴿Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾.
'Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are Abu Bakr and his companions.
Mujahid said: They are the people of Yemen.
Ghiyath ibn Ghanm al-Ash'ari said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured toward Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and said: "They are the people of this one."
The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The people of Yemen have come to you; they are gentler of heart and more tender of hearts. Faith is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni."
[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/252.]]
al-Kalbi said: They are tribes from Yemen: two thousand from al-Nakha', five thousand from Kindah and Bajilah, and three thousand from the rest of the people, who fought in the way of Allah at al-Qadisiyyah.
[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/91; see Tarikh al-Tabari: 3/7.]]
al-Suddi said: They are the Ansar.
It is related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about this verse, so he struck his hand on the shoulder of Salman al-Farisi and said: "This one and his people. Then he said: 'If the religion were suspended from the Pleiades, men from the sons of Persia would reach it.'"
[[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/64; Tarikh Dimashq: 51/47.]] [83]

﴿Humble toward the believers﴾, meaning gentle and merciful, like His saying ﴿and lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy﴾. It was said: it is from humility (dhull), from the saying "a beast that is docile (dhalul), clearly docile," meaning they are humble, like His saying ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾.
[[Surah al-Furqan: 63. H 34130.]]
﴿Mighty toward the disbelievers﴾, meaning fierce and harsh, from the Arabs' saying "his side became mighty (a'azza), mighty."

Ibn Mas'ud read: "Humble toward the believers, harsh toward the disbelievers," with the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal).

'Ata' said: ﴿Humble toward the believers﴾, like a child to his father and a slave to his master. ﴿Mighty toward the disbelievers﴾, like a predator toward its prey. The parallel to the verse is ﴿Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves, who strive in the way of Allah and fear not the blame of any blamer﴾.

'Abdullah ibn Hamdun narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Shabib narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"A group of my companions will come to me on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be driven away from the Basin. I will say: 'My Lord, my companions, my companions!' It will be said: 'You have no knowledge of what they innovated after you. Indeed, they turned back on their heels.'"
[[Sahih al-Bukhari: 7/208.]] [84]

﴿Your allies are only Allah and His Messenger﴾, the verse.

Abu 'Abdullah al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan, from Shabr ibn Musa al-Asadi, from Isma'il ibn Khalil al-Kufi, from Salamah ibn Raja', from Salamah ibn Sabur, who said: I heard 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi say: Ibn 'Abbas said: 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul embraced Islam, then he said: "Between me and Qurayzah and al-Nadir there is an alliance, and I fear the reversals of fortune," so he apostatized and became a disbeliever. And 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: "I disavow before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the alliance with Qurayzah and al-Nadir, and I take as allies Allah, the Messenger, and those who believe." Then Allah, Exalted, revealed:
﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ up to His saying ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, up to His saying ﴿Your allies are only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, meaning 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit and the companions of the Messenger of Allah. Then He said: ﴿And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies﴾.

Some exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah wanted to kill the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa' when they broke the covenant, and they were allies of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy was greatly troubled by that and said: "Three hundred coat-of-mail wearers and four hundred men have protected me from the black and the red, and you would leave them to be destroyed in a single morning?" As for Sa'd and 'Ubadah, they said: "We are innocent before Allah and His Messenger of their alliance and their covenant." Then Allah revealed this verse.

Jabir ibn 'Abdullah said: 'Abdullah ibn Salam came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, our people of Qurayzah and al-Nadir have shunned us and separated from us, and they swore that they would not sit with us, and we cannot sit with your companions because of the distance of the dwellings," and he complained of the harm he received from the Jews. Then the verse was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it and said: "We are content with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as brothers." According to this interpretation, by His saying ﴿those who bow (raki'un)﴾ he meant voluntary prayer by night and day.

Ibn 'Abbas said, al-Suddi said, 'Utbah ibn Hakim, and Thabit ibn 'Abdullah said: What is meant by His saying ﴿And those who believe﴾ is ﴿those who establish prayer﴾, the verse. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) was passed by a beggar while he was bowing in the mosque, and he gave him his ring.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad, Abu Muhammad 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Sha'rani, Abu 'Ali Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Zarin, al-Muzaffar ibn al-Hasan al-Ansari, al-Sadi ibn 'Ali al-'Azzaq, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-A'mash, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Rabi'i, who said: While 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas was sitting at the edge of Zamzam, a man wearing a turban came, and Ibn 'Abbas kept saying "The Messenger of Allah said," and the man kept saying: "The Messenger of Allah said?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "I ask you by Allah, who are you?"
He uncovered the turban from his face and said: "O people, whoever knows me, knows me; and whoever does not know me, I am Jundab ibn Junadah al-Badri, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with these two ears, or else let them be deaf, and I saw him with these two eyes, or else let them be blind, saying: 'Ali is the leader of the righteous, the slayer of the disbelievers, whoever helps him is victorious, whoever forsakes him is forsaken. Indeed, one day I prayed the noon prayer with the Messenger of Allah, and a beggar entered the mosque, and no one gave him anything. The beggar raised his hand to the sky and said: "O Allah, bear witness that I asked in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah and no one gave me anything." 'Ali was bowing, so he gestured to him with his right little finger, on which he used to wear a ring. The beggar came and took the ring from his finger, and that was in the sight of the Prophet (ﷺ). When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the prayer, he raised his head to the sky and said:
"O Allah, my brother Musa asked You, saying: 'My Lord, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my affair, and appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother; strengthen through him my back' [Surah Ta-Ha: 25–31], the verse. Then You sent down to him a speaking Qur'an: ﴿We will strengthen your arm through your brother and give you both authority﴾ [Surah al-Qasas: 35]. O Allah, and I am Muhammad, Your prophet and Your chosen one. O Allah, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my affair, and appoint for me a minister from my family: 'Ali, strengthen my back through him.'"
[[Shawahid al-Tanzil: 1/231; al-Ghadir: 2/52, from al-Tha'labi, whose sources were extracted.]] [85]

Abu Dharr said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah had not finished his words before Jibril came down to him from Allah and said: "O Muhammad, recite." He said: "What shall I recite?" He said: "Recite: ﴿Your allies are only Allah and His Messenger﴾, up to ﴿those who bow﴾."

I heard Abu Mansur al-Jamshadi, I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Hafiz, I heard Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn al-Hasan, I heard Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami, I heard Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi, I heard Ahmad ibn Hanbal say: No virtue has come for any of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) like what has come for 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).
[['Umdat al-Talib li-Ibn 'Inbah: 60; Tarikh Dimashq: 42/418, ed. Dar al-Fikr; Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/107.]]

Abu 'Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh, Muhammad ibn Raja' al-'Abbadani.

'Umar ibn Abi Ibrahim narrated to me, al-Mubarak ibn Sa'id and 'Ammar ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr: ﴿Your allies are only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, the two verses, the report.
[[Mentioned in Diya' al-Shams fi Nabi al-Islam 'ala Khams: ijma' of the Muslims on the revelation of the verse concerning 'Ali (peace be upon him):

2/ 4. Among those who stated that the verse was revealed concerning him are: al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, al-Wahidi, al-Zamakhshari, al-Tabari, Ibn 'Asakir, al-Baladhuri, al-Tirmidhi, al-Qazwini and Ibn Kathir. See: Tafsir al-Kashshaf 1/624; al-Tadwin fi Akhbar Qazwin 3/212, biography of 'Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 7/130, hadith no. 6228; Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 133; Rabi' al-Abrar 2/147; Tafsir al-Tabari 1/624; Tarikh Dimashq 2/409.]].
From Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Busti, Hamid ibn Shu'ayb, Shurayh ibn Yunus, Hushaym ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far concerning His words, ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾. He said: They are the believers. ﴿Some of them are allies of others﴾.
﴿And whoever takes as allies Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, then indeed the party of Allah — they are the victorious﴾. He meant: my helpers from Allah.
The rajiz said:
"And how could I be made weak [أضوي: i.e., I am deemed weak and oppressed by something], when Bilal is my party," i.e., my helper.
Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/222.

Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Has it deceived you that you struck a group of Quraysh who had no knowledge of fighting? If we had resolved to gather against you, you would have had no power to kill us."

'Ubadah ibn al-Samit al-Khazraji came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have many allies among the Jews, numerous in their number, strong in their spirit, mighty in their power, abundant in their weapons. I disavow before Allah and His Messenger their allegiance and the allegiance of the Jews. I have no ally except Allah and His Messenger." 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: "But I do not disavow the allegiance of the Jews, for I fear the reversals of fortune and I cannot do without them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu al-Hubab, what you have withheld from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit regarding the allegiance of the Jews, it is yours instead of him." He said: "I have accepted." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: When the battle of Uhud took place, it weighed heavily on a group of people, and they feared that the disbelievers would gain the upper hand over them.

A man among the Muslims said: "As for me, I will go to Dhimmi (a Jew) and take safe-conduct from him, for I fear the Jews will inform on us." Another man said: "As for me, I will go to so-and-so, a Christian from some of the people of Syria, and take safe-conduct from him." Allah revealed this verse forbidding both of them.
