The Messenger (ﷺ) wrote similarly to the Himyar, to the chiefs of Yemen: 'Amir ibn Sahw, Dhu Ru'ud, Dhu Mirān, Dhu al-Kala' and Dhu Zulm.
[[See al-Isabah: 2/158.]]
They did what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded them, and they fought al-Aswad until Allah destroyed al-Aswad at the hands of Fayruz al-Daylami, who struck him and killed him by hitting his head.

Ibn 'Umar said: News came to the Prophet (ﷺ) from heaven on the night in which al-Ansi was killed.
He (ﷺ) said: "al-Aswad was killed last night; he was killed by a blessed man." It was asked: "And who is he?" He said: "Fayruz."
Fayruz triumphed. So he gave glad tidings to his companions of the destruction of al-Aswad today. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, and news of the killing of al-Ansi reached Madinah at the end of Rabi' al-Awwal, after the departure of Usamah. That was the first conquest that came to Abu Bakr.
[[See Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/473.]]

The second group: the Banu Hanifah and al-Yamamah, and their prophet Musaylimah the liar. He had claimed prophethood in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the end of the tenth year, and he asserted that he was made a partner with Muhammad in prophethood.
He wrote to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "From Musaylimah, the Messenger of Allah, to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. As to what follows, the earth is half mine and half yours." He sent this with two of his men, al-Rajjal ibn Shahb and al-Hakam ibn al-Tufayl, who was one of the chiefs of the people of al-Yamamah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Do you two testify that Musaylimah is the Messenger of Allah?"
They said: "Yes." He said: "Were it not that messengers are not killed, I would have struck your necks." Then he replied: "From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Musaylimah the liar. As to what follows: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous﴾."
[[Surah al-A'raf: 128.]] [82] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/315.]]

The Messenger (ﷺ) fell ill and died, and Musaylimah's affair kept rising in al-Yamamah day after day. Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to him with a large army, until Allah destroyed him at the hands of Wahshi, the slave of Mut'im ibn 'Adi, who had killed Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, after a fierce and hard battle. Wahshi used to say: "I killed the best of people in the Jahiliyyah and I killed the worst of people in Islam."

The third group: the Banu Asad and their chief Tulayhah ibn Khuwaylid. Tulayhah was the last to apostatize; he claimed prophethood in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and was the first of the people of apostasy to be killed after his death (ﷺ). He mustered his forces and tested his position. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid against him, and they defeated them with Khalid after a fierce battle. Tulayhah escaped and passed by his wife fleeing toward Syria, and took refuge with the Banu Jafnah, who gave him protection. Then he embraced Islam afterward and his Islam was good.

These are the three who apostatized in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

As for the seven who apostatized after the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the caliphate of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) died, the Jews and the Christians rejoiced, those who had concealed hypocrisy displayed it, the people were in turmoil, and rumor and gossip increased. The Arabs turned back on their heels. Banu Fazarah apostatized and appointed as their leader 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Badr. Ghatafan apostatized and appointed over them Qurrah ibn Salamah al-Qushayri. Banu Sulaym apostatized and appointed as their leader al-Najjah ibn 'Abd Yalil. Banu Yarbu' apostatized and appointed as their leader Malik ibn Nuwayrah. Another group of Banu Tamim apostatized, and they appointed as their leader a woman of theirs called Sajah bint al-Mundhir, who claimed prophethood; then she married herself to Musaylimah the liar.
Kindah apostatized and made al-Ash'ath ibn Qays their leader. Banu Bakr ibn Wa'il apostatized in the land of Bahrain and appointed over them al-Hutam ibn Zayd. Allah then dealt with the affair of these apostates and gave victory to His religion at the hands of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him).
As for those in the time of 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), their leader was al-Ghani and his companions.
The accounts of the people of apostasy are well known in the histories and written down, and mentioning them would lengthen the book.
[[See Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/482, 489.]]

﴿Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾.
'Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are Abu Bakr and his companions.
Mujahid said: They are the people of Yemen.
Ghiyath ibn Ghanm al-Ash'ari said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured toward Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and said: "They are the people of this one."
The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The people of Yemen have come to you; they are gentler of heart and more tender of hearts. Faith is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni."
[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/252.]]
al-Kalbi said: They are tribes from Yemen: two thousand from al-Nakha', five thousand from Kindah and Bajilah, and three thousand from the rest of the people, who fought in the way of Allah at al-Qadisiyyah.
[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/91; see Tarikh al-Tabari: 3/7.]]
al-Suddi said: They are the Ansar.
It is related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about this verse, so he struck his hand on the shoulder of Salman al-Farisi and said: "This one and his people. Then he said: 'If the religion were suspended from the Pleiades, men from the sons of Persia would reach it.'"
[[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/64; Tarikh Dimashq: 51/47.]] [83]

﴿Humble toward the believers﴾, meaning gentle and merciful, like His saying ﴿and lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy﴾. It was said: it is from humility (dhull), from the saying "a beast that is docile (dhalul), clearly docile," meaning they are humble, like His saying ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾.
[[Surah al-Furqan: 63. H 34130.]]
﴿Mighty toward the disbelievers﴾, meaning fierce and harsh, from the Arabs' saying "his side became mighty (a'azza), mighty."

Ibn Mas'ud read: "Humble toward the believers, harsh toward the disbelievers," with the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal).

'Ata' said: ﴿Humble toward the believers﴾, like a child to his father and a slave to his master. ﴿Mighty toward the disbelievers﴾, like a predator toward its prey. The parallel to the verse is ﴿Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves, who strive in the way of Allah and fear not the blame of any blamer﴾.

'Abdullah ibn Hamdun narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Shabib narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"A group of my companions will come to me on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be driven away from the Basin. I will say: 'My Lord, my companions, my companions!' It will be said: 'You have no knowledge of what they innovated after you. Indeed, they turned back on their heels.'"
[[Sahih al-Bukhari: 7/208.]] [84]

﴿Your allies are only Allah and His Messenger﴾, the verse.

Abu 'Abdullah al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan, from Shabr ibn Musa al-Asadi, from Isma'il ibn Khalil al-Kufi, from Salamah ibn Raja', from Salamah ibn Sabur, who said: I heard 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi say: Ibn 'Abbas said: 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul embraced Islam, then he said: "Between me and Qurayzah and al-Nadir there is an alliance, and I fear the reversals of fortune," so he apostatized and became a disbeliever. And 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: "I disavow before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the alliance with Qurayzah and al-Nadir, and I take as allies Allah, the Messenger, and those who believe." Then Allah, Exalted, revealed:
﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ up to His saying ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, up to His saying ﴿Your allies are only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, meaning 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit and the companions of the Messenger of Allah. Then He said: ﴿And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies﴾.

Some exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah wanted to kill the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa' when they broke the covenant, and they were allies of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy was greatly troubled by that and said: "Three hundred coat-of-mail wearers and four hundred men have protected me from the black and the red, and you would leave them to be destroyed in a single morning?" As for Sa'd and 'Ubadah, they said: "We are innocent before Allah and His Messenger of their alliance and their covenant." Then Allah revealed this verse.

Jabir ibn 'Abdullah said: 'Abdullah ibn Salam came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, our people of Qurayzah and al-Nadir have shunned us and separated from us, and they swore that they would not sit with us, and we cannot sit with your companions because of the distance of the dwellings," and he complained of the harm he received from the Jews. Then the verse was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it and said: "We are content with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as brothers." According to this interpretation, by His saying ﴿those who bow (raki'un)﴾ he meant voluntary prayer by night and day.

Ibn 'Abbas said, al-Suddi said, 'Utbah ibn Hakim, and Thabit ibn 'Abdullah said: What is meant by His saying ﴿And those who believe﴾ is ﴿those who establish prayer﴾, the verse. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) was passed by a beggar while he was bowing in the mosque, and he gave him his ring.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad, Abu Muhammad 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Sha'rani, Abu 'Ali Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Zarin, al-Muzaffar ibn al-Hasan al-Ansari, al-Sadi ibn 'Ali al-'Azzaq, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-A'mash, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Rabi'i, who said: While 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas was sitting at the edge of Zamzam, a man wearing a turban came, and Ibn 'Abbas kept saying "The Messenger of Allah said," and the man kept saying: "The Messenger of Allah said?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "I ask you by Allah, who are you?"
He uncovered the turban from his face and said: "O people, whoever knows me, knows me; and whoever does not know me, I am Jundab ibn Junadah al-Badri, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with these two ears, or else let them be deaf, and I saw him with these two eyes, or else let them be blind, saying: 'Ali is the leader of the righteous, the slayer of the disbelievers, whoever helps him is victorious, whoever forsakes him is forsaken. Indeed, one day I prayed the noon prayer with the Messenger of Allah, and a beggar entered the mosque, and no one gave him anything. The beggar raised his hand to the sky and said: "O Allah, bear witness that I asked in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah and no one gave me anything." 'Ali was bowing, so he gestured to him with his right little finger, on which he used to wear a ring. The beggar came and took the ring from his finger, and that was in the sight of the Prophet (ﷺ). When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the prayer, he raised his head to the sky and said:
"O Allah, my brother Musa asked You, saying: 'My Lord, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my affair, and appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother; strengthen through him my back' [Surah Ta-Ha: 25–31], the verse. Then You sent down to him a speaking Qur'an: ﴿We will strengthen your arm through your brother and give you both authority﴾ [Surah al-Qasas: 35]. O Allah, and I am Muhammad, Your prophet and Your chosen one. O Allah, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my affair, and appoint for me a minister from my family: 'Ali, strengthen my back through him.'"
[[Shawahid al-Tanzil: 1/231; al-Ghadir: 2/52, from al-Tha'labi, whose sources were extracted.]] [85]

Abu Dharr said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah had not finished his words before Jibril came down to him from Allah and said: "O Muhammad, recite." He said: "What shall I recite?" He said: "Recite: ﴿Your allies are only Allah and His Messenger﴾, up to ﴿those who bow﴾."

I heard Abu Mansur al-Jamshadi, I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Hafiz, I heard Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn al-Hasan, I heard Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami, I heard Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi, I heard Ahmad ibn Hanbal say: No virtue has come for any of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) like what has come for 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).
[['Umdat al-Talib li-Ibn 'Inbah: 60; Tarikh Dimashq: 42/418, ed. Dar al-Fikr; Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/107.]]

Abu 'Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh, Muhammad ibn Raja' al-'Abbadani.

'Umar ibn Abi Ibrahim narrated to me, al-Mubarak ibn Sa'id and 'Ammar ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr: ﴿Your allies are only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, the two verses, the report.
[[Mentioned in Diya' al-Shams fi Nabi al-Islam 'ala Khams: ijma' of the Muslims on the revelation of the verse concerning 'Ali (peace be upon him):

2/ 4. Among those who stated that the verse was revealed concerning him are: al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, al-Wahidi, al-Zamakhshari, al-Tabari, Ibn 'Asakir, al-Baladhuri, al-Tirmidhi, al-Qazwini and Ibn Kathir. See: Tafsir al-Kashshaf 1/624; al-Tadwin fi Akhbar Qazwin 3/212, biography of 'Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 7/130, hadith no. 6228; Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 133; Rabi' al-Abrar 2/147; Tafsir al-Tabari 1/624; Tarikh Dimashq 2/409.]].
From Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Busti, Hamid ibn Shu'ayb, Shurayh ibn Yunus, Hushaym ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far concerning His words, ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾. He said: They are the believers. ﴿Some of them are allies of others﴾.
﴿And whoever takes as allies Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, then indeed the party of Allah — they are the victorious﴾. He meant: my helpers from Allah.
The rajiz said:
"And how could I be made weak [أضوي: i.e., I am deemed weak and oppressed by something], when Bilal is my party," i.e., my helper.
Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/222.

O you who believe, do not take those who took your religion as a mockery and a game (for Allah's words: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game﴾), and the rest of the verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When the caller (muezzin) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews said: "They have risen, may they not rise! They have prayed, may they not pray! They have bowed, may they not bow! They have prostrated, may they not prostrate!" in a manner of mockery and laughter. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Christians who, whenever he heard the muezzin say, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "May Allah burn the liar." One night his servant came in with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark flew from it into the house, and it burned the house, and he and his family were burned.

Others said: When the disbelievers heard the adhan, they denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims over it, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you have invented something we have never heard of in the past nations. If you claim prophethood, you have opposed the prophets before you in this adhan you have introduced. If there were good in this matter, the first to abandon it would have been the people after the prophets and messengers before you. So where do you get a cry like the cry of a camel? No voice is uglier, and no disbelief is more repulsive." So Allah revealed this verse. (Source cited above.) ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work?﴾

As for after the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj, Ziyad ibn Ayyub, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr al-Asadi, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad said: Ibn Jurayj related from Nafi' from Ibn Umar; Abu al-Husayn said: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj, Muhammad ibn Suhayl ibn Askar, Abu Sa'id al-Haddad, Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn [Yahya], from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father; and a narration from al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, Isma'il ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i, Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from his father, who said: When the Muslims arrived in Medina, they would gather and anticipate the prayer, and no one called to it. They discussed this matter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted the Muslims about how to summon them to prayer. Some said: "Raise a banner on top of the mosque at the time of prayer, so when they see it, they will inform one another." He did not like that. It was said: "Rather, we light a fire." Others said: "Rather, a horn like the horn of the Jews." He disliked it because of the Jews. It was said: "A bell," and he disliked it because of the Christians. But they stood for it, and he ordered the bell to be used so that they might respond.

Abd Allah ibn Zayd said: That night I saw in a dream a man wearing two green garments, carrying a bell. I said: "O servant of Allah, will you sell the bell?" He said: "What will you do with it?" I said: "We call people to prayer with it." He said: "Shall I not guide you to something better than it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" until the end of the adhan. Then he withdrew a short distance and said: "When the prayer is established, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" and he described the iqamah to him, its phrases being singular. When I awoke, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of it. He said: "It is a true vision, if Allah wills. Recite it to Bilal, for he has a more resonant voice than you." So we went out to the mosque, and I began reciting it to Bilal while he was calling the adhan. Umar heard it in his house and came out dragging his cloak, saying: "I saw the same as what he saw." The Prophet ﷺ rejoiced and said: "That is more firmly established."

Abu al-Zahiriya related from Abu Shajara, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The first to call the adhan in heaven was the one whom Umar ibn al-Khattab heard." (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu)

As for the section on the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi, Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya, Abu Ja'far ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Sayyah, Abu Umar al-Duri, Abu Ibrahim al-Burjumani, from Sa'id ibn Sa'id, from Nahshal Abu Abd Allah al-Qurashi, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will not be troubled by the reckoning, nor will the cry frighten them, nor will the greatest terror grieve them: the bearer of the Qur'an who delivers it to Allah with what is in it, arriving before his Lord as a noble master; a muezzin who calls the adhan for seven years, taking payment for his adhan out of greed; and a slave who worships his Lord excellently and fulfils the right of his master." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/831, no. 43308, with slight variation.] [86]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu Amr ibn Uthman, related to them: Abu Thumayla, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for seven years seeking reward, a written quittance from the Fire is recorded for him." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/683, no. 20904; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/561, no. 8376.] [87]

Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi, Abu al-Ala Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir, [...] [illegible word], Muhammad ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd al-Tusi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for a year with a sincere intention, seeking no wage for it, will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection, stand at the gate of Paradise, and be told: Intercede for whom you wish." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/689, no. 20936.] [88]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamd al-Tammar, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Dinar, Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Isa, Ibrahim ibn Rustam, Hammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibn Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven, and whoever leads his companions in five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/562, no. 8378.] [89]

Abu al-Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jasham Abu al-Mawja, Abdan, Abd al-Warith, Murra al-Hanafi, Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When the adhan is called, the gates of heaven are opened and supplication is answered; and when the iqamah is called, a supplication is not turned away." [Kanz al-Ummal: 2/108, no. 3372.] [90]

Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn al-Ma'arri, Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Muqri in Basra, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Jassas, Yazid ibn Amr, Abu al-Bar al-Ghanawi, Nail ibn Najih, Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Salim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The muezzin who seeks reward is like a martyr writhing in his blood until he finishes his adhan; every moist and dry thing bears witness for him, and when he dies, his grave will not decay." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/3.] [91]

Abu Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Safyani, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari said: Hammad ibn al-Hasan, Salih ibn Sulayman, the owner of the qarati(s), Attab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Sadusi, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Waqqas, that he said: The arrows of the muezzins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the emigrants.

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: If I were a muezzin, I would not mind not performing Hajj, not performing Umrah, and not fighting in jihad.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not being counted among those who pray at night or fast by day. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins."

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have left us, though we are the best, to call the adhan with swords." He said: "Not so, O Umar. There will come upon people a time when they abandon the adhan for their weak ones; and those are flesh which Allah has forbidden to the Fire: the flesh of the muezzins." [92]

Say: O People of the Book, do you blame us only because… (the verse).

Ibn Abbas said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Abu Yasir ibn al-Khattab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', Azar, Zayd ibn Khalid, and Azarail Abu Washa'. They asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "I believe in Allah, and in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to Abraham… and to Him we are submitting Muslims." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/233, where it reads "yu'min" instead of "u'min".] [93] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "By Allah, we know of no people whose religion is more favoured in this world and the next than ours; the worst of religions is your religion." So Allah revealed this verse.

Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that?"—i.e., I will inform you of what you described, their saying, "We have not seen a people more favoured in this world and the next than you." He mentioned the answer in the form of a beginning, though the beginning itself is not evil, like His saying to the disbelievers: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 72]. ﴿Requital (mathuba) with Allah﴾: reward and recompense, and it is in the accusative as an explanation, like His saying ﴿more in wealth and mightier in following﴾. Its original form is mathuwba, on the pattern of its object-form, as some verbal nouns came on the pattern of the passive participle, such as al-maf'ul and al-maysur; the vowel of the middle radical was dropped because of the heaviness of the waw, and its vowel was transferred to the first radical, which is tha', so it became mathuba, like ma'una and maghuth and maqula. ﴿Whom Allah has cursed﴾: it may be in the genitive as a substitution from "bi-sharrin," or with the meaning "for whom Allah has cursed"; it may be in the nominative with an implied "huwa" (he); and it may be in the accusative by placing "unabbi'ukum" upon it. ﴿And Allah became angry with him, and made some of them apes and swine﴾: the apes are the people of the Sabbath, and the swine are the disbelievers among the people of the table of Jesus.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas that both groups transformed were from their leaders: the ones who were transformed into apes were from their nobles, and their elders were transformed into swine. ﴿And worshipped the Taghut﴾: there are ten readings for it. ﴿Wa-'abada al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the ba', the 'ayn, and the ta', as a verb, which is the reading of the common people; and ﴿and made from them one who worshipped the Taghut﴾, and its confirmation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿and those who worshipped the Taghut﴾. Ibn Wathhab and Hamza read ﴿'abdu al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the 'ayn, damma on the ba', and kasra on the dal, meaning "the servant," and both are dialects: 'abd and 'abd, like sab' and sab', qird and qird.

Hamza recited in support of this: "How polished is the ape…" with damma on the ra'. Another interpretation is that he meant the plural, i.e., the servants of the Taghut. The plural of 'abd is 'ibad, then the plural of 'ibad is 'abad, a plural of a plural, like thimar and thamr. He encountered two successive dammas, so he changed the first to fatha; hence in the reading of al-A'mash it is ﴿wa-'ubudu al-Taghut﴾ with damma on the 'ayn and the ta', and kasra on the dal.

The poet said:
"Trace the servant to his fathers, black-skinned of the people of 'abd."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/369.]

It is related from Abu Ja'far al-Qari that he read ﴿wa-'ubida al-Taghut﴾ as a passive verb. Al-Hasan read ﴿wa-'abda al-Taghut﴾ in the singular. Abu Burda al-Aslami read ﴿wa-'abid al-Taghut﴾ in the singular [with variation; so it is in the original]. Ibn Abbas read ﴿wa-'ubayd al-Taghut﴾ in the plural. Abu Waqid al-Laythi read ﴿wa-'abbad al-Taghut﴾, like kafir and kuffar. Awn al-'Uqayli and Aban ibn Tha'lab read ﴿wa-'ubbida al-Taghut﴾, like raka' and sajad. Ibn 'Umayr read ﴿wa-'ubd al-Taghut﴾, like kalb and aklub.

﴿Those are worse in place and further astray from the right way.﴾ When this verse was revealed, the Jews were humbled, saying: "Brothers of the apes and swine," and they fell silent and were confounded. Concerning them the poet said:
"So the curse of Allah be upon the Jews; indeed the Jews are brothers of the apes."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/236.]

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾ and the rest of the verse: these are the hypocrites, as the exegetes have said.

Ibn Zayd said: These are those who said: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day﴾ and the rest of the verse.

This interpretation is more fitting to the apparent sense of the revelation, because these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. ﴿And you see many of them—meaning of the Jews—hastening into sin and transgression and their consuming of the forbidden﴾ up to His saying ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ The "rabbis" (rabbaniyyun) are the scholars, and the "scholars" (ahbar) are the learned men; some said the rabbaniyyun are the Christian scholars and the ahbar are the Jewish scholars.

Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Ibn al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿al-Rabbiyyun﴾, like His saying ﴿with him were many rabbis﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 146].

﴿from their saying sin﴾. This is the most severe verse concerning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, since it places them in the position of those who commit it and joins them together in rebuke.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Adi, [al-Ahmasi] [as in the original], al-Bukhari, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No man lives as a neighbour among a people, practising sins in their midst, and they do not restrain his hands, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 2/332.] [94]

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, Abd Allah ibn Usama, Usayl ibn Zayd al-Jammal, Yahya ibn Salma ibn Muhanna, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of the wicked person among a people is like a people who boarded a ship and divided it, so each person had a share in it. A man among them took an axe and began striking at his place. His companions said: 'What are you doing? Do you want to sink it and sink us?' He said: 'It is my place. If they seize his hands, they are saved and he is saved; and if they leave him, they sink and he sinks.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 8/240, with variation.] [95]

Malik ibn Dinar said: Allah revealed to the angels that they should punish such-and-such a town. The angels cried out to their Lord: "O Lord, among them is Your servant, the worshipper." He said: "Let Me hear his cry, for his face has not changed in anger for My prohibitions." And Allah revealed to Joshua ibn Nun: "I will destroy forty thousand of your people, from their best, and sixty thousand of their worst." He said: "O Lord, these are the wicked; but what of the good?" He said: "They did not become angry for My anger, and they ate and drank with them."

O you who believe, do not take those who took your religion as a mockery and a game (for Allah's words: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game﴾), and the rest of the verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When the caller (muezzin) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews said: "They have risen, may they not rise! They have prayed, may they not pray! They have bowed, may they not bow! They have prostrated, may they not prostrate!" in a manner of mockery and laughter. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Christians who, whenever he heard the muezzin say, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "May Allah burn the liar." One night his servant came in with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark flew from it into the house, and it burned the house, and he and his family were burned.

Others said: When the disbelievers heard the adhan, they denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims over it, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you have invented something we have never heard of in the past nations. If you claim prophethood, you have opposed the prophets before you in this adhan you have introduced. If there were good in this matter, the first to abandon it would have been the people after the prophets and messengers before you. So where do you get a cry like the cry of a camel? No voice is uglier, and no disbelief is more repulsive." So Allah revealed this verse. (Source cited above.) ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work?﴾

As for after the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj, Ziyad ibn Ayyub, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr al-Asadi, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad said: Ibn Jurayj related from Nafi' from Ibn Umar; Abu al-Husayn said: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj, Muhammad ibn Suhayl ibn Askar, Abu Sa'id al-Haddad, Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn [Yahya], from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father; and a narration from al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, Isma'il ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i, Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from his father, who said: When the Muslims arrived in Medina, they would gather and anticipate the prayer, and no one called to it. They discussed this matter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted the Muslims about how to summon them to prayer. Some said: "Raise a banner on top of the mosque at the time of prayer, so when they see it, they will inform one another." He did not like that. It was said: "Rather, we light a fire." Others said: "Rather, a horn like the horn of the Jews." He disliked it because of the Jews. It was said: "A bell," and he disliked it because of the Christians. But they stood for it, and he ordered the bell to be used so that they might respond.

Abd Allah ibn Zayd said: That night I saw in a dream a man wearing two green garments, carrying a bell. I said: "O servant of Allah, will you sell the bell?" He said: "What will you do with it?" I said: "We call people to prayer with it." He said: "Shall I not guide you to something better than it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" until the end of the adhan. Then he withdrew a short distance and said: "When the prayer is established, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" and he described the iqamah to him, its phrases being singular. When I awoke, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of it. He said: "It is a true vision, if Allah wills. Recite it to Bilal, for he has a more resonant voice than you." So we went out to the mosque, and I began reciting it to Bilal while he was calling the adhan. Umar heard it in his house and came out dragging his cloak, saying: "I saw the same as what he saw." The Prophet ﷺ rejoiced and said: "That is more firmly established."

Abu al-Zahiriya related from Abu Shajara, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The first to call the adhan in heaven was the one whom Umar ibn al-Khattab heard." (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu)

As for the section on the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi, Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya, Abu Ja'far ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Sayyah, Abu Umar al-Duri, Abu Ibrahim al-Burjumani, from Sa'id ibn Sa'id, from Nahshal Abu Abd Allah al-Qurashi, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will not be troubled by the reckoning, nor will the cry frighten them, nor will the greatest terror grieve them: the bearer of the Qur'an who delivers it to Allah with what is in it, arriving before his Lord as a noble master; a muezzin who calls the adhan for seven years, taking payment for his adhan out of greed; and a slave who worships his Lord excellently and fulfils the right of his master." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/831, no. 43308, with slight variation.] [86]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu Amr ibn Uthman, related to them: Abu Thumayla, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for seven years seeking reward, a written quittance from the Fire is recorded for him." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/683, no. 20904; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/561, no. 8376.] [87]

Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi, Abu al-Ala Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir, [...] [illegible word], Muhammad ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd al-Tusi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for a year with a sincere intention, seeking no wage for it, will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection, stand at the gate of Paradise, and be told: Intercede for whom you wish." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/689, no. 20936.] [88]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamd al-Tammar, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Dinar, Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Isa, Ibrahim ibn Rustam, Hammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibn Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven, and whoever leads his companions in five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/562, no. 8378.] [89]

Abu al-Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jasham Abu al-Mawja, Abdan, Abd al-Warith, Murra al-Hanafi, Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When the adhan is called, the gates of heaven are opened and supplication is answered; and when the iqamah is called, a supplication is not turned away." [Kanz al-Ummal: 2/108, no. 3372.] [90]

Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn al-Ma'arri, Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Muqri in Basra, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Jassas, Yazid ibn Amr, Abu al-Bar al-Ghanawi, Nail ibn Najih, Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Salim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The muezzin who seeks reward is like a martyr writhing in his blood until he finishes his adhan; every moist and dry thing bears witness for him, and when he dies, his grave will not decay." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/3.] [91]

Abu Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Safyani, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari said: Hammad ibn al-Hasan, Salih ibn Sulayman, the owner of the qarati(s), Attab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Sadusi, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Waqqas, that he said: The arrows of the muezzins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the emigrants.

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: If I were a muezzin, I would not mind not performing Hajj, not performing Umrah, and not fighting in jihad.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not being counted among those who pray at night or fast by day. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins."

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have left us, though we are the best, to call the adhan with swords." He said: "Not so, O Umar. There will come upon people a time when they abandon the adhan for their weak ones; and those are flesh which Allah has forbidden to the Fire: the flesh of the muezzins." [92]

Say: O People of the Book, do you blame us only because… (the verse).

Ibn Abbas said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Abu Yasir ibn al-Khattab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', Azar, Zayd ibn Khalid, and Azarail Abu Washa'. They asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "I believe in Allah, and in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to Abraham… and to Him we are submitting Muslims." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/233, where it reads "yu'min" instead of "u'min".] [93] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "By Allah, we know of no people whose religion is more favoured in this world and the next than ours; the worst of religions is your religion." So Allah revealed this verse.

Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that?"—i.e., I will inform you of what you described, their saying, "We have not seen a people more favoured in this world and the next than you." He mentioned the answer in the form of a beginning, though the beginning itself is not evil, like His saying to the disbelievers: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 72]. ﴿Requital (mathuba) with Allah﴾: reward and recompense, and it is in the accusative as an explanation, like His saying ﴿more in wealth and mightier in following﴾. Its original form is mathuwba, on the pattern of its object-form, as some verbal nouns came on the pattern of the passive participle, such as al-maf'ul and al-maysur; the vowel of the middle radical was dropped because of the heaviness of the waw, and its vowel was transferred to the first radical, which is tha', so it became mathuba, like ma'una and maghuth and maqula. ﴿Whom Allah has cursed﴾: it may be in the genitive as a substitution from "bi-sharrin," or with the meaning "for whom Allah has cursed"; it may be in the nominative with an implied "huwa" (he); and it may be in the accusative by placing "unabbi'ukum" upon it. ﴿And Allah became angry with him, and made some of them apes and swine﴾: the apes are the people of the Sabbath, and the swine are the disbelievers among the people of the table of Jesus.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas that both groups transformed were from their leaders: the ones who were transformed into apes were from their nobles, and their elders were transformed into swine. ﴿And worshipped the Taghut﴾: there are ten readings for it. ﴿Wa-'abada al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the ba', the 'ayn, and the ta', as a verb, which is the reading of the common people; and ﴿and made from them one who worshipped the Taghut﴾, and its confirmation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿and those who worshipped the Taghut﴾. Ibn Wathhab and Hamza read ﴿'abdu al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the 'ayn, damma on the ba', and kasra on the dal, meaning "the servant," and both are dialects: 'abd and 'abd, like sab' and sab', qird and qird.

Hamza recited in support of this: "How polished is the ape…" with damma on the ra'. Another interpretation is that he meant the plural, i.e., the servants of the Taghut. The plural of 'abd is 'ibad, then the plural of 'ibad is 'abad, a plural of a plural, like thimar and thamr. He encountered two successive dammas, so he changed the first to fatha; hence in the reading of al-A'mash it is ﴿wa-'ubudu al-Taghut﴾ with damma on the 'ayn and the ta', and kasra on the dal.

The poet said:
"Trace the servant to his fathers, black-skinned of the people of 'abd."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/369.]

It is related from Abu Ja'far al-Qari that he read ﴿wa-'ubida al-Taghut﴾ as a passive verb. Al-Hasan read ﴿wa-'abda al-Taghut﴾ in the singular. Abu Burda al-Aslami read ﴿wa-'abid al-Taghut﴾ in the singular [with variation; so it is in the original]. Ibn Abbas read ﴿wa-'ubayd al-Taghut﴾ in the plural. Abu Waqid al-Laythi read ﴿wa-'abbad al-Taghut﴾, like kafir and kuffar. Awn al-'Uqayli and Aban ibn Tha'lab read ﴿wa-'ubbida al-Taghut﴾, like raka' and sajad. Ibn 'Umayr read ﴿wa-'ubd al-Taghut﴾, like kalb and aklub.

﴿Those are worse in place and further astray from the right way.﴾ When this verse was revealed, the Jews were humbled, saying: "Brothers of the apes and swine," and they fell silent and were confounded. Concerning them the poet said:
"So the curse of Allah be upon the Jews; indeed the Jews are brothers of the apes."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/236.]

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾ and the rest of the verse: these are the hypocrites, as the exegetes have said.

Ibn Zayd said: These are those who said: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day﴾ and the rest of the verse.

This interpretation is more fitting to the apparent sense of the revelation, because these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. ﴿And you see many of them—meaning of the Jews—hastening into sin and transgression and their consuming of the forbidden﴾ up to His saying ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ The "rabbis" (rabbaniyyun) are the scholars, and the "scholars" (ahbar) are the learned men; some said the rabbaniyyun are the Christian scholars and the ahbar are the Jewish scholars.

Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Ibn al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿al-Rabbiyyun﴾, like His saying ﴿with him were many rabbis﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 146].

﴿from their saying sin﴾. This is the most severe verse concerning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, since it places them in the position of those who commit it and joins them together in rebuke.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Adi, [al-Ahmasi] [as in the original], al-Bukhari, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No man lives as a neighbour among a people, practising sins in their midst, and they do not restrain his hands, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 2/332.] [94]

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, Abd Allah ibn Usama, Usayl ibn Zayd al-Jammal, Yahya ibn Salma ibn Muhanna, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of the wicked person among a people is like a people who boarded a ship and divided it, so each person had a share in it. A man among them took an axe and began striking at his place. His companions said: 'What are you doing? Do you want to sink it and sink us?' He said: 'It is my place. If they seize his hands, they are saved and he is saved; and if they leave him, they sink and he sinks.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 8/240, with variation.] [95]

Malik ibn Dinar said: Allah revealed to the angels that they should punish such-and-such a town. The angels cried out to their Lord: "O Lord, among them is Your servant, the worshipper." He said: "Let Me hear his cry, for his face has not changed in anger for My prohibitions." And Allah revealed to Joshua ibn Nun: "I will destroy forty thousand of your people, from their best, and sixty thousand of their worst." He said: "O Lord, these are the wicked; but what of the good?" He said: "They did not become angry for My anger, and they ate and drank with them."

O you who believe, do not take those who took your religion as a mockery and a game (for Allah's words: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game﴾), and the rest of the verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When the caller (muezzin) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews said: "They have risen, may they not rise! They have prayed, may they not pray! They have bowed, may they not bow! They have prostrated, may they not prostrate!" in a manner of mockery and laughter. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Christians who, whenever he heard the muezzin say, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "May Allah burn the liar." One night his servant came in with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark flew from it into the house, and it burned the house, and he and his family were burned.

Others said: When the disbelievers heard the adhan, they denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims over it, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you have invented something we have never heard of in the past nations. If you claim prophethood, you have opposed the prophets before you in this adhan you have introduced. If there were good in this matter, the first to abandon it would have been the people after the prophets and messengers before you. So where do you get a cry like the cry of a camel? No voice is uglier, and no disbelief is more repulsive." So Allah revealed this verse. (Source cited above.) ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work?﴾

As for after the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj, Ziyad ibn Ayyub, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr al-Asadi, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad said: Ibn Jurayj related from Nafi' from Ibn Umar; Abu al-Husayn said: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj, Muhammad ibn Suhayl ibn Askar, Abu Sa'id al-Haddad, Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn [Yahya], from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father; and a narration from al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, Isma'il ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i, Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from his father, who said: When the Muslims arrived in Medina, they would gather and anticipate the prayer, and no one called to it. They discussed this matter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted the Muslims about how to summon them to prayer. Some said: "Raise a banner on top of the mosque at the time of prayer, so when they see it, they will inform one another." He did not like that. It was said: "Rather, we light a fire." Others said: "Rather, a horn like the horn of the Jews." He disliked it because of the Jews. It was said: "A bell," and he disliked it because of the Christians. But they stood for it, and he ordered the bell to be used so that they might respond.

Abd Allah ibn Zayd said: That night I saw in a dream a man wearing two green garments, carrying a bell. I said: "O servant of Allah, will you sell the bell?" He said: "What will you do with it?" I said: "We call people to prayer with it." He said: "Shall I not guide you to something better than it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" until the end of the adhan. Then he withdrew a short distance and said: "When the prayer is established, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" and he described the iqamah to him, its phrases being singular. When I awoke, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of it. He said: "It is a true vision, if Allah wills. Recite it to Bilal, for he has a more resonant voice than you." So we went out to the mosque, and I began reciting it to Bilal while he was calling the adhan. Umar heard it in his house and came out dragging his cloak, saying: "I saw the same as what he saw." The Prophet ﷺ rejoiced and said: "That is more firmly established."

Abu al-Zahiriya related from Abu Shajara, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The first to call the adhan in heaven was the one whom Umar ibn al-Khattab heard." (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu)

As for the section on the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi, Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya, Abu Ja'far ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Sayyah, Abu Umar al-Duri, Abu Ibrahim al-Burjumani, from Sa'id ibn Sa'id, from Nahshal Abu Abd Allah al-Qurashi, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will not be troubled by the reckoning, nor will the cry frighten them, nor will the greatest terror grieve them: the bearer of the Qur'an who delivers it to Allah with what is in it, arriving before his Lord as a noble master; a muezzin who calls the adhan for seven years, taking payment for his adhan out of greed; and a slave who worships his Lord excellently and fulfils the right of his master." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/831, no. 43308, with slight variation.] [86]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu Amr ibn Uthman, related to them: Abu Thumayla, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for seven years seeking reward, a written quittance from the Fire is recorded for him." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/683, no. 20904; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/561, no. 8376.] [87]

Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi, Abu al-Ala Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir, [...] [illegible word], Muhammad ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd al-Tusi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for a year with a sincere intention, seeking no wage for it, will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection, stand at the gate of Paradise, and be told: Intercede for whom you wish." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/689, no. 20936.] [88]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamd al-Tammar, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Dinar, Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Isa, Ibrahim ibn Rustam, Hammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibn Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven, and whoever leads his companions in five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/562, no. 8378.] [89]

Abu al-Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jasham Abu al-Mawja, Abdan, Abd al-Warith, Murra al-Hanafi, Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When the adhan is called, the gates of heaven are opened and supplication is answered; and when the iqamah is called, a supplication is not turned away." [Kanz al-Ummal: 2/108, no. 3372.] [90]

Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn al-Ma'arri, Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Muqri in Basra, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Jassas, Yazid ibn Amr, Abu al-Bar al-Ghanawi, Nail ibn Najih, Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Salim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The muezzin who seeks reward is like a martyr writhing in his blood until he finishes his adhan; every moist and dry thing bears witness for him, and when he dies, his grave will not decay." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/3.] [91]

Abu Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Safyani, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari said: Hammad ibn al-Hasan, Salih ibn Sulayman, the owner of the qarati(s), Attab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Sadusi, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Waqqas, that he said: The arrows of the muezzins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the emigrants.

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: If I were a muezzin, I would not mind not performing Hajj, not performing Umrah, and not fighting in jihad.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not being counted among those who pray at night or fast by day. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins."

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have left us, though we are the best, to call the adhan with swords." He said: "Not so, O Umar. There will come upon people a time when they abandon the adhan for their weak ones; and those are flesh which Allah has forbidden to the Fire: the flesh of the muezzins." [92]

Say: O People of the Book, do you blame us only because… (the verse).

Ibn Abbas said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Abu Yasir ibn al-Khattab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', Azar, Zayd ibn Khalid, and Azarail Abu Washa'. They asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "I believe in Allah, and in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to Abraham… and to Him we are submitting Muslims." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/233, where it reads "yu'min" instead of "u'min".] [93] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "By Allah, we know of no people whose religion is more favoured in this world and the next than ours; the worst of religions is your religion." So Allah revealed this verse.

Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that?"—i.e., I will inform you of what you described, their saying, "We have not seen a people more favoured in this world and the next than you." He mentioned the answer in the form of a beginning, though the beginning itself is not evil, like His saying to the disbelievers: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 72]. ﴿Requital (mathuba) with Allah﴾: reward and recompense, and it is in the accusative as an explanation, like His saying ﴿more in wealth and mightier in following﴾. Its original form is mathuwba, on the pattern of its object-form, as some verbal nouns came on the pattern of the passive participle, such as al-maf'ul and al-maysur; the vowel of the middle radical was dropped because of the heaviness of the waw, and its vowel was transferred to the first radical, which is tha', so it became mathuba, like ma'una and maghuth and maqula. ﴿Whom Allah has cursed﴾: it may be in the genitive as a substitution from "bi-sharrin," or with the meaning "for whom Allah has cursed"; it may be in the nominative with an implied "huwa" (he); and it may be in the accusative by placing "unabbi'ukum" upon it. ﴿And Allah became angry with him, and made some of them apes and swine﴾: the apes are the people of the Sabbath, and the swine are the disbelievers among the people of the table of Jesus.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas that both groups transformed were from their leaders: the ones who were transformed into apes were from their nobles, and their elders were transformed into swine. ﴿And worshipped the Taghut﴾: there are ten readings for it. ﴿Wa-'abada al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the ba', the 'ayn, and the ta', as a verb, which is the reading of the common people; and ﴿and made from them one who worshipped the Taghut﴾, and its confirmation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿and those who worshipped the Taghut﴾. Ibn Wathhab and Hamza read ﴿'abdu al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the 'ayn, damma on the ba', and kasra on the dal, meaning "the servant," and both are dialects: 'abd and 'abd, like sab' and sab', qird and qird.

Hamza recited in support of this: "How polished is the ape…" with damma on the ra'. Another interpretation is that he meant the plural, i.e., the servants of the Taghut. The plural of 'abd is 'ibad, then the plural of 'ibad is 'abad, a plural of a plural, like thimar and thamr. He encountered two successive dammas, so he changed the first to fatha; hence in the reading of al-A'mash it is ﴿wa-'ubudu al-Taghut﴾ with damma on the 'ayn and the ta', and kasra on the dal.

The poet said:
"Trace the servant to his fathers, black-skinned of the people of 'abd."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/369.]

It is related from Abu Ja'far al-Qari that he read ﴿wa-'ubida al-Taghut﴾ as a passive verb. Al-Hasan read ﴿wa-'abda al-Taghut﴾ in the singular. Abu Burda al-Aslami read ﴿wa-'abid al-Taghut﴾ in the singular [with variation; so it is in the original]. Ibn Abbas read ﴿wa-'ubayd al-Taghut﴾ in the plural. Abu Waqid al-Laythi read ﴿wa-'abbad al-Taghut﴾, like kafir and kuffar. Awn al-'Uqayli and Aban ibn Tha'lab read ﴿wa-'ubbida al-Taghut﴾, like raka' and sajad. Ibn 'Umayr read ﴿wa-'ubd al-Taghut﴾, like kalb and aklub.

﴿Those are worse in place and further astray from the right way.﴾ When this verse was revealed, the Jews were humbled, saying: "Brothers of the apes and swine," and they fell silent and were confounded. Concerning them the poet said:
"So the curse of Allah be upon the Jews; indeed the Jews are brothers of the apes."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/236.]

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾ and the rest of the verse: these are the hypocrites, as the exegetes have said.

Ibn Zayd said: These are those who said: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day﴾ and the rest of the verse.

This interpretation is more fitting to the apparent sense of the revelation, because these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. ﴿And you see many of them—meaning of the Jews—hastening into sin and transgression and their consuming of the forbidden﴾ up to His saying ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ The "rabbis" (rabbaniyyun) are the scholars, and the "scholars" (ahbar) are the learned men; some said the rabbaniyyun are the Christian scholars and the ahbar are the Jewish scholars.

Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Ibn al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿al-Rabbiyyun﴾, like His saying ﴿with him were many rabbis﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 146].

﴿from their saying sin﴾. This is the most severe verse concerning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, since it places them in the position of those who commit it and joins them together in rebuke.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Adi, [al-Ahmasi] [as in the original], al-Bukhari, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No man lives as a neighbour among a people, practising sins in their midst, and they do not restrain his hands, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 2/332.] [94]

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, Abd Allah ibn Usama, Usayl ibn Zayd al-Jammal, Yahya ibn Salma ibn Muhanna, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of the wicked person among a people is like a people who boarded a ship and divided it, so each person had a share in it. A man among them took an axe and began striking at his place. His companions said: 'What are you doing? Do you want to sink it and sink us?' He said: 'It is my place. If they seize his hands, they are saved and he is saved; and if they leave him, they sink and he sinks.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 8/240, with variation.] [95]

Malik ibn Dinar said: Allah revealed to the angels that they should punish such-and-such a town. The angels cried out to their Lord: "O Lord, among them is Your servant, the worshipper." He said: "Let Me hear his cry, for his face has not changed in anger for My prohibitions." And Allah revealed to Joshua ibn Nun: "I will destroy forty thousand of your people, from their best, and sixty thousand of their worst." He said: "O Lord, these are the wicked; but what of the good?" He said: "They did not become angry for My anger, and they ate and drank with them."

O you who believe, do not take those who took your religion as a mockery and a game (for Allah's words: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game﴾), and the rest of the verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When the caller (muezzin) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews said: "They have risen, may they not rise! They have prayed, may they not pray! They have bowed, may they not bow! They have prostrated, may they not prostrate!" in a manner of mockery and laughter. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Christians who, whenever he heard the muezzin say, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "May Allah burn the liar." One night his servant came in with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark flew from it into the house, and it burned the house, and he and his family were burned.

Others said: When the disbelievers heard the adhan, they denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims over it, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you have invented something we have never heard of in the past nations. If you claim prophethood, you have opposed the prophets before you in this adhan you have introduced. If there were good in this matter, the first to abandon it would have been the people after the prophets and messengers before you. So where do you get a cry like the cry of a camel? No voice is uglier, and no disbelief is more repulsive." So Allah revealed this verse. (Source cited above.) ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work?﴾

As for after the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj, Ziyad ibn Ayyub, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr al-Asadi, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad said: Ibn Jurayj related from Nafi' from Ibn Umar; Abu al-Husayn said: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj, Muhammad ibn Suhayl ibn Askar, Abu Sa'id al-Haddad, Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn [Yahya], from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father; and a narration from al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, Isma'il ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i, Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from his father, who said: When the Muslims arrived in Medina, they would gather and anticipate the prayer, and no one called to it. They discussed this matter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted the Muslims about how to summon them to prayer. Some said: "Raise a banner on top of the mosque at the time of prayer, so when they see it, they will inform one another." He did not like that. It was said: "Rather, we light a fire." Others said: "Rather, a horn like the horn of the Jews." He disliked it because of the Jews. It was said: "A bell," and he disliked it because of the Christians. But they stood for it, and he ordered the bell to be used so that they might respond.

Abd Allah ibn Zayd said: That night I saw in a dream a man wearing two green garments, carrying a bell. I said: "O servant of Allah, will you sell the bell?" He said: "What will you do with it?" I said: "We call people to prayer with it." He said: "Shall I not guide you to something better than it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" until the end of the adhan. Then he withdrew a short distance and said: "When the prayer is established, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" and he described the iqamah to him, its phrases being singular. When I awoke, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of it. He said: "It is a true vision, if Allah wills. Recite it to Bilal, for he has a more resonant voice than you." So we went out to the mosque, and I began reciting it to Bilal while he was calling the adhan. Umar heard it in his house and came out dragging his cloak, saying: "I saw the same as what he saw." The Prophet ﷺ rejoiced and said: "That is more firmly established."

Abu al-Zahiriya related from Abu Shajara, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The first to call the adhan in heaven was the one whom Umar ibn al-Khattab heard." (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu)

As for the section on the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi, Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya, Abu Ja'far ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Sayyah, Abu Umar al-Duri, Abu Ibrahim al-Burjumani, from Sa'id ibn Sa'id, from Nahshal Abu Abd Allah al-Qurashi, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will not be troubled by the reckoning, nor will the cry frighten them, nor will the greatest terror grieve them: the bearer of the Qur'an who delivers it to Allah with what is in it, arriving before his Lord as a noble master; a muezzin who calls the adhan for seven years, taking payment for his adhan out of greed; and a slave who worships his Lord excellently and fulfils the right of his master." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/831, no. 43308, with slight variation.] [86]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu Amr ibn Uthman, related to them: Abu Thumayla, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for seven years seeking reward, a written quittance from the Fire is recorded for him." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/683, no. 20904; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/561, no. 8376.] [87]

Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi, Abu al-Ala Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir, [...] [illegible word], Muhammad ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd al-Tusi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for a year with a sincere intention, seeking no wage for it, will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection, stand at the gate of Paradise, and be told: Intercede for whom you wish." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/689, no. 20936.] [88]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamd al-Tammar, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Dinar, Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Isa, Ibrahim ibn Rustam, Hammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibn Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven, and whoever leads his companions in five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/562, no. 8378.] [89]

Abu al-Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jasham Abu al-Mawja, Abdan, Abd al-Warith, Murra al-Hanafi, Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When the adhan is called, the gates of heaven are opened and supplication is answered; and when the iqamah is called, a supplication is not turned away." [Kanz al-Ummal: 2/108, no. 3372.] [90]

Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn al-Ma'arri, Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Muqri in Basra, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Jassas, Yazid ibn Amr, Abu al-Bar al-Ghanawi, Nail ibn Najih, Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Salim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The muezzin who seeks reward is like a martyr writhing in his blood until he finishes his adhan; every moist and dry thing bears witness for him, and when he dies, his grave will not decay." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/3.] [91]

Abu Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Safyani, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari said: Hammad ibn al-Hasan, Salih ibn Sulayman, the owner of the qarati(s), Attab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Sadusi, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Waqqas, that he said: The arrows of the muezzins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the emigrants.

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: If I were a muezzin, I would not mind not performing Hajj, not performing Umrah, and not fighting in jihad.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not being counted among those who pray at night or fast by day. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins."

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have left us, though we are the best, to call the adhan with swords." He said: "Not so, O Umar. There will come upon people a time when they abandon the adhan for their weak ones; and those are flesh which Allah has forbidden to the Fire: the flesh of the muezzins." [92]

Say: O People of the Book, do you blame us only because… (the verse).

Ibn Abbas said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Abu Yasir ibn al-Khattab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', Azar, Zayd ibn Khalid, and Azarail Abu Washa'. They asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "I believe in Allah, and in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to Abraham… and to Him we are submitting Muslims." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/233, where it reads "yu'min" instead of "u'min".] [93] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "By Allah, we know of no people whose religion is more favoured in this world and the next than ours; the worst of religions is your religion." So Allah revealed this verse.

Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that?"—i.e., I will inform you of what you described, their saying, "We have not seen a people more favoured in this world and the next than you." He mentioned the answer in the form of a beginning, though the beginning itself is not evil, like His saying to the disbelievers: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? Ibn Wathhab and Hamza read ﴿'abdu al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the 'ayn, damma on the ba', and kasra on the dal, meaning "the servant," and both are dialects: 'abd and 'abd, like sab' and sab', qird and qird.

"Trace the servant to his fathers, black-skinned of the people of 'abd."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/369.]

Abu Burda al-Aslami read ﴿wa-'abid al-Taghut﴾ in the singular [with variation; so it is in the original]. Ibn Abbas read ﴿wa-'ubayd al-Taghut﴾ in the plural. Abu Waqid al-Laythi read ﴿wa-'abbad al-Taghut﴾, like kafir and kuffar. Awn al-'Uqayli and Aban ibn Tha'lab read ﴿wa-'ubbida al-Taghut﴾, like raka' and sajad. Ibn 'Umayr read ﴿wa-'ubd al-Taghut﴾, like kalb and aklub.

﴿Those are worse in place and further astray from the right way.﴾ When this verse was revealed, the Jews were humbled, saying: "Brothers of the apes and swine," and they fell silent and were confounded. Concerning them the poet said:
"So the curse of Allah be upon the Jews; indeed the Jews are brothers of the apes."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/236.]

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾ and the rest of the verse: these are the hypocrites, as the exegetes have said.
