Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Ibn al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿al-Rabbiyyun﴾, like His saying ﴿with him were many rabbis﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 146].

﴿from their saying sin﴾. This is the most severe verse concerning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, since it places them in the position of those who commit it and joins them together in rebuke.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Adi, [al-Ahmasi] [as in the original], al-Bukhari, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No man lives as a neighbour among a people, practising sins in their midst, and they do not restrain his hands, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 2/332.] [94]

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, Abd Allah ibn Usama, Usayl ibn Zayd al-Jammal, Yahya ibn Salma ibn Muhanna, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of the wicked person among a people is like a people who boarded a ship and divided it, so each person had a share in it. A man among them took an axe and began striking at his place. His companions said: 'What are you doing? Do you want to sink it and sink us?' He said: 'It is my place. If they seize his hands, they are saved and he is saved; and if they leave him, they sink and he sinks.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 8/240, with variation.] [95]

Malik ibn Dinar said: Allah revealed to the angels that they should punish such-and-such a town. The angels cried out to their Lord: "O Lord, among them is Your servant, the worshipper." He said: "Let Me hear his cry, for his face has not changed in anger for My prohibitions." And Allah revealed to Joshua ibn Nun: "I will destroy forty thousand of your people, from their best, and sixty thousand of their worst." He said: "O Lord, these are the wicked; but what of the good?" He said: "They did not become angry for My anger, and they ate and drank with them."

O you who believe, do not take those who took your religion as a mockery and a game (for Allah's words: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game﴾), and the rest of the verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When the caller (muezzin) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews said: "They have risen, may they not rise! They have prayed, may they not pray! They have bowed, may they not bow! They have prostrated, may they not prostrate!" in a manner of mockery and laughter. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Christians who, whenever he heard the muezzin say, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "May Allah burn the liar." One night his servant came in with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark flew from it into the house, and it burned the house, and he and his family were burned.

Others said: When the disbelievers heard the adhan, they denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims over it, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you have invented something we have never heard of in the past nations. If you claim prophethood, you have opposed the prophets before you in this adhan you have introduced. If there were good in this matter, the first to abandon it would have been the people after the prophets and messengers before you. So where do you get a cry like the cry of a camel? No voice is uglier, and no disbelief is more repulsive." So Allah revealed this verse. (Source cited above.) ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work?﴾

As for after the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj, Ziyad ibn Ayyub, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr al-Asadi, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad said: Ibn Jurayj related from Nafi' from Ibn Umar; Abu al-Husayn said: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj, Muhammad ibn Suhayl ibn Askar, Abu Sa'id al-Haddad, Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn [Yahya], from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father; and a narration from al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, Isma'il ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i, Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from his father, who said: When the Muslims arrived in Medina, they would gather and anticipate the prayer, and no one called to it. They discussed this matter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted the Muslims about how to summon them to prayer. Some said: "Raise a banner on top of the mosque at the time of prayer, so when they see it, they will inform one another." He did not like that. It was said: "Rather, we light a fire." Others said: "Rather, a horn like the horn of the Jews." He disliked it because of the Jews. It was said: "A bell," and he disliked it because of the Christians. But they stood for it, and he ordered the bell to be used so that they might respond.

Abd Allah ibn Zayd said: That night I saw in a dream a man wearing two green garments, carrying a bell. I said: "O servant of Allah, will you sell the bell?" He said: "What will you do with it?" I said: "We call people to prayer with it." He said: "Shall I not guide you to something better than it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" until the end of the adhan. Then he withdrew a short distance and said: "When the prayer is established, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" and he described the iqamah to him, its phrases being singular. When I awoke, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of it. He said: "It is a true vision, if Allah wills. Recite it to Bilal, for he has a more resonant voice than you." So we went out to the mosque, and I began reciting it to Bilal while he was calling the adhan. Umar heard it in his house and came out dragging his cloak, saying: "I saw the same as what he saw." The Prophet ﷺ rejoiced and said: "That is more firmly established."

Abu al-Zahiriya related from Abu Shajara, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The first to call the adhan in heaven was the one whom Umar ibn al-Khattab heard." (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu)

As for the section on the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi, Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya, Abu Ja'far ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Sayyah, Abu Umar al-Duri, Abu Ibrahim al-Burjumani, from Sa'id ibn Sa'id, from Nahshal Abu Abd Allah al-Qurashi, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will not be troubled by the reckoning, nor will the cry frighten them, nor will the greatest terror grieve them: the bearer of the Qur'an who delivers it to Allah with what is in it, arriving before his Lord as a noble master; a muezzin who calls the adhan for seven years, taking payment for his adhan out of greed; and a slave who worships his Lord excellently and fulfils the right of his master." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/831, no. 43308, with slight variation.] [86]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu Amr ibn Uthman, related to them: Abu Thumayla, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for seven years seeking reward, a written quittance from the Fire is recorded for him." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/683, no. 20904; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/561, no. 8376.] [87]

Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi, Abu al-Ala Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir, [...] [illegible word], Muhammad ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd al-Tusi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for a year with a sincere intention, seeking no wage for it, will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection, stand at the gate of Paradise, and be told: Intercede for whom you wish." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/689, no. 20936.] [88]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamd al-Tammar, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Dinar, Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Isa, Ibrahim ibn Rustam, Hammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibn Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven, and whoever leads his companions in five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/562, no. 8378.] [89]

Abu al-Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jasham Abu al-Mawja, Abdan, Abd al-Warith, Murra al-Hanafi, Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When the adhan is called, the gates of heaven are opened and supplication is answered; and when the iqamah is called, a supplication is not turned away." [Kanz al-Ummal: 2/108, no. 3372.] [90]

Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn al-Ma'arri, Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Muqri in Basra, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Jassas, Yazid ibn Amr, Abu al-Bar al-Ghanawi, Nail ibn Najih, Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Salim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The muezzin who seeks reward is like a martyr writhing in his blood until he finishes his adhan; every moist and dry thing bears witness for him, and when he dies, his grave will not decay." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/3.] [91]

Abu Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Safyani, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari said: Hammad ibn al-Hasan, Salih ibn Sulayman, the owner of the qarati(s), Attab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Sadusi, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Waqqas, that he said: The arrows of the muezzins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the emigrants.

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: If I were a muezzin, I would not mind not performing Hajj, not performing Umrah, and not fighting in jihad.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not being counted among those who pray at night or fast by day. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins."

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have left us, though we are the best, to call the adhan with swords." He said: "Not so, O Umar. There will come upon people a time when they abandon the adhan for their weak ones; and those are flesh which Allah has forbidden to the Fire: the flesh of the muezzins." [92]

Say: O People of the Book, do you blame us only because… (the verse).

Ibn Abbas said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Abu Yasir ibn al-Khattab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', Azar, Zayd ibn Khalid, and Azarail Abu Washa'. They asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "I believe in Allah, and in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to Abraham… and to Him we are submitting Muslims." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/233, where it reads "yu'min" instead of "u'min".] [93] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "By Allah, we know of no people whose religion is more favoured in this world and the next than ours; the worst of religions is your religion." So Allah revealed this verse.

Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that?"—i.e., I will inform you of what you described, their saying, "We have not seen a people more favoured in this world and the next than you." He mentioned the answer in the form of a beginning, though the beginning itself is not evil, like His saying to the disbelievers: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 72]. ﴿Requital (mathuba) with Allah﴾: reward and recompense, and it is in the accusative as an explanation, like His saying ﴿more in wealth and mightier in following﴾. Its original form is mathuwba, on the pattern of its object-form, as some verbal nouns came on the pattern of the passive participle, such as al-maf'ul and al-maysur; the vowel of the middle radical was dropped because of the heaviness of the waw, and its vowel was transferred to the first radical, which is tha', so it became mathuba, like ma'una and maghuth and maqula. ﴿Whom Allah has cursed﴾: it may be in the genitive as a substitution from "bi-sharrin," or with the meaning "for whom Allah has cursed"; it may be in the nominative with an implied "huwa" (he); and it may be in the accusative by placing "unabbi'ukum" upon it. ﴿And Allah became angry with him, and made some of them apes and swine﴾: the apes are the people of the Sabbath, and the swine are the disbelievers among the people of the table of Jesus.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas that both groups transformed were from their leaders: the ones who were transformed into apes were from their nobles, and their elders were transformed into swine. ﴿And worshipped the Taghut﴾: there are ten readings for it. ﴿Wa-'abada al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the ba', the 'ayn, and the ta', as a verb, which is the reading of the common people; and ﴿and made from them one who worshipped the Taghut﴾, and its confirmation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿and those who worshipped the Taghut﴾. Ibn Wathhab and Hamza read ﴿'abdu al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the 'ayn, damma on the ba', and kasra on the dal, meaning "the servant," and both are dialects: 'abd and 'abd, like sab' and sab', qird and qird.

Hamza recited in support of this: "How polished is the ape…" with damma on the ra'. Another interpretation is that he meant the plural, i.e., the servants of the Taghut. The plural of 'abd is 'ibad, then the plural of 'ibad is 'abad, a plural of a plural, like thimar and thamr. He encountered two successive dammas, so he changed the first to fatha; hence in the reading of al-A'mash it is ﴿wa-'ubudu al-Taghut﴾ with damma on the 'ayn and the ta', and kasra on the dal.

The poet said:
"Trace the servant to his fathers, black-skinned of the people of 'abd."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/369.]

It is related from Abu Ja'far al-Qari that he read ﴿wa-'ubida al-Taghut﴾ as a passive verb. Al-Hasan read ﴿wa-'abda al-Taghut﴾ in the singular. Abu Burda al-Aslami read ﴿wa-'abid al-Taghut﴾ in the singular [with variation; so it is in the original]. Ibn Abbas read ﴿wa-'ubayd al-Taghut﴾ in the plural. Abu Waqid al-Laythi read ﴿wa-'abbad al-Taghut﴾, like kafir and kuffar. Awn al-'Uqayli and Aban ibn Tha'lab read ﴿wa-'ubbida al-Taghut﴾, like raka' and sajad. Ibn 'Umayr read ﴿wa-'ubd al-Taghut﴾, like kalb and aklub.

﴿Those are worse in place and further astray from the right way.﴾ When this verse was revealed, the Jews were humbled, saying: "Brothers of the apes and swine," and they fell silent and were confounded. Concerning them the poet said:
"So the curse of Allah be upon the Jews; indeed the Jews are brothers of the apes."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/236.]

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾ and the rest of the verse: these are the hypocrites, as the exegetes have said.

Ibn Zayd said: These are those who said: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day﴾ and the rest of the verse.

This interpretation is more fitting to the apparent sense of the revelation, because these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. ﴿And you see many of them—meaning of the Jews—hastening into sin and transgression and their consuming of the forbidden﴾ up to His saying ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ The "rabbis" (rabbaniyyun) are the scholars, and the "scholars" (ahbar) are the learned men; some said the rabbaniyyun are the Christian scholars and the ahbar are the Jewish scholars.

Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Ibn al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿al-Rabbiyyun﴾, like His saying ﴿with him were many rabbis﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 146].

﴿from their saying sin﴾. This is the most severe verse concerning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, since it places them in the position of those who commit it and joins them together in rebuke.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Adi, [al-Ahmasi] [as in the original], al-Bukhari, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No man lives as a neighbour among a people, practising sins in their midst, and they do not restrain his hands, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 2/332.] [94]

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, Abd Allah ibn Usama, Usayl ibn Zayd al-Jammal, Yahya ibn Salma ibn Muhanna, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of the wicked person among a people is like a people who boarded a ship and divided it, so each person had a share in it. A man among them took an axe and began striking at his place. His companions said: 'What are you doing? Do you want to sink it and sink us?' He said: 'It is my place. If they seize his hands, they are saved and he is saved; and if they leave him, they sink and he sinks.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 8/240, with variation.] [95]

Malik ibn Dinar said: Allah revealed to the angels that they should punish such-and-such a town. The angels cried out to their Lord: "O Lord, among them is Your servant, the worshipper." He said: "Let Me hear his cry, for his face has not changed in anger for My prohibitions." And Allah revealed to Joshua ibn Nun: "I will destroy forty thousand of your people, from their best, and sixty thousand of their worst." He said: "O Lord, these are the wicked; but what of the good?" He said: "They did not become angry for My anger, and they ate and drank with them."

O you who believe, do not take those who took your religion as a mockery and a game (for Allah's words: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game﴾), and the rest of the verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When the caller (muezzin) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews said: "They have risen, may they not rise! They have prayed, may they not pray! They have bowed, may they not bow! They have prostrated, may they not prostrate!" in a manner of mockery and laughter. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Christians who, whenever he heard the muezzin say, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "May Allah burn the liar." One night his servant came in with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark flew from it into the house, and it burned the house, and he and his family were burned.

Others said: When the disbelievers heard the adhan, they denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims over it, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you have invented something we have never heard of in the past nations. If you claim prophethood, you have opposed the prophets before you in this adhan you have introduced. If there were good in this matter, the first to abandon it would have been the people after the prophets and messengers before you. So where do you get a cry like the cry of a camel? No voice is uglier, and no disbelief is more repulsive." So Allah revealed this verse. (Source cited above.) ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work?﴾

As for after the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj, Ziyad ibn Ayyub, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr al-Asadi, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad said: Ibn Jurayj related from Nafi' from Ibn Umar; Abu al-Husayn said: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj, Muhammad ibn Suhayl ibn Askar, Abu Sa'id al-Haddad, Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn [Yahya], from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father; and a narration from al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, Isma'il ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i, Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from his father, who said: When the Muslims arrived in Medina, they would gather and anticipate the prayer, and no one called to it. They discussed this matter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted the Muslims about how to summon them to prayer. Some said: "Raise a banner on top of the mosque at the time of prayer, so when they see it, they will inform one another." He did not like that. It was said: "Rather, we light a fire." Others said: "Rather, a horn like the horn of the Jews." He disliked it because of the Jews. It was said: "A bell," and he disliked it because of the Christians. But they stood for it, and he ordered the bell to be used so that they might respond.

Abd Allah ibn Zayd said: That night I saw in a dream a man wearing two green garments, carrying a bell. I said: "O servant of Allah, will you sell the bell?" He said: "What will you do with it?" I said: "We call people to prayer with it." He said: "Shall I not guide you to something better than it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" until the end of the adhan. Then he withdrew a short distance and said: "When the prayer is established, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" and he described the iqamah to him, its phrases being singular. When I awoke, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of it. He said: "It is a true vision, if Allah wills. Recite it to Bilal, for he has a more resonant voice than you." So we went out to the mosque, and I began reciting it to Bilal while he was calling the adhan. Umar heard it in his house and came out dragging his cloak, saying: "I saw the same as what he saw." The Prophet ﷺ rejoiced and said: "That is more firmly established."

Abu al-Zahiriya related from Abu Shajara, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The first to call the adhan in heaven was the one whom Umar ibn al-Khattab heard." (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu)

As for the section on the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi, Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya, Abu Ja'far ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Sayyah, Abu Umar al-Duri, Abu Ibrahim al-Burjumani, from Sa'id ibn Sa'id, from Nahshal Abu Abd Allah al-Qurashi, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will not be troubled by the reckoning, nor will the cry frighten them, nor will the greatest terror grieve them: the bearer of the Qur'an who delivers it to Allah with what is in it, arriving before his Lord as a noble master; a muezzin who calls the adhan for seven years, taking payment for his adhan out of greed; and a slave who worships his Lord excellently and fulfils the right of his master." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/831, no. 43308, with slight variation.] [86]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu Amr ibn Uthman, related to them: Abu Thumayla, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for seven years seeking reward, a written quittance from the Fire is recorded for him." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/683, no. 20904; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/561, no. 8376.] [87]

Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi, Abu al-Ala Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir, [...] [illegible word], Muhammad ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd al-Tusi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for a year with a sincere intention, seeking no wage for it, will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection, stand at the gate of Paradise, and be told: Intercede for whom you wish." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/689, no. 20936.] [88]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamd al-Tammar, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Dinar, Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Isa, Ibrahim ibn Rustam, Hammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibn Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven, and whoever leads his companions in five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/562, no. 8378.] [89]

Abu al-Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jasham Abu al-Mawja, Abdan, Abd al-Warith, Murra al-Hanafi, Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When the adhan is called, the gates of heaven are opened and supplication is answered; and when the iqamah is called, a supplication is not turned away." [Kanz al-Ummal: 2/108, no. 3372.] [90]

Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn al-Ma'arri, Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Muqri in Basra, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Jassas, Yazid ibn Amr, Abu al-Bar al-Ghanawi, Nail ibn Najih, Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Salim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The muezzin who seeks reward is like a martyr writhing in his blood until he finishes his adhan; every moist and dry thing bears witness for him, and when he dies, his grave will not decay." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/3.] [91]

Abu Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Safyani, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari said: Hammad ibn al-Hasan, Salih ibn Sulayman, the owner of the qarati(s), Attab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Sadusi, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Waqqas, that he said: The arrows of the muezzins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the emigrants.

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: If I were a muezzin, I would not mind not performing Hajj, not performing Umrah, and not fighting in jihad.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not being counted among those who pray at night or fast by day. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins."

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have left us, though we are the best, to call the adhan with swords." He said: "Not so, O Umar. There will come upon people a time when they abandon the adhan for their weak ones; and those are flesh which Allah has forbidden to the Fire: the flesh of the muezzins." [92]

Say: O People of the Book, do you blame us only because… (the verse).

Ibn Abbas said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Abu Yasir ibn al-Khattab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', Azar, Zayd ibn Khalid, and Azarail Abu Washa'. They asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "I believe in Allah, and in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to Abraham… and to Him we are submitting Muslims." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/233, where it reads "yu'min" instead of "u'min".] [93] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "By Allah, we know of no people whose religion is more favoured in this world and the next than ours; the worst of religions is your religion." So Allah revealed this verse.

Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that?"—i.e., I will inform you of what you described, their saying, "We have not seen a people more favoured in this world and the next than you." He mentioned the answer in the form of a beginning, though the beginning itself is not evil, like His saying to the disbelievers: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 72]. ﴿Requital (mathuba) with Allah﴾: reward and recompense, and it is in the accusative as an explanation, like His saying ﴿more in wealth and mightier in following﴾. Its original form is mathuwba, on the pattern of its object-form, as some verbal nouns came on the pattern of the passive participle, such as al-maf'ul and al-maysur; the vowel of the middle radical was dropped because of the heaviness of the waw, and its vowel was transferred to the first radical, which is tha', so it became mathuba, like ma'una and maghuth and maqula. ﴿Whom Allah has cursed﴾: it may be in the genitive as a substitution from "bi-sharrin," or with the meaning "for whom Allah has cursed"; it may be in the nominative with an implied "huwa" (he); and it may be in the accusative by placing "unabbi'ukum" upon it. ﴿And Allah became angry with him, and made some of them apes and swine﴾: the apes are the people of the Sabbath, and the swine are the disbelievers among the people of the table of Jesus.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas that both groups transformed were from their leaders: the ones who were transformed into apes were from their nobles, and their elders were transformed into swine. ﴿And worshipped the Taghut﴾: there are ten readings for it. ﴿Wa-'abada al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the ba', the 'ayn, and the ta', as a verb, which is the reading of the common people; and ﴿and made from them one who worshipped the Taghut﴾, and its confirmation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿and those who worshipped the Taghut﴾. Ibn Wathhab and Hamza read ﴿'abdu al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the 'ayn, damma on the ba', and kasra on the dal, meaning "the servant," and both are dialects: 'abd and 'abd, like sab' and sab', qird and qird.

Hamza recited in support of this: "How polished is the ape…" with damma on the ra'. Another interpretation is that he meant the plural, i.e., the servants of the Taghut. The plural of 'abd is 'ibad, then the plural of 'ibad is 'abad, a plural of a plural, like thimar and thamr. He encountered two successive dammas, so he changed the first to fatha; hence in the reading of al-A'mash it is ﴿wa-'ubudu al-Taghut﴾ with damma on the 'ayn and the ta', and kasra on the dal.

The poet said:
"Trace the servant to his fathers, black-skinned of the people of 'abd."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/369.]

It is related from Abu Ja'far al-Qari that he read ﴿wa-'ubida al-Taghut﴾ as a passive verb. Al-Hasan read ﴿wa-'abda al-Taghut﴾ in the singular. Abu Burda al-Aslami read ﴿wa-'abid al-Taghut﴾ in the singular [with variation; so it is in the original]. Ibn Abbas read ﴿wa-'ubayd al-Taghut﴾ in the plural. Abu Waqid al-Laythi read ﴿wa-'abbad al-Taghut﴾, like kafir and kuffar. Awn al-'Uqayli and Aban ibn Tha'lab read ﴿wa-'ubbida al-Taghut﴾, like raka' and sajad. Ibn 'Umayr read ﴿wa-'ubd al-Taghut﴾, like kalb and aklub.

﴿Those are worse in place and further astray from the right way.﴾ When this verse was revealed, the Jews were humbled, saying: "Brothers of the apes and swine," and they fell silent and were confounded. Concerning them the poet said:
"So the curse of Allah be upon the Jews; indeed the Jews are brothers of the apes."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/236.]

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾ and the rest of the verse: these are the hypocrites, as the exegetes have said.

Ibn Zayd said: These are those who said: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day﴾ and the rest of the verse.

This interpretation is more fitting to the apparent sense of the revelation, because these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. ﴿And you see many of them—meaning of the Jews—hastening into sin and transgression and their consuming of the forbidden﴾ up to His saying ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ The "rabbis" (rabbaniyyun) are the scholars, and the "scholars" (ahbar) are the learned men; some said the rabbaniyyun are the Christian scholars and the ahbar are the Jewish scholars.

Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Ibn al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿al-Rabbiyyun﴾, like His saying ﴿with him were many rabbis﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 146].

﴿from their saying sin﴾. This is the most severe verse concerning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, since it places them in the position of those who commit it and joins them together in rebuke.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Adi, [al-Ahmasi] [as in the original], al-Bukhari, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No man lives as a neighbour among a people, practising sins in their midst, and they do not restrain his hands, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 2/332.] [94]

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, Abd Allah ibn Usama, Usayl ibn Zayd al-Jammal, Yahya ibn Salma ibn Muhanna, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of the wicked person among a people is like a people who boarded a ship and divided it, so each person had a share in it. A man among them took an axe and began striking at his place. His companions said: 'What are you doing? Do you want to sink it and sink us?' He said: 'It is my place. If they seize his hands, they are saved and he is saved; and if they leave him, they sink and he sinks.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 8/240, with variation.] [95]

Malik ibn Dinar said: Allah revealed to the angels that they should punish such-and-such a town. The angels cried out to their Lord: "O Lord, among them is Your servant, the worshipper." He said: "Let Me hear his cry, for his face has not changed in anger for My prohibitions." And Allah revealed to Joshua ibn Nun: "I will destroy forty thousand of your people, from their best, and sixty thousand of their worst." He said: "O Lord, these are the wicked; but what of the good?" He said: "They did not become angry for My anger, and they ate and drank with them."

O you who believe, do not take those who took your religion as a mockery and a game (for Allah's words: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who took your religion as a mockery and a game﴾), and the rest of the verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When the caller (muezzin) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews said: "They have risen, may they not rise! They have prayed, may they not pray! They have bowed, may they not bow! They have prostrated, may they not prostrate!" in a manner of mockery and laughter. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Christians who, whenever he heard the muezzin say, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," would say: "May Allah burn the liar." One night his servant came in with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark flew from it into the house, and it burned the house, and he and his family were burned.

Others said: When the disbelievers heard the adhan, they denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims over it, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you have invented something we have never heard of in the past nations. If you claim prophethood, you have opposed the prophets before you in this adhan you have introduced. If there were good in this matter, the first to abandon it would have been the people after the prophets and messengers before you. So where do you get a cry like the cry of a camel? No voice is uglier, and no disbelief is more repulsive." So Allah revealed this verse. (Source cited above.) ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work?﴾

As for after the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj, Ziyad ibn Ayyub, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr al-Asadi, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad said: Ibn Jurayj related from Nafi' from Ibn Umar; Abu al-Husayn said: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj, Muhammad ibn Suhayl ibn Askar, Abu Sa'id al-Haddad, Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn [Yahya], from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father; and a narration from al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, Isma'il ibn Ubayd al-Khuza'i, Muhammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, from his father, who said: When the Muslims arrived in Medina, they would gather and anticipate the prayer, and no one called to it. They discussed this matter, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted the Muslims about how to summon them to prayer. Some said: "Raise a banner on top of the mosque at the time of prayer, so when they see it, they will inform one another." He did not like that. It was said: "Rather, we light a fire." Others said: "Rather, a horn like the horn of the Jews." He disliked it because of the Jews. It was said: "A bell," and he disliked it because of the Christians. But they stood for it, and he ordered the bell to be used so that they might respond.

Abd Allah ibn Zayd said: That night I saw in a dream a man wearing two green garments, carrying a bell. I said: "O servant of Allah, will you sell the bell?" He said: "What will you do with it?" I said: "We call people to prayer with it." He said: "Shall I not guide you to something better than it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" until the end of the adhan. Then he withdrew a short distance and said: "When the prayer is established, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar…" and he described the iqamah to him, its phrases being singular. When I awoke, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of it. He said: "It is a true vision, if Allah wills. Recite it to Bilal, for he has a more resonant voice than you." So we went out to the mosque, and I began reciting it to Bilal while he was calling the adhan. Umar heard it in his house and came out dragging his cloak, saying: "I saw the same as what he saw." The Prophet ﷺ rejoiced and said: "That is more firmly established."

Abu al-Zahiriya related from Abu Shajara, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The first to call the adhan in heaven was the one whom Umar ibn al-Khattab heard." (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu)

As for the section on the adhan:

Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi, Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya, Abu Ja'far ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Sayyah, Abu Umar al-Duri, Abu Ibrahim al-Burjumani, from Sa'id ibn Sa'id, from Nahshal Abu Abd Allah al-Qurashi, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will not be troubled by the reckoning, nor will the cry frighten them, nor will the greatest terror grieve them: the bearer of the Qur'an who delivers it to Allah with what is in it, arriving before his Lord as a noble master; a muezzin who calls the adhan for seven years, taking payment for his adhan out of greed; and a slave who worships his Lord excellently and fulfils the right of his master." [Kanz al-Ummal: 15/831, no. 43308, with slight variation.] [86]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu Amr ibn Uthman, related to them: Abu Thumayla, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for seven years seeking reward, a written quittance from the Fire is recorded for him." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/683, no. 20904; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/561, no. 8376.] [87]

Abu al-Hasan al-Farisi, Abu al-Ala Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir, [...] [illegible word], Muhammad ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd ibn Salama al-Wasiti, Humayd al-Tusi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for a year with a sincere intention, seeking no wage for it, will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection, stand at the gate of Paradise, and be told: Intercede for whom you wish." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/689, no. 20936.] [88]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamd al-Tammar, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Dinar, Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Isa, Ibrahim ibn Rustam, Hammad ibn Salama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibn Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls the adhan for five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven, and whoever leads his companions in five prayers in faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/562, no. 8378.] [89]

Abu al-Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jasham Abu al-Mawja, Abdan, Abd al-Warith, Murra al-Hanafi, Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When the adhan is called, the gates of heaven are opened and supplication is answered; and when the iqamah is called, a supplication is not turned away." [Kanz al-Ummal: 2/108, no. 3372.] [90]

Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn al-Ma'arri, Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Muqri in Basra, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Jassas, Yazid ibn Amr, Abu al-Bar al-Ghanawi, Nail ibn Najih, Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Salim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The muezzin who seeks reward is like a martyr writhing in his blood until he finishes his adhan; every moist and dry thing bears witness for him, and when he dies, his grave will not decay." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/3.] [91]

Abu Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Safyani, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari said: Hammad ibn al-Hasan, Salih ibn Sulayman, the owner of the qarati(s), Attab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Sadusi, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Waqqas, that he said: The arrows of the muezzins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the emigrants.

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: If I were a muezzin, I would not mind not performing Hajj, not performing Umrah, and not fighting in jihad.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not being counted among those who pray at night or fast by day. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins, O Allah, forgive the muezzins."

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have left us, though we are the best, to call the adhan with swords." He said: "Not so, O Umar. There will come upon people a time when they abandon the adhan for their weak ones; and those are flesh which Allah has forbidden to the Fire: the flesh of the muezzins." [92]

Say: O People of the Book, do you blame us only because… (the verse).

Ibn Abbas said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Abu Yasir ibn al-Khattab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', Azar, Zayd ibn Khalid, and Azarail Abu Washa'. They asked him about which of the messengers he believed in. He said: "I believe in Allah, and in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to Abraham… and to Him we are submitting Muslims." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/233, where it reads "yu'min" instead of "u'min".] [93] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "By Allah, we know of no people whose religion is more favoured in this world and the next than ours; the worst of religions is your religion." So Allah revealed this verse.

Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that?"—i.e., I will inform you of what you described, their saying, "We have not seen a people more favoured in this world and the next than you." He mentioned the answer in the form of a beginning, though the beginning itself is not evil, like His saying to the disbelievers: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 72]. ﴿Requital (mathuba) with Allah﴾: reward and recompense, and it is in the accusative as an explanation, like His saying ﴿more in wealth and mightier in following﴾. Its original form is mathuwba, on the pattern of its object-form, as some verbal nouns came on the pattern of the passive participle, such as al-maf'ul and al-maysur; the vowel of the middle radical was dropped because of the heaviness of the waw, and its vowel was transferred to the first radical, which is tha', so it became mathuba, like ma'una and maghuth and maqula. ﴿Whom Allah has cursed﴾: it may be in the genitive as a substitution from "bi-sharrin," or with the meaning "for whom Allah has cursed"; it may be in the nominative with an implied "huwa" (he); and it may be in the accusative by placing "unabbi'ukum" upon it. ﴿And Allah became angry with him, and made some of them apes and swine﴾: the apes are the people of the Sabbath, and the swine are the disbelievers among the people of the table of Jesus.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas that both groups transformed were from their leaders: the ones who were transformed into apes were from their nobles, and their elders were transformed into swine. ﴿And worshipped the Taghut﴾: there are ten readings for it. ﴿Wa-'abada al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the ba', the 'ayn, and the ta', as a verb, which is the reading of the common people; and ﴿and made from them one who worshipped the Taghut﴾, and its confirmation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿and those who worshipped the Taghut﴾. Ibn Wathhab and Hamza read ﴿'abdu al-Taghut﴾ with fatha on the 'ayn, damma on the ba', and kasra on the dal, meaning "the servant," and both are dialects: 'abd and 'abd, like sab' and sab', qird and qird.

Hamza recited in support of this: "How polished is the ape…" with damma on the ra'. Another interpretation is that he meant the plural, i.e., the servants of the Taghut. The plural of 'abd is 'ibad, then the plural of 'ibad is 'abad, a plural of a plural, like thimar and thamr. He encountered two successive dammas, so he changed the first to fatha; hence in the reading of al-A'mash it is ﴿wa-'ubudu al-Taghut﴾ with damma on the 'ayn and the ta', and kasra on the dal.

The poet said:
"Trace the servant to his fathers, black-skinned of the people of 'abd."
[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 3/369.]

It is related from Abu Ja'far al-Qari that he read ﴿wa-'ubida al-Taghut﴾ as a passive verb. Al-Hasan read ﴿wa-'abda al-Taghut﴾ in the singular. Abu Burda al-Aslami read ﴿wa-'abid al-Taghut﴾ in the singular [with variation; so it is in the original]. Ibn Abbas read ﴿wa-'ubayd al-Taghut﴾ in the plural. Abu Waqid al-Laythi read ﴿wa-'abbad al-Taghut﴾, like kafir and kuffar. Awn al-'Uqayli and Aban ibn Tha'lab read ﴿wa-'ubbida al-Taghut﴾, like raka' and sajad. Ibn 'Umayr read ﴿wa-'ubd al-Taghut﴾, like kalb and aklub.

﴿Those are worse in place and further astray from the right way.﴾ When this verse was revealed, the Jews were humbled, saying: "Brothers of the apes and swine," and they fell silent and were confounded. Concerning them the poet said:
"So the curse of Allah be upon the Jews; indeed the Jews are brothers of the apes."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/236.]

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾ and the rest of the verse: these are the hypocrites, as the exegetes have said.

Ibn Zayd said: These are those who said: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day﴾ and the rest of the verse.

This interpretation is more fitting to the apparent sense of the revelation, because these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. ﴿And you see many of them—meaning of the Jews—hastening into sin and transgression and their consuming of the forbidden﴾ up to His saying ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them?﴾ The "rabbis" (rabbaniyyun) are the scholars, and the "scholars" (ahbar) are the learned men; some said the rabbaniyyun are the Christian scholars and the ahbar are the Jewish scholars.

Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Ibn al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿al-Rabbiyyun﴾, like His saying ﴿with him were many rabbis﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 146].

﴿from their saying sin﴾. This is the most severe verse concerning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, since it places them in the position of those who commit it and joins them together in rebuke.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Adi, [al-Ahmasi] [as in the original], al-Bukhari, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No man lives as a neighbour among a people, practising sins in their midst, and they do not restrain his hands, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 2/332.] [94]

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, Abd Allah ibn Usama, Usayl ibn Zayd al-Jammal, Yahya ibn Salma ibn Muhanna, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of the wicked person among a people is like a people who boarded a ship and divided it, so each person had a share in it. A man among them took an axe and began striking at his place. His companions said: 'What are you doing? Do you want to sink it and sink us?' He said: 'It is my place. If they seize his hands, they are saved and he is saved; and if they leave him, they sink and he sinks.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 8/240, with variation.] [95]

Malik ibn Dinar said: Allah revealed to the angels that they should punish such-and-such a town. The angels cried out to their Lord: "O Lord, among them is Your servant, the worshipper." He said: "Let Me hear his cry, for his face has not changed in anger for My prohibitions." And Allah revealed to Joshua ibn Nun: "I will destroy forty thousand of your people, from their best, and sixty thousand of their worst." He said: "O Lord, these are the wicked; but what of the good?" He said: "They did not become angry for My anger, and they ate and drank with them."

﴿And the Jews said: "The hand of God is shackled."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: God had expanded [His provision] for the Jews, so they were among the people with the most wealth and the most abundant lands. When they disobeyed God regarding Muhammad (ﷺ) and denied him, God withheld from them the expansion He had bestowed upon them. At that point Finhas ibn 'Azura said: "The hand of God is shackled." They did not mean that His neck was bound, but that His hand was closed, meaning He withheld provision, and so they attributed stinginess to Him.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani, those who study the semantic dimensions of the Qur'an) said: Finhas made this statement and the others did not forbid him; they accepted his words. Therefore God included them in it. By "hand" they meant giving, because a person's giving is generally the extending of his kindness by his hands. People use "hand" to describe a person's generosity and stinginess.

The poet said:

"Your hands are hands of glory, a generous palm,
and a palm that, when it withholds wealth, spends it."
[Jami' al-Bayan: 6/404, where it reads "bi'l-zad" (with provision) instead of "bi'l-mal" (with wealth). In Lisan al-'Arab: 9/301, it reads "sadaqa" instead of "majd," and "ukhra" instead of "wakaf."]

The stingy person is described as "one with curled fingertips, a closed palm, tight fingers, and shackled hands." God said: ﴿Do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ (Qur'an 17:29).

The poet said:

"Khurasan was a land when Yazid was in it,
and every gate of good things was open.
Then after him, it took on a man with curled fingertips,
as if his face were eating cooked meat."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/238.]

Al-Hasan said: The meaning is "the hand of God is restrained from punishing us, so He punishes us only to the extent of the punishment our fathers received for worshipping the calf," which was seven days.

Mujahid and al-Suddi said: The Jews said that when God removed our kingdom from us, He placed His hand on His chest, showing compassion toward us, and said: "O children of Israel, O sons of my scholars, I will not extend it until I return the kingdom to you." The first view is more correct, due to His words: ﴿He spends as He wills﴾ (Qur'an 5:64). It is also said that this is an interrogative, with the meaning: "Is the hand of God shackled from us?" because He made our livelihood scarce. God said: ﴿Their hands were shackled﴾ (Qur'an 5:64), meaning their hands were restrained from good things and withheld from extending gifts.

Yaman ibn Ri'ab said: It means the laws were made hard and burdensome for them. Evidence for this is His words: ﴿and the shackles that were upon them﴾ (Qur'an 7:157). It is also said that it refers to chaining in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, as in His words: ﴿when the shackles are around their necks﴾ (Qur'an 40:71). ﴿And they were cursed for what they said. Rather, His hands are both outstretched; He spends as He wills﴾ (Qur'an 5:64). The scholars differed concerning the meaning of "the hand of God," Glorified is He. Some said: He has a hand unlike hands, and by "hand" they pointed to a limb, then intended to negate resemblance by saying "unlike hands." This view is not accepted, and its flaw is evident.

Others said: His hand is His power, based on His words: ﴿those of might and insight﴾ (Qur'an 38:45).

It was also said: It is His dominion, as it is said of a man's slave: "he is under his right hand" (milk yamin). God said: ﴿or the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage﴾ (Qur'an 2:237), meaning he possesses that. According to these two views, the wording is figurative while the meaning is singular. This is like His words: ﴿and for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ (Qur'an 55:46), meaning one garden. Al-Farra' said: I was recited a line by one of them:

"Among them, two hands and two feet, twice,
cut by pain, not by the two fat ones."
He meant one of them, and one fat [flesh].

He said: And another recited:

"He walks hunched, with two jaws,
the arta [tree] has made two gardens."
He meant one jaw and one garden.

It was also said: He meant His blessings, as it is said: "So-and-so has a hand (yad) of blessing with me." According to this view, the wording is plural in meaning, like His words: ﴿If you count God's blessing, you cannot enumerate it﴾ (Qur'an 14:34). People use "hand" to describe a person's generosity and stinginess.

The poet said:

"Your hands are hands of glory, a generous palm,
and a palm that, when it withholds wealth, spends it."
[Jami' al-Bayan: 6/404, where it reads "bi'l-zad" (with provision) instead of "bi'l-mal" (with wealth). In Lisan al-'Arab: 9/301, it reads "sadaqa" instead of "majd," and "ukhra" instead of "wakaf."]

The poet said:

"Khurasan was a land when Yazid was in it,
and every gate of good things was open.
Then after him, it took on a man with curled fingertips,
as if his face were eating cooked meat."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/238.]

It is also said that it refers to chaining in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, as in His words: ﴿when the shackles are around their necks﴾ (Qur'an 40:71). ﴿And they were cursed for what they said. cut by pain, not by the two fat ones."
He meant one of them, and one fat [flesh].

O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you.

There is disagreement about the occasion of revelation (tanzil) of this verse and its interpretation (ta'wil).

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made camp at a place, his Companions would choose a shady tree for him, and he would dismount beneath it and take a midday rest. One day he dismounted beneath a tree and hung his sword on it. A Bedouin came, took the sword from the tree, drew it, and then came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was asleep. He said: "O Muhammad, who will protect you from me?" He replied: "Allah." The Bedouin's hand trembled, the sword fell from him, and he struck his head against the tree until he lay unconscious for a while. Then Allah revealed the verse [96].

Anas said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to be guarded. Aisha said: One night I was beside him, and he stayed awake that night. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with you?" He said: "I wish a righteous man would guard me tonight." She said: While we were in that state, I heard the sound of weapons. He said: "Who is this?" It was said: "Sa'd and Hudhayfa; we have come to guard you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then slept until I heard his snoring. Then the verse was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) put his head out from a leather tent and said: "Disperse, O people, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has protected me" [97].

Al-Hasan narrated as a mursal report that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Allah sent me with His message, I was distressed by it, and I knew that some people would deny me." [98] He was rebuking the Quraysh, the Jews, and the Christians, so Allah revealed the verse. I say:

When He revealed His saying ﴿And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah﴾, the Prophet (peace be upon him) refrained from denouncing their gods. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 67], meaning: the faults of their gods.

It has also been said: it was revealed concerning the denunciation of the Jews. That is because he (peace be upon him) invited the Jews to Islam, and they said: "We submitted before you," and they began to mock him and say: "You want us to take you as a lord, just as the Christians took Jesus as a lord." When the Prophet (peace be upon him) saw this, he fell silent. So Allah urged him to call them to Islam and commanded him to say to them ﴿O People of the Book, you do not stand on anything﴾, and so on.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: This is the most correct of the opinions, because there is no separation between His saying ﴿convey what has been sent down to you﴾ and His saying ﴿you do not stand on anything﴾.

When the verse was revealed, he (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever comes from me and helps me..." [99]

It has also been said: it was revealed concerning the story of Uyayna ibn Husayn and the poor people of the Ahl al-Suffa (the companions who lived in the mosque). It has also been said: ﴿convey what has been sent down to you﴾ refers to stoning and retaliation, which has been mentioned in a story. It has also been said: ﴿convey what has been sent down to you﴾ refers to the matter of his wives. That is because when the verse of choice (al-takhyir) was revealed, the Messenger of Allah did not present it to them, out of fear that they would choose this world. So Allah revealed this verse. It has also been said: ﴿convey what has been sent down to you﴾ refers to the matter of Zaynab bint Jahsh.

It has also been said: it was revealed concerning jihad. That is because the hypocrites disliked it, and Allah said ﴿But when a decisive surah is revealed in which fighting is mentioned﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 20], the verse. Some of the believers also disliked it, and Allah said ﴿Have you not seen those who were told: "Restrain your hands"﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 77], the verse. The Prophet (peace be upon him) would refrain from urging some Muslims toward jihad, because he knew of the people's aversion, so Allah revealed this verse.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali said: its meaning is: convey what has been sent down to you concerning the virtue of Ali ibn Abi Talib. When the verse was revealed, he (peace be upon him) took Ali by the hand and said: "Whoever I am his master, Ali is his master" [Musnad Ahmad: 1/84] [100].

Abu al-Qasim Ya'qub ibn Ahmad al-Sarri, Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, Abu Muslim Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Ka'bi, al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal, and Hammad, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' who said: When we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hijjat al-Wada'), we were at Ghadir Khumm. He called out: "Prayer is gathered!" The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) swept the ground beneath two trees, took Ali by the hand, and said: "Am I not closer to the believers than their own selves?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Am I not closer to every believer than his own self?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "This is the master of whomever I am his master. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be an enemy to whoever is his enemy" [al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 5/229].

He said: Then Umar met him and said: "Congratulations to you, O son of Abu Talib! You have become the master of every believing man and woman."

Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Qa'ini narrated to us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Nasibi narrated to us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Subay'i narrated to us: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Dahhan and al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim al-Jassas narrated to us, both saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Hakam narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿O Messenger, convey﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning Ali (may Allah be pleased with him). The Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to convey it, so he (peace be upon him) took Ali by the hand and said: "Whoever I am his master, Ali is his master. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be an enemy to whoever is his enemy" [Musnad Ahmad: 5/370] [101].

It has also been said that ﴿convey what has been sent down to you﴾ refers to the rights of the Muslims.

When the verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon on a certain day, this hadith being in the sermon of the Farewell Pilgrimage. Then he said: "Have I conveyed?"

His saying ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾. Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Qaffal, Abu Amr, al-A'mash and Shibl read "risalatahu" in the singular. This is the reading of the companions of Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud). The rest read it in the plural.

If it is asked: what is the benefit of His saying ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾, since one does not say: "Whoever eats this food, and if he does not eat it, then he has not eaten it"?

The answer to this is what I heard from Abu al-Qasim ibn Jundub, who heard Ali ibn Mahdi al-Tabari say: The command to convey what has been sent down to you concerns both the time and the manner of conveying it, so that the number of supporters and the preparation increase. If he does not do so, then it is as though he has not conveyed everything that Allah entrusted to him, and Allah has made some of it unlawful, because his abandoning the conveying of part of it is comprehensive of the conveying of what he did convey. Compare His saying ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to differentiate...﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 150], the verse.

Know that their belief in some of it to the exclusion of others, and their disbelief in some of it, nullifies belief in the rest. Far be it from the Messenger of Allah to conceal anything of what Allah has revealed.

The scholars said: the call (da'wa) is by reciting the prayer, since part of it is a pillar of its pillars.

I also heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn al-Akhdash [as in the original] report from al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl that he said: The meaning of the verse ﴿convey what has been sent down to you﴾ is: at the time when the strength and the numbers increase. Whoever does not do this is recorded as one who has not conveyed. It has also been said: convey as one who strives, seeking reward, patient, not fearful. It has also been said: ﴿convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾ to all people [and do not fear].

These are among the limits which the state of certainty indicates [see al-Jassas, Ahkam al-Qur'an: 561].

﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾: He will guard and defend you from them. Regarding the question about this verse, when his forehead was wounded, his front tooth was broken, and he was harmed in many situations with various kinds of harm: the answer is that its meaning is, "Allah will protect you from them, so that they cannot reach the likes of you." It has also been said: this verse was revealed after his forehead was wounded and his tooth was broken, because Surat al-Ma'ida is among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed.

It has also been said: its meaning is ﴿And Allah will protect you﴾, that is, He singles you out for protection from among the people, because he was the prophet of his time, and a prophet is protected.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾.

From Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad [al-Daylami], Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sabti, Abu Urwa, Amr ibn Hisham, Muhammad ibn Salama, from Abu Abd al-Rahim, from Abu Abd al-Malik, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama who said: There was a man from the Banu Hashim called Rukana, who was one of the most daring and most fierce of people. He was a polytheist, and he used to tend his sheep, which were called Aqsam. One day the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) left the house of Aisha, heading toward that valley. Rukana met him, and the Prophet of Allah had no one with him. Rukana stood up before him and said:

"O Muhammad, are you the one who insults our gods, al-Lat and al-Uzza, and calls to your God, the Mighty, the Wise? Were it not for the kinship between me and you, I would not speak to you until I killed you. But let your God, the Mighty, the Wise, save you from me today. I will put a proposal to you: will you wrestle with me, and call on your God, the Mighty, the Wise, to help you against me, while I call on al-Lat and al-Uzza? If you throw me down, you will have ten of my sheep, and you may choose them." He (peace be upon him) said: "Stand up, if you wish, and let us make the covenant." The Prophet (ﷺ) called on his God, the Mighty, the Wise, to help him against Rukana, and Rukana called on his god, [al-Lat and al-Uzza], saying: "Help me today against Muhammad." The Prophet (peace be upon him) seized him, threw him down, and sat on his chest.

Rukana said: "O Muhammad, get up. You are not the one who did this to me; it was your God, the Mighty, the Wise, and al-Lat and al-Uzza abandoned me. No one has ever put my side to the ground before you." Rukana said: "Go again. If you throw me down, you will have ten more, and some of the best." The Prophet (peace be upon him) got up and each of them called on his god as they had done the first time. The Prophet (ﷺ) threw him down and sat on his liver. Rukana said to him: "Are you not the one who did this to me? It was your God, the Mighty, the Wise, who did it, and al-Lat and al-Uzza abandoned me. No one has put my side down before you." Rukana said to him: "Go again. If you throw me down, you will have ten more that you choose." Then God took him, and each of them called on his god, and the Prophet of Allah threw him down a third time. Rukana said to him: "You are not the one who did this to me; it was your God, the Mighty, the Wise, who did it, and al-Lat and al-Uzza abandoned me. Take thirty of my sheep, and drive them off."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "I do not want that. Rather, I call you to Islam and its pillars, and I would hate to see you go to the Fire. If you submit, you will be safe." Rukana said: "Will you not show me a sign?" The Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: "Allah is witness against you: if I call upon my Lord, the Mighty, the Majestic, for this, will you answer me with what I have called you to?" He said: "Yes." Near them was a tree with branches and twigs. The Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) pointed to it and said to it: "Come forward by the permission of Allah." It split into two, and half of it came, with its twigs and branches, until it was between the hands of the Prophet (ﷺ) and Rukana. Rukana said to him: "You have shown me something great. Now command it to return." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Allah is witness against you: if I call upon my Lord, the Mighty, the Majestic, and command it, it returns, will you answer me with what I have called you to?"

He said: "Yes." The Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded it, and it returned with its twigs and branches until it joined together again. When the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Submit and you will be safe," Rukana said to him: "Why should I not? I have seen something great. But I dislike that the people of Madina and their youths should talk about me. I will answer you only because of a terror that entered my heart from you. But you know, among the people of Madina and their children, that my side was never put down, and no terror entered my heart for a single moment, night or day. So take your sheep." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "I have no need of your sheep, since you refuse to submit."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went back. Abu Bakr and Umar came, asking him in Aisha's house. I told them that he had gone toward the valley of Adam. They knew that it was the valley of Rukana, which he does not stray from. So they went out in search of him, fearing that Rukana would meet him and kill him. They kept climbing every height and looking. While they were in that state, the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) was seen approaching. They said:

"O Prophet of Allah, how could you go out into this valley alone, when you know it is Rukana's territory, and that he is one of the most daring of people and the most fierce in denying you?" The Prophet (ﷺ) smiled at them and said: "Did not Allah say: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾? He could not reach me, and Allah was with me." He began to tell them the story of Rukana, what had been done to him, and what he had seen. They were amazed at that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we know Rukana. By Him who sent you with the truth, we know that no person has ever put his sides down." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "I called upon my Lord, the Mighty, the Majestic, and He helped me against him. My Lord said: 'Take ten for yourself, and with the strength of ten.'" [102]

Qul, ya ahl al-kitab, lastum 'ala shay'in min al-din hatta tuqimu al-Tawrah wal-Injil wa ma unzila ilaykum min rabbikum...

Translation:

Say, "O People of the Scripture, you have no standing [in religion] until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." And that which has been revealed to you, O Muhammad, from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief, [since] He commanded them with the Qur'an while the proof and argument against them were established. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people. Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians and the Christians...

Translation of the passage:

[The passage is reproduced below in full translation.]

"Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything of the religion until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." And what has been revealed to you, O Muhammad, from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief, since He commanded them with the Qur'an while the proof and the argument were established against them. "So do not grieve over the disbelieving people" — do not be sad over the people who disbelieve. "Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians and the Christians" — the proper form would have been "wa al-Sabi'in" (accusative), but it was put in the nominative as a conjunction with "alladhina" before "inna" entered, so it does not change the meaning, just as you say "Zayd is standing" and "inna Zaydan qa'im" have the same meaning. Al-Hasan read "inna Allaha wa mala'ikatuhu" with the "ta'" in the nominative. "...and the Christians, whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteous deeds," and so on to the verse.

"Indeed, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel concerning tawhid (monotheism, the oneness of God) and prophethood, and We sent to them messengers..." to His words "and they thought there would be no trial," meaning they thought there would be no test or trial. Some Iraqi readers gave the "nun" a nominative vowel; whoever reads it in the accusative does so by dropping concern with "la" (as a negation governing the verb), and whoever reads it in the nominative does so according to the meaning "there would not be." "Then they were blind and deaf" — from al-Hasan: they did not see Him, and they did not hear Him, and that was their punishment. "Then God turned to them in forgiveness; then many of them were blind and deaf again after that, by their abandonment" — some of them, in fighting, "many of them," and they were disbelievers among the People of the Scripture. "And God is Seeing of what they do."

"Certainly those who said, 'God is the Messiah, son of Mary,' have disbelieved" — meaning the Melkites. "And the Messiah said, 'O Children of Israel...'" to the verse.

"Certainly those who said, 'God is the third of three' have disbelieved" — this is the Nestorians, because they said Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. "And there is no god except one God" — to His words "will surely afflict those who disbelieved among them" — He singled out disbelief because He knew that some of them [for them] [[as in the original]] "a painful punishment." "Will they not repent?" to the verse.

"The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger..." to His words "and his mother was a truthful woman" — the verse. "Ṣiddīqa" means one who affirms the truth. Muqatil said: she was called "truthful" because when Gabriel came to her while she was in seclusion and said, "I am only a messenger of your Lord," she believed him. "They both used to eat food" — in this sense, this is an expression for the occurrence of bodily waste, and whoever eats and excretes does not deserve to be God. "Look, O Muhammad, how We make the signs clear" — to His words "how they are turned away" — that is, turned away from the truth. "Say, 'Do you worship...'" — the verse. "Say, O People of the Scripture" — meaning the Christians — "do not go to extremes in your religion beyond the truth" — do not exceed the truth to something else. "And do not follow..." — the verse.

Qul, ya ahl al-kitab, lastum 'ala shay'in min al-din hatta tuqimu al-Tawrah wal-Injil wa ma unzila ilaykum min rabbikum...

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 78–81:

﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾ — i.e., they were punished through (the curse of) the Messiah. So [the curse] was spoken "on the tongue of Dawud (David)."

That is, the people of Ayla (Eilat), when they transgressed on the Sabbath, Dawud said: "O Allah, curse them and make them a sign," so they were transformed into apes. ﴿And ʿIsa (Jesus), son of Maryam﴾ — that is, the disbelievers among the companions of the Table (al-Ma'idah), when they did not believe, ʿIsa said: "O Allah, curse them and make them a sign," so they were transformed into swine. ﴿That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing﴾ — the verse. ﴿They did not forbid one another from the wrong they committed﴾ — i.e., they did not forbid one another from an evil that they did, the verse.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah, ʿAbd Allah ibn Sinan, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn al-Khattab, Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah, al-ʿAla' ibn al-Musayyib, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abu ʿUbaydah, from Ibn Mas'ud; al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Abu ʿAli al-Mawsili, Wahb ibn Munabbih, Khalid, from al-ʿAla' ibn al-Musayyib, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abu ʿUbaydah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when one of those before you among the Children of Israel committed a sin, one who forbade him would admonish him, but when the next day came, [the forbidder] would sit with him, eat with him, and drink with him, as if he had not seen him in sin the day before. When Allah saw that from them, He struck their hearts, one against another, and made from them apes and swine, and cursed them on the tongue of Dawud and ʿIsa son of Maryam, and that is because they disobeyed and were transgressing."

"By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, and you must hold the wrongdoer by the hand and turn him toward the truth, or Allah will surely strike your hearts one against another and curse you as He cursed them." [Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 3/77, no. 5573.] [103]

﴿You see many of them﴾ — i.e., of the Jews, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions — ﴿taking as allies those who disbelieve﴾ — an evil upon evil, when they went out to them, aiding them against Muhammad (peace be upon him). ﴿Evil is what their souls have sent forth for them, that Allah became wrathful toward them, and in the punishment they will abide﴾ — i.e., the punishment of Allah. ﴿And had they believed in Allah, and the Prophet, Muhammad, and in what was revealed to him﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿they would not have taken them as allies, but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ — i.e., those who did not embrace Islam.
