﴿أحل لكم صيد البحر﴾ على المحرم والحلال، وهو على ثلاثة أوجه: الحيتان وأجناسها، وكلها حلال. والثاني: الضفادع وأجناسها، وكلها حرام. والثالث فيه قولان، أحدهما: حلال، والثاني: حرام، وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة.

وقال بعضهم: كل ما كان مثاله في البر فهو حلال في البحر، وما كان مثاله [جزاء ما] في البر فهو حرام في البحر.

فأراد بالبحر جميع المياه، لقوله: ﴿ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر﴾. ﴿وطعامه﴾: قال بعضهم: هو ما مات في الماء فقذفه الماء إلى الساحل ميتا، وهو قول أبي بكر وعمر وابنه وأبي هريرة وابن عباس. وقال بعضهم: هو المليح منه، وهو قول ابن جبير وعكرمة والنخعي وابن المسيب وقتادة. ﴿متاعا لكم وللسيارة﴾ يعني: المارة.

﴿وحرم عليكم صيد البر ما دمتم حرما﴾: لا يجوز للمحرم أكل الصيد إذا صاده هو، أو صيد له بأمره. فأما إذا صاده حلال بغير أمره ولا له، فيجوز له بلا خلاف.

فأما إذا قتله المحرم، فهل يجوز أكله أم لا؟

قال الشافعي: يجوز، لأنه ذكاة مسلم. وعند أبي حنيفة لا يجوز، فأحلّه محل ذكاة المجوس. ودليل الشافعي:

أبو عبد الله [الفنجوي]، وأبو بكر السني، والنامي، ومحمود بن عبد الله، وأبو داود، عن سعيد، عن عثمان بن عبد الله بن موهب: سمعت عبد الله بن أبي قتادة يحدث عن أبيه أنهم كانوا في مسير لهم، وبعضهم ليس بمحرم، قال: فرأيت حمارا وحشيا، فركبت فرسي، وأخذت الرمح، واستعنتهم فأبوا أن يعينوني، فاختلست سوطا من بعضهم، فشددت على الحمار وأخذته. فأكلوا منه، فأشفقوا، فسئل عن ذلك النبي (عليه السلام)، فقال: «هل معكم منه شيء؟» قالوا: لا. قال: «فكلوا».

وبإسناده عن النسائي قال: [حدّثنا] قتيبة بن سعيد، عن يعقوب، وهو ابن عبد الرحمن بن عمرو، عن المطلب، عن جابر، سمعت رسول الله (ﷺ) يقول: «إن صيد البر حلال لكم ما لم تصيدوه، أو يُصَد لكم». [كنز العمال: 5/ 37، ح 11948.] [119]

﴿واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون﴾.

يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر﴾. وقد مرّ تفسيره، فإن جمعه تحريمها. وسنذكر أخبارا في الوعيد الوارد في شربها واتخاذها وبيعها. وبالله التوفيق.

عن الشيخ أبو عمرو أحمد بن أبي الفراني، والحاكم أبو الفضل محمد بن أحمد بن عبد الله المروزي، قالا: حدثني عبد الله بن يحيى، حدثني الحسين بن المبارك، حدثني عتبة بن الوليد، عن عبد الله بن حبيب، عن الزهري، عن ابن المسيب، عن عثمان بن عفان قال: قال رسول الله (ﷺ): «إن الله لا يجمع الخمر والإيمان في امرئ أبدا». [بتفاوت في الدر المنثور: 2/ 322.] [110]

أحمد بن أبي، وعمران بن موسى، ومارود بن بطن، وعثمان بن أبي شيبة، ومحمد بن أبي سلمى الأصفهاني، عن سهيل بن أبي صالح، عن أبيه، عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله (ﷺ):

«مدمن الخمر كعابد الوثن». [111] [سنن ابن ماجة: 2/ 1120.]

أحمد بن أبي، ومحمد بن يعقوب، والربيع بن سليمان، والشافعي، عن مالك، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله (ﷺ) قال: «من شرب الخمر في الدنيا، ثم لم يتب منها، حرمها في الآخرة». [كنز العمال: 5/ 349، ح 13178.] [112]

أحمد بن أبي، وأبو عبد الله بن محمد بن موسى الرازي، والحارث بن أبي أسامة البغدادي، وداود بن المحسن الواسطي، وميسر بن عبد ربه، عن أبي عائشة السعدي، عن يزيد بن عمر بن عبد العزيز، عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبي هريرة وابن عباس جميعا، قالا: قال رسول الله (ﷺ):

«من شرب الخمر في الدنيا سقاه الله من سم الأساود وسم العقارب، ومن شربها تساقط لحم وجهه في الإناء قبل أن يشربها، فإذا شربها [تفسخ لحمه]. [هكذا في المصدر.] ينادي به أهل الجمع، ثم يؤمر به إلى النار. إلا وشاربها وعاصرها ومعتصرها وبايعها ومبتاعها وحاملها والمحمول إليه، وكل فيها سواء في إثمها وحاد بها، ولا يقبل الله منه صلاة ولا صياما ولا حجا ولا عمرة حتى يتوب، فإن مات قبل أن يتوب منها كان حقا على الله أن يعاقبه فيه بكل جرعة شربها في الدنيا شربة من صديد جهنم. ألا وكل مسكر خمر، وكل خمر حرام». [بغية الباحث: 74، بتفاوت يسير.] [113]

أحمد بن أبي، وأبو العباس الأصم، وأحمد بن إسحاق الصنعاني، وأبو نعيم، وعبد العزيز بن محمد بن عبد العزيز، عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله الغافقي من أهل مصر، عن ابن عمر أنه قال:

أشهد أني سمعت رسول الله (ﷺ) وهو يقول: «لعن الله الخمر وشاربها وساقيها وبائعها ومبتاعها وعاصرها ومعتصرها وحاملها والمحمول إليه وآكل ثمنها». [كنز العمال: 5/ 348، ح 13177.] [114]

أحمد بن أبي، وأبو العباس الأصم، ومحمد بن إسحاق بن جعفر الصنعاني، ونعيم بن ماد، وعبد العزيز بن محمد، عن أبي عمرو، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله (ﷺ): «اجتنبوا الخمر فإنها مفتاح كل شر، [كنز العمال: 5/ 345، ح 13159.] ولا يموتن أحدكم وعليه دين، فإنه ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم، وإنما يقتسمون هناك الحسنات والسيئات، واحد بيمينه وواحد بشماله». [جامع البيان: 1/ 381، بتفاوت يسير.] [115]

أبو بكر أحمد بن محمد القطان، ومحمد بن الحسين بن محمد الدهقان، وعثمان بن سعيد الدارمي، والربيع بن الروح أبو توبة الحلبي، ومحمد بن الحرمي، عن حكم بن عيينة، عن محمد بن [المنكدر]، عن علي بن أبي طالب (رضي الله عنه) قال: قال رسول الله (ﷺ): «من شرب الخمر بعد أن حرمها الله على لساني، فليس له أن يزوج إذا خطب، ولا يصدق إذا حدث، ولا يشفع إذا شفع، ولا يؤتمن على أمانة، فمن ائتمنه على أمانة فاستهلكها، فحق على الله عز وجل ألا يخلف عليه». [كنز العمال: 5/ 361، ح 13231، بتفاوت يسير.] [116]

أنشدنا أبو القاسم الحبيبي، أنشدنا أبو العباس عبد الله بن محمد الجبّائي، أنشدنا رضوان بن أحمد الصيدلاني شعرا:

تركت النبيذ لأهل النبيذ ... وصرت حليفا لما عابه
شرابا يدنس عرض الفتى ... ويفتح للشر أبوابه [تفسير القرطبي: 6/ 294.]

﴿والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه لعلكم تفلحون﴾. والأنصاب: أي الأوثان، سميت بذلك لأنهم كانوا ينصبونها، واحدها: نَصَب، بفتح النون وجزم الصاد، ونَصُب منهم النون مثقلا ومخففا. والأزلام: يعني القداح التي كانوا يقتسمون بها. ﴿رجس من عمل الشيطان﴾ تزينه. ﴿فاجتنبوه﴾ رد الكناية إلى الرجس. ﴿لعلكم تفلحون﴾.

﴿إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر﴾ أي يلقي بينكم العداوة والبغضاء، كما فعل الأنصاري الذي [شجّ] سعد بن أبي وقاص [بلحي] الجمل. ﴿ويصدكم عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة﴾ كما فعل بأضياف عبد الرحمن بن عوف. ﴿فهل أنتم منتهون﴾ أي: انتهوا. لفظه استفهام ومعناه أمر، كقوله: ﴿فهل أنتم شاكرون﴾. ﴿وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول واحذروا﴾ المحارم والملاهي. ﴿فإن توليتم﴾ عن ذلك، ﴿فاعلموا أنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين﴾. فأما التوفيق والخذلان، والثواب والعقاب، فإلى الله سبحانه.

فلما نزل تحريم الخمر والميسر، قالت الصحابة: يا رسول الله، ما تقول في إخواننا الذين ماتوا وهم يشربون الخمر ويأكلون مال الميسر؟ فأنزل الله: ﴿ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا﴾، أي: شربوا الخمر. ونظيره قوله: ﴿ومن لم يطعمه فإنه مني﴾. ﴿وفيما أكلوا من الميسر﴾، وذلك ذكر المنعم، لأنه لفظ جامع. ﴿إذا ما اتقوا﴾ الشهوات، ﴿وآمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم اتقوا﴾ الخمر والميسر بعد تحريمهما، ﴿ثم اتقوا﴾ ما حرم الله عليهم كله، ﴿وأحسنوا والله يحب المحسنين﴾.

الحسين بن محمد بن فنجويه، وعمر بن الخطاب، ومحمد بن إسحاق الممسوحي، وأبو بكر بن أبي شيبة، ومحمد بن بكر، عن سعد بن عوف، عن محمد بن حاطب قال: ذكر عثمان، فقال الحسن بن علي: هذا أمير المؤمنين يأتيكم خبركم. فجاء علي فقال: إن عثمان من ﴿الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم اتقوا وآمنوا ثم اتقوا وأحسنوا والله يحب المحسنين﴾.

﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله بشيء من الصيد﴾ الآية.

نزلت عام الحديبية، ابتلاهم الله بالصيد، فكان الوحش يغشى رجالهم كثيرا وهم محرمون. فبينما هم يسيرون بين مكة والمدينة إذ عرض لهم حمار وحش، فحمل عليه أبو اليسر بن عمرو فطعنه برمحه فقتله. فقيل له: إنك قتلت الصيد وأنت حرام، فأتى رسول الله (ﷺ) فسأله عن ذلك، فأنزل الله: ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله﴾، أي: ليختبرنكم الله ﴿بشيء من الصيد﴾، وإنما قال: "بشيء" لأنه ابتلاهم بصيد البر خاصة. ﴿تناله أيديكم﴾ وهي الفراخ والبيض وما لا يستطيع أن يفر من الصيد، ﴿ورماحكم﴾ وهي الوحش وكبار الصيد. ﴿ليعلم الله﴾ أي: ليرى الله ﴿من يخافه بالغيب﴾ ولم يره، أي: من يخافه فلا يصطاد في حال الإحرام. ﴿فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك﴾ أي صاده بعد تحريمه فاستحله، ﴿فله عذاب أليم﴾.

﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقتلوا الصيد وأنتم حرم﴾ أي: محرمون بالحج والعمرة، وهو جمع "إحرام"، ويقال: رجل حرام، وامرأة حرام. ﴿ومن قتله منكم متعمدا﴾: اختلفوا في صيغة العمد الموجب للجزاء والكفارة في قتل الصيد. قال قوم: حرّموا العمد في قتل الصيد مع نسيانه لإحرامه في حال قتله؛ فأما إذا قتله عمدا وهو ذاكر لإحرامه فلا حكم عليه، وأمره إلى الله، لأنه أعظم من أن يكون له كفارة.

قرأ مجاهد والحسن، وقال آخرون: هو العمد، من يحرم بقتل الصيد ذاكرا للحرمة، فيحكم عليه في العمد والخطأ، وهو اختيار الشافعي وأكثر الفقهاء.

وقال الزهري: نزل القرآن بالعمد، وجرت السنة في الخطأ.

وقال ابن عباس: إن قتله متعمدا مختارا سئل: هل قتلت قبله شيئا من الصيد؟ فإن قال: نعم، لم يحكم عليه، وقيل له: اذهب، فينتقم الله منك. وإن قال: لم أقتل قبله شيئا، حكم عليه. فإن عاد وقتل الصيد محرما بعد ما حكم عليه، لم يحكم عليه، ولكن يملأ ظهره وصدره ضربا وجيعا. وكذلك حكم رسول الله (عليه السلام) في وَجّ [وقيل: وَجّ موضع بالبادية، وقيل: بلد بالطائف، وقيل: هي الطائف، وقيل: موضع باليمامة. راجع كتاب العين: 6/ 198، وتاج العروس: 2/ 110.]، وهو وادٍ بالطائف. وعندنا: إذا عاد يحكم عليه، وعليه الجمهور بذلك.

قوله: ﴿فجزاء مثل ما قتل من النعم﴾: نوّنها يعقوب وأهل الكوفة، ورفعوا "مثل" على البدل من "جزاء"، كأنه فسّر الجزاء فقال: ﴿مثل ما قتل من النعم﴾. وأضافها الآخرون، لاختلاف الاسمين. ﴿يحكم به﴾ أي: بالجزاء ﴿ذوا عدل منكم﴾ أي: فقيهان عدلان، فينظران إلى أشبه الأشياء به من النعم فيحكمان به، حتى يفديه ويهديه إلى الكعبة. فإن قتل نعامة فعليه بدنة، فإن قتل بقرة أو إبلا أو حمارا فعليه بقرة، وإن قتل بقرة وحشية فعليه عجل إنسي. وفي الضبع كبش، لأنه صيد وأكله حلال. وأما السباع فلا شيء فيها. وإن قتل ضبيا فعليه شاة، وفي الغزال والأرنب جمل، وفي الضب واليربوع سخلة، وفي الحمام والفواخت والقمري والدبسي [وهو نوع من الفواخت.] وذوات الأطواق، وكل ما عَبّ وهَدَر، شاة.

واختلفوا في الجراد، وروي عن عمر أنه قال لكعب، وقد قتل جرادتين: ما جعلت على نفسك؟ قال: درهما. قال: بخ! درهم خير من مائة جرادة.

وروي عن عمر أيضا: في الجرادة تمرة.

قال ابن عباس: قبضة من طعام. فإن أصاب فرخا أو بيضا أو شيئا لا يبلغ بهيمة، فعليه قيمته طعاما، وهو قول عمر وعثمان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف وابن عباس وابن عمر، وإليه ذهب الشافعي، وعليه جمهور أهل العلم.

قال النخعي: يقوّم الصيد المقتول قيمته من الدراهم، فيشتري بثمنه فداء من النعم ويهديه إلى الكعبة.

وروى عبد الملك بن عمير، عن قبيصة بن جابر قال: خرجنا حجاجا، وكنا إذا صلينا الغداة أفسدنا رواحلنا، نتماشى ونتحدث. فبينا نحن ذات غداة إذ سنح لنا ضبي، فابتدرناه، فابتدرته ورميته بحجر فأصاب حشاه، فركب ردعه فمات. فلما قدمنا مكة سألنا عمر بن الخطاب (رضي الله عنه)، وكان حاجا، وكان جالسا وإلى جنبه عبد الرحمن بن عوف، فسألته عن ذلك. فقال عمر لعبد الرحمن: ما ترى؟ فقال: عليه شاة. قال: وأنا أرى ذلك. قال: اذهب فأهد شاة. فخرجت إلى صاحبي فقلت: إن أمير المؤمنين لم يدر ما يقول حتى سأل غيره. قال: فلم [يفجأنا] إلا وعمر معه درّة، فعلاني بالدرّة، فقال: أتقتل في الحرم وتسفّه الحكم؟ قال الله: ﴿يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم﴾، فأنا عمر وهذا عبد الرحمن. [بتفاوت وتفصيل في تاريخ دمشق: 49/ 242.]

محمد بن عبدوس، عن محمد بن الحسن، عن علي بن عبد العزيز، عن القاسم بن علام، عن أبي أمية، عن أبي [صوليه]، عن عبد الملك بن عمير: ﴿أو كفارة طعام مساكين﴾ إذا لم يكن واجدا للفدية، أو لم يكن للمقتول مثل من النعم، فكفارته حينئذ الإطعام. يقوّم الصيد المقتول دراهم، ثم يقوّم الدراهم طعاما، فيتصدق على مساكين الحرم. فإن لم يجد فصيام، لكل نصف صاع يوما عند أبي حنيفة، وقال الشافعي: لكل مدّ. وعنده أنه يخير من هذه الأشياء الثلاثة، فإنه ذكرها تلفظا، وهو قول مجاهد وعطاء. واختلفوا في تقويم الطعام.

فقال الشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأكثر الفقهاء: يقوّم الصيد بقيمة الأرض التي أصابه بها.

وقال الشعبي: يقوّم بسعر الأرض التي يكفر بها. قال جابر: سأل الشعبي عن محرم أصاب صيدا بخراسان. قال: يكفر بمكة بثمن مكة.

واختلفوا في الإطعام: أين يطعم؟

فقال قوم: يطعم بمكة، فلا يجزي إلا بها، وهذا قول عطاء، وإليه ذهب الشافعي.

فأما الهدي فلا يجوز إلا بمكة بلا خلاف. وأما الصوم فيجوز بأي موضع صام بلا خلاف. فلو أكل من لحم صيد، فلا جزاء عليه، إلا في قتله أو جرحه. ولو دلّ على صيد كان مسيئا، وعليه الجزاء، كما لو أمر بقتل مسلم، لا قصاص عليه، وكان مسيئا.

واعلم أن الصيد الذي لا يجوز قتله في الحرم وفي حال الإحرام هو ما حلّ أكله.

أبو عبد الله الحسين بن محمد الدينوري، وأبو بكر البستي، وأبو عبد الرحمن البستي، وقتيبة بن سعد، عن مالك، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله (ﷺ) قال: «خمس ليس على المحرم في قتلهن جناح: الغراب، والحدأة، والعقرب، والفأرة، والكلب العقور». [سنن النسائي: 5/ 188.] [117]

وبه عن عبد الرحمن، عمرو بن علي، عن يحيى، عن شعبة، عن قتادة، عن ابن المسيب، عن عائشة، عن النبي (ﷺ) قال: «خمس يقتلهن المحرم: الحية، والفأرة، والحدأة، والغراب الأبقع، والكلب العقور». [سنن النسائي: 5/ 188.] [118]

﴿ليذوق وبال أمره﴾: جزاء معصيته. ﴿عفا الله عما سلف﴾ في الجاهلية. ﴿ومن عاد في الإسلام فينتقم الله منه﴾ في الآخرة.

وقال ابن عباس: يملأ ظهره سوطا حتى يموت.

قال السدي: عاد رجل بعد ما حكم عليه بالتحريم، فأحرقه الله بالنار.

﴿والله عزيز ذو انتقام﴾.

﴿أحل لكم صيد البحر﴾ على المحرم والحلال، وهو على ثلاثة أوجه: الحيتان وأجناسها، وكلها حلال. والثاني: الضفادع وأجناسها، وكلها حرام. والثالث فيه قولان، أحدهما: حلال، والثاني: حرام، وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة.

وقال بعضهم: كل ما كان مثاله في البر فهو حلال في البحر، وما كان مثاله [جزاء ما] في البر فهو حرام في البحر.

فأراد بالبحر جميع المياه، لقوله: ﴿ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر﴾. ﴿وطعامه﴾: قال بعضهم: هو ما مات في الماء فقذفه الماء إلى الساحل ميتا، وهو قول أبي بكر وعمر وابنه وأبي هريرة وابن عباس. وقال بعضهم: هو المليح منه، وهو قول ابن جبير وعكرمة والنخعي وابن المسيب وقتادة. ﴿متاعا لكم وللسيارة﴾ يعني: المارة.

﴿وحرم عليكم صيد البر ما دمتم حرما﴾: لا يجوز للمحرم أكل الصيد إذا صاده هو، أو صيد له بأمره. فأما إذا صاده حلال بغير أمره ولا له، فيجوز له بلا خلاف.

فأما إذا قتله المحرم، فهل يجوز أكله أم لا؟

قال الشافعي: يجوز، لأنه ذكاة مسلم. وعند أبي حنيفة لا يجوز، فأحلّه محل ذكاة المجوس. ودليل الشافعي:

أبو عبد الله [الفنجوي]، وأبو بكر السني، والنامي، ومحمود بن عبد الله، وأبو داود، عن سعيد، عن عثمان بن عبد الله بن موهب: سمعت عبد الله بن أبي قتادة يحدث عن أبيه أنهم كانوا في مسير لهم، وبعضهم ليس بمحرم، قال: فرأيت حمارا وحشيا، فركبت فرسي، وأخذت الرمح، واستعنتهم فأبوا أن يعينوني، فاختلست سوطا من بعضهم، فشددت على الحمار وأخذته. فأكلوا منه، فأشفقوا، فسئل عن ذلك النبي (عليه السلام)، فقال: «هل معكم منه شيء؟» قالوا: لا. قال: «فكلوا».

وبإسناده عن النسائي قال: [حدّثنا] قتيبة بن سعيد، عن يعقوب، وهو ابن عبد الرحمن بن عمرو، عن المطلب، عن جابر، سمعت رسول الله (ﷺ) يقول: «إن صيد البر حلال لكم ما لم تصيدوه، أو يُصَد لكم». [كنز العمال: 5/ 37، ح 11948.] [119]

﴿واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون﴾.

**God made the Kaaba the Sacred House** ﴿God has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House...﴾ (the verse).

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They used to betray one another and fight, so God revealed ﴿God has made the Kaaba...﴾.

Mujahid said: It was called the Kaaba because it is square (*murabbaʿ*), and the Arabs call every square building a *kaʿbah*.

Muqatil said: It was called the Kaaba because it stands apart from other buildings.

The lexicographers said: Its root meaning is protrusion and elevation. The ankle (*kaʿb*) was so named because it protrudes from the two sides of the foot. From this comes the saying about a girl who is nearing puberty and whose breasts have begun to protrude: *qad takaʿʿabat* (she has developed breasts). So the Kaaba was named for its height above the ground and its firm position on an elevated place. It was called the Sacred House (*al-Bayt al-Haram*) because God made it sacred and magnified its sanctity.

It is recorded in a hadith: "Written at the base of the Maqam (the Station of Abraham): I am God, Lord of Bakkah. I made it sacred the day I created the heavens and the earth, and the day I placed these two mountains and surrounded them with seven rows of angels. Whoever comes to me as a visitor to this House, knowing its right and submitting to me in lordship, I will forbid his body to the Fire."

**Standing for mankind** (*qiyaman lil-nas*): a means of support (*qiwam*) for them in the affairs of their religion and their worldly life, and the betterment of their livelihood and their final return (*maʿad*), because of what comes to them through the Hajj (pilgrimage), the ʿUmrah (lesser pilgrimage), visitation and trade, what is brought to it of fruits, and what appears in it of various kinds of blessings.

Ibn Jubayr said: Whoever comes to this House seeking something of this world and the Hereafter, he will obtain it. **And the sacred month**: he meant the sacred months, in which people are safe. **And the offerings and the garlands** ﴿...and the sacred month, and the offerings and the garlands. That is so that you may know that God knows...﴾ (the verse).

An objection was raised regarding this verse, and it was said: How does the beginning of the verse fit with its end? The answer is that the implied meaning (*majaz*) of the verse is: God knows the welfare of people just as He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth... ﴿Know that God is severe in punishment...﴾ (two verses), ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal...﴾, meaning the lawful and the unlawful.

﴿And even if the abundance of the evil should impress you...﴾ was revealed concerning Sharih ibn Subayʿah and the pilgrims of Bakr ibn Wail. ﴿So fear God, O people of understanding...﴾ (the verse): do not molest the pilgrims, even if they are polytheists.

The story has already passed at the beginning of the surah, ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made apparent to you, would distress you...﴾ (the verse). They differed concerning its revelation.

Al-Zuhri and Qatadah narrated from Anas, and Abu Salih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, both saying: The people asked the Messenger of God ﷺ until they pressed him with questions. He stood up angry, delivering a sermon, and said: "Ask me! By God, you will not ask me about anything in this station of mine except that I will tell you of it." The Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ became apprehensive that some matter had come about that had already passed. Anas said: I kept looking to the right and to the left, and I found every man with his head wrapped in his garment, weeping. A man of Quraysh, of Banu Tamim, called ʿAbd Allah ibn Hudhafah stood up to him. He used to be disparaged concerning his lineage, and when he quarrelled he would be called by someone other than his father. He said: "O Prophet of God, who is my father?" He said: "Abu Hudhafah ibn Qays."

Al-Zuhri said: The mother of ʿAbd Allah ibn Hudhafah said: "I have never seen a child more disobedient than you! Did you feel secure that your mother had committed what the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) committed, so that you would disgrace her before the people?"

He said: "By God, if he had attributed me to a black slave, I would have been attached to him."

Another man stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, where am I?" He said: "In the Fire."

Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) stood up, and a man kissed the Messenger of God, and he said: "We are content with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, with Muhammad as prophet, and with the Quran as imam. We, O Messenger of God, are people newly come from the Jahiliyyah and polytheism, so pardon us; may God pardon you." His anger subsided, and he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, Paradise and the Fire were just now displayed to me on the face of this wall, and I have never seen the like of today in good and evil."

[Tafsir ʿAbd al-Razzaq: 1/196; Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/109.]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They were a people who would ask the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) as a test of his command and in mockery of him. One of them would say, "Who is my father?" Another would say, "Where am I?" And another, when his camel had strayed, would say, "Where is my camel?"

So God the Exalted revealed this verse.

ʿAli and Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: The Messenger of God ﷺ addressed us and said: "God has prescribed the Hajj upon you." A man of Banu Asad called ʿUkkashah ibn Mihsan stood up and said: "Every year, O Messenger of God?" He turned away from him until the man had repeated it two or three times. Then he (peace be upon him) said: "Woe to you! What makes you secure that I would not say yes? By God, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory you would not have been able to fulfil it, and if you had left it you would have disbelieved. So leave me as I have left you, for those before you perished through their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. When I command you with something, do of it what you are able; and when I forbid you from something, avoid it."

[Tafsir Majmaʿ al-Bayan: 3/428.] [120]

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed when they asked the Messenger of God about the *baḥīrah* (a she-camel marked as forbidden, its ear split) and the *sāʾibah* (a freed animal left to roam). Do you not see that He says after it: ﴿God has not ordained any baḥīrah or sāʾibah...﴾ (the verse). ﴿And if you ask about them when the Quran is being revealed, they will be made apparent to you. God has pardoned that; and God is Forgiving and Forbearing. A people before you asked about such things, then became disbelievers because of them.﴾ This is because the Quran is only revealed with the imposition of an obligation that becomes difficult for you, or something that had been lawful for you. As the people of Thamud asked Salih for the she-camel, and the people of Jesus asked for the table (of food), ﴿then they became disbelievers in it﴾ and were destroyed.

Makhul al-Shami narrated from Abu Thaʿlabah al-Khushani, who said: God has prescribed obligations, so do not neglect them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; He has set limits, so do not transgress them; and He has pardoned some things, not out of forgetfulness, so do not search after them.

**What God has not ordained** (*ma jaʿala Allah*): what God did not reveal, nor did it come from God, nor did He command it. Its parallel is His saying ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Quran﴾ (43:3), meaning: We revealed it. ﴿...of baḥīrah, sāʾibah, wasīlah (a she-sheep marked for its line of births), or ḥām (a stallion camel marked as protected)...﴾ (the verse).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Abu Salih al-Sammān, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to Aktham ibn al-Jawn: "O Aktham, I saw ʿAmr ibn Luhayy ibn Qamaʿah ibn Khindif dragging his intestines in the Fire. I have not seen a man more like a man than he is like you, nor you like him. He was the first to change the religion of Ishmael, to set up idols, to slaughter the baḥīrah, to release the sāʾibah, to join the wasīlah, and to protect the ḥām. I saw him in the Fire harming the people of the Fire with the stench of his intestines." Aktham said: "O Messenger of God, do you fear that his resemblance will harm me?" He said: "No, you are a believer and he is a disbeliever."

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/117; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/111.] [121]

He said: That is because when a she-camel bears twelve females in succession, she is released (*sība*), her back is not ridden, her wool is not shorn, and her milk is not drunk except by a guest. Whatever female she bears after that has its ear split, and then it is left to go free. Yet it is among the camels, its back is not ridden, its wool is not shorn, and its milk is not drunk except by a guest, just as was done with its mother; and it is the baḥīrah, the daughter of the sāʾibah.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When a she-camel gave birth to five litters, they examined the fifth. If it was a male, they slaughtered it, and both men and women ate it. If it was a female, they split its ear, and it is the baḥīrah: its wool is not shorn, the name of God is not mentioned over it when it is slaughtered, it is not ridden, and it is forbidden to women, who may not drink its milk or benefit from it. Its milk and benefits were exclusively for men and not for women until it died. When it died, men and women shared in eating it.

It was also said: When a young camel (*saqb*) was born, they split its ear and said: "O God, if it lives, it is a male; if it dies, it is slaughtered." When it died, they ate it.

As for the sāʾibah, a man would release a part of his property and bring it to the *sadanah* (the custodians of the idols), who would give it to them. They would feed from it wayfarers, its milk and its meat, except that they did not give any of it to women until it died. When it died, men and women together ate it.

[See Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 12/81.]

Alqamah said: It is the slave who is released (*yusayyab*) on condition that he has no clientage (*walaʾ*) and no blood-money (*ʿaql*), but he inherits.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Clientage belongs only to the one who manumits."

[Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 4/247.] [122]

He used the feminine form *fāʿilah* (sāʾibah) while it carries the meaning of the passive *mafʿūlah* (released), according to the usage of His saying ﴿from a gushing fluid﴾ (86:6) and ﴿in a pleasing life﴾ (69:21).

As for the wasīlah, it is the sheep that gives birth to seven litters. If the seventh litter was a male, they slaughtered it and offered it to the gods; if it was a female, they spared it; and if it was a male and a female together, they spared the male for the sake of the female. They said: It has joined its brother, so they did not slaughter it.

As for the ḥām, it is the stallion camel that has sired offspring. His back was protected, so he was not ridden, not burdened, and not prevented from water or pasture, unless he died, whereupon men and women ate him.

God said: ﴿But those who disbelieve invent falsehoods against God, and most of them do not use reason.﴾ (the verse), meaning they fabricate (*yakhtalilūn*) against God in their saying: "And God commanded us with them." ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ (the verse), meaning concerning the permission of the cattle and crops and the explanation of laws and rulings. A parallel to this is found in Surat al-Baqarah and Surat Luqman.

As for the ḥām, it is the stallion camel that has sired offspring. His back was protected, so he was not ridden, not burdened, and not prevented from water or pasture, unless he died, whereupon men and women ate him.

God said: ﴿But those who disbelieve invent falsehoods against God, and most of them do not use reason.﴾ (the verse), meaning they fabricate (*yakhtalilūn*) against God in their saying: "And God commanded us with them." ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ (the verse), meaning concerning the permission of the cattle and crops and the explanation of laws and rulings. A parallel to this is found in Surat al-Baqarah and Surat Luqman.

**God made the Kaaba the Sacred House** ﴿God has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House...﴾ (the verse).

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They used to betray one another and fight, so God revealed ﴿God has made the Kaaba...﴾.

Mujahid said: It was called the Kaaba because it is square (*murabbaʿ*), and the Arabs call every square building a *kaʿbah*.

Muqatil said: It was called the Kaaba because it stands apart from other buildings.

The lexicographers said: Its root meaning is protrusion and elevation. The ankle (*kaʿb*) was so named because it protrudes from the two sides of the foot. From this comes the saying about a girl who is nearing puberty and whose breasts have begun to protrude: *qad takaʿʿabat* (she has developed breasts). So the Kaaba was named for its height above the ground and its firm position on an elevated place. It was called the Sacred House (*al-Bayt al-Haram*) because God made it sacred and magnified its sanctity.

It is recorded in a hadith: "Written at the base of the Maqam (the Station of Abraham): I am God, Lord of Bakkah. I made it sacred the day I created the heavens and the earth, and the day I placed these two mountains and surrounded them with seven rows of angels. Whoever comes to me as a visitor to this House, knowing its right and submitting to me in lordship, I will forbid his body to the Fire."

**Standing for mankind** (*qiyaman lil-nas*): a means of support (*qiwam*) for them in the affairs of their religion and their worldly life, and the betterment of their livelihood and their final return (*maʿad*), because of what comes to them through the Hajj (pilgrimage), the ʿUmrah (lesser pilgrimage), visitation and trade, what is brought to it of fruits, and what appears in it of various kinds of blessings.

Ibn Jubayr said: Whoever comes to this House seeking something of this world and the Hereafter, he will obtain it. **And the sacred month**: he meant the sacred months, in which people are safe. **And the offerings and the garlands** ﴿...and the sacred month, and the offerings and the garlands. That is so that you may know that God knows...﴾ (the verse).

An objection was raised regarding this verse, and it was said: How does the beginning of the verse fit with its end? The answer is that the implied meaning (*majaz*) of the verse is: God knows the welfare of people just as He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth... ﴿Know that God is severe in punishment...﴾ (two verses), ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal...﴾, meaning the lawful and the unlawful.

﴿And even if the abundance of the evil should impress you...﴾ was revealed concerning Sharih ibn Subayʿah and the pilgrims of Bakr ibn Wail. ﴿So fear God, O people of understanding...﴾ (the verse): do not molest the pilgrims, even if they are polytheists.

The story has already passed at the beginning of the surah, ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made apparent to you, would distress you...﴾ (the verse). They differed concerning its revelation.

Al-Zuhri and Qatadah narrated from Anas, and Abu Salih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, both saying: The people asked the Messenger of God ﷺ until they pressed him with questions. He stood up angry, delivering a sermon, and said: "Ask me! By God, you will not ask me about anything in this station of mine except that I will tell you of it." The Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ became apprehensive that some matter had come about that had already passed. Anas said: I kept looking to the right and to the left, and I found every man with his head wrapped in his garment, weeping. A man of Quraysh, of Banu Tamim, called ʿAbd Allah ibn Hudhafah stood up to him. He used to be disparaged concerning his lineage, and when he quarrelled he would be called by someone other than his father. He said: "O Prophet of God, who is my father?" He said: "Abu Hudhafah ibn Qays."

Al-Zuhri said: The mother of ʿAbd Allah ibn Hudhafah said: "I have never seen a child more disobedient than you! Did you feel secure that your mother had committed what the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) committed, so that you would disgrace her before the people?"

He said: "By God, if he had attributed me to a black slave, I would have been attached to him."

Another man stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, where am I?" He said: "In the Fire."

Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) stood up, and a man kissed the Messenger of God, and he said: "We are content with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, with Muhammad as prophet, and with the Quran as imam. We, O Messenger of God, are people newly come from the Jahiliyyah and polytheism, so pardon us; may God pardon you." His anger subsided, and he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, Paradise and the Fire were just now displayed to me on the face of this wall, and I have never seen the like of today in good and evil."

[Tafsir ʿAbd al-Razzaq: 1/196; Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/109.]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They were a people who would ask the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) as a test of his command and in mockery of him. One of them would say, "Who is my father?" Another would say, "Where am I?" And another, when his camel had strayed, would say, "Where is my camel?"

So God the Exalted revealed this verse.

ʿAli and Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: The Messenger of God ﷺ addressed us and said: "God has prescribed the Hajj upon you." A man of Banu Asad called ʿUkkashah ibn Mihsan stood up and said: "Every year, O Messenger of God?" He turned away from him until the man had repeated it two or three times. Then he (peace be upon him) said: "Woe to you! What makes you secure that I would not say yes? By God, if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory you would not have been able to fulfil it, and if you had left it you would have disbelieved. So leave me as I have left you, for those before you perished through their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. When I command you with something, do of it what you are able; and when I forbid you from something, avoid it."

[Tafsir Majmaʿ al-Bayan: 3/428.] [120]

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed when they asked the Messenger of God about the *baḥīrah* (a she-camel marked as forbidden, its ear split) and the *sāʾibah* (a freed animal left to roam). Do you not see that He says after it: ﴿God has not ordained any baḥīrah or sāʾibah...﴾ (the verse). ﴿And if you ask about them when the Quran is being revealed, they will be made apparent to you. God has pardoned that; and God is Forgiving and Forbearing. A people before you asked about such things, then became disbelievers because of them.﴾ This is because the Quran is only revealed with the imposition of an obligation that becomes difficult for you, or something that had been lawful for you. As the people of Thamud asked Salih for the she-camel, and the people of Jesus asked for the table (of food), ﴿then they became disbelievers in it﴾ and were destroyed.

Makhul al-Shami narrated from Abu Thaʿlabah al-Khushani, who said: God has prescribed obligations, so do not neglect them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; He has set limits, so do not transgress them; and He has pardoned some things, not out of forgetfulness, so do not search after them.

**What God has not ordained** (*ma jaʿala Allah*): what God did not reveal, nor did it come from God, nor did He command it. Its parallel is His saying ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Quran﴾ (43:3), meaning: We revealed it. ﴿...of baḥīrah, sāʾibah, wasīlah (a she-sheep marked for its line of births), or ḥām (a stallion camel marked as protected)...﴾ (the verse).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Abu Salih al-Sammān, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to Aktham ibn al-Jawn: "O Aktham, I saw ʿAmr ibn Luhayy ibn Qamaʿah ibn Khindif dragging his intestines in the Fire. I have not seen a man more like a man than he is like you, nor you like him. He was the first to change the religion of Ishmael, to set up idols, to slaughter the baḥīrah, to release the sāʾibah, to join the wasīlah, and to protect the ḥām. I saw him in the Fire harming the people of the Fire with the stench of his intestines." Aktham said: "O Messenger of God, do you fear that his resemblance will harm me?" He said: "No, you are a believer and he is a disbeliever."

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/117; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/111.] [121]

He said: That is because when a she-camel bears twelve females in succession, she is released (*sība*), her back is not ridden, her wool is not shorn, and her milk is not drunk except by a guest. Whatever female she bears after that has its ear split, and then it is left to go free. Yet it is among the camels, its back is not ridden, its wool is not shorn, and its milk is not drunk except by a guest, just as was done with its mother; and it is the baḥīrah, the daughter of the sāʾibah.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When a she-camel gave birth to five litters, they examined the fifth. If it was a male, they slaughtered it, and both men and women ate it. If it was a female, they split its ear, and it is the baḥīrah: its wool is not shorn, the name of God is not mentioned over it when it is slaughtered, it is not ridden, and it is forbidden to women, who may not drink its milk or benefit from it. Its milk and benefits were exclusively for men and not for women until it died. When it died, men and women shared in eating it.

It was also said: When a young camel (*saqb*) was born, they split its ear and said: "O God, if it lives, it is a male; if it dies, it is slaughtered." When it died, they ate it.

As for the sāʾibah, a man would release a part of his property and bring it to the *sadanah* (the custodians of the idols), who would give it to them. They would feed from it wayfarers, its milk and its meat, except that they did not give any of it to women until it died. When it died, men and women together ate it.

[See Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 12/81.]

Alqamah said: It is the slave who is released (*yusayyab*) on condition that he has no clientage (*walaʾ*) and no blood-money (*ʿaql*), but he inherits.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Clientage belongs only to the one who manumits."

[Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 4/247.] [122]

He used the feminine form *fāʿilah* (sāʾibah) while it carries the meaning of the passive *mafʿūlah* (released), according to the usage of His saying ﴿from a gushing fluid﴾ (86:6) and ﴿in a pleasing life﴾ (69:21).

As for the wasīlah, it is the sheep that gives birth to seven litters. If the seventh litter was a male, they slaughtered it and offered it to the gods; if it was a female, they spared it; and if it was a male and a female together, they spared the male for the sake of the female. They said: It has joined its brother, so they did not slaughter it.

As for the ḥām, it is the stallion camel that has sired offspring. His back was protected, so he was not ridden, not burdened, and not prevented from water or pasture, unless he died, whereupon men and women ate him.

God said: ﴿But those who disbelieve invent falsehoods against God, and most of them do not use reason.﴾ (the verse), meaning they fabricate (*yakhtalilūn*) against God in their saying: "And God commanded us with them." ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ (the verse), meaning concerning the permission of the cattle and crops and the explanation of laws and rulings. A parallel to this is found in Surat al-Baqarah and Surat Luqman.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 105–109 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ – the verse. The scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse. Some of them left it to its apparent meaning.

Damrah ibn Rabi'ah said: al-Hasan recited this verse and said, "Praise be to God for it, and praise be to God for acting upon it. There has never been a believer in the past, nor a believer in what remains, except that beside him is a hypocrite who dislikes his deed."

Some of them said: its meaning is, ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾, so act in obedience to God; ﴿those who have gone astray will not harm you when you are guided﴾, that is, when you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.

Abu al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfah, regarding this verse: "When you enjoin and forbid."

Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated from Abu Zibyan, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) said from the pulpit: "You recite this verse, ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ – the verse – and you place it other than its proper place, and you do not know what it is. I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'When people see an evil and do not change it, God will surely encompass them with punishment. So enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and do not be deceived by God's words, ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾, so that one of you says, "Upon me is my own self." By God, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or [else] the worst of you will be placed in authority over you; then the best of you will call upon God, but He will not answer them.'"

[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/681, no. 8447 (similar in meaning).] It is indicated by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "We said, 'O Messenger of God, if we do not enjoin what is right and do not forbid what is wrong, until there remains no good except that we act upon it and no evil except that we refrain from it, and we never enjoin or forbid anyone again?'"

He (peace be upon him) said: "Enjoin what is right; if they do not accept all of it, [at least] they will not be forbidden from [what is] wrong entirely, and if they do not refrain from all of it..."

It was also said: the meaning of the verse is, ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ when you have enjoined what is right and forbidden what is wrong, but it was not accepted from you.

Shaqiq ibn 'Uqbah said: It was said to Ibn 'Umar, "If you sat down in these days and did not enjoin or forbid, for God has said, ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves; those who have gone astray will not harm you when you are guided﴾."

Ibn 'Umar said: "It does not apply to me or to my companions, for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, 'Let the one present convey to the absent.' [Musnad Ahmad: 1/230.] So we were the present and you are the absent. But this verse is for people who will come after us, who, if they say [it], will have their words not accepted."

Sahl ibn al-Ashhab narrated from al-Husayn and al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, that this verse was recited to Ibn Mas'ud, ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "This is not its time. Say it [only] when it is accepted from you; when it is rejected by you, then upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves." Then he said: "The Qur'an was revealed when it was revealed: among it are verses whose interpretation has already passed; among it are verses whose interpretation occurred in the time of the Messenger of God; among it are verses whose interpretation will occur shortly after the Prophet (ﷺ); among it are verses that will occur and not be fulfilled after today; among it are verses that will occur at the end of time; and among it are verses whose interpretation will occur on the Day of Resurrection, such as what is mentioned of the reckoning, Paradise and Hell. So as long as your hearts and your desires are united, and you have not been divided into factions, and some of you have not tasted the violence of others, then enjoin and forbid. But when hearts and desires diverge, you are divided into factions, and some of you taste the violence of others, then it is each man for himself – and at that point the interpretation of this verse arrives."

Abu Umayyah al-Sam'ani said: I heard Abu Tha'labah [al-Khushani] about this verse, ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾.

Abu Tha'labah said: "I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it, and he said: 'Enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, until you see a religion being preferred, miserliness being obeyed, desire being followed, and every person of opinion being pleased with his own opinion; then take care of your own self and leave aside their common folk, for behind you are days of patience. Whoever acts in obedience to God in those days, the one who has gone astray and perished after him will not harm him, and the reward of the doer on that day will be like the reward of fifty doers of what you are upon.'" [al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi: 10/92.] [123]

They said: "O Messenger of God, the reward of fifty doers from among them?" He said: "No, rather the reward of fifty doers from among you."

Some of them said: this verse was revealed concerning the people of desires.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said: A young man from among the people of desires came to Safwan ibn Harith and mentioned something of his affair. Safwan said: "Shall I not direct you to the particular [mark] of God by which He distinguishes His friends: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ – the verse." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/132.]

al-Dahhak said: ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ when desires differ, so long as there is no sword or whip.

Ibn Jubayr said: this verse was revealed concerning the People of the Book, meaning, ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves; those who have gone astray will not harm you﴾ from among the People of the Book.

al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wrote to the people of Hajar, whose governor was al-Mundhir ibn Sawi al-Tamimi, calling them to Islam; and whoever refused should pay the jizyah. When the letter reached him, he presented it to those with him from among the Jews, Arabs, Christians and Magians, and they acknowledged the jizyah but disliked Islam. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wrote to him: "As for the Arabs, nothing is accepted from them except Islam or the sword; as for the People of the Book and the Magians, accept the jizyah from them." [Asbab al-Nuzul: 142; Zad al-Masir: 2/330.] [124] When the letter of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was read to them, the Arabs embraced Islam, and the People of the Book and the Magians gave the jizyah. The hypocrites of Makkah said concerning this: "How strange! Muhammad claims that God sent him to fight people until they say, 'There is no god but God,' yet he accepted the jizyah from the Magians of Hajar and the People of the Book, and he has not compelled them to Islam, while he returned it to our Arab brothers?" This was very grievous to the Muslims, so God revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾, meaning: after the message has been delivered by Muhammad, so beware. And He revealed, after the Arabs had embraced Islam, ﴿There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become distinct from error﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning all the disbelievers. That was because when a man embraced Islam, they would say, "You have made your father foolish, and you have gone astray, and you have done such and such." So God revealed: ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves; those who have gone astray from among your fathers will not harm you when you are guided﴾. This is an expression of urging, and the Arabs use such words as "'alayka" (upon you), "labbayka" (at your service), "ilayka" (to you), "'indaka" (with you) and "dunaka" (beside you). [See Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/138.]

Then He said: ﴿To God is your return, all of you﴾, the misguided and the guided, ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾.

﴿O you who have believed, testimony between you [is required] when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest – the verse﴾

It was revealed concerning three men who went out as merchants from Madinah to Syria: 'Adi ibn Fadi and Tamim ibn Aws al-Dari, both of them Christians, and Budayl, the freedman of 'Amr ibn al-'As al-Sahmi, who was a Muslim emigrant. They differed about the kunyah of his father.

al-Kalbi said: "Budayl ibn Abi Mazinah." Qatadah, Ibn Sirin and 'Ikrimah said: "He is Ibn Abi Mariyah," as did Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and Ibn Abi Maryam. When they reached Syria, Budayl fell ill and wrote a document containing everything he had with him, and placed it among his goods, without informing his companions. When his illness grew severe, he made a bequest to Tamim and 'Adi and instructed them to deliver his goods to his family when they returned. Budayl died, and they searched his goods and took from them a vessel of silver, engraved with gold, containing three hundred mithqal of silver adorned with gold. They concealed it, then completed their business, returned, and came to Madinah, and they delivered the goods to the family of the deceased. They searched [and found] the document, in which was listed everything he had, and they found that the vessel was missing from it, [namely] the silver vessel adorned with gold, weighing three hundred mithqal. They came to Tamim and 'Adi and said: "Did our companion sell any of his goods?" They said, "No." "Did he suffer a loss in trade?" They said, "No." "Did his illness last long so that he spent on himself?" They said, "No." They said, "We found in his goods a document in which was listed what he had, and we are missing from it a silver vessel adorned with gold, three hundred mithqal of silver." They said: "We do not know; he only bequeathed something to us and instructed us to deliver it to you, and we delivered it; we have nothing but what was decided." So they brought the matter to the Prophet (ﷺ), and God revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, testimony between you [is required] when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest: two just witnesses from among you﴾. [Tarikh Dimashq: 11/71.]

The people of Kufa said: its meaning is "let two witness," the wording of the verse being a report but its meaning an command. The people of Basra said: its meaning is "the testimony between you is the testimony of two," so the testimony was elided and the two were placed in its stead, like His saying, ﴿and ask the town﴾, meaning "ask the people of the town," and the town was placed in his stead and so put in the accusative.

Some of them said: its meaning is, "the testimony between you when death approaches one of you, that two should bear witness, [being] just, trustworthy and sound of mind, ﴿from among you﴾, O assembly of believers, from among the people of your religion and your community."

This was said by all the exegetes except 'Ikrimah and 'Ubaydah, who said: its meaning is "from the tribe of the one making the bequest."

They differed concerning the description of the two. Some people said: they are the two witnesses who bear witness to the bequest of the one making it.

Others said: they are the two executors. God intended to emphasize the matter, so He made the executor two. The evidence for this interpretation is that He followed it with His saying, ﴿you detain them after the prayer, and they swear by God﴾, and a witness is not bound by an oath; and because the verse was revealed concerning the two executors. According to this view, "testimony" means presence, as in your saying, "I witnessed so-and-so," meaning "I was present." God said, ﴿Were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub?﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 133] – the verse – and He said, ﴿and let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾. [Surah al-Nur: 2]

﴿or two others from outside your [community]﴾, that is, outside your religion. This is the view of Ibn al-Musayyab, al-Nakha'i, Ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, 'Ubaydah, Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Abu Mahjan, who said: "If they do not find two Muslims, let them bear witness with two disbelievers."

Shurayh said: "If a man is in a foreign land and finds no Muslim to witness his bequest, let him call a Jew, a Christian, a Magian, or a worshipper of idols – whichever disbeliever it is – and his testimony is permissible. The testimony of disbelievers against Muslims is not permissible except during travel, and it is not permissible during travel except in a bequest. If two Muslim men come and testify contrary to their testimony, the testimony of the Muslims is accepted and the testimony of the disbelievers is nullified."

It is related from al-Sha'bi: a man from among the Muslims was overtaken by death and made a bequest, but he found no one from among the Muslims to witness his bequest. al-Ash'ari said: "This is a matter that had not occurred in the time of the Messenger of God." So he made them swear and upheld their testimony.

Others said: its meaning is "from outside your tribe and your clan." This is the view of al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and 'Ikrimah, who said: the testimony of a disbeliever is not permissible, whether in travel or at home.

﴿If you are travelling in the land﴾, that is, you journey and travel in the land, ﴿and the calamity of death befalls you﴾, and you make a bequest to them both and deliver your property to them, ﴿and they are not trusted [regarding] the rights of the heirs﴾, so they are suspected in that matter and the heirs accuse them of betrayal. Then the ruling in that case is ﴿you detain them﴾, that is, you stop them ﴿after the prayer﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: this is connected to His saying, ﴿or two others from outside your [community]﴾, from among the disbelievers. As for when the two are Muslims, there is no oath upon them.

They differed about what this prayer is. al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, Ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: it is after the 'Asr prayer. al-Suddi said: it is after the prayer of the people of their religion and community, because they do not regard the 'Asr prayer. ﴿and they swear by God﴾, that is, they swear, ﴿if you doubt﴾, that is, if you have doubts: ﴿We will not exchange it for any price﴾, meaning: we will not swear falsely by God for the sake of worldly gain that we would take on account of it, ﴿even if he were a near relative﴾, even if the one for whom we swear were a near relative of ours, ﴿and we will not conceal the testimony of God﴾. al-Sha'bi recited, "we will not conceal testimony of God" with tanwin, and "God" with a kasrah on the ha' by attachment, meaning "by God" as an oath. It is related from Abu Ja'far, "testimony of Allah" with the alif cut and its initial vowel kasrah, meaning "and we will not conceal testimony," then he began an oath, saying, "Allah," i.e., "by God" [...] [an illegible word] [...] with tanwin on the testimony, "Allah" with the alif and lam and a kasrah on the ha', making the interrogative a particle of oath. It is related from some of them, "testimony" with tanwin, "Allah" with a fathah on the ha', meaning "and we will not conceal the testimony of God." Otherwise, ﴿indeed we would then be among the sinners﴾.

When this verse was revealed upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he performed the 'Asr prayer and summoned 'Adi and Tamim, and they were made to swear beside the pulpit by God, besides whom there is no god, that they had not betrayed anything of what had been entrusted to them. He swore to that, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) let them go once they had sworn. Then they concealed the vessel for as long as God willed them to conceal it, and then it came to light. They differed about how the vessel came to light.

Ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas that the vessel was found in Makkah, and they said: "We bought it from 'Adi and Tamim."

Others said: when the time passed, the vessel was made public, and this reached the Banu Tamim, so they came to the two about it. They said: "We had indeed bought this from them." They said: "Did you not both claim that our companion had sold nothing of his goods?" They said: "We did not have its price, so we disliked acknowledging it to you, and therefore we concealed it from you." So they brought them both before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and God revealed:

﴿Then if it becomes known﴾, that is, it is discovered and comes to light. The root of "ʿathar" is falling upon or stumbling over something, and from it is the saying, "I stumbled upon such-and-such" when I struck it and fell upon it.

al-A'mash said:

"With a she-camel of firm stride, when she stumbles, / a fall is nearer to her than my saying 'ah'."

By his saying "'athart" he means: she struck the tip of her hoof on a stone or something else. Then it is used for everything that one comes upon unexpectedly after it had been hidden, as in their proverbs: "He stumbled upon the yarn at the last moment, so he left not a monkey in Najd."

﴿that they both﴾, meaning the two executors, ﴿have incurred sin﴾, that is, they have deserved sin by their false oaths and their betrayal. ﴿then two others from among the heirs of the deceased﴾ will ﴿stand in their place﴾, meaning in place of the two executors, ﴿from among those who have a claim﴾.

Ḥasan and Ḥafs read it with a fatḥah on the tā', and this is the reading of 'Ali and Ubayy ibn Ka'b, meaning "the one who has become due" – "ḥaqqa" and "istaḥqqa" have the same meaning. He said: ﴿al-awlayān﴾ refers back to "two others," "the two more deserving," and it was not made nominative by "istiḥqāq."

The rest read it with a ḍammah on the tā' in the passive, meaning those about whom and for whose sake the sin was incurred, namely the heirs of the deceased; the two swearers incurred guilt on their account and concerning them, according to the sense, as in His saying, ﴿over the kingdom of Solomon﴾.

Ṣakhr al-Ghayy said:

"Whenever you deny it, you will know it, / upon its edges is a sturdy, oozing [brand]."

﴿al-awlayān﴾ in the dual is read by most of the people of Kufa, and it is Ya'qub's preference, meaning "from among the first ones."

Ḥasan read "al-awwalūn," and the others read "al-awlayān" according to the dialect of "the others" (the second). That is permissible because "al-awwalān" is definite, while "al-ākharān" [is definite] by frequency, since when He said "from among those who" and made them two and described them, it became like a definite in meaning.

﴿They swear by God: "Our testimony is more worthy than their testimony"﴾, that is, by God, our testimony is more worthy than their testimony, meaning our oath is more worthy than their oath. Its parallel is His saying, in the matter of li'an, ﴿then the testimony of each of them is four testimonies﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 6], meaning oaths. This is like the speaker's saying, "I testify by God" and "I swear by Him." ﴿and we have not transgressed﴾ in our oath; ﴿indeed we would then be among the wrongdoers.﴾

When this verse was revealed, 'Amr ibn al-'As and al-Muttalib ibn Wada'ah al-Sahmi stood up and swore by God once after the 'Asr prayer, and the cup was handed over to them and to the heirs of the deceased. Tamim al-Dari, after he had embraced Islam and pledged allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ), used to say: "God, mighty and majestic, has spoken truly: I took the cup, and so I repent to God and seek His forgiveness."

The oath passed to the two heirs because the two executors were proven to have possessed the vessel, then they claimed they had bought it. Likewise, if an executor claims that the one making the bequest bequeathed something to him and there is no evidence; and likewise if a man claims against another man a sum of money, and the defendant acknowledges that, then claims that he bought it from the claimant or that the claimant gifted it to him. In these cases and their like, it is ruled that the oath be returned to the claimant.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Abu al-Nadr, from Badhan, freed slave of Umm Hani, from Ibn Abbas, from Tamim al-Dari, who said: "We sold the cup for a thousand dirhams, and I and 'Adi divided it. When I embraced Islam, I felt guilty about that, after I had sworn falsely. I went to the heirs of the deceased and informed them that my companion had a similar amount. They rushed at him and brought him to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he asked them for evidence, but they found none. So he ordered the heirs to swear, and 'Amr and al-Muttalib swore. Then the five hundred was taken from 'Adi, and I returned the five hundred."

[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/156.]

This is His saying, ﴿That is more suitable that they should bring the testimony in its proper form﴾. That is, that is more fitting and more appropriate for the two executors to bring the testimony in its proper form, and likewise for all people, when they fear that the oaths will be returned and the rights imposed upon them.

﴿And fear God and listen﴾, and so on. The scholars differed concerning the ruling of this verse. Some of them said: it is abrogated (mansukh), and this was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Others said: it is muhkam (not abrogated), and this is the correct view.

﴿On the day﴾, that is, remember and beware, the day when ﴿God will gather the messengers﴾, and this is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and say, "What was your answer?"﴾, that is, what did your peoples answer you, and what did your nations reject from you, when you called them to My monotheism and My obedience? ﴿They will say﴾, that is, they will say, ﴿"We have no knowledge."﴾ Ibn Abbas said: "We have no knowledge, except the knowledge that You know better than us."

Ibn Jurayj said: the meaning of His saying "What was your answer?" is: what did they carry, and did they believe after you, so that they would say, "We have no knowledge."

Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and al-Suddi, among those who say this: on that day they will be terrified and confused and will be unable to answer; then, after their minds return to them, they will bear witness concerning their nations.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 5, verse 105–109 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ – the verse. The scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse. Some of them left it to its apparent meaning.

Damrah ibn Rabi'ah said: al-Hasan recited this verse and said, "Praise be to God for it, and praise be to God for acting upon it. There has never been a believer in the past, nor a believer in what remains, except that beside him is a hypocrite who dislikes his deed."

Some of them said: its meaning is, ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾, so act in obedience to God; ﴿those who have gone astray will not harm you when you are guided﴾, that is, when you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.

Abu al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfah, regarding this verse: "When you enjoin and forbid."

Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated from Abu Zibyan, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) said from the pulpit: "You recite this verse, ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ – the verse – and you place it other than its proper place, and you do not know what it is. I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'When people see an evil and do not change it, God will surely encompass them with punishment. So enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and do not be deceived by God's words, ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾, so that one of you says, "Upon me is my own self." By God, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or [else] the worst of you will be placed in authority over you; then the best of you will call upon God, but He will not answer them.'"

[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/681, no. 8447 (similar in meaning).] It is indicated by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "We said, 'O Messenger of God, if we do not enjoin what is right and do not forbid what is wrong, until there remains no good except that we act upon it and no evil except that we refrain from it, and we never enjoin or forbid anyone again?'"

He (peace be upon him) said: "Enjoin what is right; if they do not accept all of it, [at least] they will not be forbidden from [what is] wrong entirely, and if they do not refrain from all of it..."

It was also said: the meaning of the verse is, ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ when you have enjoined what is right and forbidden what is wrong, but it was not accepted from you.

Shaqiq ibn 'Uqbah said: It was said to Ibn 'Umar, "If you sat down in these days and did not enjoin or forbid, for God has said, ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves; those who have gone astray will not harm you when you are guided﴾."

Ibn 'Umar said: "It does not apply to me or to my companions, for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, 'Let the one present convey to the absent.' [Musnad Ahmad: 1/230.] So we were the present and you are the absent. But this verse is for people who will come after us, who, if they say [it], will have their words not accepted."

Sahl ibn al-Ashhab narrated from al-Husayn and al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, that this verse was recited to Ibn Mas'ud, ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "This is not its time. Say it [only] when it is accepted from you; when it is rejected by you, then upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves." Then he said: "The Qur'an was revealed when it was revealed: among it are verses whose interpretation has already passed; among it are verses whose interpretation occurred in the time of the Messenger of God; among it are verses whose interpretation will occur shortly after the Prophet (ﷺ); among it are verses that will occur and not be fulfilled after today; among it are verses that will occur at the end of time; and among it are verses whose interpretation will occur on the Day of Resurrection, such as what is mentioned of the reckoning, Paradise and Hell. So as long as your hearts and your desires are united, and you have not been divided into factions, and some of you have not tasted the violence of others, then enjoin and forbid. But when hearts and desires diverge, you are divided into factions, and some of you taste the violence of others, then it is each man for himself – and at that point the interpretation of this verse arrives."

Abu Umayyah al-Sam'ani said: I heard Abu Tha'labah [al-Khushani] about this verse, ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾.

Abu Tha'labah said: "I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it, and he said: 'Enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, until you see a religion being preferred, miserliness being obeyed, desire being followed, and every person of opinion being pleased with his own opinion; then take care of your own self and leave aside their common folk, for behind you are days of patience. Whoever acts in obedience to God in those days, the one who has gone astray and perished after him will not harm him, and the reward of the doer on that day will be like the reward of fifty doers of what you are upon.'" [al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi: 10/92.] [123]

They said: "O Messenger of God, the reward of fifty doers from among them?" He said: "No, rather the reward of fifty doers from among you."

Some of them said: this verse was revealed concerning the people of desires.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said: A young man from among the people of desires came to Safwan ibn Harith and mentioned something of his affair. Safwan said: "Shall I not direct you to the particular [mark] of God by which He distinguishes His friends: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ – the verse." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/132.]

al-Dahhak said: ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾ when desires differ, so long as there is no sword or whip.

Ibn Jubayr said: this verse was revealed concerning the People of the Book, meaning, ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves; those who have gone astray will not harm you﴾ from among the People of the Book.

al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wrote to the people of Hajar, whose governor was al-Mundhir ibn Sawi al-Tamimi, calling them to Islam; and whoever refused should pay the jizyah. When the letter reached him, he presented it to those with him from among the Jews, Arabs, Christians and Magians, and they acknowledged the jizyah but disliked Islam. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wrote to him: "As for the Arabs, nothing is accepted from them except Islam or the sword; as for the People of the Book and the Magians, accept the jizyah from them." [Asbab al-Nuzul: 142; Zad al-Masir: 2/330.] [124] When the letter of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was read to them, the Arabs embraced Islam, and the People of the Book and the Magians gave the jizyah. The hypocrites of Makkah said concerning this: "How strange! Muhammad claims that God sent him to fight people until they say, 'There is no god but God,' yet he accepted the jizyah from the Magians of Hajar and the People of the Book, and he has not compelled them to Islam, while he returned it to our Arab brothers?" This was very grievous to the Muslims, so God revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾, meaning: after the message has been delivered by Muhammad, so beware. And He revealed, after the Arabs had embraced Islam, ﴿There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become distinct from error﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning all the disbelievers. That was because when a man embraced Islam, they would say, "You have made your father foolish, and you have gone astray, and you have done such and such." So God revealed: ﴿upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves; those who have gone astray from among your fathers will not harm you when you are guided﴾. This is an expression of urging, and the Arabs use such words as "'alayka" (upon you), "labbayka" (at your service), "ilayka" (to you), "'indaka" (with you) and "dunaka" (beside you). [See Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/138.]

Then He said: ﴿To God is your return, all of you﴾, the misguided and the guided, ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾.

﴿O you who have believed, testimony between you [is required] when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest – the verse﴾

It was revealed concerning three men who went out as merchants from Madinah to Syria: 'Adi ibn Fadi and Tamim ibn Aws al-Dari, both of them Christians, and Budayl, the freedman of 'Amr ibn al-'As al-Sahmi, who was a Muslim emigrant. They differed about the kunyah of his father.

al-Kalbi said: "Budayl ibn Abi Mazinah." Qatadah, Ibn Sirin and 'Ikrimah said: "He is Ibn Abi Mariyah," as did Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and Ibn Abi Maryam. When they reached Syria, Budayl fell ill and wrote a document containing everything he had with him, and placed it among his goods, without informing his companions. When his illness grew severe, he made a bequest to Tamim and 'Adi and instructed them to deliver his goods to his family when they returned. Budayl died, and they searched his goods and took from them a vessel of silver, engraved with gold, containing three hundred mithqal of silver adorned with gold. They concealed it, then completed their business, returned, and came to Madinah, and they delivered the goods to the family of the deceased. They searched [and found] the document, in which was listed everything he had, and they found that the vessel was missing from it, [namely] the silver vessel adorned with gold, weighing three hundred mithqal. They came to Tamim and 'Adi and said: "Did our companion sell any of his goods?" They said, "No." "Did he suffer a loss in trade?" They said, "No." "Did his illness last long so that he spent on himself?" They said, "No." They said, "We found in his goods a document in which was listed what he had, and we are missing from it a silver vessel adorned with gold, three hundred mithqal of silver." They said: "We do not know; he only bequeathed something to us and instructed us to deliver it to you, and we delivered it; we have nothing but what was decided." So they brought the matter to the Prophet (ﷺ), and God revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, testimony between you [is required] when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest: two just witnesses from among you﴾. [Tarikh Dimashq: 11/71.]

The people of Kufa said: its meaning is "let two witness," the wording of the verse being a report but its meaning an command. The people of Basra said: its meaning is "the testimony between you is the testimony of two," so the testimony was elided and the two were placed in its stead, like His saying, ﴿and ask the town﴾, meaning "ask the people of the town," and the town was placed in his stead and so put in the accusative.

Some of them said: its meaning is, "the testimony between you when death approaches one of you, that two should bear witness, [being] just, trustworthy and sound of mind, ﴿from among you﴾, O assembly of believers, from among the people of your religion and your community."

This was said by all the exegetes except 'Ikrimah and 'Ubaydah, who said: its meaning is "from the tribe of the one making the bequest."

They differed concerning the description of the two. Some people said: they are the two witnesses who bear witness to the bequest of the one making it.

Others said: they are the two executors. God intended to emphasize the matter, so He made the executor two. The evidence for this interpretation is that He followed it with His saying, ﴿you detain them after the prayer, and they swear by God﴾, and a witness is not bound by an oath; and because the verse was revealed concerning the two executors. According to this view, "testimony" means presence, as in your saying, "I witnessed so-and-so," meaning "I was present." God said, ﴿Were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub?﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 133] – the verse – and He said, ﴿and let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾. [Surah al-Nur: 2]

﴿or two others from outside your [community]﴾, that is, outside your religion. This is the view of Ibn al-Musayyab, al-Nakha'i, Ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, 'Ubaydah, Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Abu Mahjan, who said: "If they do not find two Muslims, let them bear witness with two disbelievers."

Shurayh said: "If a man is in a foreign land and finds no Muslim to witness his bequest, let him call a Jew, a Christian, a Magian, or a worshipper of idols – whichever disbeliever it is – and his testimony is permissible. The testimony of disbelievers against Muslims is not permissible except during travel, and it is not permissible during travel except in a bequest. If two Muslim men come and testify contrary to their testimony, the testimony of the Muslims is accepted and the testimony of the disbelievers is nullified."

It is related from al-Sha'bi: a man from among the Muslims was overtaken by death and made a bequest, but he found no one from among the Muslims to witness his bequest. al-Ash'ari said: "This is a matter that had not occurred in the time of the Messenger of God." So he made them swear and upheld their testimony.

Others said: its meaning is "from outside your tribe and your clan." This is the view of al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and 'Ikrimah, who said: the testimony of a disbeliever is not permissible, whether in travel or at home.

﴿If you are travelling in the land﴾, that is, you journey and travel in the land, ﴿and the calamity of death befalls you﴾, and you make a bequest to them both and deliver your property to them, ﴿and they are not trusted [regarding] the rights of the heirs﴾, so they are suspected in that matter and the heirs accuse them of betrayal. Then the ruling in that case is ﴿you detain them﴾, that is, you stop them ﴿after the prayer﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: this is connected to His saying, ﴿or two others from outside your [community]﴾, from among the disbelievers. As for when the two are Muslims, there is no oath upon them.

They differed about what this prayer is. al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, Ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: it is after the 'Asr prayer. al-Suddi said: it is after the prayer of the people of their religion and community, because they do not regard the 'Asr prayer. ﴿and they swear by God﴾, that is, they swear, ﴿if you doubt﴾, that is, if you have doubts: ﴿We will not exchange it for any price﴾, meaning: we will not swear falsely by God for the sake of worldly gain that we would take on account of it, ﴿even if he were a near relative﴾, even if the one for whom we swear were a near relative of ours, ﴿and we will not conceal the testimony of God﴾. al-Sha'bi recited, "we will not conceal testimony of God" with tanwin, and "God" with a kasrah on the ha' by attachment, meaning "by God" as an oath. It is related from Abu Ja'far, "testimony of Allah" with the alif cut and its initial vowel kasrah, meaning "and we will not conceal testimony," then he began an oath, saying, "Allah," i.e., "by God" [...] [an illegible word] [...] with tanwin on the testimony, "Allah" with the alif and lam and a kasrah on the ha', making the interrogative a particle of oath. It is related from some of them, "testimony" with tanwin, "Allah" with a fathah on the ha', meaning "and we will not conceal the testimony of God." Otherwise, ﴿indeed we would then be among the sinners﴾.

When this verse was revealed upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he performed the 'Asr prayer and summoned 'Adi and Tamim, and they were made to swear beside the pulpit by God, besides whom there is no god, that they had not betrayed anything of what had been entrusted to them. He swore to that, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) let them go once they had sworn. Then they concealed the vessel for as long as God willed them to conceal it, and then it came to light. They differed about how the vessel came to light.

Ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas that the vessel was found in Makkah, and they said: "We bought it from 'Adi and Tamim."

Others said: when the time passed, the vessel was made public, and this reached the Banu Tamim, so they came to the two about it. They said: "We had indeed bought this from them." They said: "Did you not both claim that our companion had sold nothing of his goods?" They said: "We did not have its price, so we disliked acknowledging it to you, and therefore we concealed it from you." So they brought them both before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and God revealed:
